托马斯·S·库恩（1922-1996）是麻省理工学院劳伦斯·洛克菲勒语言学和哲学荣誉退休教授。他的著作包括《本质张力》、《黑体理论与量子不连续性，1894-1912》和《哥白尼革命》。

Thomas S. Kuhn (1922–96) was the Laurence Rockefeller Professor Emeritus of linguistics and philosophy at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology. His books include The Essential Tension; Black-Body Theory and the Quantum Discontinuity, 1894–1912; and The Copernican Revolution.

Introductory Essay

伊恩·哈金

IAN HACKING

伟大的书籍凤毛麟角，而这本就是其中之一。读过之后，你就会明白。

Great books are rare. This is one. Read it and you will see.

可以跳过这段引言。如果您想了解这本书半个世纪前的创作缘起、它的影响以及围绕其论点的激烈争论，可以稍后再阅读。如果您想了解一位资深人士对这本书如今地位的看法，也可以稍后再阅读。

Skip this introduction. Come back to it if you want to know how the book came into being half a century ago, what its impact was, and the disputes that raged around its theses. Come back if you want one experienced opinion of the status of the book today.

这些话介绍的是这本书，而非库恩及其毕生著作。他通常称这本书为《结构》，在日常对话中则简称为“那本书”。我沿用他的用法。《本质张力》是一部杰出的哲学论文集（而非历史论文集），收录了库恩在《结构》出版前后不久发表的论文。1它可以被视为一系列评注和扩展，因此是极佳的辅助读物。

These remarks introduce the book, not Kuhn and his life work. He usually referred to the book as Structure, and in conversation simply as “the book.” I follow his usage. The Essential Tension is a superb collection of philosophical (as opposed to historical) papers that he published immediately before or soon after Structure.1 It can be thought of as a series of commentaries and expansions, so it is excellent companion reading.

由于这是对《结构》一书的介绍，因此本文将不再讨论“本质张力”之外的内容。但需要注意的是，他经常在谈话中提到， 《黑体与量子不连续性》一书研究了马克斯·普朗克在……开启的第一次量子革命。十九世纪末期，正是结构主义精髓的完美体现。2

Since this is an introduction to Structure, nothing beyond The Essential Tension will be discussed here. Note, however, that he often said in conversation that Black-Body and the Quantum Discontinuity, a study of the first quantum revolution launched by Max Planck at the end of the nineteenth century, is an exact example of what Structure is all about.2

《结构》一书固然伟大，但它可以从无数种角度解读，并应用于多种用途。因此，这篇导言只是众多解读方式中的一种。这本书开启了一系列关于库恩生平和著作的书籍。斯坦福哲学百科全书在线版中有一篇视角与本文不同的、对托马斯·塞缪尔·库恩（1922-1996）著作的精彩简明导论。 3 关于库恩对其生平和思想的最后回忆，请参阅阿里斯蒂德斯·巴尔塔斯、科斯塔斯·加夫罗格鲁和瓦西莉基·金迪于1995年对他进行的访谈。 4他最欣赏的关于他著作的书籍是保罗·霍伊宁根-休恩的《重构科学革命》。5关于库恩所有出版物的列表，请参阅詹姆斯·科南特和约翰·豪格兰德合著的《结构之后的道路》。6

Just because Structure is a great book, it can be read in endless ways and put to many uses. Hence this introduction is only one among many possible ones. The book launched a fleet of books about Kuhn’s life and work. An excellent short introduction to the work of Thomas Samuel Kuhn (1922–96), with a different slant from this one, is to be found in the online Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy.3 For Kuhn’s final reminiscences of his life and thoughts, see the interview conducted in 1995 by Aristides Baltas, Kostas Gavroglu, and Vassiliki Kindi.4 The book about his work that he most admired was Paul Hoyningen-Huene’s Reconstructing Scientific Revolutions.5 For a list of all Kuhn’s publications, see James Conant and John Haugeland’s The Road since Structure.6

有一点常被忽略：如同所有伟大的著作一样，这本书饱含激情，作者渴望将一切公之于众。这一点甚至从第一页开篇那句朴实无华的话就能看出：“如果将历史视为一个包含更多内容的宝库，而不仅仅是轶事或年表，那么它就能彻底改变我们如今所受制于的科学观念。” 7 托马斯·库恩致力于改变我们对科学的理解——也就是改变我们对那些使我们人类得以主宰地球（无论好坏）的活动的理解。他成功了。

One thing is not said often enough: like all great books, this is a work of passion and a passionate desire to get things right. This is plain even from its modest first sentence on page 1: “History, if viewed as a repository for more than anecdote or chronology, could produce a decisive transformation in the image of science by which we are now possessed.”7 Thomas Kuhn was out to change our understanding of the sciences—that is, of the activities that have enabled our species, for better or worse, to dominate the planet. He succeeded.

1962

1962

本版是为了纪念《结构》杂志创刊五十周年而出版的。一九六二年已是遥远的过去。科学本身也发生了翻天覆地的变化。当时，物理学是科学的女王。库恩接受过物理学训练。虽然很少有人精通物理学，但人人都知道物理学才是关键所在。冷战正酣，所以人人都知道原子弹的存在。美国的小学生不得不练习躲在课桌下。城镇每年至少会拉响一次空袭警报，所有人都必须躲避。那些公开抗议核武器、不躲避的人可能会被逮捕，而且确实有人因此被捕。鲍勃·迪伦于1962年9月首次演唱了《暴雨将至》（A Hard Rain's A-Gonna Fall）；人人都以为这首歌是关于核辐射的。1962年10月爆发了古巴导弹危机，这是自1945年以来，世界距离核战争最近的一次。物理学及其带来的威胁是每个人都在关注的问题。

The present edition commemorates the fiftieth anniversary of Structure. Nineteen sixty-two was a long time ago. The sciences themselves have radically changed. The queen of the sciences, then, was physics. Kuhn had been trained as a physicist. Few people knew much physics, but everybody knew that physics was where the action was. A cold war was in progress, so everyone knew about the Bomb. American schoolchildren had to practice cowering under their desks. At least once a year towns sounded an air raid siren, at which everyone had to take shelter. Those who protested against a nuclear weapon, by ostentatiously not taking shelter, could be arrested, and some were. Bob Dylan first performed “A Hard Rain’s A-Gonna Fall” in September 1962; everyone assumed it was about nuclear fallout. In October 1962 there was the Cuban Missile Crisis, the closest the world has come, after 1945, to nuclear war. Physics and its threat were on everyone’s mind.

冷战早已结束，物理学也不再是科学界的中心。1962年的另一件大事是弗朗西斯·克里克和詹姆斯·沃森因DNA分子生物学的发现而荣获诺贝尔奖，马克斯·佩鲁茨和约翰·肯德鲁因血红蛋白分子生物学的发现而荣获诺贝尔奖。这预示着变革的到来。如今，生物技术才是主导。库恩以物理科学及其发展史为模型。读完他的著作后，您需要自行判断，他关于物理科学的论述在如今蓬勃发展的生物技术领域中，究竟在多大程度上仍然适用。此外，信息科学也发挥了重要作用。计算机对科学实践的影响更是不可忽视。就连实验也已今非昔比，它已被计算机模拟所改变，并在某种程度上被其取代。众所周知，计算机改变了人们的交流方式。1962年，科学成果的发布方式多种多样，包括会议、专题研讨会、预印本，以及后来发表在专业期刊上的文章。而如今，主要的发布方式是电子存档。

The Cold War is long over, and physics is no longer where the action is. Another event of 1962 was the awarding of Nobel prizes to Francis Crick and James Watson for the molecular biology of DNA and to Max Perutz and John Kendrew for the molecular biology of hemoglobin. That was the harbinger of change. Today, biotechnology rules. Kuhn took physical science and its history as his model. You will have to decide, after reading his book, about the extent to which what he said about the physical sciences holds true in the teeming, present world of biotechnology. Add in information science. Add in what the computer has done to the practice of science. Even experiment is not what it was, for it has been modified and to a certain extent replaced by computer simulation. And everyone knows that the computer has changed communication. In 1962 scientific results were announced at meetings, in special seminars, in preprints, and then in articles published in specialist journals. Today the primary mode of publication is in an electronic archive.

2012 年和 1962 年之间还有另一个根本性的区别。它影响到本书的核心——基础物理学。1962 年当时存在着相互竞争的宇宙学理论：稳态宇宙学和大爆炸宇宙学，这两种理论对宇宙及其起源的描述截然不同。1965年，宇宙背景辐射的发现几乎是偶然的，此后便只剩下大爆炸宇宙学，而大爆炸宇宙学本身也充满了悬而未决的问题，这些问题只能作为常规科学的研究课题。1962年，高能物理学似乎是一个无穷无尽的粒子集合体。所谓的标准模型使混沌变得有序。它的预测准确得令人难以置信，即便我们仍然不知道如何将其与引力理论结合起来。或许基础物理学不会再有另一场革命，但可以肯定的是，未来还会有无数的惊喜出现。

There is yet another fundamental difference between 2012 and 1962. It affects the heart of the book, fundamental physics. In 1962 there were competing cosmologies: steady state and big bang, two completely different pictures of the universe and its origin. After 1965 and the almost fortuitous discovery of universal background radiation, there is only the big bang, full of outstanding problems pursued as normal science. In 1962 high-energy physics seemed to be an endless collection of more and more particles. What is called the standard model brought order out of chaos. It is unbelievably accurate in its predictions, even if we have no idea how to fit it together with gravity. Perhaps there will not be another revolution in fundamental physics, although for sure there will be surprises galore.

因此，《科学革命的结构》一书可能——我不是说它一定——与科学史上的某个过去时期比与当今科学实践更为相关。

Thus The Structure of Scientific Revolutions may be—I do not say is—more relevant to a past epoch in the history of science than it is to the sciences as they are practiced today.

但这本书究竟是历史还是哲学？1968年，库恩在一次演讲中开篇便强调：“我站在你们面前，是一位从事科学史研究的学者……我是美国历史学会的成员，而非美国哲学学会的成员。” 8但随着他重新梳理自己的过往，他越来越倾向于将自己呈现为一位始终主要关注哲学的学者。 9虽然《结构》一书对科学史研究界产生了巨大的直接影响，但其更为深远的影响或许在于科学哲学，乃至公共文化。本文导言正是基于此视角撰写的。

But is the book history or philosophy? In 1968 Kuhn began a lecture insisting, “I stand before you as a practicing historian of science. . . . I am a member of the American Historical, not the American Philosophical, Association.”8 But as he reorganized his own past, he increasingly presented himself as always having had primarily philosophical interests.9 Although Structure had an immense immediate impact on the community of historians of science, its more enduring effects have probably been upon philosophy of science and, indeed, on public culture. That is the perspective from which this introduction is written.

结构

Structure

本书标题恰如其分地将“结构”和“革命”置于首位。库恩不仅认为存在科学革命，而且认为它们具有结构。他精心构建了这一结构，并为结构中的每个节点赋予了一个恰当的名称。他擅长格言警句；他所命名的名称也获得了非凡的地位，因为尽管它们曾经晦涩难懂，但其中一些现在已成为英语口语的一部分。以下是其顺序：（1）常规科学（第II-IV节——他（1）他称这些部分为“节”，而不是“章”，因为他认为《结构》更像是一本书的提纲，而不是一本书）；（2）解谜（§IV）；（3）范式（§V），这个词在他使用时相当不常见，但在库恩之后已经变得很平庸（更不用说范式转变了！）；（4）异常（§VI）；（5）危机（§VII–VIII）；以及（6）革命（§IX），建立新的范式。

Structure and revolution are rightly put up front in the book’s title. Kuhn thought not only that there are scientific revolutions but also that they have a structure. He laid out this structure with great care, attaching a useful name to each node in the structure. He had a gift for aphorism; and his names have acquired an unusual status, for although they were once arcane, some of them are now part of colloquial English. Here is the sequence: (1) normal science (§§II–IV—he called these sections, not chapters, for he thought of Structure as more of a book outline than a book); (2) puzzle-solving (§IV); (3) paradigm (§V), a word which, when he used it, was rather uncommon, but which after Kuhn has become banal (not to mention paradigm shift!); (4) anomaly (§VI); (5) crisis (§§VII–VIII); and (6) revolution (§IX), establishing a new paradigm.

这就是科学革命的结构：先是拥有范式和致力于解决难题的常规科学；随后出现严重的异常现象，最终引发危机；最后，新的范式解决危机。另一个著名的词汇并未出现在各章节标题中：不可通约性。它指的是，在革命和范式转变的过程中，新的思想和论断无法与旧的思想和论断进行严格的比较。即使使用的词语相同，它们的含义也发生了改变。这反过来又引出了一个观点：新理论的出现并非因为其正确性而取代旧理论，而是因为世界观的转变（第十节）。本书以一个令人不安的观点结尾：科学的进步并非一条通往真理的简单路径，而是一条远离对世界认知和互动方式的不完善之路（第十三节）。

That is the structure of scientific revolutions: normal science with a paradigm and a dedication to solving puzzles; followed by serious anomalies, which lead to a crisis; and finally resolution of the crisis by a new paradigm. Another famous word does not occur in the section titles: incommensurability. This is the idea that, in the course of a revolution and paradigm shift, the new ideas and assertions cannot be strictly compared to the old ones. Even if the same words are in use, their very meaning has changed. That in turn led to the idea that a new theory was not chosen to replace an old one, because it was true but more because of a change in world view (§X). The book ends with the disconcerting thought that progress in science is not a simple line leading to the truth. It is more progress away from less adequate conceptions of, and interactions with, the world (§XIII).

让我们逐一审视这些观点。显然，这种结构过于严谨。历史学家会抗议说，历史并非如此。但正是库恩作为物理学家的直觉，促使他找到了一个简洁而深刻的通用结构。这是一种普通读者也能理解的科学图景。它的优点在于，它在某种程度上是可检验的。科学史学家可以考察并发现，他们各自专业领域中的重大变革在多大程度上确实符合库恩的结构。不幸的是，它也被一股怀疑论知识分子浪潮所滥用，他们质疑真理本身的存在。库恩并没有这样的意图。他热爱事实，追求真理。

Let us look at each idea in turn. Obviously the structure is all too neat. History, the historian protests, just is not like that. But it was precisely Kuhn’s instinct as a physicist that led him to find a simple and insightful all-purpose structure. It was a picture of science that the general reader could pick up. It had the merit of being to some extent testable. Historians of the sciences could look and see the extent to which momentous changes in their fields of expertise did in fact conform to Kuhn’s structure. Unfortunately it was also abused by the wave of skeptical intellectuals who called the very idea of truth in question. Kuhn had no such intention. He was a fact lover and a truth seeker.

革命

Revolution

我们首先想到的是政治意义上的革命：美国革命、法国革命、俄国革命。一切都是旧秩序被推翻；新的世界秩序开始。第一个将这种革命概念延伸到科学领域的思想家可能是伊曼努尔·康德。他见证了两次伟大的思想革命。在他最伟大的杰作《纯粹理性批判》（另一部罕见的伟大著作，但不如《结构》那样引人入胜！）的第一版（1781年）中，并未提及这两次革命。在第二版（1787年）的序言中，他以近乎华丽的辞藻描述了两次革命性的事件。10其一是数学实践的转变，巴比伦和埃及的数学技巧在希腊被转化为基于公理的证明。其二是实验方法和实验室的出现，他认为这一系列事件始于伽利略。在短短两段篇幅中，他多次重复了“革命”一词。

We think first of revolution in political terms: the American Revolution, the French Revolution, the Russian Revolution. Everything is overthrown; a new world order begins. The first thinker to extend this notion of revolution to the sciences may have been Immanuel Kant. He saw two great intellectual revolutions. They are not mentioned in the first edition (1781) of his greatest masterpiece The Critique of Pure Reason (another rare great book, but not a page turner like Structure!). In the preface to the second edition (1787), he speaks in almost purple prose of two revolutionary events.10 One was the transition in mathematical practice in which techniques familiar in Babylonia and Egypt were transformed in Greece to proofs from postulates. The second was the emergence of the experimental method and the laboratory, a series of events that he identified as beginning with Galileo. He repeats the word revolution several times in just two long paragraphs.

请注意，尽管我们认为康德是最纯粹的学者，但他生活在一个动荡的时代。人人都知道，一场意义深远的变革正在整个欧洲酝酿，事实上，法国大革命也仅剩两年之遥。正是康德提出了科学革命的理念。11作为一名哲学家，我觉得康德本人在脚注中坦言自己无暇顾及历史细节，这既有趣又完全可以理解。12

Notice that although we think of Kant as the purest of scholars, he was living in turbulent times. Everyone knew that something profound was afoot all over Europe, and indeed the French Revolution was only two years away. It was Kant who set in place the idea of a scientific revolution.11 As a philosopher I find it amusing, and certainly forgivable, that honest Kant himself confesses, in a footnote, that he is not in a position to pay attention to the minutiae of historical details.12

库恩的第一本关于科学及其历史的书并非结构，但哥白尼革命。13科学革命的思想早已广为流传。二战后，关于十七世纪科学革命的著述汗牛充栋。弗朗西斯·培根是这场革命的先知，伽利略是它的灯塔，牛顿是它的太阳。

Kuhn’s first book concerned with science and its history was not Structure but The Copernican Revolution.13 The idea of scientific revolution was already very much in circulation. After World War II there was a great deal of writing about the scientific revolution of the seventeenth century. Francis Bacon was its prophet, Galileo its lighthouse, and Newton its sun.

首先需要注意的一点——这一点在初读《结构》时并不明显——是库恩并非在谈论科学革命。这与库恩所设想的那些革命截然不同。14事实上，在他出版《结构》之前不久，他曾提出存在一场“第二次科学革命”。 15这场革命发生在十九世纪初；全新的领域被数学化。热、光、电和磁等现象获得了范式，大量原本难以归类的现象突然变得清晰易懂。这与我们所说的工业革命同时发生——或者说相辅相成。可以说，这是我们如今所处的现代科技世界的开端。但是，与第一次科学革命一样，这场第二次科学革命也并未展现出《结构》中所描绘的那种“结构”。

A first point to notice—one that is not immediately obvious on a first skimming of Structure—is that Kuhn was not talking about the scientific revolution. That was quite a different kind of event from the revolutions whose structure Kuhn postulated.14 Indeed shortly before he published Structure, he had proposed that there was a “second scientific revolution.”15 It took place during the early years of the nineteenth century; whole new fields were mathematized. Heat, light, electricity, and magnetism acquired paradigms, and suddenly a whole mass of unsorted phenomena began to make sense. This coincided with—went hand-in-hand with—what we call the industrial revolution. It was arguably the beginning of the modern technoscientific world in which we live. But, no more than the first scientific revolution, did this second revolution exhibit the “structure” of Structure.

第二点值得注意的是，库恩之前的那一代人，也就是对十七世纪科学革命进行了大量著述的那一代人，成长于一个物理学发生翻天覆地变革的时代。爱因斯坦的狭义相对论（1905年）和广义相对论（1916年）所带来的震撼远超我们今天的想象。相对论最初在人文艺术领域的影响远大于其在物理学领域真正可验证的结论。诚然，曾有亚瑟·爱丁顿爵士著名的天文考察，旨在验证该理论的一个天文预测，但直到后来，相对论才真正融入物理学的诸多分支。

A second point to notice is that the generation preceding Kuhn, the one that wrote so extensively on the scientific revolution of the seventeenth century, had grown up in a world of radical revolution in physics. Einstein’s special (1905) and then general (1916) theory of relativity were more shattering events than we can well conceive. Relativity had, at the beginning, far more repercussions in the humanities and arts than genuine testable consequences in physics. Yes, there was the famous expedition of Sir Arthur Eddington to test an astronomical prediction of the theory, but it was only later that relativity became integral to many branches of physics.

随后是量子革命，它同样分为两个阶段：马克斯·普朗克在1900年左右引入量子概念，随后是1926-27年完整的量子理论，包括海森堡不确定性原理。相对论和量子物理学的结合，不仅推翻了旧科学，也颠覆了基本的形而上学。康德曾认为，绝对的牛顿空间和均匀因果律是思维的先验原则，是人类理解所处世界的必要条件。物理学证明他完全错误。因果关系只是表象，不确定性才是现实的根源。科学革命是那个时代的主旋律。

Then there was the quantum revolution, also a two-stage affair, with Max Planck’s introduction of quanta around 1900 and then the full quantum theory of 1926–27, complete with Heisenberg’s uncertainty principle. Combined, relativity and quantum physics overthrew not only old science but basic metaphysics. Kant had taught that absolute Newtonian space and the principle of uniform causality are a priori principles of thought, necessary conditions on how human beings comprehend the world in which they live. Physics proved him totally mistaken. Cause and effect were mere appearance, and indeterminacy was at the root of reality. Revolution was the order of the scientific day.

在库恩之前，卡尔·波普尔（1902-1994）是最具影响力的科学哲学家——我指的是他的作品被实践科学家广泛阅读，并在某种程度上被他们所信服。 16波普尔成长于第二次量子革命时期。正如他的一本书的书名所示，这场革命让他认识到，科学的发展是通过猜想和反驳来实现的。波普尔认为，科学史正是这种道德主义方法论的例证。首先，我们提出大胆的猜想，并尽可能使其可检验，但不可避免地会发现它们存在缺陷。这些猜想被反驳，然后必须找到一个符合事实的新猜想。只有可证伪的假设才能被视为“科学的”。这种纯粹主义的科学观在世纪之交的伟大革命之前是不可想象的。

Before Kuhn, Karl Popper (1902–94) was the most influential philosopher of science—I mean the most widely read, and to some extent believed, by practicing scientists.16 Popper had come of age during the second quantum revolution. It taught him that science proceeds by conjectures and refutations, to use the title of one of his books. It was a moralistic methodology that Popper claimed was exemplified by the history of science. First we frame bold conjectures, as testable as possible, and inevitably find them wanting. They are refuted, and a new conjecture must be found that fits the facts. Hypotheses can count as “scientific” only if they are falsifiable. This purist vision of science would have been unthinkable before the great turn-of-the-century revolutions.

库恩对革命的强调可以被视为波普尔反驳之后的下一个阶段。他对二者关系的阐述是“发现的逻辑还是研究的心理学”。 17 他们以物理学为所有科学的原型，并在相对论和量子力学之后形成了各自的思想体系。如今的科学面貌已截然不同。2009年，达尔文的《物种起源》发表150周年，人们为此举行了盛大的庆祝活动。鉴于当时出版的书籍、举办的展览和各种庆祝活动，我猜想，如果问许多人有史以来最具革命性的科学著作是什么，他们很可能会毫不犹豫地回答《物种起源》。因此，令人惊讶的是，《结构》一书中竟然从未提及达尔文的革命性贡献。自然选择确实在171-172页中以重要的方式出现，但仅仅是为了类比科学的发展。如今，生命科学已经取代物理学成为主导学科，我们不禁要问，达尔文的革命性贡献在多大程度上符合库恩的理论框架？

Kuhn’s emphasis on revolutions can be seen as the next stage after Popper’s refutations. His own account of the relation between the two is “Logic of Discovery or Psychology of Research.”17 Both men took physics as their prototype for all the sciences and formed their ideas in the aftermath of relativity and quanta. The sciences look different today. In 2009 the 150th anniversary of Darwin’s The Origin of Species by Means of Natural Selection was celebrated with great fanfare. With all the books, shows, and festivals, I suspect that many bystanders, if asked what was the most revolutionary scientific work of all time, would very reasonably have answered The Origin of Species. So it is striking that Darwin’s revolution is never mentioned in Structure. Natural selection does enter in an important way on pages 171–72 but only to serve as analogy to scientific development. Now that the life sciences have replaced physics as top dog, we have to ask about the extent to which Darwin’s revolution fits Kuhn’s template.

最后一点：如今“革命”一词的用法远远超出了库恩的本意。这并非是对库恩或大众的批评，而是意味着我们应该认真阅读库恩的著作，并注意他实际表达的意思。如今，“革命”几乎成了一个褒义词。每一款新冰箱、每一部大胆的新电影，都被冠以“革命”之名。我们很难想起，这个词曾经是多么谨慎地使用。在美国媒体（几乎忘记了美国革命）中，“革命”一词更多的是带有憎恶而非赞扬的意味，因为在当时，“革命”意味着“共产主义者”。我为“革命”一词如今沦为炒作而感到惋惜，但这确实让理解库恩的思想变得更加困难。

A final observation: current usage of the word revolution goes far beyond what Kuhn had in mind. This is not a criticism either of Kuhn or of the general public. It does mean that one should read Kuhn attentively and pay attention to what he actually says. Nowadays revolution is pretty much a praise word. Every new refrigerator, every daring new movie, is announced as revolutionary. It is hard to remember that the word was once used sparingly. In the American media (almost forgetful of the American Revolution) the word conveyed more loathing than praise, because revolutionary meant ‘commie.’ I regret the recent debasing of revolution to mere hype, but it is a fact that makes the comprehension of Kuhn a little more difficult.

常规科学与谜题解决（第二至四节）

Normal Science and Puzzle-Solving (§§ II–IV)

库恩的想法确实令人震惊。他认为，常规科学只不过是在解决当前知识领域中遗留的一些未解之谜。解谜让我们联想到填字游戏。拼图、谜题和数独，都是在不想做正事的时候消磨时间的好方法。正常的科学研究也是这样吗？

Kuhn’s thoughts were really quite shocking. Normal science is, he taught, just working away at a few puzzles that are left open in a current field of knowledge. Puzzle-solving makes us think of crossword puzzles, jigsaw puzzles, and sudoko, pleasant ways to keep busy when one is not up to useful work. Is normal science like that?

许多科学读者对此感到有些震惊，但随后不得不承认，这在他们的日常工作中确实很常见。研究问题的目的并非在于产生真正的新颖性。库恩在第35页的一句话概括了他的理论：“我们刚才遇到的常规研究问题最显著的特点是，它们很少旨在产生重大的新发现，无论是概念上的还是现象上的。”他写道，如果你翻阅任何一份研究期刊，你会发现其中探讨的问题主要有三种类型：（1）确定重要事实，（2）将事实与理论相匹配，以及（3）阐述理论。稍作扩展：

A lot of scientific readers were a bit shocked, but then had to admit that is how it is in much of their daily work. Research problems do not aim to produce real novelty. A single sentence of page 35 sums up Kuhn’s doctrine: “The most striking feature of the normal research problems we have just encountered is how little they aim to produce major novelties, conceptual or phenomenal.” If you look at any research journal, he wrote, you will find three types of problems addressed: (1) determination of significant facts, (2) matching of facts with theory, and (3) articulation of theory. To expand slightly:

1. 理论对某些量或现象的描述不够充分，只能定性地告诉我们应该期待什么。测量和其他方法则能更精确地确定事实。
1.  Theory leaves certain quantities or phenomena inadequately described and only qualitatively tells us what to expect. Measurement and other procedures determine the facts more precisely.
2. 已知的观测结果与理论不完全吻合。问题出在哪里？要么完善理论，要么证明实验数据存在缺陷。
2.  Known observations don’t quite tally with theory. What’s wrong? Tidy up the theory or show that the experimental data were defective.
3. 该理论可能具有严谨的数学表述，但人们尚无法理解其推论。库恩将揭示理论中隐含意义的过程恰当地称为“阐释” ，这一过程通常通过数学分析来实现。
3.  The theory may have a solid mathematical formulation, but one is not yet able to comprehend its consequences. Kuhn gives the apt name of articulation to the process of bringing out what is implicit in the theory, often by mathematical analysis.

尽管许多科研工作者认同他们的工作证实了库恩的法则，但这听起来仍然不太准确。库恩之所以这样表述，原因之一是他（像波普尔和许多其他前辈一样）认为科学的首要工作是理论研究。他重视理论，虽然他也具备良好的实验意识，但却将其视为次要的。自20世纪80年代以来，人们的关注点发生了显著转变，历史学家、社会学家和哲学家开始认真对待实验科学。正如彼得·加里森所写，研究存在三种平行但又基本独立的传统：理论研究、实验研究和工具研究。 18 对其他两者而言，理论至关重要，但它们各自拥有相当大的自主性：它们各自独立发展。库恩的理论立场完全忽略了实验或仪器方面的巨大创新，因此，常规科学可能包含大量创新，只是缺乏理论层面的创新。而对于渴望技术和疗法的大众而言，科学之所以受人推崇，通常并非源于理论层面。正因如此，库恩的言论听起来有些不合时宜。

Although many working scientists agreed that their work confirmed Kuhn’s rule, this still does not sound quite right. One reason Kuhn put things that way is that he (like Popper and many other predecessors) thought that the primary work of science was theoretical. He esteemed theory, and although he had a good sense of experimentation, presented it as of secondary importance. Since the 1980s there has been a substantial shift in emphasis, with historians, sociologists, and philosophers attending seriously to experimental science. As Peter Galison wrote, there are three parallel but largely independent traditions of research: theoretical, experimental, and instrumental.18 Each is essential to the other two, but they have a good deal of autonomy: Each has a life of its own. Immense experimental or instrumental novelty is simply missed in Kuhn’s theoretical stance, so normal science may have a great deal of novelty, just not theoretical. And for the general public, which wants technologies and cures, the novelties for which science is admired are usually not theoretical at all. That is why Kuhn’s remark sounds somehow wrongheaded.

为了更好地理解库恩的“常规科学”理念中哪些是绝对正确的，哪些又是值得商榷的，我们可以看看科学记者报道最多的高能物理研究——寻找希格斯粒子。这项研究需要投入巨额资金和人才，而所有这些资源都致力于验证现有物理学的理论——存在一种尚未被探测到的粒子，它在物质的存在中扮演着至关重要的角色。在此过程中，无数的难题，从数学到工程学，都必须得到解决。从某种意义上说，人们预期不会出现任何新的理论或现象。这正是库恩的正确之处。常规科学并不追求创新。然而，对现有理论的验证却可以孕育出新的发现。事实上，人们希望，当最终找到探测到希格斯粒子的合适条件时，一个全新的高能物理时代将会开启。

For a current illustration of what is absolutely right, and also of what is questionable, in Kuhn’s idea of normal science, notice that the high-energy physics most widely reported by science journalists is the search for the Higgs particle. This involves an incredible treasury of both money and talent, all of which is dedicated to confirming what present physics teaches—that there is an as yet undetected particle that plays an essential role in the very existence of matter. Innumerable puzzles, ranging from mathematics to engineering, must be solved en route. In one sense, nothing new in the way of theory or even phenomena is anticipated. That’s what Kuhn was right about. Normal science does not aim at novelty. But novelty can emerge from confirmation of theories already held. Indeed it is hoped that when the right conditions for eliciting the particle are finally established, an entire new generation of high-energy physics will begin.

将常规科学描述为解谜活动，表明库恩并不认为常规科学重要。恰恰相反，他认为科学活动极其重要，而且其中大部分都属于常规科学。如今，即使是对库恩的革命论持怀疑态度的科学家，也对他的常规科学论述给予了高度评价。

The characterization of normal science as puzzle-solving suggests that Kuhn did not think normal science was important. On the contrary, he thought scientific activity was enormously important and that most of it is normal science. Nowadays even scientists skeptical of Kuhn’s thought about revolutions have great respect for his account of normal science.

范式（§V）

Paradigm (§V)

这一要素需要特别关注。原因有二。首先，库恩一手改变了“范式”一词的含义，使得新读者对这个词的理解与作者在1962年时的理解截然不同。其次，正如库恩本人在其后记中明确指出的：“范式作为共享的范例”。“这正是我认为本书最新颖也最难理解之处的核心要素”（186）。在同一页，他建议用“典范”（exemplar）一词来代替。在后记之前不久写的另一篇文章中，他承认自己“失去了对这个词的控制”。19晚年，他放弃了使用这个词。但是，我们，作为《结构》出版五十年后的读者，在尘埃落定之后，希望能够欣然地让它重回人们的视野。

This element needs special attention. There are two reasons for this. First, Kuhn single-handedly changed the currency of the word paradigm so that a new reader attaches very different connotations to the word than were available to the author in 1962. Secondly, as Kuhn himself stated clearly in his postscript: “The paradigm as shared example is the central element of what I now take to be the most novel and least understood aspect of this book” (186). On the same page he suggested exemplar as a possible substitute word. In another essay written shortly before the postscript, he admitted that he had “lost control of the word.”19 In later life he abandoned it. But we, the readers of Structure fifty years after it was published and after a lot of the dust has settled, can, I hope, happily restore it to prominence.

这本书一出版，读者就抱怨“范式”一词的用法过于繁杂。玛格丽特·马斯特曼在一篇常被引用却鲜有人读的文章中，列举了库恩使用“范式”一词的二十一种不同方式。20这种批评以及类似的批评促使他做出澄清。最终，他写了一篇题为《对范式的再思考》的文章。他区分了该词的两种基本用法，一种是“全局性的”，一种是“局部性的”。关于局部性的用法，他写道：“当然，‘范式’作为标准范例的含义，正是我最初选择这个词的原因。” 但他指出，读者大多以比他预想的更为全局的方式使用它，他继续说道：“我认为几乎不可能让‘范式’恢复其最初的用法，而这才是语文学上唯一恰当的用法。” 21也许在1974年是这样，但值此五十周年之际，我们可以回归 1962 年的初衷。我将回到本地和全球层面，但首先要回顾一些事情。

As soon as the book was published, its readers complained that the word was used in all too many ways. In an often-cited but seldom-read essay, Margaret Masterman found twenty-one distinct ways in which Kuhn used the word paradigm.20 This and similar criticisms prompted him to clarify. The upshot was an essay called “Second Thoughts on Paradigms.” He distinguished what he called two basic uses of the word, one “global” and one “local.” Of the local use he wrote, “It is, of course, the sense of ‘paradigm’ as standard example that led originally to my choice of that term.” But readers, he said, had mostly used it in a more global way than he had intended, and he continued, “I see little chance of recapturing ‘paradigm’ for its original use, the only one that is philologically at all appropriate.”21 Maybe that was true in 1974, but on this fiftieth anniversary, we can return to the intended use of 1962. I shall come back to local and global but first some recapturing.

如今， “范式”（paradigm）及其姊妹词“范式转变”（paradigm shift）简直无处不在，令人尴尬。库恩写作之时，几乎无人知晓这两个词。很快，它们便成了流行语。《纽约客》杂志一向敏锐地捕捉并乐于接受当下的时尚潮流，甚至用漫画嘲讽了它们：在曼哈顿的一场鸡尾酒会上，一位身材丰满、穿着喇叭裤的年轻女子对一位秃顶的、自诩为潮人的男子说道：“太棒了，格斯顿先生。你是第一个我在现实生活中听到使用‘范式’这个词的人。” 22如今，想要摆脱这个该死的词几乎是不可能的，这也是为什么库恩早在1970年就写道，他已经无法控制这个词了。

Nowadays paradigm, along with its companion paradigm shift, is embarrassingly everywhere. When Kuhn wrote, few people had ever encountered it. Soon it became trendy. The New Yorker, ever alert to and amused by the fashion of the moment, mocked it in cartoons: at a Manhattan cocktail party, a buxom young woman in bell-bottoms says to a balding, would-be hipster, “Dynamite, Mr Gerston. You’re the first person I heard use the word ‘paradigm’ in real life.”22 Today, it is pretty hard to escape the damn word, which is why Kuhn wrote even in 1970 that he had lost control of it.

现在让我们回顾一下。希腊语单词paradeigma在亚里士多德的论证理论中扮演着重要的角色，尤其是在《修辞学》一书中。这本书探讨的是演说家和听众之间实际的论证，他们拥有许多无需赘述的共同信念。在英语译本中，我们今天所说的paradigm一词的词源通常被翻译为example，但亚里士多德的意思更接近exemplar，即一个最佳且最具启发性的例子。他认为论证有两种基本类型。一种论证本质上是演绎的，但包含许多未明示的前提。另一种论证本质上是类比的。

Now let’s backtrack. The Greek word paradeigma played an important part in Aristotle’s theory of argument, especially in the book called Rhetoric. That book is about practical argument between two parties, an orator and an audience, who share a great many beliefs that hardly need stating. In English translations the ancestor of our word paradigm is usually rendered as example, but Aristotle meant something more like exemplar, a very best and most instructive example. He thought that there are two basic types of arguments. One kind of argument is essentially deductive, but with many unstated premises. The other is essentially analogical.

在第二种基本论证类型中，存在争议。以下是亚里士多德的一个例子，许多读者会发现很容易将其从亚里士多德时代的城邦移植到今天的民族国家。雅典应该与邻邦底比斯开战吗？不应该。底比斯向邻邦福基斯发动战争是罪恶的。任何雅典听众都会同意这一点；这是一个典型的例子。争议的情况正是如此。因此，我们向底比斯开战也是罪恶的。23

In this second basic type of argument, something is in dispute. Here is one of Aristotle’s examples, which many readers will find all too easy to update from the city-states of Aristotle’s time to the nation-states of today. Should Athens go to war with its neighbor Thebes? No. It was evil of Thebes to make war on its neighbor Phocis. Any Athenian audience would agree; it is a paradigm. The situation in dispute is exactly analogous. So it would be evil for us to make war on Thebes.23

总的来说：某些事情存在争议。有人举了一个令人信服的例子。几乎所有在场的听众都会同意——这是一种范式。其含义是，争议的焦点“就是这样的”。

In general: Something is in dispute. One states a compelling example about which almost everyone in the audience will agree—a paradigm. The implication is that what is in dispute is “just like that.”

在亚里士多德的拉丁文译本中，“paradeigma”演变为“exemplum”，并在中世纪和文艺复兴时期的论证理论中发展演变。然而， “paradigm”一词在现代欧洲语言中得以保留，但基本上与修辞学脱钩。它的使用范围非常有限，通常用于需要遵循或模仿标准模式的情况。例如，学童学习拉丁语时，会被要求将表示“爱”的动词变位为“amo” 、“amas”、“amat ”等等。这就是范式，即需要用类似动词模仿的模式。 “ paradigm”一词的主要用途与语法相关，但它也一直可以作为一种比喻。作为比喻，它在英语中并不流行，但在德语中似乎更为常见。 20 世纪 30 年代，维也纳学派等颇具影响力的哲学团体成员，如莫里茨·施利克和奥托·纽拉特，在他们的哲学著作中经常使用德语词汇。24库恩可能对此并不知情，但维也纳学派以及其他移居美国的德语哲学家的哲学思想，正是库恩用他自己的话说“在思想上受到熏陶”的科学哲学（9）。

In Latin translations of Aristotle, paradeigma became exemplum, which pursued its own career in mediaeval and renaissance theories of argument. The word paradigm was, however, conserved in modern European languages but largely divorced from rhetoric. It tended to have very limited usage, for situations where a standard model was to be followed, or imitated. When schoolchildren had to learn Latin, they were told to conjugate to love—“I love,” “thou lovest,” “he/she/it loves”—as amo, amas, amat, and so on. That was the paradigm, the model to imitate with similar verbs. The primary use of the word paradigm was in connection with grammar, but it was always available as a metaphor. As metaphor it never took off in English, but it seems to have been more common in German. In the 1930s members of the influential philosophy group the Vienna Circle, such as Moritz Schlick and Otto Neurath, were comfortably using the German word in their philosophical writings.24 Kuhn was probably unaware of this, but the philosophy of the Vienna Circle and of other German-language philosophical émigrés to the United States was the philosophy of science on which Kuhn was, in his word, “weaned intellectually” (9).

随后，在《结构》逐渐成熟的十年间，一些英国分析哲学家开始推广“范式”一词。这部分是因为深受维也纳影响的路德维希·维特根斯坦在20世纪30年代于剑桥大学的讲座中大量使用了这个词。他的剑桥课程吸引了众多被其魅力所折服的学生，引发了热烈的讨论。这个词在他的《哲学研究》（另一部伟大的著作，初版于1953年）中多次出现。该词在该书中的首次使用（第20节）指的是“我们语法的范式”，尽管维特根斯坦的语法概念远比通常意义上的语法更为宽泛。后来，他又将这个词与“语言游戏”联系起来，这是一个原本晦涩难懂的德语词汇，后来被他融入了大众文化。

Then, in the decade when Structure was maturing, some English analytic philosophers promoted the word. This was partly because the profoundly Viennese Ludwig Wittgenstein had made much use of it in his lectures at Cambridge University during the 1930s. His Cambridge classes were obsessively discussed by those who fell under his spell. The word appears several times in his Philosophical Investigations (another great book, first published in 1953). The first use of the word in that book (§20) speaks of a “paradigm of our grammar,” although Wittgenstein’s idea of grammar is far more encompassing than the usual one. Later he used it in connection with “language-games,” an originally obscure German phrase which he made part of general culture.

我不知道库恩何时第一次读到维特根斯坦，但他在哈佛和伯克利都曾与斯坦利·卡维尔有过多次交流。卡维尔是一位极具原创性的思想家，深受维特根斯坦的影响。他们都认为，在当时的人生阶段，分享彼此的学术态度和问题至关重要。25而范式问题无疑在他们的讨论中被提及。26

I do not know when Kuhn first read Wittgenstein, but first at Harvard and then at Berkeley, he had many a conversation with Stanley Cavell, a fascinatingly original thinker who was deeply immersed in Wittgenstein. Each acknowledged the importance, at that moment in their lives, of sharing their intellectual attitudes and problems.25 And paradigm definitely came up as problematic in their discussions.26

与此同时，一些英国哲学家发明了一种昙花一现的“范式案例论证”，我记得这个名称是在1957年提出的。它曾引起广泛讨论，因为它似乎是一种针对各种哲学怀疑论的全新且普遍的论证。以下是对这一观点的恰当讽刺。你不能声称我们缺乏自由意志（举例来说），因为我们必须从例子中学习“自由意志”这个表达方式，而这些例子就是范式。既然我们从存在的范式中学习了这个表达方式，那么自由意志就存在。27因此，就在库恩撰写《结构》之时， “范式”一词正处于高度专业化的语境中。28

At the same time, some British philosophers invented a happily short-lived “paradigm-case argument,” so named, I think, in 1957. It was much discussed, for it seemed to be a new and general argument against various kinds of philosophical skepticism. Here is a fair parody of the idea. You cannot claim we lack free will (for example), because we had to learn the use of the expression “free will” from examples, and they are the paradigms. Since we learned the expression from the paradigms, which exist, free will exists.27 So just at the time that Kuhn was writing Structure, the word paradigm was very much in this specialist air.28

他抓住了这个机会，而他也确实抓住了它。

The word was there to grab, and grab it he did.

你会在第11页找到这个词的介绍，这是第二部分“通往常规科学之路”的第一步。常规科学建立在已被某些科学共同体认可的先前科学成就之上。在1974年的《对范式的再思考》中，库恩再次强调，范式与科学共同体是相辅相成地出现在本书中的。29这些成就为未来的研究提供了范例。需要提出的问题类型、成功的应用案例以及“示范性的观察和实验” 。30

You will find the word introduced on page 11, the first step in section II, “The Route to Normal Science.” Normal science is based on prior scientific achievements acknowledged by some scientific community. In the 1974 “Second Thoughts on Paradigms,” Kuhn reemphasized that paradigm entered the book hand in hand with scientific community.29 The achievements served as exemplars of what to do, the kinds of questions to ask, successful applications, and “exemplary observations and experiments.”30

第10页列举的成就都是英雄式的，比如牛顿之流。库恩逐渐对规模小得多的事件产生了兴趣，这些事件与小型科研群体有关。科学界存在着非常庞大的群体——例如遗传学或凝聚态（固态）物理学。但在这些群体内部，又细分为越来越小的群体，因此最终的分析应该适用于“或许只有一百名成员，有时甚至更少”的群体。 31每个群体都有其自身的一系列承诺，以及自身的运作模式。

On page 10 the examples of achievements are on the heroic scale, Newton and the like. Kuhn became increasingly interested in events much smaller in scope, which pertained to small communities of workers. There are very large scientific communities—genetics, or condensed-matter (solid-state) physics, for example. But within such communities, there are smaller and smaller groups, so that in the end the analysis should apply to “communities of perhaps a hundred members, sometimes significantly fewer.”31 Each will have its own group of commitments, its own models of how to proceed.

此外，这些成就并非平庸之作。它们是

Moreover, the achievements are not just anything notable. They are

1. “前所未有地足以吸引一批忠实的拥护者”放弃以往的局面。
1.  “sufficiently unprecedented to attract an enduring group of adherents” away from what has been going on. And
2. 它们是开放式的，有很多问题需要“重新定义的从业者群体”来解决。
2.  they are open-ended, with plenty of problems for the “redefined group of practitioners to resolve.”

库恩总结道：“具有这两个特征的成就，我以后会称之为‘范式’ ”（11，重点为笔者所加）。

Kuhn concluded: “Achievements that share these two characteristics I shall henceforth refer to as ‘paradigms’ ” (11, emphasis added).

公认的科学实践范例，包括定律、理论、应用、实验和仪器，构成了构建连贯传统的模型，并作为科学共同体赖以存在的根本承诺。刚才引用的几句话确立了结构的基本概念。范式是常规科学不可或缺的一部分，而常规科学是由科学共同体实践的。只要有大量工作要做，只要存在开放性问题，只要这些问题能够运用传统认可的方法（定律、仪器等）进行研究，科学界就会继续发展。到第12页末尾，我们已经进入了高速发展阶段。常规科学的特征在于一种范式，它使科学界研究的难题和问题合法化。一切都很顺利，直到范式所认可的方法无法应对一系列异常现象；危机由此产生并持续，直到一项新的成就重新引导研究方向，并成为新的范式。这就是范式转变（在书中，你会发现他更常使用“范式改变”，但“转变”一词更朗朗上口）。

Accepted examples of scientific practice, including laws, theories, applications, experiment, and instrumentation, provide the models that create a coherent tradition and serve as the commitments which constitute a scientific community in the first place. The few sentences just quoted establish the fundamental idea of Structure. Paradigms are integral to normal science, and a normal science, practiced by a scientific community, continues as long as there is plenty to do, open problems which yield to research using methods (laws, instruments, etc.) acknowledged by the tradition. By the end of page 12 we are away to the races. Normal science is characterized by a paradigm, which legitimates puzzles and problems on which the community works. All is well until the methods legitimated by the paradigm cannot cope with a cluster of anomalies; crisis results and persists until a new achievement redirects research and serves as a new paradigm. That is a paradigm shift (in the book, you will find that he more often says “paradigm change,” but shift has proved more catchy).

随着阅读的深入，这个简洁的概念逐渐变得模糊不清，但首先存在一个问题。几乎任何事物群体中都能找到自然的类比和相似之处；范式不仅是一种成就，也是一种以此为基础构建未来实践模式的特定方式。正如马斯特曼在《结构》一书中列举了“范式”一词令人望而生畏的二十一种用法之后，或许是第一个指出这一点的人，我们必须重新审视类比的概念本身。32一个社群如何延续某种特定的成就传承方式？在《对范式的再思考》中，库恩以一种一如既往的新颖方式给出了答案，他探讨了“科学教材章节末尾的习题主要目的是什么。学生在解答这些习题的过程中能学到什么？” 33正如他所说，《对范式的再思考》的大部分内容都指向这个出乎意料的问题，因为这是他对“自然类比过多，以至于一项成就无法定义一种传统”这一问题的主要解答。顺便提一下，他指的是他年轻时读过的物理和数学教科书，而不是生物学教科书。

As you read on in the book, this neat idea becomes increasingly blurred, but there is an initial problem. Natural analogies and resemblances can be found within almost any group of items; a paradigm is not only an achievement but also a particular way of modeling future practice upon it. As Masterman may have been the first to point out, after her daunting list of twenty-one uses of the word paradigm in Structure, we have got to reexamine the very idea of analogy.32 How does a community perpetuate particular ways of carrying on from an achievement? In “Second Thoughts on Paradigms” Kuhn answered in a, as usual, novel way, discussing “what the problems at the ends of chapters in science texts are principally for. What can it be that students learn while solving them?”33 As he says, most of his “Second Thoughts on Paradigms” is directed at this unexpected question, because it was his chief answer to the problem of there being too many natural analogies to enable an achievement to define a tradition. Note in passing that he is thinking of the physics and mathematics textbooks of his youth, not of biology.

人必须具备“发现看似截然不同的问题之间相似之处的能力”。34是的，教科书提供了大量的事实和技巧。但它们并不能使任何人成为科学家。你不是被定律和理论所引导，而是被问题所引导。章节结尾。你必须明白，看似毫不相干的一组问题，其实可以用类似的方法解决。在解决这些问题的过程中，你就能掌握如何运用“正确”的相似之处继续前进。“学生会发现一种方法，将自己的问题与之前遇到的问题联系起来。一旦发现了这种相似性或类比，剩下的就只有操作上的困难了。” 35

One has to acquire an “ability to see resemblances between apparently disparate problems.”34 Yes, textbooks present lots of facts and techniques. But they do not enable anyone to become a scientist. You are inducted not by the laws and the theories but by the problems at the ends of the chapters. You have to learn that a group of these problems, seemingly disparate, can be solved by using similar techniques. In solving those problems you grasp how to carry on using the “right” resemblances. “The student discovers a way to see his problem as like a problem he has already encountered. Once that likeness or analogy has been seen, only manipulative difficulties remain.”35

在探讨“本书结尾提出的问题”这一核心议题之前，库恩在《对范式的再思考》中承认，他之前对“范式”一词的使用过于宽泛。因此，他区分了该概念的两种用法：一种是全局性的，另一种是局部性的。局部性的用法指的是各种类型的范例。而全局性的用法则首先聚焦于科学共同体的概念。

Before he turned to this central topic of “problems at the end of the book,” Kuhn admitted in “Second Thoughts on Paradigms” that he was far too generous in his use of the word paradigm. So he distinguished two families of uses of the idea, one global and one local. The local uses are various types of exemplar. The global use focuses first on the idea of a scientific community.

他在1974年发表的著作中指出，20世纪60年代发展起来的科学社会学研究为人们提供了区分科学共同体的精准实证工具。科学共同体“是什么”本身并无疑问。问题在于，是什么将共同体的成员凝聚在一起，共同从事同一学科的研究。虽然他没有明确指出，但这正是任何特定群体——无论大小——都必须面对的社会学基本问题，无论是政治、宗教、种族群体，还是仅仅是一个青少年足球俱乐部，又或是为老年人送餐的志愿者团体。是什么维系着这个群体？又是什么导致群体分裂成不同的派别，甚至分崩离析？库恩用范式来回答这些问题。

Publishing in 1974, he could say that work on sociology of the sciences developed in the 1960s enables one to have sharp empirical tools for distinguishing scientific communities. There is no question about what a scientific community “is.” The question is what binds its members together as working in the same discipline. Although he does not say so, this is the fundamental sociological question to be asked of any identified group, large or small, be it political, religious, ethnic, or simply a soccer club for teenagers, or a group of volunteers who deliver meals on wheels to the elderly. What keeps the group together as a group? What will cause a group to divide into sects, or simply to fall apart? Kuhn answered in terms of paradigms.

“是什么共同因素造就了专业交流相对顺畅的特性以及专业判断相对一致的性？对于这个问题，《科学革命的结构》给出的答案是‘范式’或‘范式集合’。” 36这是该词的广义含义，它由各种承诺和实践构成，其中作者强调了象征性概括、模型和范例。所有这些都在《结构》中有所提及，但并未完全展开。您可以翻阅本书，了解如何阐述这一观点。有人可能会强调……当一个范式受到危机威胁时，整个物理学界都会陷入混乱。第84页引用了沃尔夫冈·泡利的两段感人至深的语录，一段是在海森堡矩阵代数发表前几个月，另一段则是在海森堡矩阵代数发表后几个月。在前一段语录中，泡利感到物理学正在分崩离析，他甚至希望自己从事其他行业；而几个月后，他又看到了清晰的未来方向。许多人都有同样的感受，在危机最严重的时候，随着范式受到挑战，整个物理学界也开始分崩离析。

“What shared elements account for the relatively unproblematic character of professional communication and for the relative unanimity of professional judgment? To this question The Structure of Scientific Revolutions licenses the answer ‘a paradigm’ or ‘a set of paradigms.’ ”36 That’s the global sense of the word, and it is constituted by various kinds of commitment and practices, among which he emphasizes symbolic generalizations, models, and exemplars. All of this is hinted at but not fully developed in Structure. You may want to flip through the book to see how to develop the idea. One could emphasize the way in which, when a paradigm is threatened by crisis, the community itself is in disarray. There are moving quotations from Wolfgang Pauli on page 84, one a few months before Heisenberg’s matrix algebra and one a few months after. In the former, Pauli feels that physics is falling apart and he wishes he were in another trade; a few months after, the way ahead is clear. Many had the same feeling, and at the height of crisis the community was falling apart as the paradigm was under challenge.

在《对范式的再思考》一文的脚注中，蕴含着一个激进的再思考。37在结构中，一门常规科学始于一项作为范式的成就。在此之前，我们经历一个范式出现之前的推测时期，例如早期对热、磁、电等现象的讨论，直到“第二次科学革命”为这些领域带来了一系列范式。弗朗西斯·培根对热的论述甚至包括太阳和腐烂的粪便；当时根本无法理清头绪，也没有一套公认的问题可供研究，正是因为没有范式。

There is one radical second thought embedded in a footnote in “Second Thoughts on Paradigms.”37 In Structure, a normal science begins with an achievement that serves as paradigm. Before then we have a pre-paradigm period of speculation, for example early discussions of phenomena of heat, of magnetism, of electricity, before “the second scientific revolution” brought with it a wave of paradigms for these fields. Francis Bacon on heat included the sun and rotting manure; there was simply no way to sort things out, no set of agreed problems to work on, precisely because there was no paradigm.

在《再思考》的第四条注释中，库恩彻底推翻了之前的观点。他称这是他“用‘范式’一词来区分某一特定科学发展早期和晚期”所造成的“最具破坏性的”后果。的确，培根时代的热学研究与焦耳时代的热学研究存在差异，但他现在断言，这种差异并不在于是否存在范式。“无论范式是什么，任何科学共同体都拥有范式，包括所谓的前范式时期的学派。” 38前范式在《结构》一书中的作用并非仅限于常规科学的开端；它贯穿全书（直至第159页）。鉴于这一推翻，这些部分需要重写。你需要决定这是否是最佳方案。再思考未必比最初的想法更好。

In note 4 of “Second Thoughts” Kuhn totally recanted. He called this “the most damaging” of the consequences of his “use of the word ‘paradigm’ in distinguishing an earlier from a later period in the development of a particular science.” Yes, there is a difference between the study of heat at the time of Bacon and the study of heat at the time of Joule, but he now asserted, it does not consist in the presence or absence of a paradigm. “Whatever paradigms may be, they are possessed by any scientific community, including the schools of the so-called preparadigm period.”38 The role of the pre-paradigm in Structure is not limited to the beginning of normal science; it recurs throughout the book (as late as page 159). Those parts would have to be rewritten in the light of this recantation. You will have to decide whether that is the best way to go. Second thoughts are not necessarily better than first thoughts.

异常（§VI）

Anomaly (§VI)

本节的完整标题是“异常现象与科学发现的出现”。第七节的标题与之类似：“危机与科学理论的出现”。这些看似不相关的章节组合是库恩科学理论不可或缺的一部分。

The full title of this section is “Anomaly and the Emergence of Scientific Discoveries.” Section VII has a parallel title: “Crisis and the Emergence of Scientific Theories.” These odd pairings are integral to Kuhn’s account of science.

常规科学的目标并非追求新奇，而是打破现状。它往往发现预期会发现的东西。发现并非源于一切顺利，而是源于出现偏差，源于出现与预期相反的新现象。简而言之，就是看似异常的现象。

Normal science does not aim at novelty but at clearing up the status quo. It tends to discover what it expects to discover. Discovery comes not when something goes right but when something is awry, a novelty that runs counter to what was expected. In short, what appears to be an anomaly.

“异常”一词中的“ a ”表示“不”，例如“不道德的”（amoral）或“无神论者”（atheist）。“ nom”源自希腊语，意为“法则”。异常现象违背了规律性的法则，更广义地说，违背了人们的预期。正如我们所见，波普尔早已将反驳作为其哲学的核心。库恩则反复强调，简单的反驳几乎不存在。我们倾向于看到我们预期的事物，即使它并不存在。人们往往需要很长时间才能真正认识到异常现象的本质——它与既定秩序相悖。

The a in anomaly is the a that means ‘not’, as in ‘amoral’ or ‘atheist’. The nom is from the Greek word for ‘law’. Anomalies are contrary to lawlike regularities, more generally, contrary to expectations. Popper, as we have seen, had already made refutation the core of his philosophy. Kuhn was at pains to say that there is seldom such a thing as simple refutation. We have a tendency to see what we expect, even when it is not there. It often takes a long time for an anomaly to be seen for what it is, something contrary to the established order.

并非所有异常现象都被视为重要。1827年，罗伯特·布朗注意到，在显微镜下观察漂浮的花粉粒，会发现它们不停地抖动。这最初只是一个令人费解的异常现象，直到它被纳入分子运动理论才得以解释。一旦理解了这种运动，它就成为了分子运动理论的有力证据，但在此之前，它仅仅是一种奇特的现象。许多与理论相悖的现象也同样如此，它们往往被束之高阁。理论与数据之间总是存在差异，其中许多差异相当显著。认识到某种现象是必须解释的重要异常现象——而不仅仅是会随着时间推移而自行解决的差异——本身就是一个复杂的历史事件，而非简单的反驳。

Not every anomaly is taken to matter. In 1827 Robert Brown noticed that floating grains of pollen, observed through a microscope, are constantly jittering around. This was just an outlier that simply did not make any sense until it was incorporated into the theory of the motion of molecules. Once understood, the motion was powerful evidence for the molecular theory, but previously it was a mere curiosity. The same is true of many phenomena that run counter to theory but are just put aside. There are always discrepancies between theory and data, many of them large. The recognition of something as a significant anomaly that must be explained—more than a discrepancy that will sort itself out in time—is itself a complex historical event, not a simple refutation.

危机（第七至第八节）

Crisis (§§VII–VIII)

危机与理论变革往往相伴而生。异常现象变得难以解决，无论如何修补都无法将其纳入既有的科学体系。但库恩坚称，这本身并不意味着要否定现有的理论。“拒绝一种范式的决定总是同时意味着接受另一种范式的决定，而做出这一决定的判断过程，需要将这两种范式与自然以及彼此进行比较”（78）。下一页的论述更为有力：“拒绝一种范式而不同时接受另一种范式，就等于否定了科学本身。”

Crisis and theory change also go hand in hand. Anomalies become intractable. No amount of tinkering will fit them into established science. But Kuhn is adamant that this does not, in itself, lead to rejection of existing theory. “The decision to reject one paradigm is always simultaneously the decision to accept another, and the judgment leading to that decision involves the comparison of both paradigms with nature and with each other” (78). An even stronger statement is made on the next page: “To reject one paradigm without simultaneously substituting another is to reject science itself.”

危机时期意味着一段非同寻常而非寻常的研究时期，其特点是“各种相互竞争的论述层出不穷，人们愿意尝试任何事物，公开表达不满，诉诸哲学并就基本原理展开辩论”（91）。正是在这种动荡中，新思想、新方法以及最终的新理论应运而生。库恩在第九节中谈到了科学革命的必要性。他似乎在强调，如果没有这种异常、危机和新范式的模式，我们将深陷泥潭，无法产生新的理论。对库恩而言，创新是科学的标志；没有革命，科学就会衰落。你或许应该思考一下他的观点是否正确。科学史上大多数意义深远的创新是否都源于一场结构与《科学结构》一书类似的革命？或许所有真正的创新，用现代广告语来说，都是“革命性的”。问题在于，《科学结构》是否是理解这些创新如何产生的正确模板。

A crisis involves a period of extraordinary, rather than normal, research, with a “proliferation of competing articulations, the willingness to try anything, the expression of explicit discontent, the recourse to philosophy and to debate over fundamentals” (91). Out of that ferment new ideas arise, new methods, and finally a new theory. Kuhn speaks in section IX of the necessity of scientific revolutions. He appears to urge that without this pattern of anomaly, crisis, and new paradigm, we would be stuck in the mud. We would simply not get new theories. Novelty, for Kuhn, was a hallmark of science; without revolution, science would degenerate. You may wish to consider whether he is right about this. Have most of the profound novelties found in the history of science arisen from a revolution with the structure of Structure? Perhaps all real novelties are, in modern advertising parlance, “revolutionary.” The question is whether Structure is a correct template for understanding how they arose.

世界观的转变（§X）

Changes of World View (§X)

大多数人并不反对一个群体或个人的世界观会随着时间而改变。最多，人们可能会对“世界观”（world view ）这个过于夸张的表达方式感到不满，它源自德语“Weltanschauung”，而这个词本身几乎已经成了英语词汇。当然，如果发生了范式转变，或者一场革命，情况就另当别论了。在思想、知识和研究项目方面，人们对我们所处世界的看法会发生变化。谨慎的人会欣然承认，人们对世界的看法会改变，但世界本身并没有改变。

Most people have no problem with the idea that the world views of a community or of an individual can change over time. At most one may be unhappy with the overly grandiose expression world view, derived from the German Weltanschauung, which is itself almost a word of English. Of course, if there has been a paradigm shift, a revolution in ideas, knowledge, and research projects, one’s vision of the kind of world in which we live will change. The cautious will gladly say that one’s view of the world changes, but the world stays the same.

库恩想表达一些更有趣的观点。一场革命之后，科学家们在变革后的领域中，如同置身于一个截然不同的世界。我们当中较为谨慎的人会说，这不过是一种比喻。从字面上讲，世界只有一个，与过去并无二致。我们或许会期盼未来世界更加美好，但严格来说，正如分析哲学家所推崇的那样，未来世界依然是同一个世界，只是有所改进。在欧洲航海时代，探险家们发现了他们称之为新法兰西、新英格兰、新斯科舍、新几内亚等等的地方；当然，这些并非我们今天所知的法国、英格兰或苏格兰。我们谈论旧世界和新世界，指的是地理和文化意义上的，但当我们思考整个世界，思考一切事物时，其实只有一个世界。当然，世界是多方面的：我生活在一个与歌剧女主角或说唱巨星的世界截然不同的世界。显然，如果开始谈论不同的世界，就会造成很多混乱。因为“不同的世界”可以指代各种各样的事物。

Kuhn wanted to say something more interesting. After a revolution, scientists, in the field that has been changed, work in a different world. The more cautious among us will say that is just a metaphor. Speaking literally, there is just one world, the same one now as in times past. We may hope for a better world in the future, but in a strict sense favored by analytic philosophers, it will be the same world, improved. In the age of the European navigators, the explorers encountered what they named New France, New England, Nova Scotia, New Guinea, and so on; and of course these were not the old France, England, or Scotland. We talk about the old world and the new world in this geographical and cultural sense, but when we think of the whole world, everything, there is just one. And of course there are many worlds: I live in a world different from that of opera divas or the great rappers. Clearly there is a lot of room for confusion if one starts talking about different worlds. All sorts of things may be meant.

在第十节“革命作为世界观的改变”中，库恩以一种我称之为“尝试”的方式探讨了这一比喻，他并没有断言某事，而是说“我们或许想说”某事。但他所指的远不止我刚才提到的任何一种比喻。

In section X, “Revolutions as Changes of World View,” Kuhn grapples with the metaphor in what I call “try-out” mode, not asserting so-and-so but saying “we may want to say” so-and-so. But he does mean more than any of the metaphors I have just mentioned.

1.“……可能会让我们想说，在哥白尼之后，天文学家生活在一个不同的世界里”（117）。
1.  “. . . may make us wish to say that, after Copernicus, astronomers lived in a different world” (117).
2.“……会促使我们说，在发现氧气之后，拉瓦锡在一个不同的世界里工作”（118）。
2.  “. . . will urge us to say that after discovering oxygen, Lavoisier worked in a different world” (118).
3.“当[化学革命]完成时……数据本身已经发生了变化。这是我们可能想说的，革命之后科学家在一个不同的世界中工作的最后一个含义”（134）。
3.  “When [the chemical revolution] was done . . . the data themselves had changed. That is the last of the senses in which we may want to say that after a revolution scientists work in a different world” (134).

在第一段引文中，他对天文学家能够轻易观察到新现象印象深刻，“用旧仪器观察旧物体”（117）。

In the first quotation he is impressed by the ease with which astronomers can observe new phenomena, “looking at old objects with old instruments” (117).

在第二段引文中，他含糊其辞地说：“如果不能诉诸于拉瓦锡‘以不同视角看待’的那种假想的、固定不变的自然”，我们就只能说“拉瓦锡生活在一个不同的世界”（118）。这时，我这个古板的评论家会说，我们不需要一个“固定不变的自然”。的确，自然是不断变化的；我现在在花园里劳作，眼前的景象与五分钟前并不完全相同。我拔了一些杂草。但这并非“假设”我耕作的世界与拉瓦锡被送上断头台的世界只有一个。（但那真是一个截然不同的世界！）我希望你能明白事情会变得多么复杂。

In the second quotation he hedges, “in the absence of some recourse to that hypothetical fixed nature that [Lavoisier] ‘saw differently’ ” we will want to say that “Lavoisier worked in a different world” (118). Here the stodgy critic (me) will say, we don’t need a “fixed nature.” Yes indeed, nature is in flux; things are not exactly the same now, as I toil in my garden, as they were five minutes ago. I’ve pulled some weeds. But it is not a “hypothesis” that there is just one world in which I am gardening, the same one in which Lavoisier went to the guillotine. (But what a different world that was!) I hope you see how confusing things can get.

至于第三段引文，库恩解释说，他指的并非更复杂、更精确的实验，从而提供更优质的数据，尽管这一点也并非无关紧要。问题的关键在于道尔顿的论点：元素以固定比例结合形成化合物，而非简单的混合物。多年来，这一论点与当时最先进的化学分析方法并不相符。但当然，这些概念必须改变：如果物质的组合并非以固定比例进行，那就不能称之为化学过程。为了使一切顺利进行，化学家们“不得不驯服自然”（134）。这听起来确实像是在改变世界，尽管我们也想指出，化学家们研究的物质与地球冷却时期存在于地球上的物质完全相同。

As for the third quotation, Kuhn explained that he did not mean more sophisticated and accurate experiments, furnishing better data, though that is not irrelevant. At issue was Dalton’s thesis that elements combine in fixed proportions to form compounds as opposed to mere mixtures. For many years this was not compatible with the best chemical analyses. But of course the concepts had to change: if a combination of substances was not more or less in fixed proportions, it was not a chemical process. To get everything to work out, chemists “had to beat nature into line” (134). This really does sound like changing the world, although we also want to say that the substances with which the chemists worked were identical to those that existed on the face of our planet during the eons in which it was cooling.

读完这一部分，库恩的意图便昭然若揭。然而，读者必须自行判断用何种措辞才能恰当地表达他的想法。“只要你清楚自己想表达的意思，想说什么就说什么”这句格言似乎很贴切，但又不完全如此。谨慎之人或许会认同，在某个领域发生革命性变革之后，科学家看待世界的方式可能会有所不同，对世界的运行规律会有不同的感受，会注意到不同的现象，会被新的难题所困扰，并以新的方式与世界互动。库恩想要表达的远不止这些。但在文字中，他始终坚持试探性的表达方式，即“可能想表达的内容”。他从未在正式的文字中断言，拉瓦锡（1743-1794）之后，化学家们生活在一个截然不同的世界，而道尔顿（1766-1844）之后，世界又发生了翻天覆地的变化。

In reading this section, it becomes clear what Kuhn is driving at. The reader must, however, decide what form of words is appropriate to express his thought. The maxim “say what you want so long as you know what you mean” seems apt. But not quite. A cautious person may agree that after a revolution in her field, a scientist may view the world differently, have a different feeling for how it works, notice different phenomena, be puzzled by new difficulties, and interact with it in new ways. Kuhn wanted to say more than that. But in print he stuck to the try-out mode, of what one “may want to say.” He never asserted in cold print that after Lavoisier (1743–94) chemists lived in a different world, and a different one again after Dalton (1766–1844).

不可通约性

Incommensurability

虽然从未出现过关于不同世界的风暴，但一个密切相关的问题却引发了一场激烈的辩论。库恩撰写《结构》时正在伯克利。我之前提到过斯坦利·卡维尔是他的亲密同事。此外，还有特立独行的保罗·费耶阿本德，他最著名的著作是《反对方法》（1975），书中明显提倡科学研究中的无政府主义（“一切皆可”）。两人都提出了“不可通约”的概念。他们似乎都乐于看到对方一度与自己走在同一条道路上，但之后便分道扬镳。然而，由此引发了一场关于革命前后不同科学理论之间可比性的激烈哲学论战。我认为，费耶阿本德那些夸张的言论更多地是加剧了辩论的激烈程度，而非库恩的言论。另一方面，费耶阿本德最终放弃了这个话题，而库恩却一直为此纠缠到生命的尽头。

There was never a storm about different worlds, but a closely related matter incited a typhoon of debate. When Structure was being written, Kuhn was at Berkeley. I have mentioned Stanley Cavell as a close colleague. There was also the iconoclast Paul Feyerabend, best known for his book Against Method (1975) and its apparent advocacy of anarchy in scientific research (“anything goes”). The two men put the word incommensurable on the table. Each seems to have been glad that the other was, for a moment, traveling a parallel road, but after that their ways diverged. But the consequence was an immense philosophical dogfight about the extent to which successive scientific theories—pre- and postrevolution—could be compared with each other. I believe that Feyerabend’s flamboyant statements had more to do with the heat of the exchanges than anything Kuhn said. On the other hand, Feyerabend dropped the topic, whereas it preoccupied Kuhn until his last days.

或许，关于不可通约性的争论只能发生在逻辑经验主义的舞台上，而逻辑经验主义正是库恩撰写《结构》时盛行的科学哲学正统观念。以下是对一种以语言学为主导、注重意义的思维方式的简化模仿。我并非说有人说过如此简单粗暴的话，但这确实抓住了要点。人们认为，可以通过指认来学习可观察事物的名称。但是，对于像电子这样无法指认的理论实体呢？人们认为，它们的意义只能从其所处的理论语境中获得。因此，理论的改变必然导致意义的改变。因此，在一种理论语境下关于电子的陈述，与在另一种理论语境下相同的表述意义不同。如果一种理论认为这句话为真，而另一种理论认为这句话为假，这并不矛盾，因为这句话在两种理论中表达的是不同的陈述，它们无法比较。

Perhaps the fight over incommensurability could have occurred only on the stage set by logical empiricism, the orthodoxy in philosophy of science which was current when Kuhn was writing Structure. Here is a simplistic parody of one line of thinking that is heavily linguistic, that is, focused on meanings. I am not saying anyone said anything quite this simpleminded, but it does capture the idea. It was thought that the names of things you can observe can be learned by pointing. But what about theoretical entities, such as electrons, at which one cannot point? They get their meaning, it was taught, only from the context of the theory in which they occur. Hence a change in theory must entail a change in meaning. Hence a statement about electrons in the context of one theory means something different from the same string of words in the context of another theory. If one theory says the sentence is true and another says it is false, there is no contradiction, for the sentence expresses different statements in the two theories, and they cannot be compared.

这个问题经常以质量为例进行辩论。质量这个概念对牛顿和爱因斯坦来说都至关重要。每个人唯一能想到的一句话就是质量。牛顿力学的经典方程是f = ma，爱因斯坦力学的经典方程是E = mc² 。但后者在经典力学中毫无意义。因此（有人认为），你无法真正比​​较这两种理论，因此（更糟糕的是！），没有任何合理的理由可以让你偏爱其中一种理论。

The issue was often debated using the example of mass. The term is essential to both Newton and Einstein. The only sentence everyone remembers from Newton is f = ma. The only one from Einstein is E = mc2. But the latter makes no sense in classical mechanics. Hence (some urged) you cannot really compare the two theories, and hence (an even worse “hence”!) there is no rational ground for preferring the one theory to the other.

因此，库恩在某些方面被指责否定了科学的理性本质。而在另一些方面，他则被誉为新相对主义的先知。这两种观点都十分荒谬。库恩直接回应了这些问题。39理论应当预测准确、前后一致、涵盖范围广、以有序连贯的方式呈现现象，并且能够有效地揭示新的现象或现象之间的关系。库恩认同这五项价值，而这些价值也正是整个科学界（更不用说历史学家）所共有的。这正是（科学）理性本质的一部分，从这个意义上讲，库恩是一位“理性主义者”。

And so Kuhn was accused, in some quarters, of denying the very rationality of science. In other quarters he was hailed as the prophet of the new relativism. Both thoughts are absurd. Kuhn addresses these issues directly.39 Theories should be accurate in their predictions, consistent, broad in scope, present phenomena in an orderly and coherent way, and be fruitful in suggesting new phenomena or relationships between phenomena. Kuhn subscribes to all five values, which he shares with the entire community of scientists (not to mention historians). That is part of what (scientific) rationality is all about, and Kuhn in this respect is a “rationalist.”

我们必须谨慎对待不可通约性理论。高中生学习牛顿力学；大学里认真学习物理的学生学习相对论。火箭的瞄准依据牛顿力学；人们常说牛顿力学是相对论力学的一个特例。而且，早期所有皈依爱因斯坦的人都对牛顿力学烂熟于心。那么，究竟什么是不可通约的呢？

We have to be careful with the incommensurability doctrine. Students in high school learn Newtonian mechanics; those who study physics seriously in college study relativity. Rockets are targeted according to Newton; people say that Newtonian mechanics is a special case of relativistic mechanics. And everybody who converted to Einstein in the early days knew Newtonian mechanics by heart. So what is incommensurable?

在《客观性、价值判断与理论选择》一文的结尾，库恩“简单地重申”了他一直以来的观点。不同理论的支持者之间能够相互交流的内容存在着“显著的局限性”。此外，“个人对不同理论的忠诚转移，与其说是选择，不如说是皈依”（同上，338页）。当时，关于理论选择的争论十分激烈；事实上，许多参与辩论的人认为，科学哲学家的首要任务就是肯定和分析理性理论选择的原则。

At the end of “Objectivity, Value Judgment, and Theory Choice,” Kuhn “simply asserts” what he has always been saying. There are “significant limits to what the proponents of different theories can communicate to one another.” Moreover, “an individual’s transfer of allegiance from theory to theory is often better described as conversion than as choice” (ibid., 338). At that time there was a great furor about theory choice; indeed many participants to the debate contended that was the primary task for philosophers of science, to affirm and analyze the principles of rational theory choice.

库恩质疑的是理论选择这一概念本身。通常来说，认为研究者会选择一个理论框架来开展研究，这种说法近乎荒谬。没错，研究生或博士后确实需要选择实验室来掌握专业技能。但即便他们选择的是未来的职业道路，他们也并非在选择理论。

Kuhn was calling in question the very idea of theory choice. It is usually close to nonsense to speak of an investigator choosing a theory within which to work. Initiates entering graduate school or postdocs have to choose the lab in which they will master the tools of their trade, yes. But they are not thereby choosing a theory, even if they are choosing their future life course.

不同理论的支持者之间沟通不畅并不意味着他们无法比较技术成果。“无论新理论对传统拥护者来说多么难以理解，令人印象深刻的具体成果的展示至少会说服他们中的一些人，让他们必须探究这些成果是如何实现的”（同上，339）。还有一种现象，若非库恩的思想，人们可能不会注意到。大规模研究，例如高能物理，通常需要许多彼此细节不透明的专业领域的合作。这怎么可能呢？它们会形成一个“交流区”，类似于两个截然不同的语言群体进行贸易时产生的混合语。40

Limitation on easy communication between advocates of different theories does not mean that they cannot compare technical results. “However incomprehensible the new theory may be to the proponents of tradition, the exhibit of impressive concrete results will persuade at least a few of them that they must discover how such results are achieved” (ibid., 339). There is another phenomenon which one would not have noticed had it not been for Kuhn’s ideas. Large-scale investigations, in for example high-energy physics, usually require collaboration between many specialties which in detail are opaque to each other. How is this possible? They evolve a “trading-zone” analogous to the creoles that emerge when two very different linguistic groups engage in trade.40

库恩逐渐意识到，不可通约性这一概念以一种意想不到的方式发挥着作用。专业化是人类文明的必然结果，也是科学发展的必然结果。在十七世纪，我们还能拥有包罗万象的期刊，其原型是伦敦皇家学会的《哲学汇刊》。多学科交叉的科学仍在继续，周刊《科学》和《自然》便是明证。但即便在电子出版时代之前，科学期刊的数量也一直在不断增长，每一种期刊都代表着一个学科共同体。库恩认为这是可以预见的。他说，科学是达尔文式的，革命往往如同物种形成事件，一个物种分裂成两个，或者一个物种延续下去，但其分支却沿着自身的轨迹发展。在危机中，可能会出现不止一种范式，每一种范式都能涵盖不同的异常现象，并开辟新的研究方向。随着这些新的子学科的发展，每个子学科都有其自身的特点。由于双方的研究成果都以自身成就为蓝本，因此一方的实践者越来越难以理解另一方的研究工作。这并非什么深奥的形而上学问题，而是任何科研工作者都熟知的现实。

Kuhn came to realize that the idea of incommensurability is helpful in an unexpected way. Specialization is a fact of human civilization, and it is a fact of the sciences. In the seventeenth century we could get on with all-purpose journals, whose prototype was the Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society of London. Multidisciplinary science does continue, as attested by the weeklies Science and Nature. But there has been a constant proliferation of scientific journals even before we entered the age of electronic publication, and each journal represents a disciplinary community. Kuhn thought this was predictable. Science, he said, is Darwinian, and revolutions are often like speciation events, in which one species splits into two, or in which one species continues but with a variant on the side following its own trajectory. In crisis more than one paradigm may emerge, each able to incorporate a different group of anomalies and branch out in new research directions. As these new subdisciplines develop, each with its own achievements on which research is modeled, it becomes increasingly difficult for practitioners of one to understand what the other is doing. This is not a deep metaphysical point; it is a familiar fact of life to any working scientist.

正如新物种的特征在于它们无法相互杂交一样，新的学科在某种程度上也是相互无法理解的。这是对不可通约性概念的一种真正意义上的运用，与关于理论选择的伪问题毫无关系。库恩毕生致力于用一种新的科学语言理论来解释这种以及其他类型的不可通约性。他始终是一位物理学家，他提出的理论也同样具有将一切事物简化为一种简单而抽象的结构的倾向。尽管我们假定他与《结构》一书有相似之处，但这种结构与《结构》截然不同，它同样体现了物理学家对清晰组织各种现象的渴望。这部著作尚未出版。41人们常说库恩彻底推翻了维也纳学派及其后继者的哲学，开创了“后实证主义”。然而，他却延续了维也纳学派的许多预设。鲁道夫·卡尔纳普最著名的著作是《语言的逻辑句法》。可以说，库恩晚年的工作也致力于科学语言的逻辑句法研究。

Just as new species are characterized by the fact that they do not interbreed, so new disciplines are to some extent mutually incomprehensible. This is a use of the idea of incommensurability that has real content. It has nothing to do with pseudoquestions about theory choice. Kuhn devoted the end of his career to trying to explain this and other sorts of incommensurability in terms of a new theory of scientific language. He was a physicist ever, and what he proposed has the same property of trying to reduce everything to a simple rather abstract structure. It is a structure quite different from Structure, although taking that for granted, but it has the same physicist’s lust for a perspicuous organization of diverse phenomena. That work has not yet been published.41 It is often said that Kuhn completely overthrew the philosophy of the Vienna Circle and its descendants, that he inaugurated “postpositivism.” Yet he perpetuated many of its presuppositions. Rudolf Carnap’s most famous book is titled The Logical Syntax of Language. The work of Kuhn’s final years can be said to be engaged in the logical syntax of the language of science.

通过革命实现进步（§13）

Progress through Revolutions (§13)

科学发展日新月异，突飞猛进。对许多人来说，科学进步正是进步的典范。要是政治或道德生活也能如此就好了！科学知识是不断积累的，它以先前的里程碑为基础，攀登新的高峰。

The sciences progress by leaps and bounds. For many people, scientific advance is the very epitome of progress. If only political or moral life could be like that! Scientific knowledge is cumulative, building upon previous benchmarks to scale new peaks.

这正是库恩对常规科学的描述。它确实是累积性的，但一场革命会破坏这种连续性。随着新范式提出一系列新问题，旧科学的许多优点可能会被遗忘。这确实是一种看似无害的……不可通约性。革命之后，研究课题可能会发生重大转变，以至于新的科学无法涵盖所有​​旧课题。它可能会修正或摒弃许多曾经适用的概念。

That is exactly Kuhn’s picture of normal science. It is truly cumulative, but a revolution destroys the continuity. Many things that an older science did well may be forgotten as a new set of problems is posed by a new paradigm. That is indeed one unproblematic kind of incommensurability. After a revolution there may be a substantial shift in topics studied, so that the new science simply does not address all the old topics. It may modify or drop many of the concepts that were once appropriate.

那么，进步又该如何界定呢？我们曾认为科学在其领域内朝着真理不断进步。库恩并未挑战这种对常规科学的理解。他的分析独辟蹊径地解释了为什么常规科学作为一种社会制度，能够以其自身的方式快速发展。然而，革命则有所不同，它们对于另一种进步至关重要。

What then of progress? We had thought of a science as progressing towards the truth in its domain. Kuhn does not challenge that conception of a normal science. His analysis is an original account of exactly why normal science is a social institution that progresses so speedily, in its own terms. Revolutions, however, are different, and they are essential to a different kind of progress.

革命改变了研究领域，甚至（根据库恩的说法）改变了我们谈论自然界某些方面的语言。无论如何，它都将研究的焦点转移到了自然界的一个新的领域。因此，库恩提出了他的格言：革命的发展方向是摆脱那些遭遇了灾难性困境的旧有世界观。这并非朝着预设目标前进，而是摆脱那些曾经行之有效但如今已无法应对自身新问题的旧有模式。

A revolution changes the domain, changes even (according to Kuhn) the very language in which we speak about some aspect of nature. At any rate it deflects to a new portion of nature to study. So Kuhn coined his aphorism that revolutions progress away from previous conceptions of the world that have run into cataclysmic difficulties. This is not progress towards a preestablished goal. It is progress away from what once worked well, but no longer handles its own new problems.

“远离”一词似乎质疑了科学旨在探寻宇宙真理的总体理念。认为万物只有一个完整、完全的真理，这种观念深深植根于西方传统。它源于实证主义创始人孔德所称的人类探究的神学阶段。42 在犹太教、基督教和伊斯兰教的通俗宇宙论中，万物只有一个完整、完全的真理，即上帝的所知。（祂知道最小的麻雀的死亡。）

The “away from” seems to call in question the overarching notion of science as aiming at the truth about the universe. The thought that there is one and only one complete true account of everything is deep in the Western tradition. It descends from what Comte, the founder of positivism, called the theological stage of human inquiry.42 In popular versions of Jewish, Christian, and Muslim cosmology, there is one true and complete account of everything, namely what God knows. (He knows about the death of the least sparrow.)

这一图像被移植到基础物理学领域，其中许多内容……那些自诩为无神论者的实践者，理所当然地认为，自然界存在着一个完整而全面的解释，等待着人们去发现。如果你觉得这种说法有道理，那么它就构成了科学发展的理想方向。因此，库恩背离这一方向的进步在你看来就完全是误入歧途。

This image gets transposed to fundamental physics, many of whose practitioners, who might proudly proclaim themselves to be atheists, take for granted that there just is, waiting to be discovered, one full and complete account of nature. If you think that makes sense, then it offers itself as an ideal towards which the sciences are progressing. Hence Kuhn’s progress away from will seem totally misguided.

库恩否定了这种观点。他在第170页问道：“想象存在一个完整、客观、真实的自然描述，并以此作为衡量科学成就的恰当标准，即它在多大程度上使我们更接近这个最终目标，这真的有帮助吗？”许多科学家会说，是的，这很有帮助；它奠定了他们对自身工作的理解，以及这项工作的价值所在。库恩的反问过于简略，这留待读者自行思考。（我本人也和库恩一样持怀疑态度，但这些问题错综复杂，无法迅速定论。）

Kuhn rejected that picture. “Does it really help,” he asked on page 170, “to imagine that there is some one full, objective, true account of nature and that the proper measure of scientific achievement is the extent to which it brings us closer to that ultimate goal?” Many scientists would say that yes, it does; it grounds their image of what they do, and why it is worthwhile. Kuhn was too brief with his rhetorical question. It is a topic for the reader to pursue. (I myself share Kuhn’s skepticism, but the issues are difficult and not to be decided quickly.)

真相

Truth

库恩无法认真对待“存在某种完整、客观、真实的自然描述”这种说法。这是否意味着他不重视真理？完全不是。正如他所指出的，除了引用培根（169页）之外，他在书中并未提及真理。真正热爱事实、力求探求真理的人，不会提​​出“真理理论”，他们也不应该这样做。任何熟悉当代分析哲学的人都知道，存在着无数相互竞争的真理理论。

Kuhn cannot take seriously that “there is some one full, objective, true account of nature.” Does this mean that he does not take truth seriously? Not at all. As he observed, he said nothing about truth in the book, except when quoting Bacon (169). Wise lovers of facts, who try to determine the truth about something, do not state a “theory of truth.” Nor should they. Anyone familiar with contemporary analytic philosophy will know that there are myriad competing theories of truth.

库恩确实否定了简单的“符合论”，即认为真命题与关于世界的事实相符。大多数固执的分析哲学家可能也持相同观点，即便仅仅是出于显而易见的循环论证理由——除了陈述该命题本身之外，根本无法确定该命题所对应的事实。

Kuhn did reject a simple “correspondence theory” which says true statements correspond to facts about the world. A majority of hard-headed analytic philosophers probably do the same, if only on the obvious ground of circularity—there is no way to specify the fact to which an arbitrary statement corresponds except by stating the statement.

在二十世纪末席卷美国学术界的怀疑主义浪潮中，许多有影响力的知识分子将库恩视为盟友，共同否定真理作为一种美德。我指的是那些思想家，他们要么无法书写或说出“真理”这个词，要么就必须给它加上引号——以示警告。他们一想到这种有害的想法就不寒而栗。许多深思熟虑的科学家虽然钦佩库恩关于科学的许多观点，但也认为他助长了否认者的气焰。

In the wave of skepticism that swept American scholarship at the end of the twentieth century, many influential intellectuals took Kuhn as an ally in their denials of truth as a virtue. I mean the thinkers of the sort that cannot write down or utter the word true except by literally or figuratively putting quotation marks around it—to indicate how they shudder at the very thought of so harmful a notion. Many reflective scientists, who admire much of what Kuhn says about the sciences, believe he encouraged deniers.

诚然，《科学结构》极大地推动了科学社会学研究的发展。其中一些研究强调事实是“社会建构的”，并明显参与了对“真理”的否定，而这恰恰是保守派科学家所反对的。库恩明确表示，他本人对这种研究方向深恶痛绝。 43

It is true that Structure gave enormous impetus to sociological studies of science. Some of that work, with its emphasis on the idea that facts are “socially constructed” and apparent participation in the denial of “truth,” is exactly what conservative scientists protest against. Kuhn made plain that he himself detested that development of his work.43

请注意，本书中并没有社会学的内容。然而，科学共同体及其实践却是本书的核心，正如我们在第10页所见，范式问题贯穿始终，直至本书最后一页。在库恩之前，科学知识社会学就已经存在，但在《科学结构》之后，它蓬勃发展，最终演变为如今所谓的科学研究。这是一个自我发展的领域（当然，它也有自己的期刊和学会），涵盖了科学史和科学哲学方面的一些研究，但其重点在于各种社会学方法，包括观察性方法和理论性方法。库恩之后，许多，甚至可以说是绝大多数关于科学的真正原创性思考都带有社会学倾向。

Notice that there is no sociology in the book. Scientific communities and their practices are, however, at its core, entering with paradigms, as we saw, at page 10 and continuing to the final page of the book. There had been sociology of scientific knowledge before Kuhn, but after Structure it burgeoned, leading to what is now called science studies. This is a self-generating field (with, of course, its own journals and societies) that includes some work in the history and the philosophy of sciences and technology, but whose emphasis is on sociological approaches of various kinds, some observational, some theoretical. Much, and perhaps most, of the really original thinking about the sciences after Kuhn has had a sociological bent.

库恩对这些发展持敌对态度。44许多年轻学者认为这令人遗憾。我们不妨将其归因于他们对该领域发展过程中的阵痛感到不满，而不是陷入关于父子关系的冗长比喻。库恩留下的宝贵遗产之一，便是我们今天所知的科学研究。

Kuhn was hostile to these developments.44 In the opinion of many younger workers, that is regrettable. Let us put it down to dissatisfaction with growing pains of the field, rather than venturing into tedious metaphors about fathers and sons. One of Kuhn’s marvelous legacies is science studies as we know it today.

成功

Success

《结构》最初以《国际统一科学百科全书》第二卷第二期的形式出版。在第一版和第二版中，标题页（第i页）和目录页（第iii页）均有此说明。第ii页介绍了百科全书的一些信息，包括二十八个名称。编辑和顾问名单中列出了其中大多数人，即使在五十年后的今天，他们仍然相当有名——阿尔弗雷德·塔尔斯基、伯特兰·罗素、约翰·杜威、鲁道夫·卡尔纳普、尼尔斯·玻尔。

Structure was first published as volume 2, number 2, of the International Encyclopedia of Unified Science. In the first and second editions, both the title page, page i, and the table of contents, page iii, said so. Page ii gave some facts about the Encyclopedia; twenty-eight names of editors and advisors were listed. Most are rather well known even fifty years later—Alfred Tarski, Bertrand Russell, John Dewey, Rudolf Carnap, Neils Bohr.

这部百科全书是奥托·纽拉特及其维也纳学派成员发起的一个项目。随着纳粹主义的瓦解，该项目从欧洲转移到了芝加哥。45纽拉特设想至少出版十四卷，由众多专家撰写的短篇专著组成。然而，在库恩提交他的手稿之前，该项目尚未完成第二卷第一篇专著。此后，这部百科全书便陷入了停滞。大多数观察家认为，库恩出版这本书的地点颇具讽刺意味——因为这本书动摇了该项目隐含的所有实证主义教条。我此前已提出过一种不同的观点，即库恩继承了维也纳学派及其同时代人的预设；他延续了这些基本原则。

The Encyclopedia was part of a project begun by Otto Neurath and fellow members of the Vienna Circle. With the exodus from Nazism, it moved from Europe to Chicago.45 Neurath envisaged at least fourteen volumes consisting of many short monographs by experts. It did not get past volume 2, monograph 1, before Kuhn submitted his manuscript. After that, the Encyclopedia was moribund. Most observers find the site in which Kuhn published the book rather ironic—for the book undermined all the positivist doctrines implicit in that project. I have already suggested a dissenting view, that Kuhn was heir to presuppositions of the Vienna Circle and their contemporaries; he perpetuated the fundamentals.

此前国际百科全书专著的印刷量仅面向一小群专家。芝加哥大学出版社是否预料到自己手中握有一颗重磅炸弹？1962-63年度，该书售出919册，1963-64年度售出774册。次年，平装本售出4825册，此后销量一路飙升。到1971年，第一版销量已超过9万册，随后第二版（附有后记）销量接踵而至。出版25年后，截至1987年中期，总销量已接近65万册。 46

The print runs for previous monographs of the International Encyclopedia were for a small group of specialists. Did the University of Chicago Press know it had a bombshell? In 1962–63, 919 copies were sold and 774 in 1963–64. Next year the paperback sold 4,825, and then we never looked back. By 1971, the first edition had sold more than 90,000 copies, and then the second edition—with the postscript—took over. The grand total to mid-1987, after twenty-five years of publication, was just short of 650,000.46

曾几何时，人们将这本书视为被引用次数最多的著作之一——与《圣经》和弗洛伊德等耳熟能详的经典之作并驾齐驱。千禧年之际，当媒体纷纷炮制“二十世纪最佳书籍”榜单时，《结构》也常常榜上有名。

For a while people talked about the book as being one of the most cited works about anything—right up there with the usual suspects, namely the Bible and Freud. When at the millennium the media were churning out their ephemeral lists of the “best books of the twentieth century,” Structure often appeared.

更重要的是：这本书确实永远地改变了“我们如今所秉持的科学观念”。

Much more important: the book really did change “the image of science by which we are now possessed.” Forever.

前言

Preface

接下来这篇文章是关于一个构思于近十五年前的项目的首份完整发表报告。那时我是一名理论物理学研究生，即将完成我的博士论文。一次偶然的机会，我参与了一门面向非科学专业人士的实验性大学物理科学课程，这使我第一次接触到了科学史。令我完全意想不到的是，这种对过时科学理论和实践的接触，彻底颠覆了我对科学本质及其取得巨大成功原因的一些基本认知。

The essay that follows is the first full published report on a project originally conceived almost fifteen years ago. At that time I was a graduate student in theoretical physics already within sight of the end of my dissertation. A fortunate involvement with an experimental college course treating physical science for the non-scientist provided my first exposure to the history of science. To my complete surprise, that exposure to out-of-date scientific theory and practice radically undermined some of my basic conceptions about the nature of science and the reasons for its special success.

这些观念是我之前一部分源于科学训练本身，一部分源于我对科学哲学的长期业余兴趣。不知何故，无论这些观念在教学上多么有用，在抽象意义上多么合理，它们都与历史研究的本质格格不入。然而，它们过去是、现在仍然是许多科学讨论的基础，因此，它们与现实的不符之处似乎完全值得探究。结果，我的职业规划发生了巨大转变，从物理学转向科学史，然后逐渐从相对直接的历史问题回归到最初吸引我的更具哲学性的思考。这引领我走向了历史。除了几篇文章之外，本文是我发表的作品中第一篇以这些早期关注点为主导的文章。在某种程度上，我试图向自己和朋友们解释，我最初是如何从科学转向历史研究的。

Those conceptions were ones I had previously drawn partly from scientific training itself and partly from a long-standing avocational interest in the philosophy of science. Somehow, whatever their pedagogic utility and their abstract plausibility, those notions did not at all fit the enterprise that historical study displayed. Yet they were and are fundamental to many discussions of science, and their failures of verisimilitude therefore seemed thoroughly worth pursuing. The result was a drastic shift in my career plans, a shift from physics to history of science and then, gradually, from relatively straightforward historical problems back to the more philosophical concerns that had initially led me to history. Except for a few articles, this essay is the first of my published works in which these early concerns are dominant. In some part it is an attempt to explain to myself and to friends how I happened to be drawn from science to its history in the first place.

我第一次有机会深入探究下文所述的一些想法，是在哈佛大学研究员协会担任初级研究员的三年里。如果没有那段自由的时光，向新的研究领域过渡将会困难得多，甚至可能根本无法实现。在那几年里，我的一部分时间投入到了科学史的研究中。我尤其继续研读亚历山大·科伊雷的著作，并首次接触到埃米尔·梅耶森、海伦·梅茨格和安妮莉丝·迈尔的作品。 1 与大多数其他当代学者相比，这群学者更清晰地展现了在科学思想准则与当今截然不同的时代，人们是如何进行科学思考的。尽管我对他们的一些历史解读越来越存疑，但他们的著作，连同A.O.洛夫乔伊的《存在的大链》，在塑造我对科学思想史的理解方面，其重要性仅次于原始资料。

My first opportunity to pursue in depth some of the ideas set forth below was provided by three years as a Junior Fellow of the Society of Fellows of Harvard University. Without that period of freedom the transition to a new field of study would have been far more difficult and might not have been achieved. Part of my time in those years was devoted to history of science proper.
