我认为，事实性科学研究通常只有三个关注点，而且它们并非总是泾渭分明，也并非永远如此。首先是范式已证明能够特别揭示事物本质的那类事实。通过运用这些事实来解决问题，范式使得在更广泛的情境下，以更高的精度确定它们变得尤为重要。这些重要的事实性确定曾涵盖以下领域：在天文学中，包括恒星的位置和星等、食双星和行星的周期；在物理学中，包括材料的比重和压缩率、波长和光谱强度、电场强度等。例如，电导率和接触电势；以及化学中的组成和配比、沸点和溶液酸度、结构式和旋光性。为了提高此类事实的精确度和适用范围，实验和观测科学文献中占据了相当大的篇幅。为此，人们一次又一次地设计出复杂的专用仪器，而这些仪器的发明、建造和部署都需要一流的人才、大量的时间和雄厚的资金支持。同步加速器和射电望远镜只是最新的例证，它们展现了如果某种范式能够确保他们所寻求的事实具有重要意义，研究人员会不遗余力地投入其中。从第谷·布拉赫到E.O.劳伦斯，一些科学家之所以享有盛誉，并非因为他们发现了什么新颖之处，而是因为他们开发出的方法能够精确、可靠且适用范围广地重新确定先前已知的事实。

There are, I think, only three normal foci for factual scientific investigation, and they are neither always nor permanently distinct. First is that class of facts that the paradigm has shown to be particularly revealing of the nature of things. By employing them in solving problems, the paradigm has made them worth determining both with more precision and in a larger variety of situations. At one time or another, these significant factual determinations have included: in astronomy—stellar position and magnitude, the periods of eclipsing binaries and of planets; in physics—the specific gravities and compressibilities of materials, wave lengths and spectral intensities, electrical conductivities and contact potentials; and in chemistry—composition and combining weights, boiling points and acidity of solutions, structural formulas and optical activities. Attempts to increase the accuracy and scope with which facts like these are known occupy a significant fraction of the literature of experimental and observational science. Again and again complex special apparatus has been designed for such purposes, and the invention, construction, and deployment of that apparatus have demanded first-rate talent, much time, and considerable financial backing. Synchrotrons and radiotelescopes are only the most recent examples of the lengths to which research workers will go if a paradigm assures them that the facts they seek are important. From Tycho Brahe to E. O. Lawrence, some scientists have acquired great reputations, not from any novelty of their discoveries, but from the precision, reliability, and scope of the methods they developed for the redetermination of a previously known sort of fact.

第二类常见但规模较小的事实判定，针对的是那些本身往往缺乏多少内在趣味，却可以直接与范式理论预测进行比较的事实。正如我们稍后将看到的，当我从常规科学的实验问题转向理论问题时，科学理论（尤其是以数学形式表达的理论）能够与自然直接比较的领域寥寥无几。即使是爱因斯坦的广义相对论，目前也只有不超过三个这样的领域可以应用。2此外，即使在那些可以应用的领域，也常常需要理论和仪器上的近似，这严重限制了预期的一致性。如何提高这种一致性，或者找到新的一致性领域，都是亟待解决的问题。任何事物的可验证性都对实验者和观察者的技能和想象力构成持续的挑战。例如，用于验证哥白尼关于年视差的预言的特殊望远镜；在《自然哲学的数学原理》发表近一个世纪后才发明的阿特伍德仪器，它首次明确地证明了牛顿第二定律；傅科的装置证明光在空气中的速度比在水中更快；以及旨在证明中微子存在的巨型闪烁计数器——这些特殊仪器以及许多其他类似的仪器都体现了使自然与理论越来越接近一致所需的巨大努力和创造力。 3这种证明一致性的尝试是第二种类型的常规实验工作，它比第一种更明显地依赖于范式。范式的存在决定了待解决的问题；通常，范式理论直接参与到能够解决问题的仪器的设计中。例如，如果没有《原理》，用阿特伍德测量仪进行的测量就毫无意义。

A second usual but smaller class of factual determinations is directed to those facts that, though often without much intrinsic interest, can be compared directly with predictions from the paradigm theory. As we shall see shortly, when I turn from the experimental to the theoretical problems of normal science, there are seldom many areas in which a scientific theory, particularly if it is cast in a predominantly mathematical form, can be directly compared with nature. No more than three such areas are even yet accessible to Einstein’s general theory of relativity.2 Furthermore, even in those areas where application is possible, it often demands theoretical and instrumental approximations that severely limit the agreement to be expected. Improving that agreement or finding new areas in which agreement can be demonstrated at all presents a constant challenge to the skill and imagination of the experimentalist and observer. Special telescopes to demonstrate the Copernican prediction of annual parallax; Atwood’s machine, first invented almost a century after the Principia, to give the first unequivocal demonstration of Newton’s second law; Foucault’s apparatus to show that the speed of light is greater in air than in water; or the gigantic scintillation counter designed to demonstrate the existence of the neutrino—these pieces of special apparatus and many others like them illustrate the immense effort and ingenuity that have been required to bring nature and theory into closer and closer agreement.3 That attempt to demonstrate agreement is a second type of normal experimental work, and it is even more obviously dependent than the first upon a paradigm. The existence of the paradigm sets the problem to be solved; often the paradigm theory is implicated directly in the design of apparatus able to solve the problem. Without the Principia, for example, measurements made with the Atwood machine would have meant nothing at all.

我认为，第三类实验和观察穷尽了常规科学的事实收集活动。它包括为阐明范式理论而开展的经验工作，旨在解决其遗留的一些模糊之处，并解决此前仅引起关注的问题。这一类实验和观察最为重要，因此对其进行描述需要进一步细分。在更偏重数学的科学领域，一些旨在阐明范式的实验致力于确定物理常数。例如，牛顿的研究表明，单位质量物体在单位距离处的力对于宇宙中所有位置的所有类型物质都是相同的。但他自身提出的问题也可以得到解决。甚至连这种引力的大小——万有引力常数——都无法估算；而且在《自然哲学的数学原理》出版后的一个世纪里，也没有人设计出能够测定它的仪器。卡文迪什在1790年代的著名测定也并非最后一次。由于万有引力常数在物理理论中的核心地位，此后，许多杰出的实验学家不断致力于改进其数值。4其他类似的持续研究还包括天文单位、阿伏伽德罗常数、焦耳系数、电子电荷等的测定。如果没有一个定义问题并保证存在稳定解的范式理论，这些精心设计的实验几乎不可能被构思出来，更不可能得以实施。

A third class of experiments and observations exhausts, I think, the fact-gathering activities of normal science. It consists of empirical work undertaken to articulate the paradigm theory, resolving some of its residual ambiguities and permitting the solution of problems to which it had previously only drawn attention. This class proves to be the most important of all, and its description demands its subdivision. In the more mathematical sciences, some of the experiments aimed at articulation are directed to the determination of physical constants. Newton’s work, for example, indicated that the force between two unit masses at unit distance would be the same for all types of matter at all positions in the universe. But his own problems could be solved without even estimating the size of this attraction, the universal gravitational constant; and no one else devised apparatus able to determine it for a century after the Principia appeared. Nor was Cavendish’s famous determination in the 1790’s the last. Because of its central position in physical theory, improved values of the gravitational constant have been the object of repeated efforts ever since by a number of outstanding experimentalists.4Other examples of the same sort of continuing work would include determinations of the astronomical unit, Avogadro’s number, Joule’s coefficient, the electronic charge, and so on. Few of these elaborate efforts would have been conceived and none would have been carried out without a paradigm theory to define the problem and to guarantee the existence of a stable solution.

然而，阐明范式的努力并非仅限于确定普适常数。例如，它们也可能旨在发现定量定律：波义耳定律（气体压力与体积的关系）、库仑定律（电吸引力定律）以及焦耳公式（产生的热量与电阻和电流的关系）都属于此类。或许人们并不认为范式是发现此类定律的先决条件。我们经常听到这样的说法：这些定律是通过检验那些纯粹为了测量而进行的、不带任何理论预设的测量结果而发现的。但历史并不支持这种过于“培根式”的方法。在人们认识到空气是一种弹性流体，可以应用所有复杂的流体静力学概念之前，波义耳的实验是不可想象的（即使想象出来，也会得到另一种解释，或者根本得不到任何解释）。5库仑的成功取决于他建造了专门的装置来测量点电荷之间的作用力。（那些先前使用普通天平等测量电力的人们并没有发现任何一致或简单的测量结果。）（完全没有规律性。）但这种设计反过来又依赖于先前的认识，即电流体中的每个粒子都会在一定距离内作用于其他所有粒子。库仑所研究的正是这些粒子之间的作用力——唯一可以安全地假定为距离的简单函数的力。6焦耳的实验也可以用来说明定量定律是如何通过范式的阐明而产生的。事实上，定性范式和定量定律之间的关系如此普遍和紧密，以至于自伽利略以来，人们常常在设计出用于实验测定这些定律的仪器之前数年，就借助某种范式正确地推测出了这些定律。7

Efforts to articulate a paradigm are not, however, restricted to the determination of universal constants. They may, for example, also aim at quantitative laws: Boyle’s Law relating gas pressure to volume, Coulomb’s Law of electrical attraction, and Joule’s formula relating heat generated to electrical resistance and current are all in this category. Perhaps it is not apparent that a paradigm is prerequisite to the discovery of laws like these. We often hear that they are found by examining measurements undertaken for their own sake and without theoretical commitment. But history offers no support for so excessively Baconian a method. Boyle’s experiments were not conceivable (and if conceived would have received another interpretation or none at all) until air was recognized as an elastic fluid to which all the elaborate concepts of hydrostatics could be applied.5 Coulomb’s success depended upon his constructing special apparatus to measure the force between point charges. (Those who had previously measured electrical forces using ordinary pan balances, etc., had found no consistent or simple regularity at all.) But that design, in turn, depended upon the previous recognition that every particle of electric fluid acts upon every other at a distance. It was for the force between such particles—the only force which might safely be assumed a simple function of distance—that Coulomb was looking.6 Joule’s experiments could also be used to illustrate how quantitative laws emerge through paradigm articulation. In fact, so general and close is the relation between qualitative paradigm and quantitative law that, since Galileo, such laws have often been correctly guessed with the aid of a paradigm years before apparatus could be designed for their experimental determination.7

最后，还有第三种实验，其目的是阐明一种范式。与其他实验相比，这种实验更像是探索，尤其常见于那些更关注自然规律的定性而非定量方面的时期和科学领域。通常，针对某一类现象建立的范式，在应用于其他密切相关的现象时会显得模糊不清。这时，就需要通过实验来选择将该范式应用于新研究领域的几种不同方法。例如，热质理论的范式应用是混合物和状态变化引起的加热和冷却。但热量还可以通过许多其他方式释放或吸收——例如，通过化学结合、摩擦以及气体的压缩或吸收——而对于每一种其他现象，该理论都可以有多种应用方式。例如，如果真空具有热容，那么压缩加热就可以解释为气体与真空混合的结果。或者，它也可能是由于气体比热容随压力变化而变化所致。除此之外，还有其他几种解释。为了阐明这些不同的可能性并区分它们，人们进行了许多实验；所有这些实验都以热质理论为范式，并在实验设计中都充分利用了热质理论。以及在结果解释方面。8一旦压缩加热现象被确立，该领域所有后续实验都以这种方式依赖于这一范式。鉴于这一现象，还能选择怎样的实验来阐明它呢？

Finally, there is a third sort of experiment which aims to articulate a paradigm. More than the others this one can resemble exploration, and it is particularly prevalent in those periods and sciences that deal more with the qualitative than with the quantitative aspects of nature’s regularity. Often a paradigm developed for one set of phenomena is ambiguous in its application to other closely related ones. Then experiments are necessary to choose among the alternative ways of applying the paradigm to the new area of interest. For example, the paradigm applications of the caloric theory were to heating and cooling by mixtures and by change of state. But heat could be released or absorbed in many other ways—e.g., by chemical combination, by friction, and by compression or absorption of a gas—and to each of these other phenomena the theory could be applied in several ways. If the vacuum had a heat capacity, for example, heating by compression could be explained as the result of mixing gas with void. Or it might be due to a change in the specific heat of gases with changing pressure. And there were several other explanations besides. Many experiments were undertaken to elaborate these various possibilities and to distinguish between them; all these experiments arose from the caloric theory as paradigm, and all exploited it in the design of experiments and in the interpretation of results.8Once the phenomenon of heating by compression had been established, all further experiments in the area were paradigm-dependent in this way. Given the phenomenon, how else could an experiment to elucidate it have been chosen?

现在我们来看一下常规科学的理论问题，这些问题几乎可以归为与实验和观测问题相同的类别。常规理论工作的一部分（尽管只占很小一部分）仅仅是利用现有理论来预测具有内在价值的事实信息。例如，天文历表的编制、透镜特性的计算以及无线电传播曲线的绘制都属于此类问题。然而，科学家们通常认为这些工作是繁琐的，应该交给工程师或技术人员去做。这类问题很少出现在重要的科学期刊上。但这些期刊确实包含大量对问题的理论探讨，而这些问题在非科学家看来几乎完全相同。之所以进行这些理论操作，并非因为它们得出的预测结果本身具有价值，而是因为它们可以直接与实验结果进行对比。它们的目的是展示该范式的新应用，或提高现有应用的精确度。

Turn now to the theoretical problems of normal science, which fall into very nearly the same classes as the experimental and observational. A part of normal theoretical work, though only a small part, consists simply in the use of existing theory to predict factual information of intrinsic value. The manufacture of astronomical ephemerides, the computation of lens characteristics, and the production of radio propagation curves are examples of problems of this sort. Scientists, however, generally regard them as hack work to be relegated to engineers or technicians. At no time do very many of them appear in significant scientific journals. But these journals do contain a great many theoretical discussions of problems that, to the non-scientist, must seem almost identical. These are the manipulations of theory undertaken, not because the predictions in which they result are intrinsically valuable, but because they can be confronted directly with experiment. Their purpose is to display a new application of the paradigm or to increase the precision of an application that has already been made.

之所以需要这类工作，是因为在建立理论与自然之间的联系时常常会遇到巨大的困难。考察牛顿之后动力学的发展史，便可简要地说明这些困难。到了十八世纪初，那些在《自然哲学的数学原理》中找到范式的科学家们，理所当然地认为其结论具有普遍性，而他们这样做也并非没有道理。在科学史上，没有任何其他著作能够同时如此大幅度地提升研究的范围和精确度。牛顿推导出了开普勒行星运动定律，并解释了月球在某些观测现象上不符合这些定律的原因。对于地球，他……他从一些零散的关于摆和潮汐的观测中推导出了结果。借助一些临时性的假设，他还推导出了玻意耳定律以及空气中声速的一个重要公式。考虑到当时的科学水平，这些演示的成功令人印象深刻。然而，由于牛顿定律具有普遍性，这些应用并不多，牛顿几乎没有发展出其他应用。此外，与如今任何物理学研究生运用这些定律所能取得的成就相比，牛顿的少数应用甚至不够精确。最后，《自然哲学的数学原理》主要是为解决天体力学问题而设计的。如何将其应用于地球物理，特别是约束运动问题，当时还远未可知。无论如何，当时人们已经运用一套截然不同的技术，成功地解决了地球上的问题。这套技术最初由伽利略和惠更斯发展起来，并在十八世纪由伯努利、达朗贝尔等人推广到欧洲大陆。想必他们的技术以及《自然哲学的数学原理》中的技术可以被证明是某种更普遍形式的特例，但一段时间以来，没有人真正明白该如何证明。9

The need for work of this sort arises from the immense difficulties often encountered in developing points of contact between a theory and nature. These difficulties can be briefly illustrated by an examination of the history of dynamics after Newton. By the early eighteenth century those scientists who found a paradigm in the Principia took the generality of its conclusions for granted, and they had every reason to do so. No other work known to the history of science has simultaneously permitted so large an increase in both the scope and precision of research. For the heavens Newton had derived Kepler’s Laws of planetary motion and also explained certain of the observed respects in which the moon failed to obey them. For the earth he had derived the results of some scattered observations on pendulums and the tides. With the aid of additional but ad hoc assumptions, he had also been able to derive Boyle’s Law and an important formula for the speed of sound in air. Given the state of science at the time, the success of the demonstrations was extremely impressive. Yet given the presumptive generality of Newton’s Laws, the number of these applications was not great, and Newton developed almost no others. Furthermore, compared with what any graduate student of physics can achieve with those same laws today, Newton’s few applications were not even developed with precision. Finally, the Principia had been designed for application chiefly to problems of celestial mechanics. How to adapt it for terrestrial applications, particularly for those of motion under constraint, was by no means clear. Terrestrial problems were, in any case, already being attacked with great success by a quite different set of techniques developed originally by Galileo and Huyghens and extended on the Continent during the eighteenth century by the Bernoullis, d’Alembert, and many others. Presumably their techniques and those of the Principia could be shown to be special cases of a more general formulation, but for some time no one saw quite how.9

暂且将注意力集中在精度问题上。我们已经阐述了它的经验层面。为了获得牛顿范式具体应用所需的特殊数据，需要使用特殊的设备，例如卡文迪什装置、阿特伍德机或改进型望远镜。在理论方面，也存在类似的难以达成共识的困难。例如，在将牛顿定律应用于单摆时，为了给出单摆长度的唯一定义，牛顿不得不将摆锤视为质点。他的大多数定理，少数例外是假设性的，都是基于假设的。此外，初步推导也忽略了空气阻力的影响。这些都是合理的物理近似。然而，作为近似，它们限制了牛顿预测与实际实验结果之间预期的一致性。将牛顿理论应用于天体时，同样的困难表现得更为明显。简单的定量望远镜观测表明，行星并不完全遵循开普勒定律，而牛顿理论表明它们本就不应该遵循。为了推导出这些定律，牛顿不得不忽略除行星与太阳之间引力之外的所有引力。由于行星之间也存在引力，因此应用的理论与望远镜观测结果之间只能预期存在近似的一致性。 10

Restrict attention for the moment to the problem of precision. We have already illustrated its empirical aspect. Special equipment—like Cavendish’s apparatus, the Atwood machine, or improved telescopes—was required in order to provide the special data that the concrete applications of Newton’s paradigm demanded. Similar difficulties in obtaining agreement existed on the side of theory. In applying his laws to pendulums, for example, Newton was forced to treat the bob as a mass point in order to provide a unique definition of pendulum length. Most of his theorems, the few exceptions being hypothetical and preliminary, also ignored the effect of air resistance. These were sound physical approximations. Nevertheless, as approximations they restricted the agreement to be expected between Newton’s predictions and actual experiments. The same difficulties appear even more clearly in the application of Newton’s theory to the heavens. Simple quantitative telescopic observations indicate that the planets do not quite obey Kepler’s Laws, and Newton’s theory indicates that they should not. To derive those laws, Newton had been forced to neglect all gravitational attraction except that between individual planets and the sun. Since the planets also attract each other, only approximate agreement between the applied theory and telescopic observation could be expected.10

当然，对于那些达成共识的人来说，这样的共识已经非常令人满意了。除了某些实际问题之外，没有任何其他理论能够如此完美地解决这些问题。那些质疑牛顿理论有效性的人，并非因为牛顿的理论与实验和观测结果的吻合度有限。然而，这些吻合度的局限性却为牛顿的后继者们留下了许多引人入胜的理论难题。例如，处理两个以上同时相互吸引的物体的运动，以及研究摄动轨道的稳定性，都需要运用理论方法。诸如此类的问题在十八世纪和十九世纪初占据了欧洲众多顶尖数学家的思想。欧拉、拉格朗日、拉普拉斯和高斯都曾致力于解决旨在改进牛顿理论范式与天体观测结果之间匹配度的问题，并在此基础上做出了他们最杰出的贡献。许多数学家同时致力于发展牛顿和当时的欧陆力学学派都未曾尝试过的应用所需的数学理论。例如，他们创作了大量文献，并发展出一些非常强大的数学技巧，用于研究流体动力学和弦振动问题。这些应用问题构成了或许是最精彩、最引人入胜的科学研究领域。这是十八世纪的著作。其他例子可以通过考察热力学、光的波动理论、电磁理论或任何其他基本定律完全定量的科学分支的后范式时期发展来发现。至少在数学性较强的科学领域，大多数理论著作都属于此类。

The agreement obtained was, of course, more than satisfactory to those who obtained it. Excepting for some terrestrial problems, no other theory could do nearly so well. None of those who questioned the validity of Newton’s work did so because of its limited agreement with experiment and observation. Nevertheless, these limitations of agreement left many fascinating theoretical problems for Newton’s successors. Theoretical techniques were, for example, required for treating the motions of more than two simultaneously attracting bodies and for investigating the stability of perturbed orbits. Problems like these occupied many of Europe’s best mathematicians during the eighteenth and early nineteenth century. Euler, Lagrange, Laplace, and Gauss all did some of their most brilliant work on problems aimed to improve the match between Newton’s paradigm and observation of the heavens. Many of these figures worked simultaneously to develop the mathematics required for applications that neither Newton nor the contemporary Continental school of mechanics had even attempted. They produced, for example, an immense literature and some very powerful mathematical techniques for hydrodynamics and for the problem of vibrating strings. These problems of application account for what is probably the most brilliant and consuming scientific work of the eighteenth century. Other examples could be discovered by an examination of the post-paradigm period in the development of thermodynamics, the wave theory of light, electromagnetic theory, or any other branch of science whose fundamental laws are fully quantitative. At least in the more mathematical sciences, most theoretical work is of this sort.

但并非所有问题都如此。即使在数学领域，也存在范式阐释方面的理论问题；在科学发展以定性为主的时期，这些问题尤为突出。无论是在更偏重定量还是更偏重定性的科学领域，有些问题都旨在通过重新表述来加以澄清。例如，《自然哲学的数学原理》并非总是易于应用，部分原因是它保留了初次尝试中不可避免的一些笨拙之处，部分原因是其许多含义仅隐含于其应用中。无论如何，对于许多实际应用而言，一套看似无关的欧陆技术似乎更为强大。因此，从十八世纪的欧拉和拉格朗日到十九世纪的汉密尔顿、雅可比和赫兹，许多欧洲最杰出的数学物理学家反复尝试以一种等价但逻辑和美学上更令人满意的形式重新表述力学理论。也就是说，他们希望以逻辑上更加连贯的方式展现《原理》和欧陆力学的显性和隐性教训，使其在应用于新提出的力学问题时更加统一且明确。11

But it is not all of this sort. Even in the mathematical sciences there are also theoretical problems of paradigm articulation; and during periods when scientific development is predominantly qualitative, these problems dominate. Some of the problems, in both the more quantitative and more qualitative sciences, aim simply at clarification by reformulation. The Principia, for example, did not always prove an easy work to apply, partly because it retained some of the clumsiness inevitable in a first venture and partly because so much of its meaning was only implicit in its applications. For many terrestrial applications, in any case, an apparently unrelated set of Continental techniques seemed vastly more powerful. Therefore, from Euler and Lagrange in the eighteenth century to Hamilton, Jacobi, and Hertz in the nineteenth, many of Europe’s most brilliant mathematical physicists repeatedly endeavored to reformulate mechanical theory in an equivalent but logically and aesthetically more satisfying form. They wished, that is, to exhibit the explicit and implicit lessons of the Principia and of Continental mechanics in a logically more coherent version, one that would be at once more uniform and less equivocal in its application to the newly elaborated problems of mechanics.11

在所有科学领域，类似的范式重构都曾反复出现，但其中大多数都比上文提到的《原理》的重构带来了更为实质性的范式改变。这些改变源于前文所述的旨在阐明范式的实证研究。事实上，将这类研究归类为实证研究本身就带有主观性。与其他任何类型的常规研究相比，范式阐明的问题更兼具理论性和实验性；前文给出的例子将进一步说明这一点。这一点在这里同样适用。库仑在制造设备并进行测量之前，必须运用电学理论来确定设备的构造。他的测量结果反过来又完善了这一理论。再比如，那些设计实验以区分各种压缩加热理论的人，通常也是那些提出被比较理论的人。他们既运用事实，也运用理论，他们的工作不仅产生了新的信息，而且通过消除原始理论中存在的歧义，建立了一个更精确的范式。在许多科学领域，大多数常规工作都是如此。

Similar reformulations of a paradigm have occurred repeatedly in all of the sciences, but most of them have produced more substantial changes in the paradigm than the reformulations of the Principia cited above. Such changes result from the empirical work previously described as aimed at paradigm articulation. Indeed, to classify that sort of work as empirical was arbitrary. More than any other sort of normal research, the problems of paradigm articulation are simultaneously theoretical and experimental; the examples given previously will serve equally well here. Before he could construct his equipment and make measurements with it, Coulomb had to employ electrical theory to determine how his equipment should be built. The consequence of his measurements was a refinement in that theory. Or again, the men who designed the experiments that were to distinguish between the various theories of heating by compression were generally the same men who had made up the versions being compared. They were working both with fact and with theory, and their work produced not simply new information but a more precise paradigm, obtained by the elimination of ambiguities that the original from which they worked had retained. In many sciences, most normal work is of this sort.

我认为，这三类问题——确定重要事实、将事实与理论相匹配以及阐明理论——涵盖了常规科学（包括经验科学和理论科学）的全部文献。当然，它们并不能完全涵盖所有科学文献。科学领域还存在一些非常规问题，而正是这些问题的解决，才使得整个科学事业如此具有特殊的价值。然而，非常规问题并非唾手可得。它们只会在常规研究取得进展的特殊时期出现。因此，即使是最优秀的科学家所研究的绝大多数问题，也必然属于上述三类问题之一。在既定范式下开展工作别无他法，背离既定范式就意味着停止实践它所定义的科学。我们很快就会发现，这种背离确实存在。它们是科学革命的枢纽。但在开始研究这些革命之前，我们需要对铺平道路的常规科学研究有一个更全面的了解。

These three classes of problems—determination of significant fact, matching of facts with theory, and articulation of theory—exhaust, I think, the literature of normal science, both empirical and theoretical. They do not, of course, quite exhaust the entire literature of science. There are also extraordinary problems, and it may well be their resolution that makes the scientific enterprise as a whole so particularly worthwhile. But extraordinary problems are not to be had for the asking. They emerge only on special occasions prepared by the advance of normal research. Inevitably, therefore, the overwhelming majority of the problems undertaken by even the very best scientists usually fall into one of the three categories outlined above. Work under the paradigm can be conducted in no other way, and to desert the paradigm is to cease practicing the science it defines. We shall shortly discover that such desertions do occur. They are the pivots about which scientific revolutions turn. But before beginning the study of such revolutions, we require a more panoramic view of the normal-scientific pursuits that prepare the way.

[ IV ]

[IV]

将普通科学视为解谜

Normal Science as Puzzle-solving

我们刚才遇到的这些常规研究问题最显著的特点或许在于，它们很少旨在产生重大创新，无论是概念上的还是现象上的。有时，例如波长测量，除了最深奥的细节之外，结果的其余部分都是预先已知的，而预期范围也只是略微宽阔一些而已。库仑的测量结果或许不必符合平方反比定律；研究压缩加热的科学家们通常也做好了应对多种结果的准备。然而，即便在这些情况下，预期结果的范围，也就是可理解的结果范围，与想象力所能构想的范围相比，也总是很小的。而那些结果不在这个狭窄范围内的研究项目，通常只是一次失败，它反映的不是自然，而是科学家自身的问题。

Perhaps the most striking feature of the normal research problems we have just encountered is how little they aim to produce major novelties, conceptual or phenomenal. Sometimes, as in a wave-length measurement, everything but the most esoteric detail of the result is known in advance, and the typical latitude of expectation is only somewhat wider. Coulomb’s measurements need not, perhaps, have fitted an inverse square law; the men who worked on heating by compression were often prepared for any one of several results. Yet even in cases like these the range of anticipated, and thus of assimilable, results is always small compared with the range that imagination can conceive. And the project whose outcome does not fall in that narrower range is usually just a research failure, one which reflects not on nature but on the scientist.

例如，在十八世纪，人们很少关注用天平等装置测量电吸引力的实验。由于这些实验的结果既不一致也不简单，因此无法用来阐明它们所源自的范式。所以，它们仅仅是事实，与电学研究的持续进展无关。只有在回顾过去，并拥有了后来的范式之后，我们才能看到它们所具有的特征。它们所展现的电现象。​​当然，库仑和他的同时代人也拥有这种后来的范式，或者说，当这种范式应用于引力问题时，会产生相同的预期。正因如此，库仑才能设计出能够用范式阐释来解释的结果的装置。但也正因如此，这个结果并没有让任何人感到惊讶，库仑的几位同时代人也能够提前预测到它。即使是旨在阐释范式的项目，其目标也并非在于发现意料之外的新奇事物。

In the eighteenth century, for example, little attention was paid to the experiments that measured electrical attraction with devices like the pan balance. Because they yielded neither consistent nor simple results, they could not be used to articulate the paradigm from which they derived. Therefore, they remained mere facts, unrelated and unrelatable to the continuing progress of electrical research. Only in retrospect, possessed of a subsequent paradigm, can we see what characteristics of electrical phenomena they display. Coulomb and his contemporaries, of course, also possessed this later paradigm or one that, when applied to the problem of attraction, yielded the same expectations. That is why Coulomb was able to design apparatus that gave a result assimilable by paradigm articulation. But it is also why that result surprised no one and why several of Coulomb’s contemporaries had been able to predict it in advance. Even the project whose goal is paradigm articulation does not aim at the unexpected novelty.

但如果常规科学的目标并非取得重大实质性创新——如果未能接近预期结果通常就意味着科学家的失败——那么，这些问题为何还要被研究呢？部分答案已经存在。至少对科学家而言，常规研究的成果之所以意义重大，是因为它们拓展了范式的应用范围，提高了其精确度。然而，这个答案无法解释科学家对常规研究问题的热情和投入。没有人会仅仅因为所获得信息的重要性，就花费数年时间去研发更好的光谱仪或改进弦振动问题的解决方案。通过计算星历表或利用现有仪器进行进一步测量所获得的数据通常同样重要，但科学家们常常对这些活动不屑一顾，因为它们在很大程度上是对先前已完成程序的重复。这种排斥恰恰揭示了常规研究问题的魅力所在。尽管结果往往可以预见，甚至细节详尽到让未知本身都显得索然无味，但实现这一结果的方式却仍然充满未知。解决一个常规的研究问题，实际上是以一种全新的方式达成预期目标，这需要解决各种复杂的仪器、概念和数学难题。成功者证明自己是解谜高手，而难题带来的挑战正是驱动他不断前进的重要动力。

But if the aim of normal science is not major substantive novelties—if failure to come near the anticipated result is usually failure as a scientist—then why are these problems undertaken at all? Part of the answer has already been developed. To scientists, at least, the results gained in normal research are significant because they add to the scope and precision with which the paradigm can be applied. That answer, however, cannot account for the enthusiasm and devotion that scientists display for the problems of normal research. No one devotes years to, say, the development of a better spectrometer or the production of an improved solution to the problem of vibrating strings simply because of the importance of the information that will be obtained. The data to be gained by computing ephemerides or by further measurements with an existing instrument are often just as significant, but those activities are regularly spurned by scientists because they are so largely repetitions of procedures that have been carried through before. That rejection provides a clue to the fascination of the normal research problem. Though its outcome can be anticipated, often in detail so great that what remains to be known is itself uninteresting, the way to achieve that outcome remains very much in doubt. Bringing a normal research problem to a conclusion is achieving the anticipated in a new way, and it requires the solution of all sorts of complex instrumental, conceptual, and mathematical puzzles. The man who succeeds proves himself an expert puzzle-solver, and the challenge of the puzzle is an important part of what usually drives him on.

“谜题”和“解谜者”这两个词突显了前文中逐渐凸显的几个主题。谜题，就此处采用的完全标准含义而言，这类问题的特殊之处在于，它们可以用来检验解决问题的创造力或技巧。字典里的例子有“拼图”和“填字游戏”，而我们现在需要探讨的是，这些例子与常规科学问题有哪些共同之处。其中一个例子我们刚才已经提到了。一个谜题的好坏，并不取决于其结果本身是否有趣或重要。相反，真正紧迫的问题，例如癌症的治疗方法或持久和平的设计，往往根本就不是谜题，这主要是因为它们可能根本没有答案。试想一下，如果拼图的碎片分别从两个不同的盒子里随机抽取，那么这个问题很可能（尽管也可能不会）难倒最聪明的人，因此它不能用来检验解决问题的技巧。在任何通常意义上，它根本就不是一个谜题。虽然内在价值不是评判谜题的标准，但答案的确定性却是。

The terms ‘puzzle’ and ‘puzzle-solver’ highlight several of the themes that have become increasingly prominent in the preceding pages. Puzzles are, in the entirely standard meaning here employed, that special category of problems that can serve to test ingenuity or skill in solution. Dictionary illustrations are ‘jigsaw puzzle’ and ‘crossword puzzle,’ and it is the characteristics that these share with the problems of normal science that we now need to isolate. One of them has just been mentioned. It is no criterion of goodness in a puzzle that its outcome be intrinsically interesting or important. On the contrary, the really pressing problems, e.g., a cure for cancer or the design of a lasting peace, are often not puzzles at all, largely because they may not have any solution. Consider the jigsaw puzzle whose pieces are selected at random from each of two different puzzle boxes. Since that problem is likely to defy (though it might not) even the most ingenious of men, it cannot serve as a test of skill in solution. In any usual sense it is not a puzzle at all. Though intrinsic value is no criterion for a puzzle, the assured existence of a solution is.

然而，我们已经看到，科学共同体通过范式获得的一项重要成果，便是选择问题的标准。在范式被奉为圭臬的前提下，这些问题被认为有解决方案。在很大程度上，这些是共同体唯一承认为科学问题或鼓励其成员着手解决的问题。其他问题，包括许多先前被视为标准的问题，则被斥为形而上学问题、其他学科的范畴问题，或者有时仅仅是因为过于复杂而不值得花费时间。事实上，范式甚至可以将共同体与那些无法简化为难题形式的、具有重要社会意义的问题隔离开来，因为这些问题无法用范式提供的概念和工具来表述。这类问题会分散注意力，十七世纪培根主义的某些方面以及一些当代社会科学都精彩地诠释了这一点。常规科学之所以发展如此迅速，原因之一在于其实践者专注于那些只有自身创造力不足才会阻碍他们解决的问题。

We have already seen, however, that one of the things a scientific community acquires with a paradigm is a criterion for choosing problems that, while the paradigm is taken for granted, can be assumed to have solutions. To a great extent these are the only problems that the community will admit as scientific or encourage its members to undertake. Other problems, including many that had previously been standard, are rejected as metaphysical, as the concern of another discipline, or sometimes as just too problematic to be worth the time. A paradigm can, for that matter, even insulate the community from those socially important problems that are not reducible to the puzzle form, because they cannot be stated in terms of the conceptual and instrumental tools the paradigm supplies. Such problems can be a distraction, a lesson brilliantly illustrated by several facets of seventeenth-century Baconianism and by some of the contemporary social sciences. One of the reasons why normal science seems to progress so rapidly is that its practitioners concentrate on problems that only their own lack of ingenuity should keep them from solving.

然而，如果常规科学的问题在这个意义上是谜题，我们就无需再问科学家们为何如此满怀热情和奉献精神地攻克它们了。一个人投身科学的原因可能多种多样，其中包括渴望有所作为，以及探索的兴奋感。探索新领域、寻求秩序的渴望以及检验既有知识的动力。这些动机以及其他因素也决定了他之后会关注的具体问题。此外，尽管结果有时会令人沮丧，但正是这些动机首先吸引他，然后引导他不断前进，这其中自有其道理。1

If, however, the problems of normal science are puzzles in this sense, we need no longer ask why scientists attack them with such passion and devotion. A man may be attracted to science for all sorts of reasons. Among them are the desire to be useful, the excitement of exploring new territory, the hope of finding order, and the drive to test established knowledge. These motives and others besides also help to determine the particular problems that will later engage him. Furthermore, though the result is occasional frustration, there is good reason why motives like these should first attract him and then lead him on.1

科学事业整体而言，的确不时会展现出其价值，开辟新的领域，揭示秩序，并检验长期以来被接受的观点。然而，从事一般研究工作的个人几乎从未做到过上述任何一点。一旦投入研究，他的动机便截然不同。他所面临的挑战在于，他坚信只要自己足够精湛，就能成功解开一个前人未曾解开或解得如此完美的谜题。许多最伟大的科学家都将毕生精力投入到此类极具挑战性的谜题中。在大多数情况下，任何特定专业领域都别无其他可做之事，而这恰恰使它对真正热爱科学的人更具吸引力。

The scientific enterprise as a whole does from time to time prove useful, open up new territory, display order, and test long-accepted belief. Nevertheless, the individual engaged on a normal research problem is almost never doing any one of these things. Once engaged, his motivation is of a rather different sort. What then challenges him is the conviction that, if only he is skilful enough, he will succeed in solving a puzzle that no one before has solved or solved so well. Many of the greatest scientific minds have devoted all of their professional attention to demanding puzzles of this sort. On most occasions any particular field of specialization offers nothing else to do, a fact that makes it no less fascinating to the proper sort of addict.

现在让我们来看看谜题与常规科学问题之间相似之处的另一个更难、也更具启发性的方面。如果一个问题要被归类为谜题，它必须具备的特征不仅仅是一个确定的答案。它还必须有一些规则，既限制了可接受答案的性质，也限制了获得答案的步骤。例如，解拼图并非仅仅是“拼出一幅画”。无论是孩子还是当代艺术家，都可以通过将选定的拼图碎片以抽象形状散落在某个中性背景上来做到这一点。这样拼出的画可能比拼图所用的原图要好得多，也肯定更具原创性。然而，这样的画并不是一个答案。要做到这一点，必须使用所有的拼图碎片，必须将它们的平面朝下，并且必须在不强行用力的情况下将它们相互咬合，直到没有留下任何空隙。这些是拼图解法所遵循的部分规则。类似的限制也适用于其他问题。只要有合理的答案，填字游戏、谜语、国际象棋问题等等就很容易被发现。

Turn now to another, more difficult, and more revealing aspect of the parallelism between puzzles and the problems of normal science. If it is to classify as a puzzle, a problem must be characterized by more than an assured solution. There must also be rules that limit both the nature of acceptable solutions and the steps by which they are to be obtained. To solve a jigsaw puzzle is not, for example, merely “to make a picture.” Either a child or a contemporary artist could do that by scattering selected pieces, as abstract shapes, upon some neutral ground. The picture thus produced might be far better, and would certainly be more original, than the one from which the puzzle had been made. Nevertheless, such a picture would not be a solution. To achieve that all the pieces must be used, their plain sides must be turned down, and they must be interlocked without forcing until no holes remain. Those are among the rules that govern jigsaw-puzzle solutions. Similar restrictions upon the admissible solutions of crossword puzzles, riddles, chess problems, and so on, are readily discovered.

如果我们接受对“规则”一词更宽泛的用法——有时将其等同于“既定观点”或“先入之见”——那么在特定研究传统下可解决的问题就展现出与这组谜题非常相似的特征。制造一台用于测定光波长的仪器的人，绝不能满足于仅仅将特定数字与特定光谱线对应起来的设备。他不仅仅是一位探索者或测量者。相反，他必须通过运用既有的光学理论分析他的仪器，证明他仪器产生的数字正是理论中定义的波长。如果理论中某些残留的模糊之处，或者他仪器中某些未经分析的组成部分阻碍了他完成这一论证，他的同事很可能会得出结论：他根本没有测量任何东西。例如，后来被诊断为电子波长指标的电子散射极大值，在最初被观察和记录时并没有明显的意义。在它们成为任何测量指标之前，必须先将它们与预测运动物质波动行为的理论联系起来。即使指出了这种关系，也必须重新设计实验装置，才能使实验结果与理论明确对应。2在这些条件得到满足之前，任何问题都无法解决。

If we can accept a considerably broadened use of the term ‘rule’—one that will occasionally equate it with ‘established viewpoint’ or with ‘preconception’—then the problems accessible within a given research tradition display something much like this set of puzzle characteristics. The man who builds an instrument to determine optical wave lengths must not be satisfied with a piece of equipment that merely attributes particular numbers to particular spectral lines. He is not just an explorer or measurer. On the contrary, he must show, by analyzing his apparatus in terms of the established body of optical theory, that the numbers his instrument produces are the ones that enter theory as wave lengths. If some residual vagueness in the theory or some unanalyzed component of his apparatus prevents his completing that demonstration, his colleagues may well conclude that he has measured nothing at all. For example, the electron-scattering maxima that were later diagnosed as indices of electron wave length had no apparent significance when first observed and recorded. Before they became measures of anything, they had to be related to a theory that predicted the wave-like behavior of matter in motion. And even after that relation was pointed out, the apparatus had to be redesigned so that the experimental results might be correlated unequivocally with theory.2 Until those conditions had been satisfied, no problem had been solved.

类似的限制也制约了理论问题的可行解。整个十八世纪，那些试图从牛顿运动定律和万有引力定律推导出月球观测运动的科学家们始终未能成功。因此，他们中的一些人建议用一条在小距离上偏离平方反比定律的定律来取代它。然而，这样做就意味着改变范式，定义一个新的难题，而且并非为了解决旧问题。事实上，科学家们一直保留着这些规则，直到1750年，其中一位科学家才发现了如何成功应用这些规则。3只有改变游戏规则才能提供替代方案。

Similar sorts of restrictions bound the admissible solutions to theoretical problems. Throughout the eighteenth century those scientists who tried to derive the observed motion of the moon from Newton’s laws of motion and gravitation consistently failed to do so. As a result, some of them suggested replacing the inverse square law with a law that deviated from it at small distances. To do that, however, would have been to change the paradigm, to define a new puzzle, and not to solve the old one. In the event, scientists preserved the rules until, in 1750, one of them discovered how they could successfully be applied.3 Only a change in the rules of the game could have provided an alternative.

对常规科学传统的考察揭示了许多其他规则，这些规则提供了大量信息，让我们得以了解科学家从其范式中得出的承诺。这些规则主要可以归为哪几类呢？4最明显、也可能是最具约束力的规则，正如我们刚才提到的那些概括性陈述。这些陈述明确地阐述了科学定律以及科学概念和理论。尽管它们仍然受到尊重，但这些陈述也有助于提出难题并限制可接受的解决方案。例如，牛顿定律在十八、十九世纪就发挥了这些作用。只要它们发挥着这样的作用，物质的数量就是物理科学家的一个基本本体论范畴，而物质粒子之间的作用力也是研究的主要课题。5在化学领域，固定比例定律长期以来也发挥着完全相同的作用——它设定了原子量的问题，限定了化学分析结果的可接受范围，并告知化学家什么是原子和分子，什么是化合物和混合物。6麦克斯韦方程组和统计热力学定律在今天仍然适用。

The study of normal-scientific traditions discloses many additional rules, and these provide much information about the commitments that scientists derive from their paradigms. What can we say are the main categories into which these rules fall?4 The most obvious and probably the most binding is exemplified by the sorts of generalizations we have just noted. These are explicit statements of scientific law and about scientific concepts and theories. While they continue to be honored, such statements help to set puzzles and to limit acceptable solutions. Newton’s Laws, for example, performed those functions during the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries. As long as they did so, quantity-of-matter was a fundamental ontological category for physical scientists, and the forces that act between bits of matter were a dominant topic for research.5 In chemistry the laws of fixed and definite proportions had, for a long time, an exactly similar force—setting the problem of atomic weights, bounding the admissible results of chemical analyses, and informing chemists what atoms and molecules, compounds and mixtures were.6 Maxwell’s equations and the laws of statistical thermodynamics have the same hold and function today.

然而，诸如此类的规则并非历史研究中展现的唯一类型，甚至也不是最有趣的类型。例如，在比法律和理论更低或更具体的层面上，存在着许多关于首选仪器类型以及如何合法使用公认仪器的承诺。十七世纪，人们对火在化学分析中的作用态度转变，对化学的发展起到了至关重要的作用。 7 十九世纪，亥姆霍兹在生理学领域遭遇了强烈的抵制，他们认为物理实验无法阐明他们的研究领域。 8而本世纪化学色谱法的奇特发展史再次表明，仪器实验的持久性，如同定律和理论一样，为科学家们提供了研究规则。 9当我们分析X射线的发现时，就会发现这类实验的根源所在。

Rules like these are, however, neither the only nor even the most interesting variety displayed by historical study. At a level lower or more concrete than that of laws and theories, there is, for example, a multitude of commitments to preferred types of instrumentation and to the ways in which accepted instruments may legitimately be employed. Changing attitudes toward the role of fire in chemical analyses played a vital part in the development of chemistry in the seventeenth century.7 Helmholtz, in the nineteenth, encountered strong resistance from physiologists to the notion that physical experimentation could illuminate their field.8 And in this century the curious history of chemical chromatography again illustrates the endurance of instrumental commitments that, as much as laws and theory, provide scientists with rules of the game.9 When we analyze the discovery of X-rays, we shall find reasons for commitments of this sort.

科学的特征并非一成不变，而是不那么局限于局部和暂时的，而是更高层次的、准形而上学的倾向，而历史研究也经常展现这些倾向。例如，大约在1630年之后，尤其是在笛卡尔极具影响力的科学著作问世之后，大多数物理科学家都假定宇宙是由微观粒子构成的，所有自然现象都可以用粒子的形状、大小、运动和相互作用来解释。这一系列的倾向既具有形而上学的意义，也具有方法论的意义。从形而上学的角度来看，它告诉科学家们宇宙包含哪些实体，不包含哪些实体：宇宙中只有运动的、有形状的物质。从方法论的角度来看，它告诉科学家们终极法则和基本解释应该是什么样的：法则必须具体说明粒子的运动和相互作用，解释必须将任何给定的自然现象还原为粒子在这些法则下的作用。更重要的是，这种基于粒子的宇宙观告诉科学家们，他们的许多研究问题应该是什么。例如，一位像波义耳一样接受新哲学的化学家，特别关注那些可以被视为嬗变的反应。这些反应比其他任何反应都更清晰地展现了构成所有化学反应基础的粒子重排过程。变化。10在力学、光学和热学的研究中，也可以观察到类似的微粒效应。

Less local and temporary, though still not unchanging characteristics of science, are the higher level, quasi-metaphysical commitments that historical study so regularly displays. After about 1630, for example, and particularly after the appearance of Descartes’s immensely influential scientific writings, most physical scientists assumed that the universe was composed of microscopic corpuscles and that all natural phenomena could be explained in terms of corpuscular shape, size, motion, and interaction. That nest of commitments proved to be both metaphysical and methodological. As metaphysical, it told scientists what sorts of entities the universe did and did not contain: there was only shaped matter in motion. As methodological, it told them what ultimate laws and fundamental explanations must be like: laws must specify corpuscular motion and interaction, and explanation must reduce any given natural phenomenon to corpuscular action under these laws. More important still, the corpuscular conception of the universe told scientists what many of their research problems should be. For example, a chemist who, like Boyle, embraced the new philosophy gave particular attention to reactions that could be viewed as transmutations. More clearly than any others these displayed the process of corpuscular rearrangement that must underlie all chemical change.10 Similar effects of corpuscularism can be observed in the study of mechanics, optics, and heat.

最后，在更高的层面上，还有另一套不可或缺的承诺，没有这些承诺，任何人都不能称之为科学家。例如，科学家必须致力于理解世界，并拓展人们对世界的认知精度和范围。这种承诺反过来又会促使他亲自或通过同事，对自然界的某些方面进行细致入微的实证研究。而且，如果这种研究揭示出一些明显的混乱之处，那么这些混乱就必须促使他改进观察方法或进一步完善理论。毫无疑问，还有其他类似的规则，这些规则自古以来就适用于科学家。

Finally, at a still higher level, there is another set of commitments without which no man is a scientist. The scientist must, for example, be concerned to understand the world and to extend the precision and scope with which it has been ordered. That commitment must, in turn, lead him to scrutinize, either for himself or through colleagues, some aspect of nature in great empirical detail. And, if that scrutiny displays pockets of apparent disorder, then these must challenge him to a new refinement of his observational techniques or to a further articulation of his theories. Undoubtedly there are still other rules like these, ones which have held for scientists at all times.

这种强大的承诺网络——包括概念、理论、工具和方法论层面的承诺——的存在，是将常规科学与解谜联系起来这一隐喻的主要来源。因为它提供了一套规则，告诉成熟专业的实践者世界和他们所从事的科学究竟是什么样的，所以他们能够充满信心地专注于这些规则和现有知识为他们定义的深奥问题。接下来，他们面临的个人挑战是如何解决剩余的难题。在这些以及其他方面，对难题和规则的探讨阐明了常规科学实践的本质。然而，从另一个角度来看，这种阐明可能具有很大的误导性。尽管显然存在一些所有特定科学专业的实践者在特定时期都遵循的规则，但这些规则本身并不能完全阐明这些专家实践的共同之处。常规科学是一项高度确定性的活动，但它并非完全由规则决定。正因如此，在本文开头，我引入了共享范式，而非共享规则、假设和观点，作为常规研究传统连贯性的来源。我认为，规则源于范式，但即使没有规则，范式也可以指导研究。

The existence of this strong network of commitments—conceptual, theoretical, instrumental, and methodological—is a principal source of the metaphor that relates normal science to puzzle-solving. Because it provides rules that tell the practitioner of a mature specialty what both the world and his science are like, he can concentrate with assurance upon the esoteric problems that these rules and existing knowledge define for him. What then personally challenges him is how to bring the residual puzzle to a solution. In these and other respects a discussion of puzzles and of rules illuminates the nature of normal scientific practice. Yet, in another way, that illumination may be significantly misleading. Though there obviously are rules to which all the practitioners of a scientific specialty adhere at a given time, those rules may not by themselves specify all that the practice of those specialists has in common. Normal science is a highly determined activity, but it need not be entirely determined by rules. That is why, at the start of this essay, I introduced shared paradigms rather than shared rules, assumptions, and points of view as the source of coherence for normal research traditions. Rules, I suggest, derive from paradigms, but paradigms can guide research even in the absence of rules.

[ V ]

[V]

范式优先性

The Priority of Paradigms

为了探究规则、范式和常规科学之间的关系，首先要考察历史学家如何甄别出那些已被公认为规则的特定承诺点。对特定时期某一特定学科进行细致的历史考察，会发现一系列反复出现且近乎标准的例证，这些例证体现了各种理论在概念、观察和工具应用方面的差异。这些便是该学科的范式，它们体现在教科书、讲座和实验练习中。通过学习和实践这些范式，相关学科的成员得以掌握其专业技能。当然，历史学家还会发现一些地位尚存争议的成就，但已解决问题的核心和技术通常是清晰可见的。尽管偶尔会出现一些模糊之处，但一个成熟的科学共同体的范式相对容易确定。

To discover the relation between rules, paradigms, and normal science, consider first how the historian isolates the particular loci of commitment that have just been described as accepted rules. Close historical investigation of a given specialty at a given time discloses a set of recurrent and quasi-standard illustrations of various theories in their conceptual, observational, and instrumental applications. These are the community’s paradigms, revealed in its textbooks, lectures, and laboratory exercises. By studying them and by practicing with them, the members of the corresponding community learn their trade. The historian, of course, will discover in addition a penumbral area occupied by achievements whose status is still in doubt, but the core of solved problems and techniques will usually be clear. Despite occasional ambiguities, the paradigms of a mature scientific community can be determined with relative ease.

然而，确定共同范式并不等同于确定共同规则。后者需要第二个步骤，而且是一个略有不同的步骤。在进行这一步骤时，历史学家必须将社群的范式彼此比较，并与其当前的研究报告进行比较。这样做的目的是为了发现该社群成员所共有的、显性或隐性的可分离要素。他们或许从更宏观的范式中抽象出一些概念，并将其作为研究规则加以运用。任何试图描述或分析特定科学传统演变的人，都必然会寻求此类公认的原则和规则。几乎可以肯定的是，正如前文所述，他至少会取得部分成功。但是，如果他的经历与我的经历相似，他就会发现，寻找规则比寻找范式更加困难，也更令人失望。他用来描述社群共同信念的一些概括不会有问题。然而，另一些概括，包括上文用作例证的一些概括，则显得过于绝对。如果以这种措辞，或者以他能想到的任何其他方式表达，几乎肯定会被他所研究的群体中的某些成员所拒绝。尽管如此，如果要用规则来理解研究传统的连贯性，就需要明确相应领域的共同基础。因此，寻找一套足以构成特定常规研究传统的规则体系，便成了持续而深刻的挫败感之源。

The determination of shared paradigms is not, however, the determination of shared rules. That demands a second step and one of a somewhat different kind. When undertaking it, the historian must compare the community’s paradigms with each other and with its current research reports. In doing so, his object is to discover what isolable elements, explicit or implicit, the members of that community may have abstracted from their more global paradigms and deployed as rules in their research. Anyone who has attempted to describe or analyze the evolution of a particular scientific tradition will necessarily have sought accepted principles and rules of this sort. Almost certainly, as the preceding section indicates, he will have met with at least partial success. But, if his experience has been at all like my own, he will have found the search for rules both more difficult and less satisfying than the search for paradigms. Some of the generalizations he employs to describe the community’s shared beliefs will present no problems. Others, however, including some of those used as illustrations above, will seem a shade too strong. Phrased in just that way, or in any other way he can imagine, they would almost certainly have been rejected by some members of the group he studies. Nevertheless, if the coherence of the research tradition is to be understood in terms of rules, some specification of common ground in the corresponding area is needed. As a result, the search for a body of rules competent to constitute a given normal research tradition becomes a source of continual and deep frustration.

然而，认识到这种挫败感，就有可能诊断出其根源。科学家们可能一致认为牛顿、拉瓦锡、麦克斯韦或爱因斯坦为一系列悬而未决的问题提出了看似永久的解决方案，但他们对于使这些解决方案永久存在的具体抽象特征仍然存在分歧，有时甚至在不知不觉中就此产生分歧。也就是说，他们可能在识别某个范式方面达成一致，却未就其完整的解释或合理化达成一致，甚至未尝试进行此类解释或合理化。缺乏标准的解释或公认的规则还原并不会阻止范式指导研究。常规科学的部分特征可以通过对范式的直接考察来确定，这一过程通常借助规则和假设的制定，但并非依赖于规则和假设的制定。事实上，范式的存在甚至无需意味着存在任何完整的规则集。1

Recognizing that frustration, however, makes it possible to diagnose its source. Scientists can agree that a Newton, Lavoisier, Maxwell, or Einstein has produced an apparently permanent solution to a group of outstanding problems and still disagree, sometimes without being aware of it, about the particular abstract characteristics that make those solutions permanent. They can, that is, agree in their identification of a paradigm without agreeing on, or even attempting to produce, a full interpretation or rationalization of it. Lack of a standard interpretation or of an agreed reduction to rules will not prevent a paradigm from guiding research. Normal science can be determined in part by the direct inspection of paradigms, a process that is often aided by but does not depend upon the formulation of rules and assumptions. Indeed, the existence of a paradigm need not even imply that any full set of rules exists.1

这些论述不可避免地会引发问题。在缺乏一套完善的规则体系的情况下，是什么将科学家限制在特定的常规科学传统之中？“直接检验范式”这一短语究竟意味着什么？已故的路德维希·维特根斯坦在截然不同的语境下，对这类问题给出了部分解答。由于他的语境更为基础也更为人所熟知，因此首先考察他的论证形式将有所助益。维特根斯坦问道，我们需要知道什么，才能毫不含糊地运用“椅子”、“树叶”或“游戏”之类的术语，而不引发争论？2

Inevitably, the first effect of those statements is to raise problems. In the absence of a competent body of rules, what restricts the scientist to a particular normal-scientific tradition? What can the phrase ‘direct inspection of paradigms’ mean? Partial answers to questions like these were developed by the late Ludwig Wittgenstein, though in a very different context. Because that context is both more elementary and more familiar, it will help to consider his form of the argument first. What need we know, Wittgenstein asked, in order that we apply terms like ‘chair,’ or ‘leaf,’ or ‘game’ unequivocally and without provoking argument?2

这个问题由来已久，通常的回答是，我们必须有意识或凭直觉知道椅子、树叶或游戏是什么。也就是说，我们必须掌握所有游戏且只有游戏才具有的共同属性。然而，维特根斯坦认为，鉴于我们使用语言的方式以及我们将其应用于何种世界，并不一定存在这样一组特征。尽管讨论一些游戏、椅子或树叶所共有的属性通常有助于我们学习如何使用相应的术语，但并不存在一组特征能够同时适用于该类别的所有成员，并且只适用于它们。相反，当我们面对一种先前未曾观察到的活动时，我们之所以使用“游戏”这个术语，是因为我们所看到的与我们先前学会称之为“游戏”的许多活动有着密切的“家族相似性”。简而言之，在维特根斯坦看来，游戏、椅子和树叶是天然的家族，每个家族都由一个相互重叠和交错的相似性网络构成。这种网络的存在足以解释我们成功识别相应对象或活动的原因。只有当我们命名的这些家族相互重叠并逐渐融合时——也就是说，只有当不存在自然家族时——才会出现这种情况。我们在识别和命名方面的成功为我们使用的每个类别名称对应的一组共同特征提供了证据。

That question is very old and has generally been answered by saying that we must know, consciously or intuitively, what a chair, or leaf, or game is. We must, that is, grasp some set of attributes that all games and that only games have in common. Wittgenstein, however, concluded that, given the way we use language and the sort of world to which we apply it, there need be no such set of characteristics. Though a discussion of some of the attributes shared by a number of games or chairs or leaves often helps us learn how to employ the corresponding term, there is no set of characteristics that is simultaneously applicable to all members of the class and to them alone. Instead, confronted with a previously unobserved activity, we apply the term ‘game’ because what we are seeing bears a close “family resemblance” to a number of the activities that we have previously learned to call by that name. For Wittgenstein, in short, games, and chairs, and leaves are natural families, each constituted by a network of overlapping and crisscross resemblances. The existence of such a network sufficiently accounts for our success in identifying the corresponding object or activity. Only if the families we named overlapped and merged gradually into one another—only, that is, if there were no natural families—would our success in identifying and naming provide evidence for a set of common characteristics corresponding to each of the class names we employ.

对于同一常规科学传统中出现的各种研究问题和技术，也可能存在类似的情况。它们的共同之处并非在于满足某些明确的、甚至是完全可发现的规则和假设，从而赋予该传统独特的特征并使其在科学界占据主导地位。相反，它们可能通过相似性和建模的方式，与相关科学界已认可的、属于其既定成就的科学体系中的某个部分相关联。科学家们运用通过教育和后续文献阅读获得的模型开展工作，他们往往并不完全了解或需要了解这些模型之所以成为共同范式，是因为它们具备哪些特征。正因如此，他们才不需要一套完整的规则。他们所参与的研究传统所展现出的连贯性，甚至可能并不意味着存在一套潜在的规则和假设，而这些规则和假设或许可以通过进一步的历史或哲学研究来揭示。科学家们通常不会询问或辩论是什么使某个特定问题或解决方案合法，这让我们倾向于认为，至少在直觉上，他们知道答案。但这可能仅仅表明，他们认为这个问题和答案都与他们的研究无关。范式可能先于任何一套可以从中明确抽象出来的研究规则，并且比这些规则更具约束力和完整性。

Something of the same sort may very well hold for the various research problems and techniques that arise within a single normal-scientific tradition. What these have in common is not that they satisfy some explicit or even some fully discoverable set of rules and assumptions that gives the tradition its character and its hold upon the scientific mind. Instead, they may relate by resemblance and by modeling to one or another part of the scientific corpus which the community in question already recognizes as among its established achievements. Scientists work from models acquired through education and through subsequent exposure to the literature often without quite knowing or needing to know what characteristics have given these models the status of community paradigms. And because they do so, they need no full set of rules. The coherence displayed by the research tradition in which they participate may not imply even the existence of an underlying body of rules and assumptions that additional historical or philosophical investigation might uncover. That scientists do not usually ask or debate what makes a particular problem or solution legitimate tempts us to suppose that, at least intuitively, they know the answer. But it may only indicate that neither the question nor the answer is felt to be relevant to their research. Paradigms may be prior to, more binding, and more complete than any set of rules for research that could be unequivocally abstracted from them.

到目前为止，这一点完全是理论上的：范式可以在没有可发现规则的情况下决定常规科学。现在，我想通过指出一些相信范式确实以这种方式运作的原因，来增强其清晰度和紧迫性。第一个原因（之前已经讨论得相当充分）是发现指导特定常规科学传统的规则极其困难。这种困难几乎与哲学家试图解释所有游戏的共同之处时遇到的困难相同。第二个原因（实际上是第一个原因的推论）根植于科学教育的本质。科学家们，这一点应该已经很清楚了：学习概念、定律和理论时，切勿抽象地、孤立地学习。相反，这些知识工具从一开始就应该在一个具有历史和教学意义的单元中接触，该单元通过应用实例来展示它们。一项新理论的提出总是伴随着对某些具体自然现象的应用；没有这些应用，它甚至连被接受的资格都没有。一旦理论被接受，这些应用实例或其他实例就会伴随理论一起被写入教科书，供未来的从业者学习。它们并非仅仅是锦上添花或文献资料。相反，学习理论的过程依赖于对应用实例的研究，包括用笔纸和实验室仪器进行实践问题解决。例如，如果一个学习牛顿动力学的学生最终理解了“力”、“质量”、“空间”和“时间”等术语的含义，他理解这些术语的方式与其说是来自教科书中那些不完整但有时有用的定义，不如说是通过观察和参与这些概念在问题解决中的应用。

So far this point has been entirely theoretical: paradigms could determine normal science without the intervention of discoverable rules. Let me now try to increase both its clarity and urgency by indicating some of the reasons for believing that paradigms actually do operate in this manner. The first, which has already been discussed quite fully, is the severe difficulty of discovering the rules that have guided particular normal-scientific traditions. That difficulty is very nearly the same as the one the philosopher encounters when he tries to say what all games have in common. The second, to which the first is really a corollary, is rooted in the nature of scientific education. Scientists, it should already be clear, never learn concepts, laws, and theories in the abstract and by themselves. Instead, these intellectual tools are from the start encountered in a historically and pedagogically prior unit that displays them with and through their applications. A new theory is always announced together with applications to some concrete range of natural phenomena; without them it would not be even a candidate for acceptance. After it has been accepted, those same applications or others accompany the theory into the textbooks from which the future practitioner will learn his trade. They are not there merely as embroidery or even as documentation. On the contrary, the process of learning a theory depends upon the study of applications, including practice problem-solving both with a pencil and paper and with instruments in the laboratory. If, for example, the student of Newtonian dynamics ever discovers the meaning of terms like ‘force,’ ‘mass,’ ‘space,’ and ‘time,’ he does so less from the incomplete though sometimes helpful definitions in his text than by observing and participating in the application of these concepts to problem-solution.

这种通过动手实践或实践学习的过程贯穿于整个职业生涯的起步阶段。随着学生从大学一年级课程一路走到博士论文阶段，他们所面临的问题变得越来越复杂，也越来越缺乏先例可循。但这些问题仍然与以往的研究成果密切相关，正如他们之后独立科研生涯中遇到的问题一样。人们或许会认为，科学家在某个阶段已经凭直觉掌握了研究规则，但这种可能性微乎其微。尽管许多科学家能够轻松自如地谈论支撑某项具体研究的假设，但他们对于描述其领域的既定基础、合理问题和研究方法却知之甚少，与外行人相差无几。如果他们确实掌握了这些抽象概念，那么他们主要体现在成功的科研能力上。然而，这种能力无需借助任何假设的规则也能被理解。

That process of learning by finger exercise or by doing continues throughout the process of professional initiation. As the student proceeds from his freshman course to and through his doctoral dissertation, the problems assigned to him become more complex and less completely precedented. But they continue to be closely modeled on previous achievements as are the problems that normally occupy him during his subsequent independent scientific career. One is at liberty to suppose that somewhere along the way the scientist has intuitively abstracted rules of the game for himself, but there is little reason to believe it. Though many scientists talk easily and well about the particular individual hypotheses that underlie a concrete piece of current research, they are little better than laymen at characterizing the established bases of their field, its legitimate problems and methods. If they have learned such abstractions at all, they show it mainly through their ability to do successful research. That ability can, however, be understood without recourse to hypothetical rules of the game.

科学教育的这些后果也存在相反的情况，即这提供了第三个理由，表明范式通过直接建模以及抽象规则来指导研究。只有当相关的科学界毫无疑问地接受已有的特定问题解决方案时，常规科学才能在没有规则的情况下继续发展。因此，一旦范式或模型被认为不可靠，规则就应该变得重要，而以往对规则漠不关心的态度也应该消失。事实上，这正是实际发生的情况。尤其是在范式出现之前的时期，经常会就合法的方法、问题和解决方案标准展开频繁而深入的辩论，尽管这些辩论与其说是为了达成共识，不如说是为了划分学派。我们已经注意到光学和电学领域的一些此类辩论，而它们在十七世纪化学和十九世纪早期地质学的发展中发挥了更大的作用。3此外，这类辩论并不会随着范式的出现而彻底消失。尽管在科学发展的正常时期几乎不存在，但这些争论却在科学革命前后频繁出现，因为在这些时期，范式首先受到冲击，然后发生改变。从牛顿力学到量子力学的过渡引发了许多关于物理学本质和标准的辩论，其中一些至今仍在继续。4如今仍有人记得麦克斯韦电磁理论和统计力学引发的类似争论。5更早之前，伽利略力学和牛顿力学的融合催生了一个特别著名的……与亚里士多德主义者、笛卡尔主义者和莱布尼茨主义者就科学的合法标准展开了一系列辩论。6当科学家们对各自领域的基本问题是否已得到解决存在分歧时，对规则的探寻便获得了它通常不具备的功能。然而，只要范式保持稳固，它们就可以在缺乏合理化共识甚至完全不进行任何合理化尝试的情况下发挥作用。

These consequences of scientific education have a converse that provides a third reason to suppose that paradigms guide research by direct modeling as well as through abstracted rules. Normal science can proceed without rules only so long as the relevant scientific community accepts without question the particular problem-solutions already achieved. Rules should therefore become important and the characteristic unconcern about them should vanish whenever paradigms or models are felt to be insecure. That is, moreover, exactly what does occur. The pre-paradigm period, in particular, is regularly marked by frequent and deep debates over legitimate methods, problems, and standards of solution, though these serve rather to define schools than to produce agreement. We have already noted a few of these debates in optics and electricity, and they played an even larger role in the development of seventeenth-century chemistry and of early nineteenth-century geology.3 Furthermore, debates like these do not vanish once and for all with the appearance of a paradigm. Though almost non-existent during periods of normal science, they recur regularly just before and during scientific revolutions, the periods when paradigms are first under attack and then subject to change. The transition from Newtonian to quantum mechanics evoked many debates about both the nature and the standards of physics, some of which still continue.4 There are people alive today who can remember the similar arguments engendered by Maxwell’s electromagnetic theory and by statistical mechanics.5 And earlier still, the assimilation of Galileo’s and Newton’s mechanics gave rise to a particularly famous series of debates with Aristotelians, Cartesians, and Leibnizians about the standards legitimate to science.6 When scientists disagree about whether the fundamental problems of their field have been solved, the search for rules gains a function that it does not ordinarily possess. While paradigms remain secure, however, they can function without agreement over rationalization or without any attempted rationalization at all.

第四个理由可以作为本节的结尾，说明为何范式的地位高于共享规则和假设。本文引言指出，既有规模巨大的革命，也有规模较小的革命；有些革命只影响特定专业领域的成员；对于这些群体而言，即使是发现一种新的、意想不到的现象，也可能具有革命性意义。下一节将介绍一些此类革命，但它们究竟如何存在，目前仍不甚明了。如果常规科学如此僵化，科学共同体又像前文所述那样紧密相连，那么范式的改变又怎会只影响到一小部分群体呢？前文似乎暗示，常规科学是一个单一的整体，它的兴衰取决于任何一个范式，也取决于所有范式的共同作用。但科学显然很少或从未如此。通常情况下，纵观所有领域，科学反而显得结构松散，各个部分之间缺乏连贯性。然而，以上所述不应与这一众所周知的观察相冲突。相反，用范式代替规则应该能使不同科学领域和专业的差异更容易理解。明确的规则（如果存在的话）通常是广泛科学群体所共有的，但范式则未必如此。例如，天文学和植物分类学等截然不同的领域的从业者，都是通过范式进行学习的。接触到的成就各不相同，而且描述的成就也千差万别。即使是那些身处相同或密切相关领域，最初研读过许多相同书籍和成就的人，在专业化过程中也可能形成截然不同的思维模式。

A fourth reason for granting paradigms a status prior to that of shared rules and assumptions can conclude this section. The introduction to this essay suggested that there can be small revolutions as well as large ones, that some revolutions affect only the members of a professional subspecialty, and that for such groups even the discovery of a new and unexpected phenomenon may be revolutionary. The next section will introduce selected revolutions of that sort, and it is still far from clear how they can exist. If normal science is so rigid and if scientific communities are so close-knit as the preceding discussion has implied, how can a change of paradigm ever affect only a small subgroup? What has been said so far may have seemed to imply that normal science is a single monolithic and unified enterprise that must stand or fall with any one of its paradigms as well as with all of them together. But science is obviously seldom or never like that. Often, viewing all fields together, it seems instead a rather ramshackle structure with little coherence among its various parts. Nothing said to this point should, however, conflict with that very familiar observation. On the contrary, substituting paradigms for rules should make the diversity of scientific fields and specialties easier to understand. Explicit rules, when they exist, are usually common to a very broad scientific group, but paradigms need not be. The practitioners of widely separated fields, say astronomy and taxonomic botany, are educated by exposure to quite different achievements described in very different books. And even men who, being in the same or in closely related fields, begin by studying many of the same books and achievements may acquire rather different paradigms in the course of professional specialization.

以物理学家群体为例，这是一个相当庞大且多元化的群体。如今，该群体中的每一位成员都会学习量子力学定律，而且他们中的大多数人都会在研究或教学中运用这些定律。但他们学习的并非都是这些定律的相同应用，因此，量子力学实践的改变对他们的影响也各不相同。在专业化道路上，一些物理学家只接触到量子力学的基本原理。另一些人则深入研究这些原理在化学领域的典型应用，还有一些人则研究其在固体物理学领域的典型应用，等等。量子力学对他们每个人的意义取决于他们所修读的课程、阅读的教材以及所研究的期刊。由此可见，尽管量子力学定律的改变对所有这些群体而言都将是革命性的，但如果改变仅仅反映在量子力学的某个典型应用领域，那么它对特定专业分支的成员而言可能只是革命性的。对于其他专业人士以及从事其他物理科学领域的人员而言，这种变化未必是革命性的。简而言之，尽管量子力学（或牛顿动力学、电磁理论）是许多科学群体的范式，但它并非对所有群体都适用。因此，它可以同时决定几个相互重叠但又不完全相同的常规科学传统。其中一个传统内部发生的革命性变革，未必会波及其他传统。

Consider, for a single example, the quite large and diverse community constituted by all physical scientists. Each member of that group today is taught the laws of, say, quantum mechanics, and most of them employ these laws at some point in their research or teaching. But they do not all learn the same applications of these laws, and they are not therefore all affected in the same ways by changes in quantum-mechanical practice. On the road to professional specialization, a few physical scientists encounter only the basic principles of quantum mechanics. Others study in detail the paradigm applications of these principles to chemistry, still others to the physics of the solid state, and so on. What quantum mechanics means to each of them depends upon what courses he has had, what texts he has read, and which journals he studies. It follows that, though a change in quantum-mechanical law will be revolutionary for all of these groups, a change that reflects only on one or another of the paradigm applications of quantum mechanics need be revolutionary only for the members of a particular professional subspecialty. For the rest of the profession and for those who practice other physical sciences, that change need not be revolutionary at all. In short, though quantum mechanics (or Newtonian dynamics, or electromagnetic theory) is a paradigm for many scientific groups, it is not the same paradigm for them all. Therefore, it can simultaneously determine several traditions of normal science that overlap without being coextensive. A revolution produced within one of these traditions will not necessarily extend to the others as well.

一个简短的例子可以说明专业化的影响，并能进一步佐证这一系列观点。一位研究者希望了解科学家们对原子理论的看法，于是他询问一位杰出的物理学家和一位著名的化学家，一个氦原子是否算作分子。两人都毫不犹豫地回答说：但他们的答案却不尽相同。化学家认为氦原子是分子，因为它符合气体分子运动论。而物理学家则认为氦原子不是分子，因为它没有分子光谱。7想必两人讨论的是同一种粒子，但他们的视角却源于各自的研究训练和实践经验。他们解决问题的经验告诉了他们分子应该是什么。毫无疑问，他们的经验有很多共同之处，但在这个例子中，这些经验并没有给两位专家带来相同的结论。随着讨论的深入，我们将发现这种范式差异有时会造成多么深远的影响。

One brief illustration of specialization’s effect may give this whole series of points additional force. An investigator who hoped to learn something about what scientists took the atomic theory to be asked a distinguished physicist and an eminent chemist whether a single atom of helium was or was not a molecule. Both answered without hesitation, but their answers were not the same. For the chemist the atom of helium was a molecule because it behaved like one with respect to the kinetic theory of gases. For the physicist, on the other hand, the helium atom was not a molecule because it displayed no molecular spectrum.7 Presumably both men were talking of the same particle, but they were viewing it through their own research training and practice. Their experience in problem-solving told them what a molecule must be. Undoubtedly their experiences had had much in common, but they did not, in this case, tell the two specialists the same thing. As we proceed we shall discover how consequential paradigm differences of this sort can occasionally be.

[ VI ]

[VI]

异常现象与科学发现的出现

Anomaly and the Emergence of Scientific Discoveries

我们刚才探讨的常规科学，即解谜活动，是一项高度累积性的事业，它成功地实现了其目标：不断扩展科学知识的范围和精确度。在所有这些方面，它都与人们通常对科学工作的印象高度吻合。然而，科学事业的一个标准成果却缺失了。常规科学并不追求事实或理论的新颖性，即便成功，也未必能发现任何新颖性。然而，科学研究却不断揭示出新的、意想不到的现象，科学家们也一次又一次地创造出全新的理论。历史甚至表明，科学事业已经发展出一种独特而强大的技巧，能够产生此类令人惊喜的发现。如果要调和科学的这一特性与上述论述，那么在既定范式下进行的研究必然是促成范式转变的一种特别有效的方式。这正是事实和理论的根本性创新所发挥的作用。它们并非偶然产生于一套规则下的博弈，而要吸收它们，就需要建立另一套规则。当它们成为科学的一部分之后，至少对于那些从事创新领域的专家来说，这项事业就再也不一样了。

Normal science, the puzzle-solving activity we have just examined, is a highly cumulative enterprise, eminently successful in its aim, the steady extension of the scope and precision of scientific knowledge. In all these respects it fits with great precision the most usual image of scientific work. Yet one standard product of the scientific enterprise is missing. Normal science does not aim at novelties of fact or theory and, when successful, finds none. New and unsuspected phenomena are, however, repeatedly uncovered by scientific research, and radical new theories have again and again been invented by scientists. History even suggests that the scientific enterprise has developed a uniquely powerful technique for producing surprises of this sort. If this characteristic of science is to be reconciled with what has already been said, then research under a paradigm must be a particularly effective way of inducing paradigm change. That is what fundamental novelties of fact and theory do. Produced inadvertently by a game played under one set of rules, their assimilation requires the elaboration of another set. After they have become parts of science, the enterprise, at least of those specialists in whose particular field the novelties lie, is never quite the same again.

考虑到以下因素，我们现在必须探究这种变化是如何发生的。首先是发现，或者说事实的新发现，然后是发明，或者说理论的新发现。然而，这种区分发现与发明、事实与理论的做法很快就会被证明是极其人为的。这种人为性是本文几个主要论点的重要线索。在本节的其余部分，我们将考察一些选定的发现，很快就会发现它们并非孤立事件，而是具有规律性重复结构的长期过程。发现始于对异常现象的认知，即认识到自然界在某种程度上违背了支配常规科学的范式预期。然后，它继续进行或多或少的对异常领域的探索。只有当范式理论被调整，使异常现象成为预期时，发现才告一段落。吸收一种新的事实需要对理论进行远超简单叠加的调整，在调整完成之前——在科学家学会以不同的方式看待自然之前——新的事实根本算不上真正的科学事实。

We must now ask how changes of this sort can come about, considering first discoveries, or novelties of fact, and then inventions, or novelties of theory. That distinction between discovery and invention or between fact and theory will, however, immediately prove to be exceedingly artificial. Its artificiality is an important clue to several of this essay’s main theses. Examining selected discoveries in the rest of this section, we shall quickly find that they are not isolated events but extended episodes with a regularly recurrent structure. Discovery commences with the awareness of anomaly, i.e., with the recognition that nature has somehow violated the paradigm-induced expectations that govern normal science. It then continues with a more or less extended exploration of the area of anomaly. And it closes only when the paradigm theory has been adjusted so that the anomalous has become the expected. Assimilating a new sort of fact demands a more than additive adjustment of theory, and until that adjustment is completed—until the scientist has learned to see nature in a different way—the new fact is not quite a scientific fact at all.

为了了解科学发现中事实创新与理论创新之间的紧密联系，我们可以考察一个特别著名的例子：氧气的发现。至少有三位不同的科学家对氧气的发现拥有合法的所有权，而且在18世纪70年代初期，肯定还有几位化学家在实验室容器中制备了富氧空气，只是他们自己并不知情。1常规科学的发展，就此而言是气相化学的发展，为这一突破性发现奠定了相当充分的基础。最早制备出相对纯净氧气样本的科学家是瑞典药剂师C.W. Scheele。然而，我们可以忽略他的工作，因为他的成果发表时，氧气的发现已被多次宣布，因此对我们这里最关注的历史进程没有影响。2第二位提出这一主张的是……英国科学家兼神学家约瑟夫·普里斯特利（Joseph Priestley）在长期研究大量固体物质释放的“气体”时，收集了加热氧化汞产生的气体。1774年，他鉴定出这种气体为一氧化二氮；1775年，通过进一步的实验，他又证实这是普通空气，只是其中的燃素含量低于通常水平。第三位氧气发现者拉瓦锡（Lavoisier）在普里斯特利1774年的实验之后，或许是受到了普里斯特利的启发，开始了最终发现氧气的研究。1775年初，拉瓦锡报告说，加热氧化汞得到的气体“完全就是空气，没有丝毫改变，只是……更加纯净，更易于呼吸”。3到1777年，拉瓦锡可能在普里斯特利的第二次暗示的帮助下，得出结论：这种气体是一种独特的物质，是大气的两大主要成分之一，普里斯特利始终无法接受这一结论。

To see how closely factual and theoretical novelty are intertwined in scientific discovery examine a particularly famous example, the discovery of oxygen. At least three different men have a legitimate claim to it, and several other chemists must, in the early 1770’s, have had enriched air in a laboratory vessel without knowing it.1 The progress of normal science, in this case of pneumatic chemistry, prepared the way to a breakthrough quite thoroughly. The earliest of the claimants to prepare a relatively pure sample of the gas was the Swedish apothecary, C. W. Scheele. We may, however, ignore his work since it was not published until oxygen’s discovery had repeatedly been announced elsewhere and thus had no effect upon the historical pattern that most concerns us here.2 The second in time to establish a claim was the British scientist and divine, Joseph Priestley, who collected the gas released by heated red oxide of mercury as one item in a prolonged normal investigation of the “airs” evolved by a large number of solid substances. In 1774 he identified the gas thus produced as nitrous oxide and in 1775, led by further tests, as common air with less than its usual quantity of phlogiston. The third claimant, Lavoisier, started the work that led him to oxygen after Priestley’s experiments of 1774 and possibly as the result of a hint from Priestley. Early in 1775 Lavoisier reported that the gas obtained by heating the red oxide of mercury was “air itself entire without alteration [except that] . . . it comes out more pure, more respirable.”3 By 1777, probably with the assistance of a second hint from Priestley, Lavoisier had concluded that the gas was a distinct species, one of the two main constituents of the atmosphere, a conclusion that Priestley was never able to accept.

这种发现模式引出了一个问题，这个问题可以针对科学家意识中出现过的每一个新现象提出：究竟是普里斯特利还是拉瓦锡，或者他们之中谁最先发现了氧气？无论如何，氧气究竟是什么时候被发现的？即使只有一个人声称发现了氧气，这个问题依然可以提出。作为关于优先权和发现日期的裁决，这个问题的答案与我们无关。然而，试图找到答案却能揭示发现的本质，因为根本不存在我们所寻求的那种答案。发现本身并不是一个适合提出此类问题的过程。事实上，人们之所以会提出这个问题——自18世纪80年代以来，氧气​​的优先权一直备受争议——恰恰反映了科学的某种固有观念存在偏差，这种观念赋予了发现如此重要的地位。让我们再来看一个例子。普里斯特利声称自己发现了氧气，是因为他优先分离出了一种后来被确认为独立物种的气体。但普里斯特利的样本并不纯净，如果说手握不纯净的氧气就能发现这一点，那么所有采集过大气空气样本的人都做过同样的事情。此外，如果普里斯特利是发现者，那么这项发现又是何时做出的呢？1774年，他认为自己获得了氧化亚氮，一种他早已知晓的物质；1775年，他又认为这种气体是脱燃素的空气，它既不是氧气，对于燃素化学家来说，也是一种完全出乎意料的气体。拉瓦锡的论断或许更有说服力，但也存在同样的问题。如果我们不把桂冠颁给普里斯特利，就不能因为拉瓦锡在1775年的工作而将桂冠授予他，因为正是那项工作使他认定这种气体就是“完整的空气”。我们或许应该期待拉瓦锡在1776年和1777年的工作，正是那项工作使他不仅看到了这种气体，还发现了这种气体的本质。然而，即使是这样的褒奖也值得商榷，因为在1777年以及他生命的尽头，拉瓦锡始终坚持认为氧是原子层面的“酸性原理”，只有当这种“原理”与热质（热的物质）结合时，氧气才会形成。4.因此，我们是否可以说，1777年时氧气尚未被发现？有些人可能会这样认为。但酸碱原理直到1810年以后才被化学界摒弃，而热力学原理则一直沿用到19世纪60年代。氧气在这两个日期之前就已经是一种标准化学物质了。

This pattern of discovery raises a question that can be asked about every novel phenomenon that has ever entered the consciousness of scientists. Was it Priestley or Lavoisier, if either, who first discovered oxygen? In any case, when was oxygen discovered? In that form the question could be asked even if only one claimant had existed. As a ruling about priority and date, an answer does not at all concern us. Nevertheless, an attempt to produce one will illuminate the nature of discovery, because there is no answer of the kind that is sought. Discovery is not the sort of process about which the question is appropriately asked. The fact that it is asked—the priority for oxygen has repeatedly been contested since the 1780’s—is a symptom of something askew in the image of science that gives discovery so fundamental a role. Look once more at our example. Priestley’s claim to the discovery of oxygen is based upon his priority in isolating a gas that was later recognized as a distinct species. But Priestley’s sample was not pure, and, if holding impure oxygen in one’s hands is to discover it, that had been done by everyone who ever bottled atmospheric air. Besides, if Priestley was the discoverer, when was the discovery made? In 1774 he thought he had obtained nitrous oxide, a species he already knew; in 1775 he saw the gas as dephlogisticated air, which is still not oxygen or even, for phlogistic chemists, a quite unexpected sort of gas. Lavoisier’s claim may be stronger, but it presents the same problems. If we refuse the palm to Priestley, we cannot award it to Lavoisier for the work of 1775 which led him to identify the gas as the “air itself entire.” Presumably we wait for the work of 1776 and 1777 which led Lavoisier to see not merely the gas but what the gas was. Yet even this award could be questioned, for in 1777 and to the end of his life Lavoisier insisted that oxygen was an atomic “principle of acidity” and that oxygen gas was formed only when that “principle” united with caloric, the matter of heat.4 Shall we therefore say that oxygen had not yet been discovered in 1777? Some may be tempted to do so. But the principle of acidity was not banished from chemistry until after 1810, and caloric lingered until the 1860’s. Oxygen had become a standard chemical substance before either of those dates.

显然，我们需要一套新的词汇和概念来分析诸如氧气发现之类的事件。虽然“氧气被发现”这句话本身无可厚非，但它却具有误导性，因为它暗示发现某物是一个单一的、简单的行为，可以等同于我们通常（也值得商榷）的“看见”的概念。正因如此，我们才如此轻易地认为，发现，就像看见或触摸一样，应该可以明确地归因于某个人和某个特定的时间点。但后者总是不可能的，前者也常常不可能。撇开舍勒不谈，我们可以肯定地说，氧气在1774年之前没有被发现，而且我们可能还会说，它在1777年或之后不久就已经被发现了。但在这些或类似的限制范围内，任何试图确定发现日期的尝试都必然带有主观性，因为发现一种新的现象必然是一个复杂的事件，它既涉及认识到某物存在，也涉及认识到它是什么。例如，如果氧气对我们来说是脱燃素的空气，那么我们应该毫不犹豫地坚持认为普里斯特利……我们最终发现了它，尽管我们仍然无法确切地知道是什么时候发现的。但如果观察与概念化、事实与理论融合在发现过程中密不可分，那么发现就是一个过程，必然需要时间。只有当所有相关的概念范畴都预先准备就绪时（在这种情况下，该现象就不是一种全新的现象），发现它和发现它本身才能毫不费力地、同时、瞬间发生。

Clearly we need a new vocabulary and concepts for analyzing events like the discovery of oxygen. Though undoubtedly correct, the sentence, “Oxygen was discovered,” misleads by suggesting that discovering something is a single simple act assimilable to our usual (and also questionable) concept of seeing. That is why we so readily assume that discovering, like seeing or touching, should be unequivocally attributable to an individual and to a moment in time. But the latter attribution is always impossible, and the former often is as well. Ignoring Scheele, we can safely say that oxygen had not been discovered before 1774, and we would probably also say that it had been discovered by 1777 or shortly thereafter. But within those limits or others like them, any attempt to date the discovery must inevitably be arbitrary because discovering a new sort of phenomenon is necessarily a complex event, one which involves recognizing both that something is and what it is. Note, for example, that if oxygen were dephlogisticated air for us, we should insist without hesitation that Priestley had discovered it, though we would still not know quite when. But if both observation and conceptualization, fact and assimilation to theory, are inseparably linked in discovery, then discovery is a process and must take time. Only when all the relevant conceptual categories are prepared in advance, in which case the phenomenon would not be of a new sort, can discovering that and discovering what occur effortlessly, together, and in an instant.

既然我们承认发现涉及一个漫长（尽管不一定很短）的概念吸收过程，那么我们是否也可以说它涉及范式的转变呢？对于这个问题，目前尚无定论，但至少就此而言，答案是肯定的。拉瓦锡从1777年开始在其论文中宣布的与其说是氧气的发现，不如说是氧气燃烧理论。这一理论是化学理论重构的基石，其影响之深远，通常被称为化学革命。事实上，如果氧气的发现并非化学新范式兴起过程中不可或缺的一部分，那么我们最初提出的优先权问题就不会显得如此重要。无论是在此案例还是其他案例中，我们对新现象及其发现者的价值评估，都取决于我们对该现象违背范式预期程度的判断。然而，需要注意的是，这一点在后文中会非常重要，氧气的发现本身并非化学理论转变的直接原因。早在参与发现这种新气体之前，拉瓦锡就确信燃素理论存在问题，并且燃烧的物体会吸收一部分大气。他在1772年将这一点记录在一份密封的笔记中，并交给了法兰西学院的秘书。 5 对氧气的研究使拉瓦锡早先的“有些不对劲”的感觉更加清晰明确。它让他意识到自己早已准备好去发现的东西——燃烧从大气中带走的物质的本质。这种对困难的预先认识必然意义重大。拉瓦锡之所以能在类似普里斯特利的实验中观察到普里斯特利本人未能观察到的气体，部分原因在于他采用了全新的范式。反之，普里斯特利终其一生都未能观察到拉瓦锡所观察到的现象，主要原因恰恰在于他需要对现有理论进行重大修正。

Grant now that discovery involves an extended, though not necessarily long, process of conceptual assimilation. Can we also say that it involves a change in paradigm? To that question, no general answer can yet be given, but in this case at least, the answer must be yes. What Lavoisier announced in his papers from 1777 on was not so much the discovery of oxygen as the oxygen theory of combustion. That theory was the keystone for a reformulation of chemistry so vast that it is usually called the chemical revolution. Indeed, if the discovery of oxygen had not been an intimate part of the emergence of a new paradigm for chemistry, the question of priority from which we began would never have seemed so important. In this case as in others, the value placed upon a new phenomenon and thus upon its discoverer varies with our estimate of the extent to which the phenomenon violated paradigm-induced anticipations. Notice, however, since it will be important later, that the discovery of oxygen was not by itself the cause of the change in chemical theory. Long before he played any part in the discovery of the new gas, Lavoisier was convinced both that something was wrong with the phlogiston theory and that burning bodies absorbed some part of the atmosphere. That much he had recorded in a sealed note deposited with the Secretary of the French Academy in 1772.5 What the work on oxygen did was to give much additional form and structure to Lavoisier’s earlier sense that something was amiss. It told him a thing he was already prepared to discover—the nature of the substance that combustion removes from the atmosphere. That advance awareness of difficulties must be a significant part of what enabled Lavoisier to see in experiments like Priestley’s a gas that Priestley had been unable to see there himself. Conversely, the fact that a major paradigm revision was needed to see what Lavoisier saw must be the principal reason why Priestley was, to the end of his long life, unable to see it.

另外两个篇幅更短的例子将进一步佐证刚才的论述，并引导我们从对发现本质的阐释，转向对科学发现产生的环境的理解。为了展现发现的主要途径，这两个例子彼此之间以及与氧气的发现都存在差异。第一个例子是X射线，这是一个典型的偶然发现案例，这种类型的发现比我们通常所理解的科学报告中那些客观的描述要频繁得多。故事始于物理学家伦琴中断对阴极射线的常规研究之时，他注意到，在放电过程中，距离他屏蔽装置一定距离的一块铂氰化钡屏发出了光芒。进一步的研究——伦琴在这七周里几乎寸步不离实验室，忙得不可开交——表明，发光的原因是阴极射线管发出的直线辐射，辐射会投射阴影，无法被磁铁偏转，以及其他许多特性。在宣布他的发现之前，伦琴已经确信，他所观察到的效应并非阴极射线造成的，而是一种至少与光有某些相似之处的物质造成的。6
