Two other and far briefer examples will reinforce much that has just been said and simultaneously carry us from an elucidation of the nature of discoveries toward an understanding of the circumstances under which they emerge in science. In an effort to represent the main ways in which discoveries can come about, these examples are chosen to be different both from each other and from the discovery of oxygen. The first, X-rays, is a classic case of discovery through accident, a type that occurs more frequently than the impersonal standards of scientific reporting allow us easily to realize. Its story opens on the day that the physicist Roentgen interrupted a normal investigation of cathode rays because he had noticed that a barium platinocyanide screen at some distance from his shielded apparatus glowed when the discharge was in process. Further investigations—they required seven hectic weeks during which Roentgen rarely left the laboratory—indicated that the cause of the glow came in straight lines from the cathode ray tube, that the radiation cast shadows, could not be deflected by a magnet, and much else besides. Before announcing his discovery, Roentgen had convinced himself that his effect was not due to cathode rays but to an agent with at least some similarity to light.6

即使如此简短的概述也揭示了与氧气发现的惊人相似之处：拉瓦锡在用氧化汞进行实验之前，曾进行过一些实验，但这些实验并未产生燃素理论预期的结果；伦琴的发现始于他意识到自己的屏幕在不应该发光的时候却发光了。在这两个例子中，对异常现象——即研究者原本的理论框架无法解释的现象——的感知，在为最终的发现铺平道路的过程中发挥了至关重要的作用。新奇之处。但是，在这两种情况下，人们意识到出了问题仅仅是发现的前奏。氧气和X射线都不是凭空出现的，它们都需要进一步的实验和吸收。例如，在伦琴的研究中，我们应该在哪个阶段说X射线真正被发现了呢？无论如何，肯定不是在最初发现的时候，那时人们只注意到一个发光的屏幕。至少还有一位研究者也看到了那个发光的屏幕，但令他后来懊恼的是，他什么也没发现。7 同样显而易见的是，发现的时刻也不能提前到研究的最后一周，那时伦琴正在探索他已经发现的新辐射的特性。我们只能说，X射线是在1895年11月8日至12月28日期间在维尔茨堡出现的。

Even so brief an epitome reveals striking resemblances to the discovery of oxygen: before experimenting with red oxide of mercury, Lavoisier had performed experiments that did not produce the results anticipated under the phlogiston paradigm; Roentgen’s discovery commenced with the recognition that his screen glowed when it should not. In both cases the perception of anomaly—of a phenomenon, that is, for which his paradigm had not readied the investigator—played an essential role in preparing the way for perception of novelty. But, again in both cases, the perception that something had gone wrong was only the prelude to discovery. Neither oxygen nor X-rays emerged without a further process of experimentation and assimilation. At what point in Roentgen’s investigation, for example, ought we say that X-rays had actually been discovered? Not, in any case, at the first instant, when all that had been noted was a glowing screen. At least one other investigator had seen that glow and, to his subsequent chagrin, discovered nothing at all.7 Nor, it is almost as clear, can the moment of discovery be pushed forward to a point during the last week of investigation, by which time Roentgen was exploring the properties of the new radiation he had already discovered. We can only say that X-rays emerged in Würzburg between November 8 and December 28, 1895.

然而，在第三个领域，氧气和X射线的发现之间是否存在显著的相似之处则远不那么明显。与氧气的发现不同，X射线的发现至少在发现后的十年内，并未引发科学理论的任何明显变革。那么，在何种意义上，对这一发现的吸收必然导致范式转变呢？否定这种转变的理由非常充分。诚然，伦琴及其同时代人所信奉的范式无法预测X射线的存在。（麦克斯韦的电磁理论当时尚未被普遍接受，阴极射线的粒子理论也只是当时众多推测之一。）但这些范式也并未像燃素理论否定拉瓦锡对普里斯特利气体的解释那样，在任何显而易见的意义上否定X射线的存在。相反，1895年公认的科学理论和实践已经承认多种形式的辐射——可见光、红外线和紫外线。为什么X射线不能被视为一种众所周知的自然现象呢？例如，为什么它们没有像其他发现一样被人们所接受？又多了一种化学元素？在伦琴时代，人们仍在寻找并发现新的元素来填补元素周期表中的空缺。这对于当时的科学研究来说是常规项目，成功只会让人感到高兴，而不会感到惊讶。

In a third area, however, the existence of significant parallels between the discoveries of oxygen and of X-rays is far less apparent. Unlike the discovery of oxygen, that of X-rays was not, at least for a decade after the event, implicated in any obvious upheaval in scientific theory. In what sense, then, can the assimilation of that discovery be said to have necessitated paradigm change? The case for denying such a change is very strong. To be sure, the paradigms subscribed to by Roentgen and his contemporaries could not have been used to predict X-rays. (Maxwell’s electromagnetic theory had not yet been accepted everywhere, and the particulate theory of cathode rays was only one of several current speculations.) But neither did those paradigms, at least in any obvious sense, prohibit the existence of X-rays as the phlogiston theory had prohibited Lavoisier’s interpretation of Priestley’s gas. On the contrary, in 1895 accepted scientific theory and practice admitted a number of forms of radiation—visible, infrared, and ultraviolet. Why could not X-rays have been accepted as just one more form of a well-known class of natural phenomena? Why were they not, for example, received in the same way as the discovery of an additional chemical element? New elements to fill empty places in the periodic table were still being sought and found in Roentgen’s day. Their pursuit was a standard project for normal science, and success was an occasion only for congratulations, not for surprise.

然而，X射线的出现不仅令人惊讶，更令人震惊。开尔文勋爵最初宣称X射线是一场精心策划的骗局。8其他人虽然无法质疑证据，但显然也对此感到匪夷所思。尽管既有理论并未禁止X射线的存在，但它却违背了人们根深蒂固的预期。我认为，这些预期隐含在既定的实验室操作流程的设计和解释之中。到了19世纪90年代，阴极射线管设备已在欧洲众多实验室广泛应用。如果伦琴的装置确实产生了X射线，那么其他一些实验者也必然在一段时间内无意中产生了这些射线。或许，这些射线（很可能还有其他未被发现的来源）与之前一些未曾提及的现象有关。至少，未来一些人们早已熟知的仪器设备将不得不加装铅屏蔽层。此前已完成的常规实验项目现在也必须重做，因为早期的科学家未能识别和控制一个相关的变量。诚然，X射线开辟了一个全新的领域，从而拓展了常规科学的潜在范畴。但更重要的是，它们也改变了既有的领域。在这个过程中，它们剥夺了先前具有代表性的仪器类型所享有的“典范”地位。

X-rays, however, were greeted not only with surprise but with shock. Lord Kelvin at first pronounced them an elaborate hoax.8 Others, though they could not doubt the evidence, were clearly staggered by it. Though X-rays were not prohibited by established theory, they violated deeply entrenched expectations. Those expectations, I suggest, were implicit in the design and interpretation of established laboratory procedures. By the 1890’s cathode ray equipment was widely deployed in numerous European laboratories. If Roentgen’s apparatus had produced X-rays, then a number of other experimentalists must for some time have been producing those rays without knowing it. Perhaps those rays, which might well have other unacknowledged sources too, were implicated in behavior previously explained without reference to them. At the very least, several sorts of long familiar apparatus would in the future have to be shielded with lead. Previously completed work on normal projects would now have to be done again because earlier scientists had failed to recognize and control a relevant variable. X-rays, to be sure, opened up a new field and thus added to the potential domain of normal science. But they also, and this is now the more important point, changed fields that had already existed. In the process they denied previously paradigmatic types of instrumentation their right to that title.

简而言之，无论是有意识还是无意识，选择使用特定仪器并以特定方式使用都包含着一种假设，即只会出现某些特定类型的情况。这种假设既包含工具性的，也包含理论性的，并且它们往往在科学发展中发挥了决定性作用。例如，氧气的迟来发现就包含着这样一种假设。普里斯特利和拉瓦锡都使用一种标准的“空气质量”测试方法，结果发现氧气质量并不理想。他们将两份气体与一份一氧化氮混合，在水中摇晃混合物，然后测量残留气体的体积。此前积累的经验使他们确信，在大气中，残留气体的体积为1，而在任何其他气体（或污染空气）中，残留气体的体积都会更大。在氧气实验中，他们都发现了接近1体积的残留气体，并据此确定了该气体。直到很久以后，部分原因是由于一次意外，普里斯特利才放弃了标准程序，并尝试以其他比例将一氧化氮与他的气体混合。他随后发现，当一氧化氮的体积增加到原来的四倍时，几乎没有残留气体。他对最初测试程序的坚持——这一程序得到了大量先前经验的认可——同时也意味着他坚信不存在像氧气那样表现的气体。9

In short, consciously or not, the decision to employ a particular piece of apparatus and to use it in a particular way carries an assumption that only certain sorts of circumstances will arise. There are instrumental as well as theoretical expectations, and they have often played a decisive role in scientific development. One such expectation is, for example, part of the story of oxygen’s belated discovery. Using a standard test for “the goodness of air,” both Priestley and Lavoisier mixed two volumes of their gas with one volume of nitric oxide, shook the mixture over water, and measured the volume of the gaseous residue. The previous experience from which this standard procedure had evolved assured them that with atmospheric air the residue would be one volume and that for any other gas (or for polluted air) it would be greater. In the oxygen experiments both found a residue close to one volume and identified the gas accordingly. Only much later and in part through an accident did Priestley renounce the standard procedure and try mixing nitric oxide with his gas in other proportions. He then found that with quadruple the volume of nitric oxide there was almost no residue at all. His commitment to the original test procedure—a procedure sanctioned by much previous experience—had been simultaneously a commitment to the non-existence of gases that could behave as oxygen did.9

此类例子不胜枚举，例如，铀裂变反应的发现就来得如此之晚。该核反应之所以难以识别，原因之一是，那些了解轰击铀会产生什么反应的科学家，选择的化学实验主要针对元素周期表上游的元素。10我们是否应该因为这类仪器操作屡屡被证明具有误导性而得出结论：科学应该放弃标准测试和标准仪器？那样做是行不通的。以一种不可思议的研究方法。范式程序和应用对于科学而言，与范式定律和理论一样必不可少，并且它们具有相同的作用。它们不可避免地限制了在任何特定时期可供科学研究的现象学领域。认识到这一点，我们或许就能从本质上理解，像X射线这样的发现必然会促使科学界的特定群体进行范式转变——进而改变他们的程序和预期。因此，我们或许也能理解，为什么X射线的发现似乎为许多科学家打开了一个陌生的新世界，并因此在引发二十世纪物理学的危机中发挥了如此重要的作用。

Illustrations of this sort could be multiplied by reference, for example, to the belated identification of uranium fission. One reason why that nuclear reaction proved especially difficult to recognize was that men who knew what to expect when bombarding uranium chose chemical tests aimed mainly at elements from the upper end of the periodic table.10 Ought we conclude from the frequency with which such instrumental commitments prove misleading that science should abandon standard tests and standard instruments? That would result in an inconceivable method of research. Paradigm procedures and applications are as necessary to science as paradigm laws and theories, and they have the same effects. Inevitably they restrict the phenomenological field accessible for scientific investigation at any given time. Recognizing that much, we may simultaneously see an essential sense in which a discovery like X-rays necessitates paradigm change—and therefore change in both procedures and expectations—for a special segment of the scientific community. As a result, we may also understand how the discovery of X-rays could seem to open a strange new world to many scientists and could thus participate so effectively in the crisis that led to twentieth-century physics.

我们最后举的科学发现例子——莱顿瓶——属于理论驱动型发现。乍一看，这个术语似乎有些矛盾。前面的论述大多表明，理论预先预测的发现属于常规科学范畴，并不会产生任何新的事实。例如，我之前就曾指出，19世纪下半叶新化学元素的发现正是源于常规科学。但并非所有理论都是范式理论。无论是在范式出现之前的时期，还是在导致范式大规模变革的危机时期，科学家通常会提出许多推测性的、尚未完善的理论，这些理论本身就能为发现指明方向。然而，这种发现往往并非推测性假设所预期的。只有当实验与推测性理论相互印证时，发现才会出现，理论才会成为范式。

Our final example of scientific discovery, that of the Leyden jar, belongs to a class that may be described as theory-induced. Initially, the term may seem paradoxical. Much that has been said so far suggests that discoveries predicted by theory in advance are parts of normal science and result in no new sort of fact. I have, for example, previously referred to the discoveries of new chemical elements during the second half of the nineteenth century as proceeding from normal science in that way. But not all theories are paradigm theories. Both during pre-paradigm periods and during the crises that lead to large-scale changes of paradigm, scientists usually develop many speculative and unarticulated theories that can themselves point the way to discovery. Often, however, that discovery is not quite the one anticipated by the speculative and tentative hypothesis. Only as experiment and tentative theory are together articulated to a match does the discovery emerge and the theory become a paradigm.

莱顿瓶的发现展现了所有这些特征，以及我们之前观察到的其他特征。在它诞生之初，电学研究并没有统一的范式。相反，许多理论相互竞争，这些理论都源于相对容易理解的现象。没有一种理论能够很好地解释所有种类的电学现象。这种失败是莱顿瓶发现过程中出现的诸多异常现象的根源。其中一个竞争的电学学派认为电是一种流体，这种观点导致许多人尝试将其装瓶。研究人员将装满水的玻璃瓶握在手中，然后将瓶中的水接触悬挂在静电发生器上的导体，以此来测试液体的性质。当他们将瓶子从机器上取下，并用另一只手触摸瓶中的水（或与之相连的导体）时，每位研究人员都遭受了严重的电击。然而，这些最初的实验并没有为电工们带来莱顿瓶。莱顿瓶的出现是一个较为缓慢的过程，而且我们无法确切地说出它的发现时间。最初储存导电液体的尝试之所以成功，仅仅是因为研究人员站在地面上，手持瓶子进行实验。电工们当时还不知道，莱顿瓶需要内外两层导电涂层，而且液体实际上并没有真正储存在瓶内。在探索过程中，他们逐渐认识到这一点，并发现了其他一些异常现象，最终，我们今天所说的莱顿瓶诞生了。此外，促成电学诞生的实验（其中许多是由富兰克林进行的）也正是导致流体理论需要彻底修正的实验，从而为电学提供了第一个完整的范式。 11

The discovery of the Leyden jar displays all these features as well as the others we have observed before. When it began, there was no single paradigm for electrical research. Instead, a number of theories, all derived from relatively accessible phenomena, were in competition. None of them succeeded in ordering the whole variety of electrical phenomena very well. That failure is the source of several of the anomalies that provide background for the discovery of the Leyden jar. One of the competing schools of electricians took electricity to be a fluid, and that conception led a number of men to attempt bottling the fluid by holding a water-filled glass vial in their hands and touching the water to a conductor suspended from an active electrostatic generator. On removing the jar from the machine and touching the water (or a conductor connected to it) with his free hand, each of these investigators experienced a severe shock. Those first experiments did not, however, provide electricians with the Leyden jar. That device emerged more slowly, and it is again impossible to say just when its discovery was completed. The initial attempts to store electrical fluid worked only because investigators held the vial in their hands while standing upon the ground. Electricians had still to learn that the jar required an outer as well as an inner conducting coating and that the fluid is not really stored in the jar at all. Somewhere in the course of the investigations that showed them this, and which introduced them to several other anomalous effects, the device that we call the Leyden jar emerged. Furthermore, the experiments that led to its emergence, many of them performed by Franklin, were also the ones that necessitated the drastic revision of the fluid theory and thus provided the first full paradigm for electricity.11

或多或少（对应于从令人震惊到预期结果的连续过程），上述三个例子所共有的特征也是所有新现象发现的共同特征。这些特征包括：先前对异常的认知、观察和概念认知的逐步同步出现，以及由此导致的范式类别和程序的改变（通常伴随着阻力）。甚至有证据表明，这些特征本身就蕴含在感知过程的本质之中。在一项心理学实验中（该实验在专业领域之外更值得广泛了解），布鲁纳和波斯特曼要求实验对象在短暂且受控的条件下识别一系列扑克牌。这些牌中有些是正常的，但有些牌是异常的，例如，一张红色的黑桃6和一张黑色的红桃4。每次实验流程是向一名受试者展示一张牌，并逐渐增加展示次数。每次展示后，受试者会被询问他看到了什么，如果连续两次识别正确，则该次实验结束。12

To a greater or lesser extent (corresponding to the continuum from the shocking to the anticipated result), the characteristics common to the three examples above are characteristic of all discoveries from which new sorts of phenomena emerge. Those characteristics include: the previous awareness of anomaly, the gradual and simultaneous emergence of both observational and conceptual recognition, and the consequent change of paradigm categories and procedures often accompanied by resistance. There is even evidence that these same characteristics are built into the nature of the perceptual process itself. In a psychological experiment that deserves to be far better known outside the trade, Bruner and Postman asked experimental subjects to identify on short and controlled exposure a series of playing cards. Many of the cards were normal, but some were made anomalous, e.g., a red six of spades and a black four of hearts. Each experimental run was constituted by the display of a single card to a single subject in a series of gradually increased exposures. After each exposure the subject was asked what he had seen, and the run was terminated by two successive correct identifications.12

即使在最短的曝光时间内，许多受试者也能识别出大部分牌，而随着曝光时间的略微增加，所有受试者都能识别出全部牌。对于正常的牌，这些识别通常是正确的，但对于异常的牌，受试者几乎总是毫不犹豫或困惑地将其识别为正常牌。例如，黑桃4可能被识别为黑桃4或红桃4。他们没有意识到任何异常，立即将其归入先前经验中预先设定的概念类别之一。我们甚至不愿说受试者看到了与他们识别出的牌不同的东西。随着对异常牌曝光时间的进一步增加，受试者开始犹豫，并表现出对异常的意识。例如，当看到红桃6时，一些人会说：“这是黑桃6，但它有点不对劲——黑色部分有红色的边框。” 曝光时间的进一步增加导致更多的犹豫和困惑，直到最后，有时甚至是突然之间，大多数受试者都能毫不犹豫地做出正确的识别。此外，在对两三张异常卡片进行过这样的处理后，他们对其他卡片的识别就不会有太大困难。然而，少数受试者始终无法对卡片类别进行必要的调整。即使给予受试者相当于识别正常卡片所需平均曝光量的四十倍，仍有超过10%的异常卡片未能被正确识别。而那些识别失败的受试者往往会感到极度沮丧。其中一位受试者惊呼：“我根本看不出是什么花色，不管是什么。它当时看起来根本不像一张牌。我现在也不知道它是什么颜色了。”或者说，它到底是黑桃还是红桃。我现在甚至都不确定黑桃长什么样了。我的天哪！” 13在下一节中，我们偶尔也会看到科学家们有这种行为。

Even on the shortest exposures many subjects identified most of the cards, and after a small increase all the subjects identified them all. For the normal cards these identifications were usually correct, but the anomalous cards were almost always identified, without apparent hesitation or puzzlement, as normal. The black four of hearts might, for example, be identified as the four of either spades or hearts. Without any awareness of trouble, it was immediately fitted to one of the conceptual categories prepared by prior experience. One would not even like to say that the subjects had seen something different from what they identified. With a further increase of exposure to the anomalous cards, subjects did begin to hesitate and to display awareness of anomaly. Exposed, for example, to the red six of spades, some would say: That’s the six of spades, but there’s something wrong with it—the black has a red border. Further increase of exposure resulted in still more hesitation and confusion until finally, and sometimes quite suddenly, most subjects would produce the correct identification without hesitation. Moreover, after doing this with two or three of the anomalous cards, they would have little further difficulty with the others. A few subjects, however, were never able to make the requisite adjustment of their categories. Even at forty times the average exposure required to recognize normal cards for what they were, more than 10 per cent of the anomalous cards were not correctly identified. And the subjects who then failed often experienced acute personal distress. One of them exclaimed: “I can’t make the suit out, whatever it is. It didn’t even look like a card that time. I don’t know what color it is now or whether it’s a spade or a heart. I’m not even sure now what a spade looks like. My God!”13 In the next section we shall occasionally see scientists behaving this way too.

无论是作为一种隐喻，还是因为它反映了心智的本质，这个心理学实验都为科学发现的过程提供了一个极其简洁明了的框架。在科学领域，正如扑克牌实验一样，新事物只有在预期的背景下，经历阻力才能出现。最初，即使在后来观察到异常情况的情况下，人们也只会体验到预期的和常见的现象。然而，进一步的了解最终会让人意识到某些地方出了问题，或者将这种现象与之前出现过的问题联系起来。这种对异常的认知开启了一个调整概念范畴的时期，直到最初的异常变成了预期之内的事情。此时，发现就完成了。我已经强调，所有基础科学新事物的出现都涉及这一过程或非常类似的过程。现在，我想指出，认识到这一过程，我们最终就能明白，为什么常规科学——一种并非以发现新事物为目标，且最初倾向于抑制新事物的追求——却能如此有效地促成新事物的出现。

Either as a metaphor or because it reflects the nature of the mind, that psychological experiment provides a wonderfully simple and cogent schema for the process of scientific discovery. In science, as in the playing card experiment, novelty emerges only with difficulty, manifested by resistance, against a background provided by expectation. Initially, only the anticipated and usual are experienced even under circumstances where anomaly is later to be observed. Further acquaintance, however, does result in awareness of something wrong or does relate the effect to something that has gone wrong before. That awareness of anomaly opens a period in which conceptual categories are adjusted until the initially anomalous has become the anticipated. At this point the discovery has been completed. I have already urged that that process or one very much like it is involved in the emergence of all fundamental scientific novelties. Let me now point out that, recognizing the process, we can at last begin to see why normal science, a pursuit not directed to novelties and tending at first to suppress them, should nevertheless be so effective in causing them to arise.

在任何科学的发展过程中，最初被接受的范式通常被认为能够相当成功地解释该学科实践者所能轻易获得的绝大多数观察和实验结果。因此，进一步的发展通常需要建造精密的设备，发展深奥的词汇和技能，以及对概念进行提炼，使其与通常的常识原型越来越不相似。这种专业化一方面导致科学家视野的巨大局限，以及对范式转变的相当大的抵制。科学变得越来越僵化。另一方面，在范式引导群体关注的领域内，常规科学能够提供详尽的信息和精确的分析。这种观察与理论的契合，唯有通过这种方式才能实现。此外，这种契合的细节和精确度，其价值远超其本身并非总是十分重要的意义。如果没有这套主要用于预期功能的特殊装置，最终导致创新成果的出现便无从谈起。即便装置存在，创新通常也只对那些能够精确预知预期结果，并能识别出异常情况的人而言才会出现。异常现象只有在既有范式的背景下才会显现。范式越精确、越全面，它对异常现象的指示就越灵敏，从而也越能预示范式转变的契机。在正常的发现模式中，即使是对变革的抵制也有其用处，我们将在下一节中对此进行更深入的探讨。通过确保范式不会轻易被打破，抵制保证了科学家不会轻易分心，也保证了那些导致范式转变的异常现象能够深入现有知识的核心。一项重要的科学创新经常同时从多个实验室中涌现，这一事实本身既表明了常规科学的强烈传统性，也表明了这种传统追求为自身变革所做的充分准备。

In the development of any science, the first received paradigm is usually felt to account quite successfully for most of the observations and experiments easily accessible to that science’s practitioners. Further development, therefore, ordinarily calls for the construction of elaborate equipment, the development of an esoteric vocabulary and skills, and a refinement of concepts that increasingly lessens their resemblance to their usual common-sense prototypes. That professionalization leads, on the one hand, to an immense restriction of the scientist’s vision and to a considerable resistance to paradigm change. The science has become increasingly rigid. On the other hand, within those areas to which the paradigm directs the attention of the group, normal science leads to a detail of information and to a precision of the observation-theory match that could be achieved in no other way. Furthermore, that detail and precision-of-match have a value that transcends their not always very high intrinsic interest. Without the special apparatus that is constructed mainly for anticipated functions, the results that lead ultimately to novelty could not occur. And even when the apparatus exists, novelty ordinarily emerges only for the man who, knowing with precision what he should expect, is able to recognize that something has gone wrong. Anomaly appears only against the background provided by the paradigm. The more precise and far-reaching that paradigm is, the more sensitive an indicator it provides of anomaly and hence of an occasion for paradigm change. In the normal mode of discovery, even resistance to change has a use that will be explored more fully in the next section. By ensuring that the paradigm will not be too easily surrendered, resistance guarantees that scientists will not be lightly distracted and that the anomalies that lead to paradigm change will penetrate existing knowledge to the core. The very fact that a significant scientific novelty so often emerges simultaneously from several laboratories is an index both to the strongly traditional nature of normal science and to the completeness with which that traditional pursuit prepares the way for its own change.

[ VII ]

[VII]

危机与科学理论的出现

Crisis and the Emergence of Scientific Theories

第六部分讨论的所有发现都是范式转变的原因或促成因素。此外，这些发现所引发的转变既有破坏性的一面，也有建设性的一面。在吸收了这些发现之后，科学家们能够解释更广泛的自然现象，或者更精确地解释一些先前已知的现象。但这种进步的实现，是通过摒弃一些先前的标准信念或程序，并同时用其他信念或程序取代先前范式中的相应组成部分来实现的。我认为，除了那些在细节上早已预料到的、不足为奇的发现之外，所有通过常规科学取得的发现都与此类转变相关。然而，发现并非这些破坏性-建设性范式转变的唯一来源。在本节中，我们将开始探讨由新理论的提出而导致的类似但通常规模更大的转变。

All the discoveries considered in Section VI were causes of or contributors to paradigm change. Furthermore, the changes in which these discoveries were implicated were all destructive as well as constructive. After the discovery had been assimilated, scientists were able to account for a wider range of natural phenomena or to account with greater precision for some of those previously known. But that gain was achieved only by discarding some previously standard beliefs or procedures and, simultaneously, by replacing those components of the previous paradigm with others. Shifts of this sort are, I have argued, associated with all discoveries achieved through normal science, excepting only the unsurprising ones that had been anticipated in all but their details. Discoveries are not, however, the only sources of these destructive-constructive paradigm changes. In this section we shall begin to consider the similar, but usually far larger, shifts that result from the invention of new theories.

既然我们已经论证了在科学领域，事实与理论、发现与发明并非截然分开，那么我们可以预料到本节内容会与上一节有所重叠。（例如，普里斯特利和拉瓦锡分别率先发现氧气和拉瓦锡的说法就显得荒谬了。）发明自有其吸引力。氧气作为一种发现已被我们认识；我们很快又会以发明的形式再次遇到它。）在探讨新理论的出现时，我们必然也会拓展对发现的理解。然而，重叠并不等同。上一节讨论的那些发现，至少并非单独促成了哥白尼革命、牛顿革命、化学革命和爱因斯坦革命等范式转变。它们也并非促成了那些规模较小、更纯粹属于专业领域的范式转变——例如光的波动理论、热的动力学理论或麦克斯韦的电磁理论。这些理论又怎能从常规科学中产生呢？常规科学活动与其说是致力于发现，不如说是致力于追求理论。

Having argued already that in the sciences fact and theory, discovery and invention, are not categorically and permanently distinct, we can anticipate overlap between this section and the last. (The impossible suggestion that Priestley first discovered oxygen and Lavoisier then invented it has its attractions. Oxygen has already been encountered as discovery; we shall shortly meet it again as invention.) In taking up the emergence of new theories we shall inevitably extend our understanding of discovery as well. Still, overlap is not identity. The sorts of discoveries considered in the last section were not, at least singly, responsible for such paradigm shifts as the Copernican, Newtonian, chemical, and Einsteinian revolutions. Nor were they responsible for the somewhat smaller, because more exclusively professional, changes in paradigm produced by the wave theory of light, the dynamical theory of heat, or Maxwell’s electromagnetic theory. How can theories like these arise from normal science, an activity even less directed to their pursuit than to that of discoveries?

如果对异常现象的认知在新型现象的出现中发挥了作用，那么，所有可接受的理论变革都以类似但更深刻的认知为前提，这一点也就不足为奇了。我认为，关于这一点，历史证据是完全确凿的。在哥白尼宣布宇宙起源之前，托勒密天文学的状况令人震惊。1伽利略对运动研究的贡献很大程度上依赖于经院哲学家在亚里士多德理论中发现的缺陷。2牛顿关于光和颜色的新理论源于发现，当时所有现有的范式前理论都无法解释光谱的长度，而取代牛顿理论的波动理论正是在人们日益关注衍射和偏振效应与牛顿理论之间关系的异常现象之际提出的。3热力学诞生于19世纪两种现有物理理论的碰撞，而量子力学……来自围绕黑体辐射、比热和光电效应的一系列难题。4此外，除了牛顿的情况外，在所有这些案例中，对异常现象的认识都持续了如此之久，渗透得如此之深，以至于我们可以恰当地将受其影响的领域描述为处于日益加剧的危机状态。由于新理论的出现需要大规模的范式颠覆以及常规科学问题和技术的重大转变，因此，新理论的出现通常伴随着一段明显的专业不安全感时期。正如人们所预料的那样，这种不安全感源于常规科学难题持续未能按预期得到解答。现有规则的失效是寻求新规则的前奏。

If awareness of anomaly plays a role in the emergence of new sorts of phenomena, it should surprise no one that a similar but more profound awareness is prerequisite to all acceptable changes of theory. On this point historical evidence is, I think, entirely unequivocal. The state of Ptolemaic astronomy was a scandal before Copernicus’ announcement.1 Galileo’s contributions to the study of motion depended closely upon difficulties discovered in Aristotle’s theory by scholastic critics.2 Newton’s new theory of light and color originated in the discovery that none of the existing pre-paradigm theories would account for the length of the spectrum, and the wave theory that replaced Newton’s was announced in the midst of growing concern about anomalies in the relation of diffraction and polarization effects to Newton’s theory.3 Thermodynamics was born from the collision of two existing nineteenth-century physical theories, and quantum mechanics from a variety of difficulties surrounding black-body radiation, specific heats, and the photoelectric effect.4 Furthermore, in all these cases except that of Newton the awareness of anomaly had lasted so long and penetrated so deep that one can appropriately describe the fields affected by it as in a state of growing crisis. Because it demands large-scale paradigm destruction and major shifts in the problems and techniques of normal science, the emergence of new theories is generally preceded by a period of pronounced professional insecurity. As one might expect, that insecurity is generated by the persistent failure of the puzzles of normal science to come out as they should. Failure of existing rules is the prelude to a search for new ones.

首先来看一个著名的范式转变案例：哥白尼天文学的兴起。它的前身托勒密体系在公元前两百年和公元后两百年间发展起来，在预测恒星和行星位置的变化方面取得了令人瞩目的成功。没有任何其他古代体系能与之媲美；对于恒星而言，托勒密天文学至今仍被广泛用作工程近似方法；对于行星而言，托勒密的预测与哥白尼的预测一样准确。然而，对于任何科学理论而言，令人瞩目的成功永远并不意味着完全的成功。无论是行星位置还是岁差，托勒密体系的预测都始终与当时最佳的观测结果存在偏差。进一步缩小这些微小的偏差构成了托勒密许多后继者进行天文研究的主要难题，正如将天体观测与牛顿理论相结合的尝试为牛顿十八世纪的后继者们提供了常规的研究难题一样。一段时间以来，天文学家完全有理由认为这些尝试会像托勒密体系的建立一样成功。对于特定的偏差，天文学家总能通过对托勒密的复合圆体系进行一些特定的调整来消除它。但是，正如……随着时间的推移，一个观察众多天文学家常规研究成果的人会发现，天文学的复杂性增长速度远远超过了其精确度的增长速度，而且在一个地方纠正的偏差很可能在其他地方再次出现。5

Look first at a particularly famous case of paradigm change, the emergence of Copernican astronomy. When its predecessor, the Ptolemaic system, was first developed during the last two centuries before Christ and the first two after, it was admirably successful in predicting the changing positions of both stars and planets. No other ancient system had performed so well; for the stars, Ptolemaic astronomy is still widely used today as an engineering approximation; for the planets, Ptolemy’s predictions were as good as Copernicus’. But to be admirably successful is never, for a scientific theory, to be completely successful. With respect both to planetary position and to precession of the equinoxes, predictions made with Ptolemy’s system never quite conformed with the best available observations. Further reduction of those minor discrepancies constituted many of the principal problems of normal astronomical research for many of Ptolemy’s successors, just as a similar attempt to bring celestial observation and Newtonian theory together provided normal research problems for Newton’s eighteenth-century successors. For some time astronomers had every reason to suppose that these attempts would be as successful as those that had led to Ptolemy’s system. Given a particular discrepancy, astronomers were invariably able to eliminate it by making some particular adjustment in Ptolemy’s system of compounded circles. But as time went on, a man looking at the net result of the normal research effort of many astronomers could observe that astronomy’s complexity was increasing far more rapidly than its accuracy and that a discrepancy corrected in one place was likely to show up in another.5

由于天文传统屡遭外部干扰，且在印刷术发明之前，天文学家之间的交流十分有限，这些困难才逐渐被人们认识到。但这种认识终究还是出现了。到了十三世纪，阿方索十世宣称，如果上帝在创造宇宙时征求过他的意见，他一定会得到很好的建议。十六世纪，哥白尼的合作者多梅尼科·达·诺瓦拉认为，像托勒密体系那样繁琐且不精确的体系，根本不可能适用于自然。哥白尼本人也在《天体运行论》的序言中写道，他所继承的天文传统最终只造就了一个怪物。到了十六世纪初，越来越多的欧洲顶尖天文学家意识到，天文范式在解决其自身固有的问题上已经失效。正是这种认识，促使哥白尼摒弃了托勒密范式，并开始寻求新的范式。他那著名的序言至今仍是对危机状态的经典描述之一。6

Because the astronomical tradition was repeatedly interrupted from outside and because, in the absence of printing, communication between astronomers was restricted, these difficulties were only slowly recognized. But awareness did come. By the thirteenth century Alfonso X could proclaim that if God had consulted him when creating the universe, he would have received good advice. In the sixteenth century, Copernicus’ coworker, Domenico da Novara, held that no system so cumbersome and inaccurate as the Ptolemaic had become could possibly be true of nature. And Copernicus himself wrote in the Preface to the De Revolutionibus that the astronomical tradition he inherited had finally created only a monster. By the early sixteenth century an increasing number of Europe’s best astronomers were recognizing that the astronomical paradigm was failing in application to its own traditional problems. That recognition was prerequisite to Copernicus’ rejection of the Ptolemaic paradigm and his search for a new one. His famous preface still provides one of the classic descriptions of a crisis state.6

当然，正常的解谜技术活动的崩溃并非哥白尼所面临的天文危机的唯一因素。更深入的探讨还会涉及当时社会对历法改革的压力，正是这种压力使得岁差之谜的解决显得尤为紧迫。此外，更全面的论述还会考虑中世纪对亚里士多德的批判、文艺复兴时期新柏拉图主义的兴起以及其他重要的历史因素。但技术崩溃仍然是这场危机的核心。在一门成熟的科学中——而古代的天文学正是这样一门科学——上述外部因素主要决定了崩溃发生的时间、其被识别的难易程度以及……由于该区域受到特别关注，因此故障首先发生于此。虽然这类问题极其重要，但超出了本文的讨论范围。

Breakdown of the normal technical puzzle-solving activity is not, of course, the only ingredient of the astronomical crisis that faced Copernicus. An extended treatment would also discuss the social pressure for calendar reform, a pressure that made the puzzle of precession particularly urgent. In addition, a fuller account would consider medieval criticism of Aristotle, the rise of Renaissance Neoplatonism, and other significant historical elements besides. But technical breakdown would still remain the core of the crisis. In a mature science—and astronomy had become that in antiquity—external factors like those cited above are principally significant in determining the timing of breakdown, the ease with which it can be recognized, and the area in which, because it is given particular attention, the breakdown first occurs. Though immensely important, issues of that sort are out of bounds for this essay.

如果哥白尼革命的例子已经足够清晰，那么让我们转向第二个截然不同的例子：拉瓦锡燃烧氧理论出现之前的危机。18世纪70年代，诸多因素共同引发了化学领域的危机，历史学家们对这些因素的性质及其相对重要性尚未达成完全一致。但其中两个因素被普遍认为至关重要：气动化学的兴起和重量关系问题。气动化学的历史始于17世纪，当时空气泵被发明并应用于化学实验。在接下来的一个世纪里，化学家们利用空气泵和其他一些气动装置，逐渐认识到空气必然是化学反应中的活性成分。但除了少数例外——这些例外情况如此模棱两可，以至于它们可能根本算不上例外——化学家们仍然认为空气是唯一的气体。直到1756年约瑟夫·布莱克证明固定空气（CO₂ ）与普通空气始终可以区分开来，人们才意识到这两种气体样本的区别仅在于杂质的不同。7

If that much is clear in the case of the Copernican revolution, let us turn from it to a second and rather different example, the crisis that preceded the emergence of Lavoisier’s oxygen theory of combustion. In the 1770’s many factors combined to generate a crisis in chemistry, and historians are not altogether agreed about either their nature or their relative importance. But two of them are generally accepted as of first-rate significance: the rise of pneumatic chemistry and the question of weight relations. The history of the first begins in the seventeenth century with development of the air pump and its deployment in chemical experimentation. During the following century, using that pump and a number of other pneumatic devices, chemists came increasingly to realize that air must be an active ingredient in chemical reactions. But with a few exceptions—so equivocal that they may not be exceptions at all—chemists continued to believe that air was the only sort of gas. Until 1756, when Joseph Black showed that fixed air (CO2) was consistently distinguishable from normal air, two samples of gas were thought to be distinct only in their impurities.7

布莱克的工作之后，气体研究迅速发展，尤其以卡文迪什、普里斯特利和舍勒最为突出。他们共同开发了一系列新技术，能够区分不同的气体样本。从布莱克到舍勒，这些人都信奉燃素说，并经常将其应用于实验的设计和解释中。舍勒实际上是第一个通过一系列精心设计的实验（旨在消除热的燃素作用）制备出氧气的人。然而，他们的实验最终产生了种类繁多的气体样本和气体性质，这些气体性质如此复杂，以至于燃素说越来越难以应对实验室实验。尽管这些化学家都没有提出要放弃燃素说，但他们却无法始终如一地应用它。到18世纪70年代初拉瓦锡开始进行空气实验时，燃素理论的版本几乎和气动化学家的数量一样多。8这种理论版本的激增是危机的一个非常常见的征兆。哥白尼在他的序言中也抱怨过这一点。

After Black’s work the investigation of gases proceeded rapidly, most notably in the hands of Cavendish, Priestley, and Scheele, who together developed a number of new techniques capable of distinguishing one sample of gas from another. All these men, from Black through Scheele, believed in the phlogiston theory and often employed it in their design and interpretation of experiments. Scheele actually first produced oxygen by an elaborate chain of experiments designed to dephlogisticate heat. Yet the net result of their experiments was a variety of gas samples and gas properties so elaborate that the phlogiston theory proved increasingly little able to cope with laboratory experience. Though none of these chemists suggested that the theory should be replaced, they were unable to apply it consistently. By the time Lavoisier began his experiments on airs in the early 1770’s, there were almost as many versions of the phlogiston theory as there were pneumatic chemists.8 That proliferation of versions of a theory is a very usual symptom of crisis. In his preface, Copernicus complained of it as well.

然而，燃素理论在气体化学领域日益模糊且实用性下降，并非拉瓦锡面临危机的唯一根源。他还非常关注如何解释大多数物体在燃烧或烘烤时重量增加的现象，而这又是一个由来已久的问题。至少有一些伊斯兰化学家知道某些金属在烘烤时会增重。17世纪，一些研究者由此得出结论：烘烤的金属会从大气中吸收某些成分。但在17世纪，大多数化学家认为这个结论没有必要。如果化学反应能够改变物质的体积、颜色和质地，为什么不能改变其重量呢？重量并非总是被视为物质数量的度量。此外，烘烤增重一直被视为一种孤立的现象。大多数天然物体（例如木材）在烘烤时都会减轻重量，正如燃素理论后来所解释的那样。

The increasing vagueness and decreasing utility of the phlogiston theory for pneumatic chemistry were not, however, the only source of the crisis that confronted Lavoisier. He was also much concerned to explain the gain in weight that most bodies experience when burned or roasted, and that again is a problem with a long prehistory. At least a few Islamic chemists had known that some metals gain weight when roasted. In the seventeenth century several investigators had concluded from this same fact that a roasted metal takes up some ingredient from the atmosphere. But in the seventeenth century that conclusion seemed unnecessary to most chemists. If chemical reactions could alter the volume, color, and texture of the ingredients, why should they not alter weight as well? Weight was not always taken to be the measure of quantity of matter. Besides, weight-gain on roasting remained an isolated phenomenon. Most natural bodies (e.g., wood) lose weight on roasting as the phlogiston theory was later to say they should.

然而，在十八世纪，这些最初对重量增加问题的有效应对措施变得越来越难以维持。部分原因是天平日益成为标准的化学工具，部分原因是气相化学的发展使得保留反应的气态产物成为可能且具有必要性，化学家们发现越来越多的烘焙过程中重量增加的情况。与此同时，牛顿万有引力理论的逐渐被接受，促使化学家们坚持认为重量的增加必然意味着物质数量的增加。这些结论并没有导致燃素说被否定，因为……理论可以从很多方面进行调整。或许燃素具有负重量，或许在燃素离开被烘烤的物体时，有火粒子或其他物质进入其中。除此之外，还有其他解释。但即便重量增加的问题没有导致理论被否定，它也确实引发了越来越多的专门研究，而这个问题在这些研究中占据了重要地位。其中一篇题为《论燃素作为一种具有重量的物质，并根据它与物体结合时产生的重量变化进行分析》的文章于1772年初提交给法兰西科学院，而这一年以拉瓦锡向科学院秘书递交他著名的密封信函而告终。在那封信函写成之前，一个多年来一直萦绕在化学家心头的问题已经成为一个悬而未决的难题。9为了应对这个问题，人们提出了许多不同版本的燃素理论。就像气体化学的问题一样，重量增加的问题也使得人们越来越难以理解燃素理论的本质。尽管十八世纪化学范式仍被视为一种实用工具并受到信赖，但它正逐渐失去其独特地位。它所指导的研究越来越类似于范式出现之前其他竞争学派的研究，这也是危机带来的又一典型后果。

During the eighteenth century, however, these initially adequate responses to the problem of weight-gain became increasingly difficult to maintain. Partly because the balance was increasingly used as a standard chemical tool and partly because the development of pneumatic chemistry made it possible and desirable to retain the gaseous products of reactions, chemists discovered more and more cases in which weight-gain accompanied roasting. Simultaneously, the gradual assimilation of Newton’s gravitational theory led chemists to insist that gain in weight must mean gain in quantity of matter. Those conclusions did not result in rejection of the phlogiston theory, for that theory could be adjusted in many ways. Perhaps phlogiston had negative weight, or perhaps fire particles or something else entered the roasted body as phlogiston left it. There were other explanations besides. But if the problem of weight-gain did not lead to rejection, it did lead to an increasing number of special studies in which this problem bulked large. One of them, “On phlogiston considered as a substance with weight and [analyzed] in terms of the weight changes it produces in bodies with which it unites,” was read to the French Academy early in 1772, the year which closed with Lavoisier’s delivery of his famous sealed note to the Academy’s Secretary. Before that note was written a problem that had been at the edge of the chemist’s consciousness for many years had become an outstanding unsolved puzzle.9 Many different versions of the phlogiston theory were being elaborated to meet it. Like the problems of pneumatic chemistry, those of weight-gain were making it harder and harder to know what the phlogiston theory was. Though still believed and trusted as a working tool, a paradigm of eighteenth-century chemistry was gradually losing its unique status. Increasingly, the research it guided resembled that conducted under the competing schools of the pre-paradigm period, another typical effect of crisis.

现在，让我们来看第三个也是最后一个例子：十九世纪末物理学的危机，这场危机为相对论的出现铺平了道路。这场危机的根源可以追溯到十七世纪末，当时一些自然哲学家，尤其是莱布尼茨，批评牛顿保留了经典绝对空间概念的更新版本。10他们几乎（尽管始终未能完全）证明，绝对位置和绝对运动在牛顿的体系中根本没有任何作用；而且，他们确实成功地暗示了完全相对论的空间和运动概念后来将展现出的巨大美学吸引力。但是，他们的他们的批判纯粹基于逻辑。就像早期哥白尼学派批评亚里士多德关于地球稳定性的证明一样，他们根本没有想到向相对论体系的过渡会对观测结果产生影响。他们从未将自己的观点与将牛顿理论应用于自然界时出现的任何问题联系起来。结果，他们的观点随着他们的逝去在十八世纪初的几十年间消亡，直到十九世纪末才得以复兴，而此时它们与物理学实践的关系已截然不同。

Consider now, as a third and final example, the late nineteenth century crisis in physics that prepared the way for the emergence of relativity theory. One root of that crisis can be traced to the late seventeenth century when a number of natural philosophers, most notably Leibniz, criticized Newton’s retention of an updated version of the classic conception of absolute space.10 They were very nearly, though never quite, able to show that absolute positions and absolute motions were without any function at all in Newton’s system; and they did succeed in hinting at the considerable aesthetic appeal a fully relativistic conception of space and motion would later come to display. But their critique was purely logical. Like the early Copernicans who criticized Aristotle’s proofs of the earth’s stability, they did not dream that transition to a relativistic system could have observational consequences. At no point did they relate their views to any problems that arose when applying Newtonian theory to nature. As a result, their views died with them during the early decades of the eighteenth century to be resurrected only in the last decades of the nineteenth when they had a very different relation to the practice of physics.

与相对论空间哲学最终相关的技术问题，大约在1815年之后随着光波动理论的被接受而开始进入常规科学领域，尽管直到19世纪90年代才引发危机。如果光是受牛顿定律支配的机械以太中传播的波动，那么天体观测和地面实验都有可能探测到以太漂移。在天体观测中，只有光行差观测有望提供足够的精度来提供相关信息，因此，通过光行差测量来探测以太漂移成为常规研究中公认的问题。人们建造了许多专用设备来解决这个问题。然而，这些设备并未探测到任何可观测的漂移，因此，这个问题从实验学家和观测者转移到了理论学家身上。在19世纪中叶的几十年里，菲涅耳、斯托克斯等人提出了许多以太理论的解释，旨在说明为何无法观测到漂移。这些理论都假定运动的物体会带动一部分以太一起运动。而且，每一种理论都足以解释天体观测以及包括著名的迈克尔逊-莫雷实验在内的地面实验的否定结果。 11除了各种理论之间的冲突外，其他理论之间并无矛盾。由于缺乏相关的实验技术，这种冲突从未变得尖锐。

The technical problems to which a relativistic philosophy of space was ultimately to be related began to enter normal science with the acceptance of the wave theory of light after about 1815, though they evoked no crisis until the 1890’s. If light is wave motion propagated in a mechanical ether governed by Newton’s Laws, then both celestial observation and terrestrial experiment become potentially capable of detecting drift through the ether. Of the celestial observations, only those of aberration promised sufficient accuracy to provide relevant information, and the detection of ether-drift by aberration measurements therefore became a recognized problem for normal research. Much special equipment was built to resolve it. That equipment, however, detected no observable drift, and the problem was therefore transferred from the experimentalists and observers to the theoreticians. During the central decades of the century Fresnel, Stokes, and others devised numerous articulations of the ether theory designed to explain the failure to observe drift. Each of these articulations assumed that a moving body drags some fraction of the ether with it. And each was sufficiently successful to explain the negative results not only of celestial observation but also of terrestrial experimentation, including the famous experiment of Michelson and Morley.11 There was still no conflict excepting that between the various articulations. In the absence of relevant experimental techniques, that conflict never became acute.

随着人们逐渐接受这一点，情况再次发生了变化。麦克斯韦的电磁理论兴起于十九世纪最后二十年。麦克斯韦本人是一位牛顿主义者，他认为光和电磁现象普遍源于机械以太粒子的位移变化。他早期版本的电磁理论直接运用了他赋予这种介质的假想属性。这些属性在他最终的版本中被舍弃，但他仍然认为他的电磁理论与牛顿力学观点的某种表达方式相容。 12对他及其后继者而言，发展出一种合适的表达方式是一项挑战。然而，在实践中，正如科学发展史上屡次发生的那样，所需的表达方式被证明极其难以实现。正如哥白尼的天文设想，尽管其提出者本人充满乐观，却给现有的运动理论带来了日益严重的危机一样，麦克斯韦的理论，尽管源于牛顿，最终也给它所源自的范式带来了危机。13此外，这场危机最严重的地点正是我们刚才讨论的问题，即相对于以太的运动问题。

The situation changed again only with the gradual acceptance of Maxwell’s electromagnetic theory in the last two decades of the nineteenth century. Maxwell himself was a Newtonian who believed that light and electromagnetism in general were due to variable displacements of the particles of a mechanical ether. His earliest versions of a theory for electricity and magnetism made direct use of hypothetical properties with which he endowed this medium. These were dropped from his final version, but he still believed his electromagnetic theory compatible with some articulation of the Newtonian mechanical view.12 Developing a suitable articulation was a challenge for him and his successors. In practice, however, as has happened again and again in scientific development, the required articulation proved immensely difficult to produce. Just as Copernicus’ astronomical proposal, despite the optimism of its author, created an increasing crisis for existing theories of motion, so Maxwell’s theory, despite its Newtonian origin, ultimately produced a crisis for the paradigm from which it had sprung.13 Furthermore, the locus at which that crisis became most acute was provided by the problems we have just been considering, those of motion with respect to the ether.

麦克斯韦对运动物体电磁行为的讨论并未提及以太拖曳，因此将这种拖曳引入他的理论非常困难。结果，一系列旨在探测物体在以太中漂移的早期观测都出现了异常。1890 年之后，人们进行了大量的实验和理论尝试，试图探测物体相对于以太的运动，并将以太拖曳纳入麦克斯韦的理论。前者均以失败告终，尽管一些分析家认为他们的结果模棱两可。后者则取得了一些有希望的进展，特别是洛伦兹和菲茨杰拉德的成果，但同时也揭示了其他一些难题，最终导致了我们之前已经发现的那种相互竞争的理论的激增。危机的伴随物。14正是在这样的历史背景下，爱因斯坦的狭义相对论于 1905 年诞生。

Maxwell’s discussion of the electromagnetic behavior of bodies in motion had made no reference to ether drag, and it proved very difficult to introduce such drag into his theory. As a result, a whole series of earlier observations designed to detect drift through the ether became anomalous. The years after 1890 therefore witnessed a long series of attempts, both experimental and theoretical, to detect motion with respect to the ether and to work ether drag into Maxwell’s theory. The former were uniformly unsuccessful, though some analysts thought their results equivocal. The latter produced a number of promising starts, particularly those of Lorentz and Fitzgerald, but they also disclosed still other puzzles and finally resulted in just that proliferation of competing theories that we have previously found to be the concomitant of crisis.14 It is against that historical setting that Einstein’s special theory of relativity emerged in 1905.

这三个例子几乎完全具有代表性。在每个案例中，新理论都是在常规问题解决活动出现明显失败后才出现的。此外，除了哥白尼的情况（科学之外的因素在其中发挥了特别重要的作用）之外，这种崩溃以及作为其标志的理论激增，都发生在新理论提出前一二十年内。新理论似乎是对危机的直接回应。还需注意的是，尽管这可能并非完全典型，但导致崩溃的问题都属于早已被人们认识到的类型。此前常规科学的实践使人们有充分的理由认为这些问题已经解决或几乎已经解决，这有助于解释为什么当失败来临时，人们会感到如此强烈。面对一种新型问题，失败往往令人失望，但从不令人意外。问题和难题通常不会在第一次尝试中就迎刃而解。最后，这些例子还有一个共同的特点，这或许有助于有力地论证危机的作用：每个问题的解决方案都至少在相应科学领域尚未出现危机的时期就已被部分预见。如果没有危机，这些预期就会被忽视。

These three examples are almost entirely typical. In each case a novel theory emerged only after a pronounced failure in the normal problem-solving activity. Furthermore, except for the case of Copernicus in which factors external to science played a particularly large role, that breakdown and the proliferation of theories that is its sign occurred no more than a decade or two before the new theory’s enunciation. The novel theory seems a direct response to crisis. Note also, though this may not be quite so typical, that the problems with respect to which breakdown occurred were all of a type that had long been recognized. Previous practice of normal science had given every reason to consider them solved or all but solved, which helps to explain why the sense of failure, when it came, could be so acute. Failure with a new sort of problem is often disappointing but never surprising. Neither problems nor puzzles yield often to the first attack. Finally, these examples share another characteristic that may help to make the case for the role of crisis impressive: the solution to each of them had been at least partially anticipated during a period when there was no crisis in the corresponding science; and in the absence of crisis those anticipations had been ignored.

唯一完全预见日心说的，也是最著名的，是公元前三世纪阿里斯塔克斯对哥白尼日心说的预言。人们常说，如果希腊科学少一些演绎推理，少一些教条束缚，日心说的发展或许会比现在早十八个世纪。 15但这忽略了所有历史背景。阿里斯塔克斯提出日心说时，更为合理的地心说体系并没有任何日心说体系可能满足的需求。托勒密天文学的整个发展历程，包括其辉煌成就和衰落，都发生在公元前十八个世纪。在阿里斯塔克斯提出方案之后，并没有明显的理由认真对待阿里斯塔克斯的方案。即使是哥白尼更为详尽的方案，也并不比托勒密的体系更简单或更精确。正如我们将在下文更清楚地看到的，现有的观测测试并没有提供任何选择依据。在这种情况下，促使天文学家转向哥白尼（而不可能促使他们转向阿里斯塔克斯）的因素之一，正是当时公认的危机，而正是这场危机催生了创新。托勒密天文学未能解决自身的问题；是时候给竞争对手一个机会了。我们另外两个例子并没有提供类似的充分预见。但可以肯定的是，雷伊、胡克和梅奥在十七世纪提出的大气吸收燃烧理论未能得到足够的重视，原因之一就是它们没有触及当时科学实践中公认的难题。16十八、十九世纪的科学家们长期以来忽视牛顿的相对论批评者，这在很大程度上肯定是由于他们在对抗中遭遇了类似的失败。

The only complete anticipation is also the most famous, that of Copernicus by Aristarchus in the third century B.C. It is often said that if Greek science had been less deductive and less ridden by dogma, heliocentric astronomy might have begun its development eighteen centuries earlier than it did.15 But that is to ignore all historical context. When Aristarchus’ suggestion was made, the vastly more reasonable geocentric system had no needs that a heliocentric system might even conceivably have fulfilled. The whole development of Ptolemaic astronomy, both its triumphs and its breakdown, falls in the centuries after Aristarchus’ proposal. Besides, there were no obvious reasons for taking Aristarchus seriously. Even Copernicus’ more elaborate proposal was neither simpler nor more accurate than Ptolemy’s system. Available observational tests, as we shall see more clearly below, provided no basis for a choice between them. Under those circumstances, one of the factors that led astronomers to Copernicus (and one that could not have led them to Aristarchus) was the recognized crisis that had been responsible for innovation in the first place. Ptolemaic astronomy had failed to solve its problems; the time had come to give a competitor a chance. Our other two examples provide no similarly full anticipations. But surely one reason why the theories of combustion by absorption from the atmosphere—theories developed in the seventeenth century by Rey, Hooke, and Mayow—failed to get a sufficient hearing was that they made no contact with a recognized trouble spot in normal scientific practice.16 And the long neglect by eighteenth- and nineteenth-century scientists of Newton’s relativistic critics must largely have been due to a similar failure in confrontation.

科学哲学家们反复证明，对于给定的数据集合，总可以构建不止一种理论框架。科学史表明，尤其是在新范式发展的早期阶段，提出这些替代方案并非难事。然而，科学家们很少会去提出替代方案，除非是在科学发展的范式形成之前，或者在随后的发展过程中出现一些特殊情况。只要一个范式提供的工具能够持续解决它所定义的问题，科学就能通过自信地运用这些工具而发展得最快、最深入。原因显而易见。正如制造业一样，科学领域也存在这种情况——工具的更新换代是一种奢侈，应该只在真正需要的时候才进行。危机的意义在于，它预示着工具更新换代的时机已经到来。

Philosophers of science have repeatedly demonstrated that more than one theoretical construction can always be placed upon a given collection of data. History of science indicates that, particularly in the early developmental stages of a new paradigm, it is not even very difficult to invent such alternates. But that invention of alternates is just what scientists seldom undertake except during the pre-paradigm stage of their science’s development and at very special occasions during its subsequent evolution. So long as the tools a paradigm supplies continue to prove capable of solving the problems it defines, science moves fastest and penetrates most deeply through confident employment of those tools. The reason is clear. As in manufacture so in science—retooling is an extravagance to be reserved for the occasion that demands it. The significance of crises is the indication they provide that an occasion for retooling has arrived.

[ VIII ]

[VIII]

应对危机

The Response to Crisis

那么，让我们假设危机是新理论出现的必要前提，接下来探讨科学家如何应对危机。答案的一部分，既显而易见又至关重要，可以通过首先观察科学家在面对哪怕是严重且持续的异常现象时从未采取的做法来发现。尽管他们可能会开始动摇信念，并考虑其他替代方案，但他们不会放弃将他们引向危机的范式。也就是说，他们不会将异常现象视为反例，尽管在科学哲学的语境中，异常现象的确如此。这种概括在某种程度上仅仅是基于历史事实的陈述，其依据包括上文以及下文更详尽的论述。这些例子暗示了我们稍后对范式摒弃的探讨将更充分地揭示的内容：一旦某个科学理论成为范式，只有当存在替代理论时，它才会被宣告无效。迄今为止，科学发展史研究揭示的任何过程都与通过与自然直接比较来证伪的方法论刻板印象截然不同。这句话并非意味着科学家不会否定科学理论，也并非意味着经验和实验在他们否定理论的过程中不重要。但它的确意味着——这最终将成为一个核心要点——导致……的判断行为。科学家否定先前被接受的理论，绝不仅仅是将该理论与现实世界进行比较。否定一种范式的决定，总是同时意味着接受另一种范式，而做出这一决定的判断过程，则包含了将这两种范式与自然界以及彼此进行比较。

Let us then assume that crises are a necessary precondition for the emergence of novel theories and ask next how scientists respond to their existence. Part of the answer, as obvious as it is important, can be discovered by noting first what scientists never do when confronted by even severe and prolonged anomalies. Though they may begin to lose faith and then to consider alternatives, they do not renounce the paradigm that has led them into crisis. They do not, that is, treat anomalies as counterinstances, though in the vocabulary of philosophy of science that is what they are. In part this generalization is simply a statement from historic fact, based upon examples like those given above and, more extensively, below. These hint what our later examination of paradigm rejection will disclose more fully: once it has achieved the status of paradigm, a scientific theory is declared invalid only if an alternate candidate is available to take its place. No process yet disclosed by the historical study of scientific development at all resembles the methodological stereotype of falsification by direct comparison with nature. That remark does not mean that scientists do not reject scientific theories, or that experience and experiment are not essential to the process in which they do so. But it does mean—what will ultimately be a central point—that the act of judgment that leads scientists to reject a previously accepted theory is always based upon more than a comparison of that theory with the world. The decision to reject one paradigm is always simultaneously the decision to accept another, and the judgment leading to that decision involves the comparison of both paradigms with nature and with each other.

此外，还有第二个理由让人怀疑科学家是否真的因为遇到反常现象或反例而拒绝既有范式。在阐述这一理由的过程中，我的论证本身也将预示本文的另一个主要论点。上文所述的质疑理由纯粹基于事实；也就是说，它们本身就是对一种主流认识论理论的反例。因此，如果我的观点正确，它们充其量只能加剧一场危机，或者更准确地说，是强化一场已经存在的危机。这些理由本身既不能也不会证伪该哲学理论，因为该理论的捍卫者会像我们已经看到的科学家在面对反常现象时那样行事。他们会设计出大量的理论阐释和临时性的修改，以消除任何明显的冲突。事实上，许多相关的修改和限定已经存在于文献中。因此，如果这些认识论上的反例不仅仅是令人烦恼的小事，那是因为它们有助于催生一种新的、不同的科学分析方法，在这种方法中，它们不再是麻烦的根源。此外，如果我们稍后将在科学革命中观察到的典型模式适用于此，那么这些反常现象就不再仅仅是事实。从新的科学知识理论的角度来看，它们反而可能更像是同义反复，是对不可能以其他方式发生的状况的陈述。

There is, in addition, a second reason for doubting that scientists reject paradigms because confronted with anomalies or counterinstances. In developing it my argument will itself foreshadow another of this essay’s main theses. The reasons for doubt sketched above were purely factual; they were, that is, themselves counterinstances to a prevalent epistemological theory. As such, if my present point is correct, they can at best help to create a crisis or, more accurately, to reinforce one that is already very much in existence. By themselves they cannot and will not falsify that philosophical theory, for its defenders will do what we have already seen scientists doing when confronted by anomaly. They will devise numerous articulations and ad hoc modifications of their theory in order to eliminate any apparent conflict. Many of the relevant modifications and qualifications are, in fact, already in the literature. If, therefore, these epistemological counter-instances are to constitute more than a minor irritant, that will be because they help to permit the emergence of a new and different analysis of science within which they are no longer a source of trouble. Furthermore, if a typical pattern, which we shall later observe in scientific revolutions, is applicable here, these anomalies will then no longer seem to be simply facts. From within a new theory of scientific knowledge, they may instead seem very much like tautologies, statements of situations that could not conceivably have been otherwise.

例如，人们经常观察到，牛顿第二运动定律虽然历经几个世纪艰苦卓绝的事实和理论研究才得以确立，但对于那些笃信牛顿理论的人来说，它却像是一个纯粹的逻辑陈述，任何观察都无法反驳。1在第十节中，我们将看到化学定律在道尔顿之前，固定比例只是一个偶尔出现的、普遍性非常值得怀疑的实验发现；而道尔顿之后，它却成为了化合物定义中不可或缺的一部分，任何实验本身都无法推翻这一定义。类似的情况也会发生在“科学家面对异常或反例时不会否定既有范式”这一概括上。他们如果否定了范式，就无法继续保持科学家的身份。

It has often been observed, for example, that Newton’s second law of motion, though it took centuries of difficult factual and theoretical research to achieve, behaves for those committed to Newton’s theory very much like a purely logical statement that no amount of observation could refute.1 In Section X we shall see that the chemical law of fixed proportion, which before Dalton was an occasional experimental finding of very dubious generality, became after Dalton’s work an ingredient of a definition of chemical compound that no experimental work could by itself have upset. Something much like that will also happen to the generalization that scientists fail to reject paradigms when faced with anomalies or counterinstances. They could not do so and still remain scientists.

尽管历史不太可能记载他们的名字，但毫无疑问，有些人因为无法忍受危机而被逼到荒漠科学的境地。如同艺术家一样，富有创造力的科学家有时也必须能够在一个失衡的世界中生存——我曾在其他地方将这种必要性描述为科学研究中隐含的“本质张力”。2但我认为，这种为了其他职业而放弃科学的做法，是唯一一种仅凭反例本身就能导致的范式否定。一旦找到了观察自然的初始范式，就不存在任何范式缺失的研究。拒绝一种范式而不同时用另一种范式取而代之，就等于拒绝科学本身。这种行为反映的不是范式本身，而是人。他的同事们必然会将他视为“抱怨工具的木匠”。

Though history is unlikely to record their names, some men have undoubtedly been driven to desert science because of their inability to tolerate crisis. Like artists, creative scientists must occasionally be able to live in a world out of joint—elsewhere I have described that necessity as “the essential tension” implicit in scientific research.2 But that rejection of science in favor of another occupation is, I think, the only sort of paradigm rejection to which counterinstances by themselves can lead. Once a first paradigm through which to view nature has been found, there is no such thing as research in the absence of any paradigm. To reject one paradigm without simultaneously substituting another is to reject science itself. That act reflects not on the paradigm but on the man. Inevitably he will be seen by his colleagues as “the carpenter who blames his tools.”

同样的观点反过来也同样有效：不存在没有反例的研究。那么，是什么将常规科学与危机状态下的科学区分开来呢？当然不是前者不存在反例。恰恰相反，我们之前所说的构成常规科学的难题之所以存在，正是因为没有任何一种作为科学研究基础的范式能够完全解决其所有问题。极少数看似能够做到这一点的范式（例如几何光学）很快就不再产生任何研究问题，转而成为工程工具。除了那些纯粹的工具性范式之外，常规科学视为难题的每一个问题，从另一个角度来看，都可以被视为反例，从而成为危机的根源。哥白尼将托勒密的大多数后继者视为难题的问题，视为反例，这些问题体现在观察与理论的匹配上。拉瓦锡将普里斯特利视为已成功解决的难题，即燃素理论的阐述，视为反例。爱因斯坦将洛伦兹、菲茨杰拉德等人视为难题的问题，即牛顿和麦克斯韦理论的阐述，视为反例。此外，危机的存在本身并不能将难题转化为反例。两者之间并没有如此泾渭分明的界限。相反，危机通过范式的多样化，打破了常规解谜的规则，最终使得新的范式得以出现。我认为只有两种可能：要么没有任何科学理论会遇到反例，要么所有科学理论都会在任何时候遇到反例。

The same point can be made at least equally effectively in reverse: there is no such thing as research without counterinstances. For what is it that differentiates normal science from science in a crisis state? Not, surely, that the former confronts no counterinstances. On the contrary, what we previously called the puzzles that constitute normal science exist only because no paradigm that provides a basis for scientific research ever completely resolves all its problems. The very few that have ever seemed to do so (e.g., geometric optics) have shortly ceased to yield research problems at all and have instead become tools for engineering. Excepting those that are exclusively instrumental, every problem that normal science sees as a puzzle can be seen, from another viewpoint, as a counterinstance and thus as a source of crisis. Copernicus saw as counterinstances what most of Ptolemy’s other successors had seen as puzzles in the match between observation and theory. Lavoisier saw as a counterinstance what Priestley had seen as a successfully solved puzzle in the articulation of the phlogiston theory. And Einstein saw as counterinstances what Lorentz, Fitzgerald, and others had seen as puzzles in the articulation of Newton’s and Maxwell’s theories. Furthermore, even the existence of crisis does not by itself transform a puzzle into a counterinstance. There is no such sharp dividing line. Instead, by proliferating versions of the paradigm, crisis loosens the rules of normal puzzle-solving in ways that ultimately permit a new paradigm to emerge. There are, I think, only two alternatives: either no scientific theory ever confronts a counterinstance, or all such theories confront counterinstances at all times.

情况怎会呈现其他面貌？这个问题必然会引向对哲学的历史和批判性阐释，而这些话题在此不予讨论。但我们至少可以指出两个原因，说明为何科学似乎如此恰当地阐释了“真假由陈述与事实的比对唯一且明确地决定”这一概括。常规科学确实并且必须不断努力使理论与事实更加吻合，而这种努力很容易被视为检验或寻求证实或证伪。然而，科学的目标是解决一个难题，而该难题的存在本身就以范式的有效性为前提。未能找到解决方案只会损害科学家的声誉，而不会损害理论本身。在此，这句谚语比上文更适用：“拙匠怪工具。”此外，科学教学将理论讨论与其典型应用相结合的方式，也强化了一种主要来源于其他来源的证实性理论。只要稍有理由，阅读科学文本的人就很容易把应用实例当作理论的证据，当作理论应该被相信的理由。但理科学生接受理论是基于老师和文本的权威，而不是基于证据。还有其他选择吗？他们真的具备这种能力吗？或者说，他们具备什么能力？教材中列举的应用案例并非作为证据，而是因为学习这些案例是理解当前实践基础范式的一部分。如果将应用案例作为证据，那么教材未能提出其他解释或探讨科学家尚未找到范式解决方案的问题，就会使作者被认定为存在极端偏见。这种指责毫无根据。

How can the situation have seemed otherwise? That question necessarily leads to the historical and critical elucidation of philosophy, and those topics are here barred. But we can at least note two reasons why science has seemed to provide so apt an illustration of the generalization that truth and falsity are uniquely and unequivocally determined by the confrontation of statement with fact. Normal science does and must continually strive to bring theory and fact into closer agreement, and that activity can easily be seen as testing or as a search for confirmation or falsification. Instead, its object is to solve a puzzle for whose very existence the validity of the paradigm must be assumed. Failure to achieve a solution discredits only the scientist and not the theory. Here, even more than above, the proverb applies: “It is a poor carpenter who blames his tools.” In addition, the manner in which science pedagogy entangles discussion of a theory with remarks on its exemplary applications has helped to reinforce a confirmation-theory drawn predominantly from other sources. Given the slightest reason for doing so, the man who reads a science text can easily take the applications to be the evidence for the theory, the reasons why it ought to be believed. But science students accept theories on the authority of teacher and text, not because of evidence. What alternatives have they, or what competence? The applications given in texts are not there as evidence but because learning them is part of learning the paradigm at the base of current practice. If applications were set forth as evidence, then the very failure of texts to suggest alternative interpretations or to discuss problems for which scientists have failed to produce paradigm solutions would convict their authors of extreme bias. There is not the slightest reason for such an indictment.

那么，回到最初的问题，科学家们如何应对理论与自然之间出现的异常现象呢？刚才的论述表明，即使这种差异比该理论在其他应用中遇到的差异大得多，也不一定会引起特别强烈的反应。差异总是存在的。即使是最顽固的差异，最终通常也会通过常规方法得到解决。科学家们常常愿意等待，尤其是在该领域其他方面还有许多问题需要研究的情况下。例如，我们已经提到，在牛顿最初计算后的六十年里，月球近地点运动的预测值始终只有观测值的一半。当欧洲最优秀的数学物理学家们继续徒劳地试图解决这个众所周知的差异时，偶尔会有人提出修改牛顿平方反比定律。但没有人认真对待这些提议，而实践证明，这种对重大异常现象的耐心是合理的。 1750年，克莱罗证明，只有应用上的数学推导出现了错误，牛顿理论依然有效。3即使在看似不可能出现纯粹错误的情况下（或许是因为所涉及的数学较为简单，或是属于人们熟知且在其他领域已取得成功的数学类型），持续存在的、已被认可的异常现象也并非总是会引发危机。由于牛顿理论的预测与声速和水星运动之间存在长期公认的差异，因此没有人认真质疑牛顿理论。第一个差异最终出人意料地被一项原本出于截然不同目的而进行的热学实验所解决；第二个差异则随着一般理论的出现而消失。相对论是在一场它并未参与制造的危机之后出现的。4显然，两者都不够根本，不足以引发伴随危机而来的不安情绪。它们可以被视为反例，仍然可以搁置起来留待以后研究。

How, then, to return to the initial question, do scientists respond to the awareness of an anomaly in the fit between theory and nature? What has just been said indicates that even a discrepancy unaccountably larger than that experienced in other applications of the theory need not draw any very profound response. There are always some discrepancies. Even the most stubborn ones usually respond at last to normal practice. Very often scientists are willing to wait, particularly if there are many problems available in other parts of the field. We have already noted, for example, that during the sixty years after Newton’s original computation, the predicted motion of the moon’s perigee remained only half of that observed. As Europe’s best mathematical physicists continued to wrestle unsuccessfully with the well-known discrepancy, there were occasional proposals for a modification of Newton’s inverse square law. But no one took these proposals very seriously, and in practice this patience with a major anomaly proved justified. Clairaut in 1750 was able to show that only the mathematics of the application had been wrong and that Newtonian theory could stand as before.3 Even in cases where no mere mistake seems quite possible (perhaps because the mathematics involved is simpler or of a familiar and elsewhere successful sort), persistent and recognized anomaly does not always induce crisis. No one seriously questioned Newtonian theory because of the long-recognized discrepancies between predictions from that theory and both the speed of sound and the motion of Mercury. The first discrepancy was ultimately and quite unexpectedly resolved by experiments on heat undertaken for a very different purpose; the second vanished with the general theory of relativity after a crisis that it had had no role in creating.4 Apparently neither had seemed sufficiently fundamental to evoke the malaise that goes with crisis. They could be recognized as counterinstances and still be set aside for later work.

由此可见，如果某种异常现象要引发危机，它通常不仅仅是异常现象本身。范式与自然之间的契合点总是存在一些问题；大多数问题迟早都会得到解决，而且往往是通过一些无法预见的机制实现的。如果科学家停下来仔细研究他所发现的每一个异常现象，那么他很少能取得什么实质性的成果。因此，我们必须探究是什么让某种异常现象值得我们集中精力进行审视，而对于这个问题，或许没有一个完全普遍适用的答案。我们已经考察过的案例具有代表性，但并不具有指导意义。有时，某种异常现象会清晰地质疑范式中明确而根本的概括，就像以太拖曳问题对那些接受麦克斯韦理论的人所造成的影响一样。或者，就像哥白尼革命那样，即使某种异常现象本身没有明显的根本意义，但如果它所阻碍的应用具有特殊的实际意义，例如在历法设计和占星术领域，那么它也可能引发危机。或者，正如十八世纪化学领域的情况一样，常规科学的发展可能会将原本只是令人烦恼的异常现象转变为危机之源：气动化学技术发展之后，重量关系问题的地位就截然不同了。想必还有其他一些因素会使异常现象变得尤为紧迫，而且通常是几种因素共同作用的结果。例如，我们已经指出，哥白尼面临的危机之一，正是天文学家们长期以来一直未能成功消除托勒密体系中残留的偏差。

It follows that if an anomaly is to evoke crisis, it must usually be more than just an anomaly. There are always difficulties somewhere in the paradigm-nature fit; most of them are set right sooner or later, often by processes that could not have been foreseen. The scientist who pauses to examine every anomaly he notes will seldom get significant work done. We therefore have to ask what it is that makes an anomaly seem worth concerted scrutiny, and to that question there is probably no fully general answer. The cases we have already examined are characteristic but scarcely prescriptive. Sometimes an anomaly will clearly call into question explicit and fundamental generalizations of the paradigm, as the problem of ether drag did for those who accepted Maxwell’s theory. Or, as in the Copernican revolution, an anomaly without apparent fundamental import may evoke crisis if the applications that it inhibits have a particular practical importance, in this case for calendar design and astrology. Or, as in eighteenth-century chemistry, the development of normal science may transform an anomaly that had previously been only a vexation into a source of crisis: the problem of weight relations had a very different status after the evolution of pneumatic-chemical techniques. Presumably there are still other circumstances that can make an anomaly particularly pressing, and ordinarily several of these will combine. We have already noted, for example, that one source of the crisis that confronted Copernicus was the mere length of time during which astronomers had wrestled unsuccessfully with the reduction of the residual discrepancies in Ptolemy’s system.

当由于这些原因或其他类似原因，某种异常现象不再仅仅是常规科学中的又一个难题时，这种转变就可能发生。危机与非凡科学的交汇点已经出现。如今，这一异常现象本身也逐渐被业界普遍认可。越来越多的杰出学者开始关注它。如果它继续顽固不化（通常情况下不会），那么许多学者可能会将解决这一问题视为其学科的研究课题。对他们而言，这个领域将不再像以前那样面目全非。这种变化的部分原因在于科学审视的新焦点。而更重要的变化来源在于，针对这一问题开展的集中研究催生了众多局部解决方案，这些方案的性质各不相同。早期针对这一顽固问题的尝试大多遵循范式规则。但随着顽固不化的持续，越来越多的尝试都涉及对范式的某种程度上的或大或小的阐释，这些阐释各有不同，都取得了一定的成功，但没有一种能够被群体接受为范式。随着各种不同表述的激增（它们越来越常被描述为临时调整），常规科学的规则变得日益模糊。尽管范式依然存在，但很少有实践者对其内容达成完全一致。甚至连以往已解决问题的标准方案也受到了质疑。

When, for these reasons or others like them, an anomaly comes to seem more than just another puzzle of normal science, the transition to crisis and to extraordinary science has begun. The anomaly itself now comes to be more generally recognized as such by the profession. More and more attention is devoted to it by more and more of the field’s most eminent men. If it still continues to resist, as it usually does not, many of them may come to view its resolution as the subject matter of their discipline. For them the field will no longer look quite the same as it had earlier. Part of its different appearance results simply from the new fixation point of scientific scrutiny. An even more important source of change is the divergent nature of the numerous partial solutions that concerted attention to the problem has made available. The early attacks upon the resistant problem will have followed the paradigm rules quite closely. But with continuing resistance, more and more of the attacks upon it will have involved some minor or not so minor articulation of the paradigm, no two of them quite alike, each partially successful, but none sufficiently so to be accepted as paradigm by the group. Through this proliferation of divergent articulations (more and more frequently they will come to be described as ad hoc adjustments), the rules of normal science become increasingly blurred. Though there still is a paradigm, few practitioners prove to be entirely agreed about what it is. Even formerly standard solutions of solved problems are called in question.

当情况严重时，相关科学家有时也会意识到这一点。哥白尼抱怨说，在他那个时代，天文学家在这些（天文）研究中如此“前后矛盾……以至于他们甚至无法解释或观察到季节长度的恒定性”。他继续说道：“对他们来说，就好像一位艺术家从不同的模特身上收集手、脚、头和其他部位来创作他的画作，每个部分都画得非常精美，但却与同一个身体毫无关联，由于它们彼此之间完全不匹配，最终得到的将是怪物而不是人。” 5 爱因斯坦由于当时的语言习惯限制，只能使用较为朴素的语言，他只写道：“就好像脚下的土地被抽走了，看不到任何坚实的基础。”任何地方，都可以以此为基础进行建设。” 6在海森堡关于矩阵力学的论文为新的量子理论指明方向之前的几个月，沃尔夫冈·泡利写信给一位朋友说：“目前物理学又变得非常混乱。无论如何，它对我来说太难了，我真希望自己是个电影喜剧演员之类的，从来没听说过物理学。”如果将这段话与泡利不到五个月后的话进行对比，这段话就显得格外令人印象深刻了：“海森堡的这种力学再次给了我希望和生活的乐趣。当然，它并没有提供谜题的答案，但我相信我们又可以继续前进了。” 7

When acute, this situation is sometimes recognized by the scientists involved. Copernicus complained that in his day astronomers were so “inconsistent in these [astronomical] investigations . . . that they cannot even explain or observe the constant length of the seasonal year.” “With them,” he continued, “it is as though an artist were to gather the hands, feet, head and other members for his images from diverse models, each part excellently drawn, but not related to a single body, and since they in no way match each other, the result would be monster rather than man.”5 Einstein, restricted by current usage to less florid language, wrote only, “It was as if the ground had been pulled out from under one, with no firm foundation to be seen anywhere, upon which one could have built.”6 And Wolfgang Pauli, in the months before Heisenberg’s paper on matrix mechanics pointed the way to a new quantum theory, wrote to a friend, “At the moment physics is again terribly confused. In any case, it is too difficult for me, and I wish I had been a movie comedian or something of the sort and had never heard of physics.” That testimony is particularly impressive if contrasted with Pauli’s words less than five months later: “Heisenberg’s type of mechanics has again given me hope and joy in life. To be sure it does not supply the solution to the riddle, but I believe it is again possible to march forward.”7

对崩溃的明确认知极为罕见，但危机的影响并非完全取决于人们对它的有意识认知。这些影响究竟是什么呢？似乎只有两种是普遍存在的。所有危机都始于范式的模糊化以及随之而来的常规研究规则的放松。在这方面，危机期间的研究与范式出现之前的研究非常相似，只是前者差异的程度更小，也更清晰。所有危机的终结方式大致分为三种。有时，尽管那些认为危机标志着现有范式终结的人感到绝望，但常规科学最终证明能够应对引发危机的问题。有时，即使是看似激进的新方法也无法解决问题。这时，科学家们可能会得出结论：在他们研究领域的现有条件下，这个问题无法得到解决。于是，问题被贴上标签，并被搁置，留给拥有更先进工具的后代。最后，也是我们最关心的情况，危机可能以新范式的出现以及随之而来的对其接受度的争夺而告终。最后一种结束方式将在后面的章节中详细讨论，但我们必须预先透露一些将在后面章节中提及的内容。为了完成关于危机状态的演变和剖析的这些论述。

Such explicit recognitions of breakdown are extremely rare, but the effects of crisis do not entirely depend upon its conscious recognition. What can we say these effects are? Only two of them seem to be universal. All crises begin with the blurring of a paradigm and the consequent loosening of the rules for normal research. In this respect research during crisis very much resembles research during the pre-paradigm period, except that in the former the locus of difference is both smaller and more clearly defined. And all crises close in one of three ways. Sometimes normal science ultimately proves able to handle the crisis-provoking problem despite the despair of those who have seen it as the end of an existing paradigm. On other occasions the problem resists even apparently radical new approaches. Then scientists may conclude that no solution will be forthcoming in the present state of their field. The problem is labelled and set aside for a future generation with more developed tools. Or, finally, the case that will most concern us here, a crisis may end with the emergence of a new candidate for paradigm and with the ensuing battle over its acceptance. This last mode of closure will be considered at length in later sections, but we must anticipate a bit of what will be said there in order to complete these remarks about the evolution and anatomy of the crisis state.

从危机中的范式过渡到能够孕育新的常规科学传统的全新范式，远非一个累积过程，也并非通过对旧范式的阐述或扩展就能实现。相反，这是一个基于全新基本原理对该领域进行重构的过程，这种重构改变了该领域一些最基本的理论概括，以及许多范式方法和应用。在过渡时期，新旧范式能够解决的问题之间将存在大量但永远不会完全重叠。但解决这些问题的模式也将存在决定性的差异。当过渡完成时，该学科将改变其对该领域、方法和目标的看法。一位富有洞察力的历史学家最近在审视一个经典的科学范式转变案例时，将其描述为“捡起棍子的另一端”，这一过程涉及“处理与之前相同的数据，但通过赋予它们不同的框架，将它们置于一个全新的相互关系系统中”。8其他一些注意到科学进步这一方面的学者强调，它与视觉格式塔的变化非常相似：纸上的痕迹最初被视为鸟，现在可能被视为羚羊，反之亦然。9这种类比可能会产生误导。科学家并非将某物视为其他事物；相反，他们只是观察它本身。我们已经探讨过，如果说普里斯特利将氧气视为脱燃素的空气，会产生哪些问题。此外，科学家并没有保留格式塔主体在不同观察方式之间自由切换的权利。尽管如此，格式塔的转换，尤其是在今天如此常见的情况下，仍然是全面范式转变的一个有用的基本原型。

The transition from a paradigm in crisis to a new one from which a new tradition of normal science can emerge is far from a cumulative process, one achieved by an articulation or extension of the old paradigm. Rather it is a reconstruction of the field from new fundamentals, a reconstruction that changes some of the field’s most elementary theoretical generalizations as well as many of its paradigm methods and applications. During the transition period there will be a large but never complete overlap between the problems that can be solved by the old and by the new paradigm. But there will also be a decisive difference in the modes of solution. When the transition is complete, the profession will have changed its view of the field, its methods, and its goals. One perceptive historian, viewing a classic case of a science’s re-orientation by paradigm change, recently described it as “picking up the other end of the stick,” a process that involves “handling the same bundle of data as before, but placing them in a new system of relations with one another by giving them a different framework.”8 Others who have noted this aspect of scientific advance have emphasized its similarity to a change in visual gestalt: the marks on paper that were first seen as a bird are now seen as an antelope, or vice versa.9 That parallel can be misleading. Scientists do not see something as something else; instead, they simply see it. We have already examined some of the problems created by saying that Priestley saw oxygen as dephlogisticated air. In addition, the scientist does not preserve the gestalt subject’s freedom to switch back and forth between ways of seeing. Nevertheless, the switch of gestalt, particularly because it is today so familiar, is a useful elementary prototype for what occurs in full-scale paradigm shift.

先前的预期或许有助于我们认识到危机是新理论出现的恰当序幕，尤其因为我们已经考察过同一过程的小规模版本。讨论新发现的出现。仅仅因为新理论的出现打破了某种科学实践传统，并引入了一种遵循不同规则、在不同的论述体系中进行的新传统，就可能只有在人们感到原有传统严重偏离正轨时才会发生。然而，这番话仅仅是对危机状态探究的序曲，而且不幸的是，它引出的问题对心理学家的能力要求甚至高于历史学家。非凡的研究究竟是什么样的？异常现象如何被转化为规律？当科学家们仅仅意识到在他们受过的训练无法应对的层面上出现了根本性的错误时，他们该如何应对？这些问题需要更深入的研究，而且研究不应局限于历史层面。接下来的内容必然会比之前的内容更加初步，也更加不完整。

The preceding anticipation may help us recognize crisis as an appropriate prelude to the emergence of new theories, particularly since we have already examined a small-scale version of the same process in discussing the emergence of discoveries. Just because the emergence of a new theory breaks with one tradition of scientific practice and introduces a new one conducted under different rules and within a different universe of discourse, it is likely to occur only when the first tradition is felt to have gone badly astray. That remark is, however, no more than a prelude to the investigation of the crisis-state, and, unfortunately, the questions to which it leads demand the competence of the psychologist even more than that of the historian. What is extraordinary research like? How is anomaly made lawlike? How do scientists proceed when aware only that something has gone fundamentally wrong at a level with which their training has not equipped them to deal? Those questions need far more investigation, and it ought not all be historical. What follows will necessarily be more tentative and less complete than what has gone before.

通常，新的范式会在危机尚未广泛发展或被明确认知之前，至少在萌芽阶段就已经出现。拉瓦锡的著作便是一个例证。在他向法兰西科学院提交密封报告时，距离燃素论中重量关系的首次全面研究还不到一年，而普里斯特利的出版物也尚未揭示气动化学危机的全部程度。再者，托马斯·杨关于光波动理论的首次论述，正值光学领域危机萌芽的早期阶段。这场危机原本几乎不会引起注意，但杨并未参与其中，却在短短十年内演变成一场国际科学丑闻。在这些案例中，我们只能说，范式的轻微崩溃以及其规则在常规科学中的首次模糊化，就足以促使人们以全新的视角看待该领域。从最初意识到问题到认识到可行的替代方案之间，必然存在着一种无意识的过程。

Often a new paradigm emerges, at least in embryo, before a crisis has developed far or been explicitly recognized. Lavoisier’s work provides a case in point. His sealed note was deposited with the French Academy less than a year after the first thorough study of weight relations in the phlogiston theory and before Priestley’s publications had revealed the full extent of the crisis in pneumatic chemistry. Or again, Thomas Young’s first accounts of the wave theory of light appeared at a very early stage of a developing crisis in optics, one that would be almost unnoticeable except that, with no assistance from Young, it had grown to an international scientific scandal within a decade of the time he first wrote. In cases like these one can say only that a minor breakdown of the paradigm and the very first blurring of its rules for normal science were sufficient to induce in someone a new way of looking at the field. What intervened between the first sense of trouble and the recognition of an available alternate must have been largely unconscious.

然而，在其他一些案例中——例如哥白尼、爱因斯坦以及当代核理论——从人们首次意识到理论崩溃到新范式的出现之间，往往间隔相当长的时间。当这种情况发生时，历史学家或许能够捕捉到一些非凡科学的蛛丝马迹。面对一个公认的……理论上的根本性反常现象，科学家的首要任务往往是更精确地将其分离出来并赋予其结构。尽管他意识到这些反常现象不可能完全正确，但他仍会比以往任何时候都更加努力地挑战常规科学的规则，以探寻在难题领域，这些规则究竟能在何处、在多大程度上发挥作用。与此同时，他还会寻求放大这种反常现象的方法，使其比以往在那些结果被认为可以预先知晓的实验中展现的更加引人注目，或许也更具启发性。在后一种努力中，与其他任何后范式科学发展阶段相比，他几乎更像我们通常印象中的科学家形象。首先，他常常看起来像一个漫无目的地探索的人，尝试各种实验只是为了看看会发生什么，寻找一种他无法完全猜透其本质的效应。同时，由于任何实验都离不开某种理论，处于危机中的科学家会不断尝试提出推测性的理论，如果成功，这些理论可能会揭示通往新范式的道路；如果失败，这些理论也可以相对容易地被放弃。

In other cases, however—those of Copernicus, Einstein, and contemporary nuclear theory, for example—considerable time elapses between the first consciousness of breakdown and the emergence of a new paradigm. When that occurs, the historian may capture at least a few hints of what extraordinary science is like. Faced with an admittedly fundamental anomaly in theory, the scientist’s first effort will often be to isolate it more precisely and to give it structure. Though now aware that they cannot be quite right, he will push the rules of normal science harder than ever to see, in the area of difficulty, just where and how far they can be made to work. Simultaneously he will seek for ways of magnifying the breakdown, of making it more striking and perhaps also more suggestive than it had been when displayed in experiments the outcome of which was thought to be known in advance. And in the latter effort, more than in any other part of the post-paradigm development of science, he will look almost like our most prevalent image of the scientist. He will, in the first place, often seem a man searching at random, trying experiments just to see what will happen, looking for an effect whose nature he cannot quite guess. Simultaneously, since no experiment can be conceived without some sort of theory, the scientist in crisis will constantly try to generate speculative theories that, if successful, may disclose the road to a new paradigm and, if unsuccessful, can be surrendered with relative ease.

开普勒对火星运动的长期研究以及普里斯特利对新气体激增的反应，都是在意识到异常现象后产生的更为随机的研究的经典范例。 10但或许最好的例证来自当代场论和基本粒子研究。如果没有一场危机迫使人们去探究常规科学规则的极限，那么探测中微子所需的巨大努力是否还显得合理？或者，如果这些规则没有在某个未公开的时刻明显失效，那么宇称不守恒这一激进假设是否还会被提出或检验？与过去十年物理学中的许多其他研究一样，这些实验在某种程度上是为了定位和确定一系列仍然弥散的异常现象的来源。

Kepler’s account of his prolonged struggle with the motion of Mars and Priestley’s description of his response to the proliferation of new gases provide classic examples of the more random sort of research produced by the awareness of anomaly.10 But probably the best illustrations of all come from contemporary research in field theory and on fundamental particles. In the absence of a crisis that made it necessary to see just how far the rules of normal science could stretch, would the immense effort required to detect the neutrino have seemed justified? Or, if the rules had not obviously broken down at some undisclosed point, would the radical hypothesis of parity non-conservation have been either suggested or tested?
