Like much other research in physics during the past decade, these experiments were in part attempts to localize and define the source of a still diffuse set of anomalies.

这种非凡的研究往往伴随着另一种研究，尽管并非总是如此。我认为，尤其是在公认的危机时期，科学家们才会转向哲学分析，将其作为解开各自领域谜题的工具。科学家们通常不需要或不想成为哲学家。事实上，常规科学通常与创造性哲学保持距离，这或许有其合理之处。如果常规研究工作能够以范式为模型进行，那么规则和假设就无需明确阐述。我们在第五节中指出，哲学分析所寻求的全部规则甚至可能并不存在。但这并不意味着，探寻假设（即使是对不存在的假设）不能成为削弱某种传统对思维的束缚、并为新传统的建立奠定基础的有效途径。十七世纪牛顿物理学的出现，以及二十世纪相对论和量子力学的兴起，都伴随着对当时研究传统的根本性哲学分析，这绝非偶然。 11同样，在这两个时期，所谓的思想实验在研究进展中发挥了如此关键的作用，也绝非偶然。正如我在其他文章中所论证的，伽利略、爱因斯坦、玻尔等人的著作中大量出现的分析性思想实验，其目的在于以一种在实验室中无法企及的清晰度，将旧范式暴露在现有知识面前，从而揭示危机的根源。 12

This sort of extraordinary research is often, though by no means generally, accompanied by another. It is, I think, particularly in periods of acknowledged crisis that scientists have turned to philosophical analysis as a device for unlocking the riddles of their field. Scientists have not generally needed or wanted to be philosophers. Indeed, normal science usually holds creative philosophy at arm’s’length, and probably for good reasons. To the extent that normal research work can be conducted by using the paradigm as a model, rules and assumptions need not be made explicit. In Section V we noted that the full set of rules sought by philosophical analysis need not even exist. But that is not to say that the search for assumptions (even for non-existent ones) cannot be an effective way to weaken the grip of a tradition upon the mind and to suggest the basis for a new one. It is no accident that the emergence of Newtonian physics in the seventeenth century and of relativity and quantum mechanics in the twentieth should have been both preceded and accompanied by fundamental philosophical analyses of the contemporary research tradition.11 Nor is it an accident that in both these periods the so-called thought experiment should have played so critical a role in the progress of research. As I have shown elsewhere, the analytical thought experimentation that bulks so large in the writings of Galileo, Einstein, Bohr, and others is perfectly calculated to expose the old paradigm to existing knowledge in ways that isolate the root of crisis with a clarity unattainable in the laboratory.12

单独或联合运用这些非常规手段，可能会带来另一件事。通过将科学注意力集中于某个特定的问题领域，并培养科学家识别实验异常现象的能力，危机往往会催生新的发现。我们已经注意到，对危机的认知使拉瓦锡对氧气的研究区别于普里斯特利；而且，氧气并非普里斯特利的研究中，那些意识到异常现象的化学家们发现的唯一一种新气体。此外，在光的波动理论出现前后，新的光学发现也迅速积累。有些发现，例如反射偏振，是集中精力研究某个棘手领域所带来的偶然结果。（发现偏振的马吕斯当时正着手撰写科学院关于双折射的获奖论文，而众所周知，双折射的研究尚不尽如人意。）另一些发现，例如圆形圆盘阴影中心的光斑，则是新假设的预测，而这些预测的成功也促使该假设成为后世研究的范式。还有一些现象，例如划痕和厚板的颜色，虽然以前经常被观察到，也偶尔被提及，但就像普里斯特利的氧气一样，它们被归入众所周知的现象之中，以至于人们无法真正认识到它们的本质。 13类似的情况也适用于自1895年左右量子力学兴起以来不断涌现的诸多发现。

With the deployment, singly or together, of these extraordinary procedures, one other thing may occur. By concentrating scientific attention upon a narrow area of trouble and by preparing the scientific mind to recognize experimental anomalies for what they are, crisis often proliferates new discoveries. We have already noted how the awareness of crisis distinguishes Lavoisier’s work on oxygen from Priestley’s; and oxygen was not the only new gas that the chemists aware of anomaly were able to discover in Priestley’s work. Or again, new optical discoveries accumulated rapidly just before and during the emergence of the wave theory of light. Some, like polarization by reflection, were a result of the accidents that concentrated work in an area of trouble makes likely. (Malus, who made the discovery, was just starting work for the Academy’s prize essay on double refraction, a subject widely known to be in an unsatisfactory state.) Others, like the light spot at the center of the shadow of a circular disk, were predictions from the new hypothesis, ones whose success helped to transform it to a paradigm for later work. And still others, like the colors of scratches and of thick plates, were effects that had often been seen and occasionally remarked before, but that, like Priestley’s oxygen, had been assimilated to well-known effects in ways that prevented their being seen for what they were.13 A similar account could be given of the multiple discoveries that, from about 1895, were a constant concomitant of the emergence of quantum mechanics.

非凡的研究必然还会产生其他表现形式和影响，但在这个领域，我们才刚刚开始探索那些需要提出的问题。然而，或许此时此刻，我们已无需再做更多。前文已足以说明，危机如何既打破了固有的成见，又提供了必要的渐进式数据，从而促成根本性的范式转变。有时，新范式的雏形就预示在非凡的研究赋予异常现象的结构之中。爱因斯坦曾写道，在他找到经典力学的替代品之前，他就能看出黑体辐射、光电效应和比热等已知异常现象之间的相互关系。 14但更多时候，并不存在这样的结构。这种新范式并非事先就能被有意识地预见。相反，新范式，或者足以让人日后清晰阐述的线索，往往是突然涌现的，有时甚至在深夜，在一位深陷危机之中的人的脑海中。至于最终阶段的本质——一个人如何发明（或发现自己发明了）一种新的方法来整理已经收集起来的数据——在此必须保持神秘，而且可能永远如此。我们在此仅需指出一点。几乎所有做出这些根本性新范式发明的人，要么非常年轻，要么对他们所改变的范式领域非常陌生。 15或许这一点无需赘述，因为显然，正是这些人，由于先前的实践经验让他们很少遵循常规科学的传统规则，因此他们特别有可能意识到这些规则已不再适用，并构想出一套可以取而代之的新规则。

Extraordinary research must have still other manifestations and effects, but in this area we have scarcely begun to discover the questions that need to be asked. Perhaps, however, no more are needed at this point. The preceding remarks should suffice to show how crisis simultaneously loosens the stereotypes and provides the incremental data necessary for a fundamental paradigm shift. Sometimes the shape of the new paradigm is foreshadowed in the structure that extraordinary research has given to the anomaly. Einstein wrote that before he had any substitute for classical mechanics, he could see the interrelation between the known anomalies of black-body radiation, the photoelectric effect, and specific heats.14 More often no such structure is consciously seen in advance. Instead, the new paradigm, or a sufficient hint to permit later articulation, emerges all at once, sometimes in the middle of the night, in the mind of a man deeply immersed in crisis. What the nature of that final stage is—how an individual invents (or finds he has invented) a new way of giving order to data now all assembled—must here remain inscrutable and may be permanently so. Let us here note only one thing about it. Almost always the men who achieve these fundamental inventions of a new paradigm have been either very young or very new to the field whose paradigm they change.15 And perhaps that point need not have been made explicit, for obviously these are the men who, being little committed by prior practice to the traditional rules of normal science, are particularly likely to see that those rules no longer define a playable game and to conceive another set that can replace them.

由此产生的向新范式的过渡就是科学革命，我们终于准备好直接探讨这个主题了。然而，首先要注意的是，前三节的内容已经为最后一个看似难以捉摸的方面做好了铺垫。在第六节首次引入“异常”概念之前，“革命”和“非常规科学”这两个术语可能看起来是等同的。更重要的是，这两个术语似乎都只意味着“非常规科学”，这种循环论证至少会让一些读者感到困惑。但实际上，这种困惑并非必然。我们即将发现，类似的循环论证也是科学理论的特征。然而，无论这种循环论证是否令人困扰，它不再是绝对的。本文的这一部分以及前两部分已经提出了许多常规科学活动崩溃的标准，这些标准与崩溃之后是否会发生革命无关。面对异常或危机，科学家们会对现有的范式采取不同的态度，他们的研究性质也会随之改变。各种相互竞争的理论层出不穷，人们愿意尝试任何新事物，公开表达不满，诉诸哲学并就基本问题展开辩论，所有这些都是研究从常规向非常规转变的征兆。常规科学的概念与其说是依赖于革命，不如说是依赖于这些转变的存在。

The resulting transition to a new paradigm is scientific revolution, a subject that we are at long last prepared to approach directly. Note first, however, one last and apparently elusive respect in which the material of the last three sections has prepared the way. Until Section VI, where the concept of anomaly was first introduced, the terms ‘revolution’ and ‘extraordinary science’ may have seemed equivalent. More important, neither term may have seemed to mean more than ‘non-normal science,’ a circularity that will have bothered at least a few readers. In practice, it need not have done so. We are about to discover that a similar circularity is characteristic of scientific theories. Bothersome or not, however, that circularity is no longer unqualified. This section of the essay and the two preceding have educed numerous criteria of a breakdown in normal scientific activity, criteria that do not at all depend upon whether breakdown is succeeded by revolution. Confronted with anomaly or with crisis, scientists take a different attitude toward existing paradigms, and the nature of their research changes accordingly. The proliferation of competing articulations, the willingness to try anything, the expression of explicit discontent, the recourse to philosophy and to debate over fundamentals, all these are symptoms of a transition from normal to extraordinary research. It is upon their existence more than upon that of revolutions that the notion of normal science depends.

[ IX ]

[IX]

科学革命的性质和必要性

The Nature and Necessity of Scientific Revolutions

这些论述最终使我们能够探讨本文标题所指的问题：什么是科学革命？它们在科学发展中扮演着怎样的角色？这些问题的答案在前文已有所涉及。特别是，前文的讨论表明，本文所指的科学革命是指那些非累积性的发展事件，在这些事件中，旧范式被一个不相容的新范式全部或部分地取代。然而，还有更多内容需要阐述，而其中一个关键部分可以通过提出另一个问题来引出：为什么范式的转变应该被称为革命？鉴于政治发展和科学发展之间存在着巨大而本质的差异，究竟是什么相似之处能够证明将二者都比作革命的合理性？

These remarks permit us at last to consider the problems that provide this essay with its title. What are scientific revolutions, and what is their function in scientific development? Much of the answer to these questions has been anticipated in earlier sections. In particular, the preceding discussion has indicated that scientific revolutions are here taken to be those non-cumulative developmental episodes in which an older paradigm is replaced in whole or in part by an incompatible new one. There is more to be said, however, and an essential part of it can be introduced by asking one further question. Why should a change of paradigm be called a revolution? In the face of the vast and essential differences between political and scientific development, what parallelism can justify the metaphor that finds revolutions in both?

这种相似性的一个方面应该已经显而易见。政治革命的开端源于一种日益增长的意识，这种意识往往局限于政治共同体中的某个群体，即现有的制度已无法充分应对它们自身在某种程度上造成的环境所带来的问题。同样，科学革命的开端也源于一种日益增长的意识，这种意识同样往往局限于科学共同体中的某个狭义分支，即现有的范式已无法充分有效地探索某个方面。自然界此前一直遵循着某种范式。在政治和科学发展中，导致危机的失灵感是革命的先决条件。此外，尽管这种比喻略显牵强，但这种类比不仅适用于像哥白尼和拉瓦锡那样的重大范式变革，也适用于与吸收某种新现象（例如氧气或X射线）相关的较小范式变革。正如我们在第五节末尾所指出的，科学革命只有在那些范式受到影响的人看来才具有革命性。对于局外人而言，它们可能就像二十世纪初的巴尔干革命一样，只是发展进程中的正常组成部分。例如，天文学家可以接受X射线仅仅是对现有知识的补充，因为他们的范式并未受到这种新辐射的影响。但对于开尔文、克鲁克斯和伦琴这样研究辐射理论或阴极射线管的人来说，X射线的出现必然打破了一种范式，同时也创造了另一种范式。正因如此，这些射线只能在常规研究出现偏差后才能被发现。

One aspect of the parallelism must already be apparent. Political revolutions are inaugurated by a growing sense, often restricted to a segment of the political community, that existing institutions have ceased adequately to meet the problems posed by an environment that they have in part created. In much the same way, scientific revolutions are inaugurated by a growing sense, again often restricted to a narrow subdivision of the scientific community, that an existing paradigm has ceased to function adequately in the exploration of an aspect of nature to which that paradigm itself had previously led the way. In both political and scientific development the sense of malfunction that can lead to crisis is prerequisite to revolution. Furthermore, though it admittedly strains the metaphor, that parallelism holds not only for the major paradigm changes, like those attributable to Copernicus and Lavoisier, but also for the far smaller ones associated with the assimilation of a new sort of phenomenon, like oxygen or X-rays. Scientific revolutions, as we noted at the end of Section V, need seem revolutionary only to those whose paradigms are affected by them. To outsiders they may, like the Balkan revolutions of the early twentieth century, seem normal parts of the developmental process. Astronomers, for example, could accept X-rays as a mere addition to knowledge, for their paradigms were unaffected by the existence of the new radiation. But for men like Kelvin, Crookes, and Roentgen, whose research dealt with radiation theory or with cathode ray tubes, the emergence of X-rays necessarily violated one paradigm as it created another. That is why these rays could be discovered only through something’s first going wrong with normal research.

政治发展与科学发展之间存在着基因层面的平行关系，这一点毋庸置疑。然而，这种平行关系还有第二个更为深刻的层面，而第一个层面的意义就取决于此。政治革命旨在以政治制度本身所禁止的方式改变这些制度。因此，革命的成功必然需要部分放弃一套制度，转而接受另一套制度；在此期间，社会并非完全由制度治理。最初，只有危机才会削弱政治制度的作用，正如我们已经看到它削弱了范式的作用一样。越来越多的人与政治生活日益疏离，并在政治生活中表现得越来越古怪。然后，随着危机的加深，这些人中的许多人会致力于在新的制度框架下重建社会的具体方案。此时，社会分裂成相互竞争的阵营或政党，一方试图捍卫旧的制度格局，另一方则试图建立新的制度。一旦这种两极分化发生，政治手段便会失效。由于各方对实现和评估政治变革的制度框架存在分歧，由于他们不承认任何超制度框架来裁决革命分歧，革命冲突各方最终不得不诉诸群众劝说技巧，其中往往包括武力。尽管革命在政治制度的演变中发挥了至关重要的作用，但这种作用取决于革命本身是否具有部分超政治或超制度的性质。

This genetic aspect of the parallel between political and scientific development should no longer be open to doubt. The parallel has, however, a second and more profound aspect upon which the significance of the first depends. Political revolutions aim to change political institutions in ways that those institutions themselves prohibit. Their success therefore necessitates the partial relinquishment of one set of institutions in favor of another, and in the interim, society is not fully governed by institutions at all. Initially it is crisis alone that attenuates the role of political institutions as we have already seen it attenuate the role of paradigms. In increasing numbers individuals become increasingly estranged from political life and behave more and more eccentrically within it. Then, as the crisis deepens, many of these individuals commit themselves to some concrete proposal for the reconstruction of society in a new institutional framework. At that point the society is divided into competing camps or parties, one seeking to defend the old institutional constellation, the others seeking to institute some new one. And, once that polarization has occurred, political recourse fails. Because they differ about the institutional matrix within which political change is to be achieved and evaluated, because they acknowledge no supra-institutional framework for the adjudication of revolutionary difference, the parties to a revolutionary conflict must finally resort to the techniques of mass persuasion, often including force. Though revolutions have had a vital role in the evolution of political institutions, that role depends upon their being partially extrapolitical or extrainstitutional events.

本文余下部分旨在论证，对范式转变的历史研究揭示了科学演进中非常相似的特征。如同在相互竞争的政治制度之间做出选择一样，在相互竞争的范式之间做出选择，最终也意味着在不相容的社群生活模式之间做出选择。正因为其具有这种性质，这种选择并非也不可能仅仅由常规科学的评价程序决定，因为这些程序部分依赖于特定的范式，而该范式正是争论的焦点。当范式不可避免地卷入关于范式选择的争论时，它们的作用必然是循环论证的。每个群体都运用自身的范式来捍卫该范式。

The remainder of this essay aims to demonstrate that the historical study of paradigm change reveals very similar characteristics in the evolution of the sciences. Like the choice between competing political institutions, that between competing paradigms proves to be a choice between incompatible modes of community life. Because it has that character, the choice is not and cannot be determined merely by the evaluative procedures characteristic of normal science, for these depend in part upon a particular paradigm, and that paradigm is at issue. When paradigms enter, as they must, into a debate about paradigm choice, their role is necessarily circular. Each group uses its own paradigm to argue in that paradigm’s defense.

当然，由此产生的循环论证并非错误或无效。在捍卫某种范式时，提出该范式的人仍然可以清晰地展示，对于那些接受这种新的自然观的人来说，科学实践将会是什么样子。这种展示可能极具说服力，甚至令人信服。然而，无论其力量如何，循环论证的本质仅限于说服。对于那些拒绝接受循环论证的人来说，它既无法在逻辑上，也无法在概率上令人信服。关于范式的辩论双方所共享的前提和价值观并不足以支撑这一点。正如政治革命一样，在范式选择中，没有比相关群体的认同更高的标准。因此，为了探究科学革命是如何发生的，我们不仅需要考察自然和逻辑的影响，还需要考察在构成科学家群体这一特殊群体内部有效的说服性论证技巧。

The resulting circularity does not, of course, make the arguments wrong or even ineffectual. The man who premises a paradigm when arguing in its defense can nonetheless provide a clear exhibit of what scientific practice will be like for those who adopt the new view of nature. That exhibit can be immensely persuasive, often compellingly so. Yet, whatever its force, the status of the circular argument is only that of persuasion. It cannot be made logically or even probabilistically compelling for those who refuse to step into the circle. The premises and values shared by the two parties to a debate over paradigms are not sufficiently extensive for that. As in political revolutions, so in paradigm choice—there is no standard higher than the assent of the relevant community. To discover how scientific revolutions are effected, we shall therefore have to examine not only the impact of nature and of logic, but also the techniques of persuasive argumentation effective within the quite special groups that constitute the community of scientists.

为了探究为何仅凭逻辑和实验永远无法彻底解决范式选择问题，我们必须简要考察传统范式的支持者与其革命性后继者之间的差异本质。这一考察是本节及下一节的主要目的。然而，我们已经列举了许多此类差异的例子，而且毫无疑问，历史还能提供更多例证。比起这些例子的存在，更可能受到质疑的——因此也必须首先考虑的——是这些例子能够提供关于科学本质的重要信息。即便范式的摒弃是历史事实，它是否仅仅揭示了人类的轻信和困惑？是否存在内在原因，使得对新现象或新科学理论的吸收必然要求摒弃旧范式？

To discover why this issue of paradigm choice can never be unequivocally settled by logic and experiment alone, we must shortly examine the nature of the differences that separate the proponents of a traditional paradigm from their revolutionary successors. That examination is the principal object of this section and the next. We have, however, already noted numerous examples of such differences, and no one will doubt that history can supply many others. What is more likely to be doubted than their existence—and what must therefore be considered first—is that such examples provide essential information about the nature of science. Granting that paradigm rejection has been a historic fact, does it illuminate more than human credulity and confusion? Are there intrinsic reasons why the assimilation of either a new sort of phenomenon or a new scientific theory must demand the rejection of an older paradigm?

首先需要注意的是，即便存在这样的理由，它们也并非源于科学知识的逻辑结构。原则上，新现象的出现并不会对过去的任何科学实践造成破坏性影响。尽管如今在月球上发现生命会颠覆现有的范式（这些范式告诉我们一些关于月球的现象，而这些现象似乎与生命存在相矛盾），但在银河系中某个鲜为人知的区域发现生命则不会。同样，新理论也未必与任何先前的理论相冲突。它可以专门研究此前未知的现象，例如量子理论（但并非完全如此）研究20世纪以前未知的亚原子现象。或者，新理论可能仅仅是比以往理论更高层次的理论，它将一系列较低层次的理论联系起来，而没有对任何现有理论进行实质性的改变。如今，能量守恒理论正是将动力学、化学、电学、光学、热力学等学科联系起来。此外，我们还可以设想新旧理论之间其他兼容的关系。它们中的任何一种或所有这些都可以在科学发展的历史进程中得到体现。如果真是如此，科学发展就真正是累积性的。新的现象只会揭示自然界某个方面的秩序。此前从未见过这种情况。在科学发展过程中，新知识会取代无知，而不是取代另一种互不相容的知识。

First notice that if there are such reasons, they do not derive from the logical structure of scientific knowledge. In principle, a new phenomenon might emerge without reflecting destructively upon any part of past scientific practice. Though discovering life on the moon would today be destructive of existing paradigms (these tell us things about the moon that seem incompatible with life’s existence there), discovering life in some less well-known part of the galaxy would not. By the same token, a new theory does not have to conflict with any of its predecessors. It might deal exclusively with phenomena not previously known, as the quantum theory deals (but, significantly, not exclusively) with subatomic phenomena unknown before the twentieth century. Or again, the new theory might be simply a higher level theory than those known before, one that linked together a whole group of lower level theories without substantially changing any. Today, the theory of energy conservation provides just such links between dynamics, chemistry, electricity, optics, thermal theory, and so on. Still other compatible relationships between old and new theories can be conceived. Any and all of them might be exemplified by the historical process through which science has developed. If they were, scientific development would be genuinely cumulative. New sorts of phenomena would simply disclose order in an aspect of nature where none had been seen before. In the evolution of science new knowledge would replace ignorance rather than replace knowledge of another and incompatible sort.

当然，科学（或其他一些或许效率稍低的事业）本可以完全以累积的方式发展。许多人曾相信科学就是这样发展的，而且大多数人似乎仍然认为，如果历史发展不常受到人类特质的扭曲，那么累积至少是历史发展的理想状态。这种信念有其重要的原因。在第十节中，我们将探讨“科学即累积”的观点与一种主流认识论之间的紧密联系，这种认识论认为知识是心灵直接建构于原始感官数据之上的产物。在第十一节中，我们将考察有效的科学教学方法如何有力地支持了同样的史学模式。然而，尽管这种理想图景极具说服力，但我们越来越有理由怀疑它是否真的能够代表科学。在范式形成之前，所有新理论和几乎所有新现象的吸收实际上都要求摧毁先前的范式，并由此引发不同科学思想流派之间的冲突。对意料之外的新事物进行累积式的获取，几乎可以忽略不计，这并非科学发展规律的例外。认真对待历史事实的人必然会怀疑，科学的发展方向并非我们所认为的那种累积性理想状态。或许，它是一种截然不同的事业。

Of course, science (or some other enterprise, perhaps less effective) might have developed in that fully cumulative manner. Many people have believed that it did so, and most still seem to suppose that cumulation is at least the ideal that historical development would display if only it had not so often been distorted by human idiosyncrasy. There are important reasons for that belief. In Section X we shall discover how closely the view of science-as-cumulation is entangled with a dominant epistemology that takes knowledge to be a construction placed directly upon raw sense data by the mind. And in Section XI we shall examine the strong support provided to the same historiographic schema by the techniques of effective science pedagogy. Nevertheless, despite the immense plausibility of that ideal image, there is increasing reason to wonder whether it can possibly be an image of science. After the pre-paradigm period the assimilation of all new theories and of almost all new sorts of phenomena has in fact demanded the destruction of a prior paradigm and a consequent conflict between competing schools of scientific thought. Cumulative acquisition of unanticipated novelties proves to be an almost non-existent exception to the rule of scientific development. The man who takes historic fact seriously must suspect that science does not tend toward the ideal that our image of its cumulativeness has suggested. Perhaps it is another sort of enterprise.

然而，如果顽固的事实能够引领我们走到这一步，那么重新审视我们已经探讨过的内容或许会表明，累积性地获取新知识不仅在事实上罕见，而且在原则上也几乎不可能。常规的研究是累积性的，其成功归功于科学家们能够定期选择那些可以用与现有技术相近的概念和仪器技术来解决的问题。（这就是为什么过度关注有用的问题，而忽略它们与现有知识和技术的关联，很容易阻碍科学发展。）致力于解决问题的人然而，受现有知识和技术的制约，并非仅仅是环顾四周。他清楚自己想要达成的目标，并据此设计工具、调整思路。只有当他对自然和工具的预期被证明是错误的，才能出现意料之外的新奇事物，即新的发现。通常，最终发现的重要性与预示它的异常现象的程度和顽固性成正比。显然，揭示异常现象的范式与后来将异常现象视为规律的范式之间必然存在冲突。第六部分探讨的通过范式颠覆而发现的案例并非仅仅是历史的偶然事件。除此之外，别无其他有效途径可以产生发现。

If, however, resistant facts can carry us that far, then a second look at the ground we have already covered may suggest that cumulative acquisition of novelty is not only rare in fact but improbable in principle. Normal research, which is cumulative, owes its success to the ability of scientists regularly to select problems that can be solved with conceptual and instrumental techniques close to those already in existence. (That is why an excessive concern with useful problems, regardless of their relation to existing knowledge and technique, can so easily inhibit scientific development.) The man who is striving to solve a problem defined by existing knowledge and technique is not, however, just looking around. He knows what he wants to achieve, and he designs his instruments and directs his thoughts accordingly. Unanticipated novelty, the new discovery, can emerge only to the extent that his anticipations about nature and his instruments prove wrong. Often the importance of the resulting discovery will itself be proportional to the extent and stubbornness of the anomaly that foreshadowed it. Obviously, then, there must be a conflict between the paradigm that discloses anomaly and the one that later renders the anomaly lawlike. The examples of discovery through paradigm destruction examined in Section VI did not confront us with mere historical accident. There is no other effective way in which discoveries might be generated.

同样的论点更适用于新理论的创立。原则上，只有三种现象可以发展出新的理论。第一种是现有范式已经能够很好地解释的现象，这类现象很少能为理论构建提供动机或出发点。即便它们确实提供了理论构建的动机或出发点，例如第七节末尾讨论的三个著名的预测，由此产生的理论也很少被接受，因为自然界本身并没有提供区分的依据。第二类现象的本质可以通过现有范式来揭示，但其细节只能通过进一步的理论阐释才能理解。科学家们常常将研究方向转向这类现象，但他们的研究目标是阐释现有范式，而不是创立新的范式。只有当这些阐释尝试失败时，科学家们才会遇到第三类现象，即那些公认的异常现象，它们的特征在于顽固地拒绝被纳入现有范式。只有这类现象才能催生新的理论。范式为除异常现象之外的所有现象在科学家的视野中提供了一个由理论决定的位置。

The same argument applies even more clearly to the invention of new theories. There are, in principle, only three types of phenomena about which a new theory might be developed. The first consists of phenomena already well explained by existing paradigms, and these seldom provide either motive or point of departure for theory construction. When they do, as with the three famous anticipations discussed at the end of Section VII, the theories that result are seldom accepted, because nature provides no ground for discrimination. A second class of phenomena consists of those whose nature is indicated by existing paradigms but whose details can be understood only through further theory articulation. These are the phenomena to which scientists direct their research much of the time, but that research aims at the articulation of existing paradigms rather than at the invention of new ones. Only when these attempts at articulation fail do scientists encounter the third type of phenomena, the recognized anomalies whose characteristic feature is their stubborn refusal to be assimilated to existing paradigms. This type alone gives rise to new theories. Paradigms provide all phenomena except anomalies with a theory-determined place in the scientist’s field of vision.

但是，如果需要提出新的理论来解决现有理论与自然关系中的异常情况，那么成功的新理论必须在某种程度上允许做出与现有理论推导出的预测不同的预测。与其前身相比，这种差异不可能出现。如果两者逻辑兼容，这种差异就不会发生。在被吸收的过程中，后一种理论必然会取代前一种。即使是像能量守恒这样的理论，如今看来它似乎是一种逻辑上的上层建筑，仅通过独立建立的理论与自然界相关联，但它在历史上的发展也并非一帆风顺，经历了范式的瓦解。相反，它诞生于一场危机之中，这场危机的关键因素在于牛顿动力学与热质理论中一些新近提出的推论之间的不兼容性。只有在热质理论被否定之后，能量守恒才能成为科学的一部分。1而只有在它成为科学的一部分一段时间之后，它才能被视为一种逻辑上更高层次的理论，一种与前身理论不再冲突的理论。很难想象，如果没有这些关于自然的信念的破坏性改变，新的理论如何能够产生。尽管逻辑上的包容性仍然是理解各个科学理论之间关系的一种合理观点，但在历史上，这却是不可能的。

But if new theories are called forth to resolve anomalies in the relation of an existing theory to nature, then the successful new theory must somewhere permit predictions that are different from those derived from its predecessor. That difference could not occur if the two were logically compatible. In the process of being assimilated, the second must displace the first. Even a theory like energy conservation, which today seems a logical superstructure that relates to nature only through independently established theories, did not develop historically without paradigm destruction. Instead, it emerged from a crisis in which an essential ingredient was the incompatibility between Newtonian dynamics and some recently formulated consequences of the caloric theory of heat. Only after the caloric theory had been rejected could energy conservation become part of science.1 And only after it had been part of science for some time could it come to seem a theory of a logically higher type, one not in conflict with its predecessors. It is hard to see how new theories could arise without these destructive changes in beliefs about nature. Though logical inclusiveness remains a permissible view of the relation between successive scientific theories, it is a historical implausibility.

我认为，一个世纪前，关于革命必要性的论证或许可以就此止步。但遗憾的是，如今已无法如此，因为如果接受当今最流行的关于科学理论本质和功能的解释，上述观点便无法成立。这种解释与早期逻辑实证主义密切相关，且并未被其后继者彻底否定。它限制了已被接受的理论的范围和意义，使其不可能与任何后来对某些相同自然现象做出预测的理论相冲突。这种对科学理论的限制性理解最著名、最有力的论证，体现在对当代爱因斯坦动力学与源自牛顿《自然哲学的数学原理》的早期动力学方程之间关系的讨论中。从本文的角度来看，这两种理论本质上是不相容的，正如哥白尼天文学与托勒密天文学之间的关系所体现的那样：爱因斯坦的理论只有在……的情况下才能被接受。人们逐渐认识到牛顿的观点是错误的。时至今日，这仍然是少数派观点。2因此，我们必须考察针对这一观点最常见的反对意见。

A century ago it would, I think, have been possible to let the case for the necessity of revolutions rest at this point. But today, unfortunately, that cannot be done because the view of the subject developed above cannot be maintained if the most prevalent contemporary interpretation of the nature and function of scientific theory is accepted. That interpretation, closely associated with early logical positivism and not categorically rejected by its successors, would restrict the range and meaning of an accepted theory so that it could not possibly conflict with any later theory that made predictions about some of the same natural phenomena. The best-known and the strongest case for this restricted conception of a scientific theory emerges in discussions of the relation between contemporary Einsteinian dynamics and the older dynamical equations that descend from Newton’s Principia. From the viewpoint of this essay these two theories are fundamentally incompatible in the sense illustrated by the relation of Copernican to Ptolemaic astronomy: Einstein’s theory can be accepted only with the recognition that Newton’s was wrong. Today this remains a minority view.2 We must therefore examine the most prevalent objections to it.

这些反对意见的要点可以阐述如下。相对论动力学不可能证明牛顿动力学是错误的，因为牛顿动力学至今仍被大多数工程师成功运用，并且在某些特定应用中也被许多物理学家使用。此外，这种对旧理论的合理性可以从在其他应用中取代它的理论本身得到证明。爱因斯坦的理论可以用来证明，在满足少数限制性条件的所有应用中，牛顿方程的预测结果将与我们的测量仪器一样精确。例如，如果牛顿理论要提供一个良好的近似解，所考虑物体的相对速度必须远小于光速。在这个条件和其他一些条件的约束下，牛顿理论似乎可以从爱因斯坦理论推导而来，因此它是爱因斯坦理论的一个特例。

The gist of these objections can be developed as follows. Relativistic dynamics cannot have shown Newtonian dynamics to be wrong, for Newtonian dynamics is still used with great success by most engineers and, in selected applications, by many physicists. Furthermore, the propriety of this use of the older theory can be proved from the very theory that has, in other applications, replaced it. Einstein’s theory can be used to show that predictions from Newton’s equations will be as good as our measuring instruments in all applications that satisfy a small number of restrictive conditions. For example, if Newtonian theory is to provide a good approximate solution, the relative velocities of the bodies considered must be small compared with the velocity of light. Subject to this condition and a few others, Newtonian theory seems to be derivable from Einsteinian, of which it is therefore a special case.

但反对意见继续指出，任何理论都不可能与其特例相冲突。如果爱因斯坦的科学似乎否定了牛顿动力学，那仅仅是因为一些牛顿主义者过于草率地声称牛顿理论能够得出完全精确的结果，或者声称它在极高的相对速度下仍然有效。由于他们不可能拥有任何证据来支持这些说法，因此他们的这些言论违背了科学的准则。只要牛顿理论曾经是一个真正有有效证据支持的科学理论，那么它现在仍然是。只有那些对该理论的夸张断言——那些原本就不是科学范畴的断言——才能被爱因斯坦证明是错误的。剔除这些纯粹出于人性的夸张断言后，牛顿理论从未受到挑战，也不可能受到挑战。

But, the objection continues, no theory can possibly conflict with one of its special cases. If Einsteinian science seems to make Newtonian dynamics wrong, that is only because some Newtonians were so incautious as to claim that Newtonian theory yielded entirely precise results or that it was valid at very high relative velocities. Since they could not have had any evidence for such claims, they betrayed the standards of science when they made them. In so far as Newtonian theory was ever a truly scientific theory supported by valid evidence, it still is. Only extravagant claims for the theory—claims that were never properly parts of science—can have been shown by Einstein to be wrong. Purged of these merely human extravagances, Newtonian theory has never been challenged and cannot be.

这种论证的某种变体足以使任何被相当数量的合格科学家使用的理论免受攻击。例如，备受诟病的燃素说就曾解释过大量的物理和化学现象。它解释了……尸体燃烧的原因在于它们富含燃素；金属的共同性质远多于其矿石。所有金属都是由不同的元素土与燃素结合而成，而燃素是所有金属共有的成分，因此赋予了它们共同的性质。此外，燃素理论还能解释许多反应，例如碳和硫等物质燃烧生成酸。它还能解释密闭空气中燃烧时体积减小的现象——燃烧释放的燃素会“破坏”吸收它的空气的弹性，就像火会“破坏”钢弹簧的弹性一样。3如果燃素理论家仅能解释这些现象，那么该理论就永远不会受到挑战。类似的论证也适用于任何曾经成功应用于各种现象的理论。

Some variant of this argument is quite sufficient to make any theory ever used by a significant group of competent scientists immune to attack. The much-maligned phlogiston theory, for example, gave order to a large number of physical and chemical phenomena. It explained why bodies burned—they were rich in phlogiston—and why metals had so many more properties in common than did their ores. The metals were all compounded from different elementary earths combined with phlogiston, and the latter, common to all metals, produced common properties. In addition, the phlogiston theory accounted for a number of reactions in which acids were formed by the combustion of substances like carbon and sulphur. Also, it explained the decrease of volume when combustion occurs in a confined volume of air—the phlogiston released by combustion “spoils” the elasticity of the air that absorbed it, just as fire “spoils” the elasticity of a steel spring.3 If these were the only phenomena that the phlogiston theorists had claimed for their theory, that theory could never have been challenged. A similar argument will suffice for any theory that has ever been successfully applied to any range of phenomena at all.

但要以这种方式保存理论，其应用范围必须限制在现有实验证据所能涵盖的现象和观测精度范围内。4进一步延伸（一旦迈出第一步，几乎无法避免），这种限制将禁止科学家声称对任何尚未被观察到的现象进行“科学”论述。即使在目前的形式下，这种限制也禁止科学家在自己的研究中依赖某个理论，只要该研究进入了以往理论实践中未曾涉及的领域或寻求了更高的精度。这些禁令在逻辑上无可指摘。但接受这些禁令的后果将是科学得以进一步发展的研究的终结。

But to save theories in this way, their range of application must be restricted to those phenomena and to that precision of observation with which the experimental evidence in hand already deals.4 Carried just a step further (and the step can scarcely be avoided once the first is taken), such a limitation prohibits the scientist from claiming to speak “scientifically” about any phenomenon not already observed. Even in its present form the restriction forbids the scientist to rely upon a theory in his own research whenever that research enters an area or seeks a degree of precision for which past practice with the theory offers no precedent. These prohibitions are logically unexceptionable. But the result of accepting them would be the end of the research through which science may develop further.

这一点现在几乎也成了同义反复。如果没有对某种范式的坚持，就不会有正常的科学。此外，这种坚持必须延伸到各个领域以及精确度的程度。这完全没有先例。如果没有先例，范式就无法提出任何尚未解决的难题。此外，并非只有常规科学依赖于对范式的坚持。如果现有理论仅仅约束科学家在现有应用方面的实践，那么就不会有惊喜、异常或危机。但这些恰恰是通往非凡科学的路标。如果对理论合法适用范围的实证主义限制被字面理解，那么告知科学界哪些问题可能导致根本性变革的机制就必然会失效。而一旦这种情况发生，科学界将不可避免地回归到与范式出现之前非常相似的状态，即所有成员都在从事科学研究，但他们的成果却几乎与科学本身毫无关联。因此，重大科学进步的代价是承担着可能出错的风险，这难道真的令人惊讶吗？

By now that point too is virtually a tautology. Without commitment to a paradigm there could be no normal science. Furthermore, that commitment must extend to areas and to degrees of precision for which there is no full precedent. If it did not, the paradigm could provide no puzzles that had not already been solved. Besides, it is not only normal science that depends upon commitment to a paradigm. If existing theory binds the scientist only with respect to existing applications, then there can be no surprises, anomalies, or crises. But these are just the signposts that point the way to extraordinary science. If positivistic restrictions on the range of a theory’s legitimate applicability are taken literally, the mechanism that tells the scientific community what problems may lead to fundamental change must cease to function. And when that occurs, the community will inevitably return to something much like its pre-paradigm state, a condition in which all members practice science but in which their gross product scarcely resembles science at all. Is it really any wonder that the price of significant scientific advance is a commitment that runs the risk of being wrong?

更重要的是，实证主义者的论证中存在一个发人深省的逻辑漏洞，它将立即让我们重新认识革命性变革的本质。牛顿动力学真的可以从相对论动力学推导出来吗？这样的推导会是什么样子？设想一组陈述E₁ , E₂ , ..., En ，它们共同体现了相对论的定律。这些陈述包含代表空间位置、时间、静止质量等的变量和参数。从这些陈述出发，结合逻辑和数学工具，可以推导出一系列进一步的陈述，其中一些可以通过观测来验证。为了证明牛顿动力学作为特例的充分性，我们必须在E₁的基础上添加一些额外的陈述，例如 ( v/c ) ² << 1，从而限制参数和变量的范围。然后，对这组扩展后的陈述进行操作，得到一个新的陈述集N₁ , N₂ , ...牛顿第二定律（N m）与牛顿运动定律、万有引力定律等形式相同。显然，牛顿动力学是在满足一些限制条件的情况下从爱因斯坦动力学推导而来的。

More important, there is a revealing logical lacuna in the positivist’s argument, one that will reintroduce us immediately to the nature of revolutionary change. Can Newtonian dynamics really be derived from relativistic dynamics? What would such a derivation look like? Imagine a set of statements, E1, E2, . . . , En, which together embody the laws of relativity theory. These statements contain variables and parameters representing spatial position, time, rest mass, etc. From them, together with the apparatus of logic and mathematics, is deducible a whole set of further statements including some that can be checked by observation. To prove the adequacy of Newtonian dynamics as a special case, we must add to the E1’s additional statements, like (v/c)2 << 1, restricting the range of the parameters and variables. This enlarged set of statements is then manipulated to yield a new set, N1, N2, . . . , Nm, which is identical in form with Newton’s laws of motion, the law of gravity, and so on. Apparently Newtonian dynamics has been derived from Einsteinian, subject to a few limiting conditions.

然而，至少到目前为止，这种推导是错误的。尽管N1定律是相对论力学定律的一个特例，但它们并非牛顿定律。或者至少，除非对牛顿定律进行重新解释，而这种解释在爱因斯坦的工作之前是不可能的，否则它们就不是牛顿定律。爱因斯坦E1定律中的变量和参数……空间位置、时间、质量等概念仍然出现在N1中；它们在那里仍然代表爱因斯坦的空间、时间和质量。但是，这些爱因斯坦概念的物理指涉对象绝非与同名的牛顿概念相同。（牛顿质量守恒；爱因斯坦质量可以与能量转换。只有在相对速度很低的情况下，两者才能以相同的方式测量，即便如此，它们也绝不能被视为相同。）除非我们改变N1中变量的定义，否则我们推导出的结论就不是牛顿式的。如果我们改变了这些定义，我们就不能说我们推导出了牛顿定律，至少不能以目前普遍认可的“推导”方式来定义。当然，我们的论证解释了为什么牛顿定律似乎曾经有效。这样一来，它也为例如汽车驾驶员的行为提供了理由，仿佛他生活在一个牛顿宇宙中。类似的论证也被用来为向测量员教授地心天文学辩护。但这种论证仍然没有达到它声称的目的。也就是说，它并没有证明牛顿定律是爱因斯坦定律的极限情况。因为在推演到极限的过程中，改变的不仅仅是定律的形式。与此同时，我们也必须改变构成这些定律所适用的宇宙的基本结构要素。

Yet the derivation is spurious, at least to this point. Though the N1’s are a special case of the laws of relativistic mechanics, they are not Newton’s Laws. Or at least they are not unless those laws are reinterpreted in a way that would have been impossible until after Einstein’s work. The variables and parameters that in the Einsteinian E1’s represented spatial position, time, mass, etc., still occur in the N1’s; and they there still represent Einsteinian space, time, and mass. But the physical referents of these Einsteinian concepts are by no means identical with those of the Newtonian concepts that bear the same name. (Newtonian mass is conserved; Einsteinian is convertible with energy. Only at low relative velocities may the two be measured in the same way, and even then they must not be conceived to be the same.) Unless we change the definitions of the variables in the N1’s, the statements we have derived are not Newtonian. If we do change them, we cannot properly be said to have derived Newton’s Laws, at least not in any sense of “derive” now generally recognized. Our argument has, of course, explained why Newton’s Laws ever seemed to work. In doing so it has justified, say, an automobile driver in acting as though he lived in a Newtonian universe. An argument of the same type is used to justify teaching earth-centered astronomy to surveyors. But the argument has still not done what it purported to do. It has not, that is, shown Newton’s Laws to be a limiting case of Einstein’s. For in the passage to the limit it is not only the forms of the laws that have changed. Simultaneously we have had to alter the fundamental structural elements of which the universe to which they apply is composed.

这种改变既定且熟悉概念含义的需求，正是爱因斯坦理论革命性影响的核心所在。尽管这种改变比从地心说到日心说、从燃素到氧气、或从微粒到波动等概念的转变更为微妙，但由此产生的概念转变对既有范式的颠覆性影响却毫不逊色。我们甚至可以将其视为科学领域革命性重塑的原型。尽管从牛顿力学到爱因斯坦力学的转变并未引入新的对象或概念，但它却格外清晰地展现了科学革命的本质——科学家看待世界的概念网络的置换。

This need to change the meaning of established and familiar concepts is central to the revolutionary impact of Einstein’s theory. Though subtler than the changes from geocentrism to heliocentrism, from phlogiston to oxygen, or from corpuscles to waves, the resulting conceptual transformation is no less decisively destructive of a previously established paradigm. We may even come to see it as a prototype for revolutionary reorientations in the sciences. Just because it did not involve the introduction of additional objects or concepts, the transition from Newtonian to Einsteinian mechanics illustrates with particular clarity the scientific revolution as a displacement of the conceptual network through which scientists view the world.

这些论述足以表明，在另一种哲学氛围下，某些观点可能被视为理所当然。至少对科学家而言，被摒弃的科学理论与其后续理论之间大多数明显的差异都是真实存在的。尽管过时的理论可能如果旧理论总是被视为其最新后继理论的特例，则必须对其进行改造才能达到目的。而这种改造只能借助后见之明的优势，以及更新理论的明确指导才能完成。此外，即使这种改造是解释旧理论的合理手段，其应用的结果也只会得到一个过于局限的理论，只能重述已知的内容。这种重述虽然简洁，但并非无用，不足以指导研究。

These remarks should suffice to show what might, in another philosophical climate, have been taken for granted. At least for scientists, most of the apparent differences between a discarded scientific theory and its successor are real. Though an out-of-date theory can always be viewed as a special case of its up-to-date successor, it must be transformed for the purpose. And the transformation is one that can be undertaken only with the advantages of hindsight, the explicit guidance of the more recent theory. Furthermore, even if that transformation were a legitimate device to employ in interpreting the older theory, the result of its application would be a theory so restricted that it could only restate what was already known. Because of its economy, that restatement would have utility, but it could not suffice for the guidance of research.

因此，我们现在不妨假定，不同范式之间的差异既是必然的，也是不可调和的。那么，我们能否更明确地阐述这些差异究竟是什么呢？最明显的差异类型已被反复阐述。不同的范式对宇宙的构成及其行为给出了不同的解释。也就是说，它们在诸如亚原子粒子的存在、光的物质性以及热或能量守恒等问题上存在分歧。这些是不同范式之间的实质性差异，无需赘述。然而，范式之间的差异远不止于实质，因为它们不仅指向自然，也指向产生它们的科学本身。它们是任何成熟科学界在任何特定时期所接受的方法、问题领域和解决方案标准的来源。因此，接受新的范式往往需要重新定义相应的科学。一些旧问题可能会被归入其他学科，或者被宣布为完全“不科学”。另一些原本不存在或微不足道的事物，在新范式的背景下，可能成为重大科学成就的典范。随着问题的变化，区分真正的科学解决方案与形而上学的推测、文字游戏或数学游戏的标准也往往随之改变。从科学革命中涌现出的常规科学传统，不仅与以往的传统不相容，而且常常根本无法与之相提并论。

Let us, therefore, now take it for granted that the differences between successive paradigms are both necessary and irreconcilable. Can we then say more explicitly what sorts of differences these are? The most apparent type has already been illustrated repeatedly. Successive paradigms tell us different things about the population of the universe and about that population’s behavior. They differ, that is, about such questions as the existence of subatomic particles, the materiality of light, and the conservation of heat or of energy. These are the substantive differences between successive paradigms, and they require no further illustration. But paradigms differ in more than substance, for they are directed not only to nature but also back upon the science that produced them. They are the source of the methods, problem-field, and standards of solution accepted by any mature scientific community at any given time. As a result, the reception of a new paradigm often necessitates a redefinition of the corresponding science. Some old problems may be relegated to another science or declared entirely “unscientific.” Others that were previously nonexistent or trivial may, with a new paradigm, become the very archetypes of significant scientific achievement. And as the problems change, so, often, does the standard that distinguishes a real scientific solution from a mere metaphysical speculation, word game, or mathematical play. The normal-scientific tradition that emerges from a scientific revolution is not only incompatible but often actually incommensurable with that which has gone before.

牛顿的著作对十七世纪科学实践的常规传统产生了显著影响，这便是其中的一个鲜明例证。这些更为微妙的范式转变的影响。在牛顿出生之前，本世纪的“新科学”终于成功地摒弃了亚里士多德和经院哲学中以物质本质来解释一切的理论。过去那种认为石头之所以落下是因为其“本性”驱使它向宇宙中心运动的说法，如今看来不过是同义反复的文字游戏，而这在以前是不存在的。从此以后，包括颜色、味道甚至重量在内的所有感官体验，都要用构成基本物质的基本微粒的大小、形状、位置和运动来解释。将其他属性归于基本原子被视为诉诸神秘学，因此被科学所排斥。莫里哀正是抓住了这种新思潮，他嘲讽了那位将鸦片的功效解释为具有催眠作用的医生。十七世纪下半叶，许多科学家倾向于认为鸦片颗粒的圆形形状使其能够舒缓所作用的神经。5

The impact of Newton’s work upon the normal seventeenth-century tradition of scientific practice provides a striking example of these subtler effects of paradigm shift. Before Newton was born the “new science” of the century had at last succeeded in rejecting Aristotelian and scholastic explanations expressed in terms of the essences of material bodies. To say that a stone fell because its “nature” drove it toward the center of the universe had been made to look a mere tautological word-play, something it had not previously been. Henceforth the entire flux of sensory appearances, including color, taste, and even weight, was to be explained in terms of the size, shape, position, and motion of the elementary corpuscles of base matter. The attribution of other qualities to the elementary atoms was a resort to the occult and therefore out of bounds for science. Molière caught the new spirit precisely when he ridiculed the doctor who explained opium’s efficacy as a soporific by attributing to it a dormitive potency. During the last half of the seventeenth century many scientists preferred to say that the round shape of the opium particles enabled them to sooth the nerves about which they moved.5

在早期，运用神秘特性进行解释一直是富有成效的科学工作的重要组成部分。然而，十七世纪对机械微粒解释的全新投入，对许多科学领域都产生了巨大的积极影响，不仅解决了那些长期以来难以被普遍接受的难题，还提出了新的解决方案。例如，在动力学领域，牛顿三大运动定律与其说是新颖实验的产物，不如说是尝试用基本中性微粒的运动和相互作用来重新解释一些众所周知的观察结果的结果。仅举一个具体的例子。由于中性微粒只能通过接触相互作用，机械微粒的自然观将科学的注意力引向了一个全新的研究课题：粒子运动因碰撞而发生的变化。笛卡尔提出了这个问题，并给出了第一个可能的解答。惠更斯、雷恩和沃利斯进一步发展了这一问题，他们部分是通过碰撞摆锤的实验，但主要还是通过应用先前已知的特性。将运动学引入新问题。牛顿将这些结果融入到他的运动定律中。第三定律中相等的“作用力”和“反作用力”指的是碰撞双方运动量的变化。同样的运动量变化也构成了第二定律中隐含的动力的定义。在这种情况下，如同十七世纪的许多其他案例一样，微粒范式既催生了一个新问题，也为该问题提供了很大一部分解决方案。6

In an earlier period explanations in terms of occult qualities had been an integral part of productive scientific work. Nevertheless, the seventeenth century’s new commitment to mechanico-corpuscular explanation proved immensely fruitful for a number of sciences, ridding them of problems that had defied generally accepted solution and suggesting others to replace them. In dynamics, for example, Newton’s three laws of motion are less a product of novel experiments than of the attempt to reinterpret well-known observations in terms of the motions and interactions of primary neutral corpuscles. Consider just one concrete illustration. Since neutral corpuscles could act on each other only by contact, the mechanico-corpuscular view of nature directed scientific attention to a brand-new subject of study, the alteration of particulate motions by collisions. Descartes announced the problem and provided its first putative solution. Huyghens, Wren, and Wallis carried it still further, partly by experimenting with colliding pendulum bobs, but mostly by applying previously well-known characteristics of motion to the new problem. And Newton embedded their results in his laws of motion. The equal “action” and “reaction” of the third law are the changes in quantity of motion experienced by the two parties to a collision. The same change of motion supplies the definition of dynamical force implicit in the second law. In this case, as in many others during the seventeenth century, the corpuscular paradigm bred both a new problem and a large part of that problem’s solution.6

然而，尽管牛顿的大部分工作都致力于解决源于机械微粒论世界观的问题并体现其标准，但他的工作所产生的范式却进一步改变了科学合法性的问题和标准，并且在某种程度上具有破坏性。引力被解释为物质中每一对粒子之间固有的吸引力，这如同经院哲学家所说的“下落倾向”一样，是一种神秘的性质。因此，尽管微粒论的标准仍然有效，但对于那些接受《自然哲学的数学原理》作为范式的人来说，寻求引力的机械解释却是最具挑战性的问题之一。牛顿对此投入了大量精力，他的许多十八世纪后继者也同样如此。当时唯一看似可行的选择是拒绝牛顿的理论，因为它无法解释引力，而这种选择也得到了广泛的接受。然而，最终这两种观点都没有取得胜利。由于既无法脱离《自然哲学的数学原理》进行科学研究，也无法使该著作符合十七世纪的微粒论标准，科学家们逐渐接受了引力确实是与生俱来的观点。到十八世纪中叶，这种解释几乎被普遍接受，其结果是科学真正回归（这与倒退不同）经院哲学标准。与生俱来的吸引力和排斥力与大小、形状、位置和运动一起，成为物质不可简化的基本属性。7

Yet, though much of Newton’s work was directed to problems and embodied standards derived from the mechanico-corpuscular world view, the effect of the paradigm that resulted from his work was a further and partially destructive change in the problems and standards legitimate for science. Gravity, interpreted as an innate attraction between every pair of particles of matter, was an occult quality in the same sense as the scholastics’ “tendency to fall” had been. Therefore, while the standards of corpuscularism remained in effect, the search for a mechanical explanation of gravity was one of the most challenging problems for those who accepted the Principia as paradigm. Newton devoted much attention to it and so did many of his eighteenth-century successors. The only apparent option was to reject Newton’s theory for its failure to explain gravity, and that alternative, too, was widely adopted. Yet neither of these views ultimately triumphed. Unable either to practice science without the Principia or to make that work conform to the corpuscular standards of the seventeenth century, scientists gradually accepted the view that gravity was indeed innate. By the mid-eighteenth century that interpretation had been almost universally accepted, and the result was a genuine reversion (which is not the same as a retrogression) to a scholastic standard. Innate attractions and repulsions joined size, shape, position, and motion as physically irreducible primary properties of matter.7

由此导致的物理科学标准和研究领域的转变再次产生了深远的影响。例如，到了18世纪40年代，电工们可以谈论电流体的迷人“特性”，而不会像一个世纪前莫里哀的医生那样遭到嘲笑。随着这种转变，电现象展现出一种与以往截然不同的秩序，不再仅仅将其视为一种只能通过接触起作用的机械逸出物。特别是，当远距离电作用成为一门独立的研究课题时，我们现在称之为感应起电的现象被认为是其效应之一。此前，即使观察到这种现象，也往往将其归因于电“氛围”的直接作用，或是任何电气实验室中不可避免的泄漏。反过来，对感应效应的新认识，又成为富兰克林分析莱顿瓶的关键，从而促成了新的牛顿式电学范式的出现。动力学和电学并非唯一受到探寻物质固有力合法化影响的科学领域。十八世纪关于化学亲和力和取代系列的大量文献也源于牛顿主义的这种超机械论观点。相信不同化学物质之间存在差异性吸引力的化学家们设计了前所未有的实验，并探索新的反应类型。如果没有这一过程中积累的数据和化学概念，拉瓦锡，尤其是道尔顿后来的工作将难以理解。8规范问题、概念和解释标准的改变可以改变一门科学。在下一节中，我甚至会探讨它们如何改变世界。

The resulting change in the standards and problem-field of physical science was once again consequential. By the 1740’s, for example, electricians could speak of the attractive “virtue” of the electric fluid without thereby inviting the ridicule that had greeted Molière’s doctor a century before. As they did so, electrical phenomena increasingly displayed an order different from the one they had shown when viewed as the effects of a mechanical effluvium that could act only by contact. In particular, when electrical action-at-a-distance became a subject for study in its own right, the phenomenon we now call charging by induction could be recognized as one of its effects. Previously, when seen at all, it had been attributed to the direct action of electrical “atmospheres” or to the leakages inevitable in any electrical laboratory. The new view of inductive effects was, in turn, the key to Franklin’s analysis of the Leyden jar and thus to the emergence of a new and Newtonian paradigm for electricity. Nor were dynamics and electricity the only scientific fields affected by the legitimization of the search for forces innate to matter. The large body of eighteenth-century literature on chemical affinities and replacement series also derives from this supramechanical aspect of Newtonianism. Chemists who believed in these differential attractions between the various chemical species set up previously unimagined experiments and searched for new sorts of reactions. Without the data and the chemical concepts developed in that process, the later work of Lavoisier and, more particularly, of Dalton would be incomprehensible.8 Changes in the standards governing permissible problems, concepts, and explanations can transform a science. In the next section I shall even suggest a sense in which they transform the world.

在任何科学发展史的各个时期，我们几乎都能找到其他例子来说明不同范式之间这些非实质性的差异。目前，我们不妨只举两个更简短的例子。在化学革命之前，化学的一项公认任务是解释化学物质的性质及其变化。这些性质在化学反应中得以体现。化学家借助少量基本“原理”（燃素是其中之一）来解释为什么有些物质是酸性的，有些是金属性的，有些是可燃的等等。在这方面已经取得了一些成功。我们已经注意到，燃素解释了为什么金属如此相似，我们也可以对酸的性质提出类似的论证。然而，拉瓦锡的改革最终废除了化学“原理”，从而使化学失去了一些实际的和巨大的潜在解释力。为了弥补这一损失，需要改变标准。在19世纪的大部分时间里，无法解释化合物的性质并不意味着化学理论本身存在缺陷。9

Other examples of these nonsubstantive differences between successive paradigms can be retrieved from the history of any science in almost any period of its development. For the moment let us be content with just two other and far briefer illustrations. Before the chemical revolution, one of the acknowledged tasks of chemistry was to account for the qualities of chemical substances and for the changes these qualities underwent during chemical reactions. With the aid of a small number of elementary “principles”—of which phlogiston was one—the chemist was to explain why some substances are acidic, others metalline, combustible, and so forth. Some success in this direction had been achieved. We have already noted that phlogiston explained why the metals were so much alike, and we could have developed a similar argument for the acids. Lavoisier’s reform, however, ultimately did away with chemical “principles,” and thus ended by depriving chemistry of some actual and much potential explanatory power. To compensate for this loss, a change in standards was required. During much of the nineteenth century failure to explain the qualities of compounds was no indictment of a chemical theory.9

或者说，克拉克·麦克斯韦与十九世纪其他光波理论的支持者一样，坚信光波必须通过物质以太传播。设计一种能够支撑这种波的机械介质，是当时许多杰出学者面临的一个常见问题。然而，他自己的理论——光的电磁理论——却完全没有提及能够支撑光波的介质，而且显然使得构建这种介质的难度远超以往。最初，麦克斯韦的理论正是因为这些原因而遭到广泛否定。但是，就像牛顿的理论一样，麦克斯韦的理论也难以被摒弃，随着它逐渐成为一种范式，学术界对它的态度也发生了转变。到了二十世纪初，麦克斯韦对机械以太存在的坚持越来越像是空谈，而事实并非如此，因此，设计这种以太介质的尝试也随之放弃了。科学家们不再认为在不具体说明位移对象的情况下谈论电“位移”是不科学的。结果，又出现了一系列新的问题和标准，而这最终与相对论的出现密切相关。 10

Or again, Clerk Maxwell shared with other nineteenth-century proponents of the wave theory of light the conviction that light waves must be propagated through a material ether. Designing a mechanical medium to support such waves was a standard problem for many of his ablest contemporaries. His own theory, however, the electromagnetic theory of light, gave no account at all of a medium able to support light waves, and it clearly made such an account harder to provide than it had seemed before. Initially, Maxwell’s theory was widely rejected for those reasons. But, like Newton’s theory, Maxwell’s proved difficult to dispense with, and as it achieved the status of a paradigm, the community’s attitude toward it changed. In the early decades of the twentieth century Maxwell’s insistence upon the existence of a mechanical ether looked more and more like lip service, which it emphatically had not been, and the attempts to design such an ethereal medium were abandoned. Scientists no longer thought it unscientific to speak of an electrical “displacement” without specifying what was being displaced. The result, again, was a new set of problems and standards, one which, in the event, had much to do with the emergence of relativity theory.10

科学界观念的这些典型转变如果假设科学的合法问题和标准总是从方法论上较低的类型发展到方法论上较高的类型，那么它们对本文论点的意义就会大大降低。在这种情况下，它们的影响似乎也是累积性的。难怪一些历史学家认为，科学史记录了人类对科学本质的理解不断成熟和完善的过程。11然而，论证科学问题和标准的累积发展比论证理论的累积发展还要困难。尽管大多数十八世纪的科学家最终放弃了解释引力的尝试，但这并非针对一个本质上不合理的问题；对固有力的反对既非本质上不科学，也非某种贬义意义上的形而上学。没有外部标准允许我们做出这样的判断。所发生的既不是标准的下降，也不是标准的提升，而仅仅是新范式采纳所带来的变化。此外，这种变化后来已被逆转，而且可能再次逆转。在二十世纪，爱因斯坦成功地解释了引力，这一解释使科学回归到一套更接近牛顿前辈而非后辈的准则和问题之中。再者，量子力学的发展逆转了源于化学革命的方法论禁忌。如今，化学家们正尝试解释实验室中使用和生产的物质的颜色、聚集状态以及其他性质，并且取得了巨大的成功。类似的转变或许正在电磁理论中发生。在当代物理学中，空间不再是牛顿和麦克斯韦理论中所描述的那种惰性且均匀的基底；它的一些新特性与曾经归于以太的特性颇为相似；我们或许有一天能够了解电位移的本质。

These characteristic shifts in the scientific community’s conception of its legitimate problems and standards would have less significance to this essay’s thesis if one could suppose that they always occurred from some methodologically lower to some higher type. In that case their effects, too, would seem cumulative. No wonder that some historians have argued that the history of science records a continuing increase in the maturity and refinement of man’s conception of the nature of science.11 Yet the case for cumulative development of science’s problems and standards is even harder to make than the case for cumulation of theories. The attempt to explain gravity, though fruitfully abandoned by most eighteenth-century scientists, was not directed to an intrinsically illegitimate problem; the objections to innate forces were neither inherently unscientific nor metaphysical in some pejorative sense. There are no external standards to permit a judgment of that sort. What occurred was neither a decline nor a raising of standards, but simply a change demanded by the adoption of a new paradigm. Furthermore, that change has since been reversed and could be again. In the twentieth century Einstein succeeded in explaining gravitational attractions, and that explanation has returned science to a set of canons and problems that are, in this particular respect, more like those of Newton’s predecessors than of his successors. Or again, the development of quantum mechanics has reversed the methodological prohibition that originated in the chemical revolution. Chemists now attempt, and with great success, to explain the color, state of aggregation, and other qualities of the substances used and produced in their laboratories. A similar reversal may even be underway in electromagnetic theory. Space, in contemporary physics, is not the inert and homogenous substratum employed in both Newton’s and Maxwell’s theories; some of its new properties are not unlike those once attributed to the ether; we may someday come to know what an electric displacement is.

通过将重点从范式的认知功能转移到规范功能，上述例子加深了我们对范式的理解。本文探讨了范式如何塑造科学生活。此前，我们主要考察了范式作为科学理论载体的作用。在这一角色中，范式通过告知科学家自然界包含和不包含哪些实体，以及这些实体的行为方式来发挥作用。这些信息构成了一张地图，其细节则由成熟的科学研究加以阐明。由于自然界过于复杂多样，无法随意探索，因此这张地图对于科学的持续发展而言，与观察和实验同样重要。范式通过其所蕴含的理论，成为研究活动的构成要素。然而，范式在其他方面也构成了科学，而这正是本文的重点。特别是，我们最新的案例表明，范式不仅为科学家提供了一张地图，还提供了绘制地图所必需的一些方向。在学习范式的过程中，科学家同时习得了理论、方法和标准，而这三者通常是密不可分地融合在一起的。因此，当范式改变时，决定问题和所提解决方案合法性的标准通常也会发生重大变化。

By shifting emphasis from the cognitive to the normative functions of paradigms, the preceding examples enlarge our understanding of the ways in which paradigms give form to the scientific life. Previously, we had principally examined the paradigm’s role as a vehicle for scientific theory. In that role it functions by telling the scientist about the entities that nature does and does not contain and about the ways in which those entities behave. That information provides a map whose details are elucidated by mature scientific research. And since nature is too complex and varied to be explored at random, that map is as essential as observation and experiment to science’s continuing development. Through the theories they embody, paradigms prove to be constitutive of the research activity. They are also, however, constitutive of science in other respects, and that is now the point. In particular, our most recent examples show that paradigms provide scientists not only with a map but also with some of the directions essential for map-making. In learning a paradigm the scientist acquires theory, methods, and standards together, usually in an inextricable mixture. Therefore, when paradigms change, there are usually significant shifts in the criteria determining the legitimacy both of problems and of proposed solutions.

这一观察使我们回到本节的起点，因为它首次明确指出，为何在相互竞争的范式之间进行选择时，经常会引发一些无法用常规科学标准解决的问题。尽管这种分歧意义重大且并不全面，但两个科学流派对于何为问题、何为解决方案存在分歧，因此，在辩论各自范式的相对优劣时，它们必然会陷入互相掣肘的境地。在由此产生的部分循环论证中，每个范式都会被证明或多或少地满足了自身设定的标准，但却在某些方面未能达到对手设定的标准。此外，还有其他原因导致逻辑联系的不完整性，而这种不完整性恰恰是范式辩论的典型特征。例如，由于没有任何范式能够解决其定义的所有问题，也没有任何两个范式会留下所有未解决的问题，因此，范式辩论总是涉及这样一个问题：哪些问题更重要？与相互竞争的标准问题一样，这个价值判断问题只能用客观存在的标准来回答。它完全脱离了常规科学的范畴，而正是这种诉诸外部标准的做法，最明显地使得范式之争具有革命性意义。然而，比标准和价值观更为根本的东西也岌岌可危。到目前为止，我只是论证了范式是科学的构成要素。现在，我想阐明它们在某种意义上也是自然的构成要素。

That observation returns us to the point from which this section began, for it provides our first explicit indication of why the choice between competing paradigms regularly raises questions that cannot be resolved by the criteria of normal science. To the extent, as significant as it is incomplete, that two scientific schools disagree about what is a problem and what a solution, they will inevitably talk through each other when debating the relative merits of their respective paradigms. In the partially circular arguments that regularly result, each paradigm will be shown to satisfy more or less the criteria that it dictates for itself and to fall short of a few of those dictated by its opponent. There are other reasons, too, for the incompleteness of logical contact that consistently characterizes paradigm debates. For example, since no paradigm ever solves all the problems it defines and since no two paradigms leave all the same problems unsolved, paradigm debates always involve the question: Which problems is it more significant to have solved? Like the issue of competing standards, that question of values can be answered only in terms of criteria that lie outside of normal science altogether, and it is that recourse to external criteria that most obviously makes paradigm debates revolutionary. Something even more fundamental than standards and values is, however, also at stake. I have so far argued only that paradigms are constitutive of science. Now I wish to display a sense in which they are constitutive of nature as well.

[X]

革命即世界观的改变

Revolutions as Changes of World View

从当代史学的视角审视过往的研究记录，科学史学家或许会不禁感叹：范式转变之时，世界本身也随之改变。在新范式的引领下，科学家们采用新的仪器，探索新的领域。更重要的是，在变革时期，科学家们即便使用熟悉的仪器在以往研究过的地方进行观察，也会发现新的、不同的事物。这仿佛整个科学界突然被传送到了另一个星球，在那里，熟悉的事物以全新的视角呈现，同时还出现了许多陌生的事物。当然，现实中并没有发生如此巨大的变化：地理上的移植并不存在；在实验室之外，日常生活通常依然如常。然而，范式转变确实促使科学家们以不同的视角看待他们所研究的世界。鉴于他们了解这个世界的唯一途径是通过他们的所见所闻和所作所为，我们可以说，在一次变革之后，科学家们面对的是一个截然不同的世界。

Examining the record of past research from the vantage of contemporary historiography, the historian of science may be tempted to exclaim that when paradigms change, the world itself changes with them. Led by a new paradigm, scientists adopt new instruments and look in new places. Even more important, during revolutions scientists see new and different things when looking with familiar instruments in places they have looked before. It is rather as if the professional community had been suddenly transported to another planet where familiar objects are seen in a different light and are joined by unfamiliar ones as well. Of course, nothing of quite that sort does occur: there is no geographical transplantation; outside the laboratory everyday affairs usually continue as before. Nevertheless, paradigm changes do cause scientists to see the world of their research-engagement differently. In so far as their only recourse to that world is through what they see and do, we may want to say that after a revolution scientists are responding to a different world.

正是作为科学家世界转变的基本原型，那些熟悉的视觉格式塔转换演示才如此具有启发性。在科学家的世界里，鸭子究竟是什么？革命前如同兔子，革命后如同兔子。最初从上方观察盒子外部的人，后来从下方观察盒子内部。诸如此类的转变，虽然通常更为渐进且几乎总是不可逆的，却是科学训练中常见的伴随现象。学生看等高线图，看到的是纸上的线条；制图师看到的是地形图。学生看气泡室照片，看到的是混乱断裂的线条；物理学家看到的是熟悉的亚核事件记录。只有经历了多次这样的视角转变，学生才能真正融入科学家的世界，看到科学家所看到的，并做出与科学家相同的反应。然而，学生随后进入的世界并非由环境本身或科学的本质一成不变。相反，它是由环境和学生所接受训练的特定常规科学传统共同决定的。因此，在变革时期，当传统的科学观念发生改变时，科学家对环境的感知必须重新调整——在某些熟悉的情境中，他必须学会以全新的视角看待事物。完成这一转变后，他所研究的世界在某些方面会显得与他以往所处的世界截然不同。这也是不同范式指导下的学派之间总是存在一些分歧的另一个原因。

It is as elementary prototypes for these transformations of the scientist’s world that the familiar demonstrations of a switch in visual gestalt prove so suggestive. What were ducks in the scientist’s world before the revolution are rabbits afterwards. The man who first saw the exterior of the box from above later sees its interior from below. Transformations like these, though usually more gradual and almost always irreversible, are common concomitants of scientific training. Looking at a contour map, the student sees lines on paper, the cartographer a picture of a terrain. Looking at a bubble-chamber photograph, the student sees confused and broken lines, the physicist a record of familiar subnuclear events. Only after a number of such transformations of vision does the student become an inhabitant of the scientist’s world, seeing what the scientist sees and responding as the scientist does. The world that the student then enters is not, however, fixed once and for all by the nature of the environment, on the one hand, and of science, on the other. Rather, it is determined jointly by the environment and the particular normal-scientific tradition that the student has been trained to pursue. Therefore, at times of revolution, when the normal-scientific tradition changes, the scientist’s perception of his environment must be re-educated—in some familiar situations he must learn to see a new gestalt. After he has done so the world of his research will seem, here and there, incommensurable with the one he had inhabited before. That is another reason why schools guided by different paradigms are always slightly at cross-purposes.

当然，格式塔实验最常见的形式仅仅揭示了知觉转换的本质。它们无法告诉我们范式或先前吸收的经验在知觉过程中的作用。但关于这一点，心理学文献浩如烟海，其中许多都源于汉诺威研究所的开创性工作。实验对象戴上装有倒置镜片的护目镜后，最初看到的整个世界都是颠倒的。起初，他的知觉系统像未戴护目镜时那样运作，结果是极度迷失方向，引发严重的个人危机。但当受试者开始适应这个新世界后，他的整个视野​​就会翻转过来，通常是在一段视觉混乱的过渡期之后。此后，物体又恢复到戴护目镜之前的样子。先前异常经验的吸收视觉领域本身已经对领域本身做出了反应并发生了改变。1无论从字面意义还是比喻意义上来说，习惯于反转透镜的人已经经历了视觉的革命性转变。

In their most usual form, of course, gestalt experiments illustrate only the nature of perceptual transformations. They tell us nothing about the role of paradigms or of previously assimilated experience in the process of perception. But on that point there is a rich body of psychological literature, much of it stemming from the pioneering work of the Hanover Institute. An experimental subject who puts on goggles fitted with inverting lenses initially sees the entire world upside down. At the start his perceptual apparatus functions as it had been trained to function in the absence of the goggles, and the result is extreme disorientation, an acute personal crisis. But after the subject has begun to learn to deal with his new world, his entire visual field flips over, usually after an intervening period in which vision is simply confused. Thereafter, objects are again seen as they had been before the goggles were put on. The assimilation of a previously anomalous visual field has reacted upon and changed the field itself.1 Literally as well as metaphorically, the man accustomed to inverting lenses has undergone a revolutionary transformation of vision.

第六节讨论的异常扑克牌实验的受试者经历了非常相似的转变。在经过长时间的接触，认识到宇宙中存在异常扑克牌之前，他们只能看到那些他们之前经验所赋予的扑克牌类型。然而，一旦经验提供了必要的其他类别，他们就能在第一次观察时就看到所有异常扑克牌，并且观察时间足够长，足以进行任何识别。其他实验也表明，实验中展示的物体的感知大小、颜色等等也会随着受试者之前的训练和经验而变化。2纵观这些例子所依据的大量实验文献，人们不禁怀疑，某种范式是感知本身的前提。一个人所看到的，既取决于他所看的东西，也取决于他之前的视觉概念经验教会他如何看待事物。如果没有这种训练，正如威廉·詹姆斯所说，只会是“一团乱麻”。

The subjects of the anomalous playing-card experiment discussed in Section VI experienced a quite similar transformation. Until taught by prolonged exposure that the universe contained anomalous cards, they saw only the types of cards for which previous experience had equipped them. Yet once experience had provided the requisite additional categories, they were able to see all anomalous cards on the first inspection long enough to permit any identification at all. Still other experiments demonstrate that the perceived size, color, and so on, of experimentally displayed objects also varies with the subject’s previous training and experience.2 Surveying the rich experimental literature from which these examples are drawn makes one suspect that something like a paradigm is prerequisite to perception itself. What a man sees depends both upon what he looks at and also upon what his previous visual-conceptual experience has taught him to see. In the absence of such training there can only be, in William James’s phrase, “a bloomin’ buzzin’ confusion.”

近年来，一些研究科学史的学者发现上述实验极具启发性。特别是NR Hanson，他运用格式塔演示来阐述一些与我在此关注的科学信念后果相同的问题。3其他一些同事也反复指出，如果假设科学家偶尔会经历类似上述的感知转变，那么科学史的研究将会更加清晰连贯。然而，尽管心理学方面……实验具有启发性，就其本质而言，它们的作用仅限于此。它们确实展现了一些可能对科学发展至关重要的感知特征，但它们并不能证明科研人员所进行的谨慎且受控的观察本身就具备这些特征。此外，这些实验的性质本身就使得直接论证这一点成为不可能。如果历史例证要使这些心理学实验显得具有现实意义，我们首先必须注意到历史可能提供和不可能提供的证据类型。

In recent years several of those concerned with the history of science have found the sorts of experiments described above immensely suggestive. N. R. Hanson, in particular, has used gestalt demonstrations to elaborate some of the same consequences of scientific belief that concern me here.3 Other colleagues have repeatedly noted that history of science would make better and more coherent sense if one could suppose that scientists occasionally experienced shifts of perception like those described above. Yet, though psychological experiments are suggestive, they cannot, in the nature of the case, be more than that. They do display characteristics of perception that could be central to scientific development, but they do not demonstrate that the careful and controlled observation exercised by the research scientist at all partakes of those characteristics. Furthermore, the very nature of these experiments makes any direct demonstration of that point impossible. If historical example is to make these psychological experiments seem relevant, we must first notice the sorts of evidence that we may and may not expect history to provide.

格式塔演示的受试者之所以知道自己的感知发生了变化，是因为他可以反复地在手中拿着同一本书或一张纸的情况下，让感知来回切换。他意识到周围环境没有任何变化，于是逐渐将注意力从图形（鸭子或兔子）转移到他正在看的纸上的线条上。最终，他甚至可能学会只看到线条而不看到任何图形，这时他可能会说（这是他之前无法合理表达的），他真正看到的是这些线条，只是他交替地将它们看作鸭子和兔子。同样，异常纸牌实验的受试者也知道（或者更准确地说，可以被说服）自己的感知一定发生了变化，因为实验者——一个外部权威——向他保证，无论他看到了什么，他始终看到的都是一张黑桃五。在这两种情况下，以及所有类似的心理学实验中，演示的有效性都取决于它是否能够以这种方式进行分析。除非存在一个外部标准来证明视觉的转换，否则就无法得出关于其他感知可能性的结论。

The subject of a gestalt demonstration knows that his perception has shifted because he can make it shift back and forth repeatedly while he holds the same book or piece of paper in his hands. Aware that nothing in his environment has changed, he directs his attention increasingly not to the figure (duck or rabbit) but to the lines on the paper he is looking at. Ultimately he may even learn to see those lines without seeing either of the figures, and he may then say (what he could not legitimately have said earlier) that it is these lines that he really sees but that he sees them alternately as a duck and as a rabbit. By the same token, the subject of the anomalous card experiment knows (or, more accurately, can be persuaded) that his perception must have shifted because an external authority, the experimenter, assures him that regardless of what he saw, he was looking at a black five of hearts all the time. In both these cases, as in all similar psychological experiments, the effectiveness of the demonstration depends upon its being analyzable in this way. Unless there were an external standard with respect to which a switch of vision could be demonstrated, no conclusion about alternate perceptual possibilities could be drawn.

然而，在科学观察中，情况恰恰相反。科学家只能依靠肉眼和仪器所观察到的事物，别无他法。如果存在某种更高的权威，可以用来证明科学家的观察结果发生了改变，那么这种权威本身就会成为数据的来源，而科学家的观察行为本身也会成为问题的根源（就像实验对象对心理学家而言一样）。如果科学家可以随意切换观察结果，也会出现同样的问题。就像格式塔实验的对象一样。光“有时是波，有时是粒子”的时期是一个危机时期——一个出了问题的时期——直到波动力学发展起来，人们才认识到光是一个自洽的实体，既不同于波也不同于粒子，这一时期才结束。因此，在科学领域，如果认知转变伴随着范式转变，我们或许不应期望科学家直接证实这些转变。例如，皈依哥白尼学派的人在观察月球时，不会说：“我以前看到的是行星，但现在看到的是卫星。”这样的说法暗示着托勒密体系曾经是正确的。相反，皈依新天文学的人会说：“我曾经认为（或看到）月球是行星，但我错了。”这种说法在科学革命之后确实会反复出现。如果它通常掩盖的是科学视野的转变或其他具有相同效果的思维转变，那么我们或许不应期待直接的证据来证明这种转变。相反，我们必须寻找间接的、行为上的证据，来证明拥有新范式的科学家看待事物的方式与以往有所不同。

With scientific observation, however, the situation is exactly reversed. The scientist can have no recourse above or beyond what he sees with his eyes and instruments. If there were some higher authority by recourse to which his vision might be shown to have shifted, then that authority would itself become the source of his data, and the behavior of his vision would become a source of problems (as that of the experimental subject is for the psychologist). The same sorts of problems would arise if the scientist could switch back and forth like the subject of the gestalt experiments. The period during which light was “sometimes a wave and sometimes a particle” was a period of crisis—a period when something was wrong—and it ended only with the development of wave mechanics and the realization that light was a self-consistent entity different from both waves and particles. In the sciences, therefore, if perceptual switches accompany paradigm changes, we may not expect scientists to attest to these changes directly. Looking at the moon, the convert to Copernicanism does not say, “I used to see a planet, but now I see a satellite.” That locution would imply a sense in which the Ptolemaic system had once been correct. Instead, a convert to the new astronomy says, “I once took the moon to be (or saw the moon as) a planet, but I was mistaken.” That sort of statement does recur in the aftermath of scientific revolutions. If it ordinarily disguises a shift of scientific vision or some other mental transformation with the same effect, we may not expect direct testimony about that shift. Rather we must look for indirect and behavioral evidence that the scientist with a new paradigm sees differently from the way he had seen before.

那么，让我们回到数据本身，探究一下相信此类变化的历史学家能够发现科学家世界中的哪些转变。威廉·赫歇尔爵士对天王星的发现便是一个例证，它与异常卡片实验极为相似。在1690年至1781年间，至少有17位天文学家，包括几位欧洲最杰出的观测者，都观测到一颗恒星出现在我们现在认为当时天王星所在的位置。其中一位最优秀的观测者甚至在1769年连续四个晚上观测到这颗恒星，却没有注意到任何可能指向其他天体的运动。12年后，赫歇尔首次观测到同一天体时，使用的是他自己制造的改进型望远镜。因此，他注意到这颗恒星的视直径至少对于恒星而言是异常的。他意识到情况不对劲，因此推迟了对天体的鉴定，等待进一步的观察。那次仔细观察揭示了天王星在群星中的运动，因此赫歇尔宣布他看到了一颗新的彗星！仅仅几个月后，在徒劳无功的尝试之后，他才发现了这颗彗星。莱克塞尔曾尝试将观测到的运动与彗星轨道进行拟合，但他随后提出该天体很可能是行星轨道。4当这一观点被接受后，专业天文学家眼中的恒星数量减少了几颗，而行星数量增加了一颗。一个断断续续观测了近一个世纪的天体，在1781年后被赋予了不同的意义，因为它就像一张特殊的扑克牌，无法再被纳入先前盛行的范式所提供的认知范畴（恒星或彗星）。

Let us then return to the data and ask what sorts of transformations in the scientist’s world the historian who believes in such changes can discover. Sir William Herschel’s discovery of Uranus provides a first example and one that closely parallels the anomalous card experiment. On at least seventeen different occasions between 1690 and 1781, a number of astronomers, including several of Europe’s most eminent observers, had seen a star in positions that we now suppose must have been occupied at the time by Uranus. One of the best observers in this group had actually seen the star on four successive nights in 1769 without noting the motion that could have suggested another identification. Herschel, when he first observed the same object twelve years later, did so with a much improved telescope of his own manufacture. As a result, he was able to notice an apparent disk-size that was at least unusual for stars. Something was awry, and he therefore postponed identification pending further scrutiny. That scrutiny disclosed Uranus’ motion among the stars, and Herschel therefore announced that he had seen a new comet! Only several months later, after fruitless attempts to fit the observed motion to a cometary orbit, did Lexell suggest that the orbit was probably planetary.4 When that suggestion was accepted, there were several fewer stars and one more planet in the world of the professional astronomer. A celestial body that had been observed off and on for almost a century was seen differently after 1781 because, like an anomalous playing card, it could no longer be fitted to the perceptual categories (star or comet) provided by the paradigm that had previously prevailed.

使天文学家得以观测到天王星这颗行星的视角转变，似乎并非仅仅影响了人们对这颗先前观测到的天体的认知。其影响更为深远。尽管证据尚不明确，但赫歇尔促成的这一微小的范式转变，或许有助于天文学家在1801年后迅速发现众多的小行星或小行星。由于体积较小，这些天体并未展现出赫歇尔所察觉的那种异常放大效应。然而，做好了寻找更多行星准备的天文学家，凭借标准仪器，在19世纪的前50年里就识别出了其中的20颗。5天文学史上还有许多其他由范式转变引发科学认知变化的例子，其中一些甚至更加明确。例如，西方天文学家在哥白尼提出新范式后的半个世纪里首次观测到先前一成不变的星空发生变化，这难道仅仅是一个巧合吗？中国人的宇宙观并不排除天体变化，他们早在很久以前就记录了许多新星的出现。此外，即使没有望远镜的辅助，中国人也在伽利略及其同时代人观测到太阳黑子之前的几个世纪，系统地记录了太阳黑子的出现。6太阳黑子和新星并非唯一发现的天象。在哥白尼之后，西方天文学中很快就出现了天体变化的例证。十六世纪末的天文学家们使用传统仪器——有些甚至只是一根线——反复发现彗星可以随意穿梭于此前被认为是永恒不变的行星和恒星的空间。7 天文学家们用旧仪器观测旧天体时，如此轻松快捷地发现新现象，这或许会让我们觉得，哥白尼之后的天文学家们仿佛生活在一个截然不同的世界。无论如何，他们的研究成果也印证了这一点。

The shift of vision that enabled astronomers to see Uranus, the planet, does not, however, seem to have affected only the perception of that previously observed object. Its consequences were more far-reaching. Probably, though the evidence is equivocal, the minor paradigm change forced by Herschel helped to prepare astronomers for the rapid discovery, after 1801, of the numerous minor planets or asteroids. Because of their small size, these did not display the anomalous magnification that had alerted Herschel. Nevertheless, astronomers prepared to find additional planets were able, with standard instruments, to identify twenty of them in the first fifty years of the nineteenth century.5 The history of astronomy provides many other examples of paradigm-induced changes in scientific perception, some of them even less equivocal. Can it conceivably be an accident, for example, that Western astronomers first saw change in the previously immutable heavens during the half-century after Copernicus’ new paradigm was first proposed? The Chinese, whose cosmological beliefs did not preclude celestial change, had recorded the appearance of many new stars in the heavens at a much earlier date. Also, even without the aid of a telescope, the Chinese had systematically recorded the appearance of sunspots centuries before these were seen by Galileo and his contemporaries.6 Nor were sunspots and a new star the only examples of celestial change to emerge in the heavens of Western astronomy immediately after Copernicus. Using traditional instruments, some as simple as a piece of thread, late sixteenth-century astronomers repeatedly discovered that comets wandered at will through the space previously reserved for the immutable planets and stars.7 The very ease and rapidity with which astronomers saw new things when looking at old objects with old instruments may make us wish to say that, after Copernicus, astronomers lived in a different world. In any case, their research responded as though that were the case.

以上例子均选自天文学，因为天体观测报告通常使用相对纯粹的观测术语。只有在这类报告中，我们才能找到科学家观察结果与心理学家实验对象观察结果之间较为完整的对应关系。但我们不必执着于这种完整的对应关系，放宽标准反而会让我们受益匪浅。如果我们能接受“看”这个动词的日常用法，我们或许会很快意识到，我们已经遇到过许多其他例子，它们都体现了伴随范式转变而来的科学认知变化。“感知”和“看”这两个词的扩展用法很快就需要明确的论证，但首先让我举例说明它们在实践中的应用。

The preceding examples are selected from astronomy because reports of celestial observation are frequently delivered in a vocabulary consisting of relatively pure observation terms. Only in such reports can we hope to find anything like a full parallelism between the observations of scientists and those of the psychologist’s experimental subjects. But we need not insist on so full a parallelism, and we have much to gain by relaxing our standard. If we can be content with the everyday use of the verb ‘to see,’ we may quickly recognize that we have already encountered many other examples of the shifts in scientific perception that accompany paradigm change. The extended use of ‘perception’ and of ‘seeing’ will shortly require explicit defense, but let me first illustrate its application in practice.

让我们再回顾一下之前提到的两个电学史上的例子。在十七世纪，当电工们的研究受到各种“逸散物理论”的指导时，他们反复观察到，吸引它们的带电物体上的金属屑颗粒会反弹或脱落。至少十七世纪的观察者是这么说的，我们没有理由怀疑他们的观察记录，就像我们没有理由怀疑我们自己的观察记录一样。如果将金属屑颗粒置于同样的装置前，现代观察者会看到静电斥力（而不是机械或引力反弹），但在历史上，除了一个普遍被忽略的例外，直到豪克斯比的大型装置极大地放大了静电斥力效应之后，人们才真正观察到静电斥力。然而，接触起电后的斥力现象却并非如此。这是豪克斯比观察到的众多新的排斥效应之一。通过他的研究，如同格式塔开关一般，排斥突然成为起电的基本表现形式，而吸引则需要加以解释。8十八世纪早期人们所观察到的电现象比十七世纪的观察者所观察到的更为微妙和多样。或者说，在吸收了富兰克林的范式之后，电工观察莱顿瓶时看到了与以往不同的景象。该装置变成了电容器，不再需要瓶状结构或玻璃材质。取而代之的是两层导电涂层——其中一层并非原始装置的一部分——变得尤为重要。正如文字讨论和图像逐渐证实的那样，两块金属板之间夹着非导体，成为了此类电容器的原型。9与此同时，其他一些感应效应得到了新的描述，还有一些效应则是首次被记录下来。

Look again for a moment at two of our previous examples from the history of electricity. During the seventeenth century, when their research was guided by one or another effluvium theory, electricians repeatedly saw chaff particles rebound from, or fall off, the electrified bodies that had attracted them. At least that is what seventeenth-century observers said they saw, and we have no more reason to doubt their reports of perception than our own. Placed before the same apparatus, a modern observer would see electrostatic repulsion (rather than mechanical or gravitational rebounding), but historically, with one universally ignored exception, electrostatic repulsion was not seen as such until Hauksbee’s large-scale apparatus had greatly magnified its effects. Repulsion after contact electrification was, however, only one of many new repulsive effects that Hauksbee saw. Through his researches, rather as in a gestalt switch, repulsion suddenly became the fundamental manifestation of electrification, and it was then attraction that needed to be explained.8 The electrical phenomena visible in the early eighteenth century were both subtler and more varied than those seen by observers in the seventeenth century. Or again, after the assimilation of Franklin’s paradigm, the electrician looking at a Leyden jar saw something different from what he had seen before. The device had become a condenser, for which neither the jar shape nor glass was required. Instead, the two conducting coatings—one of which had been no part of the original device—emerged to prominence. As both written discussions and pictorial representations gradually attest, two metal plates with a non-conductor between them had become the prototype for the class.9 Simultaneously, other inductive effects received new descriptions, and still others were noted for the first time.

这种转变并非仅限于天文学和电学领域。我们已经注意到，化学史上也存在一些类似的观念转变。我们说过，拉瓦锡在普里斯特利看到的是脱燃素的空气，而其他人则什么也看不到的地方，看到了氧气。然而，在学会观察氧气的同时，拉瓦锡也必须改变他对许多其他更熟悉的物质的看法。例如，他必须将普里斯特利及其同时代人视为基本土的物质视为一种复合矿石，除此之外还有其他类似的转变。至少，由于发现了氧气，拉瓦锡对自然的看法发生了改变。在缺乏某种假设性的固定自然（即他“以不同方式看待”的自然）的情况下，出于简洁性的考虑，我们可以说，拉瓦锡在发现氧气之后，进入了一个截然不同的世界。

Shifts of this sort are not restricted to astronomy and electricity. We have already remarked some of the similar transformations of vision that can be drawn from the history of chemistry.
