Lavoisier, we said, saw oxygen where Priestley had seen dephlogisticated air and where others had seen nothing at all. In learning to see oxygen, however, Lavoisier also had to change his view of many other more familiar substances. He had, for example, to see a compound ore where Priestley and his contemporaries had seen an elementary earth, and there were other such changes besides. At the very least, as a result of discovering oxygen, Lavoisier saw nature differently. And in the absence of some recourse to that hypothetical fixed nature that he “saw differently,” the principle of economy will urge us to say that after discovering oxygen Lavoisier worked in a different world.

我稍后会探讨如何避免使用这种奇怪的表达方式，但首先我们需要另一个使用例子，这个例子出自某部作品中最著名的部分之一。伽利略。自古以来，大多数人都见过重物在绳索或链条上来回摆动，直至最终静止。亚里士多德学派认为，重物会自然地从高处运动到低处并达到自然静止状态，因此，摆动的物体只是在艰难地下落。由于受到链条的束缚，它只能经过曲折的运动和相当长的时间才能到达最低点并停止。然而，伽利略观察摆动的物体，看到的却是一个钟摆，一个几乎能够无限重复相同运动的物体。基于此，伽利略进一步观察了钟摆的其他特性，并围绕这些特性构建了他新动力学理论中许多最重要、最具原创性的部分。例如，伽利略正是从钟摆的特性出发，推导出了他唯一完整且可靠的论证，证明了物体的重量和下落速度是独立的，以及物体沿斜面运动的垂直高度和最终速度之间的关系。10他以不同于以往的方式看待所有这些自然现象。

I shall inquire in a moment about the possibility of avoiding this strange locution, but first we require an additional example of its use, this one deriving from one of the best known parts of the work of Galileo. Since remote antiquity most people have seen one or another heavy body swinging back and forth on a string or chain until it finally comes to rest. To the Aristotelians, who believed that a heavy body is moved by its own nature from a higher position to a state of natural rest at a lower one, the swinging body was simply falling with difficulty. Constrained by the chain, it could achieve rest at its low point only after a tortuous motion and a considerable time. Galileo, on the other hand, looking at the swinging body, saw a pendulum, a body that almost succeeded in repeating the same motion over and over again ad infinitum. And having seen that much, Galileo observed other properties of the pendulum as well and constructed many of the most significant and original parts of his new dynamics around them. From the properties of the pendulum, for example, Galileo derived his only full and sound arguments for the independence of weight and rate of fall, as well as for the relationship between vertical height and terminal velocity of motions down inclined planes.10 All these natural phenomena he saw differently from the way they had been seen before.

这种视角转变是如何发生的？当然，这要归功于伽利略的个人天赋。但需要注意的是，这里的天赋并非体现在对摆动物体的观察更加精确或客观上。从描述的角度来看，亚里士多德式的感知同样准确。当伽利略报告说，摆的周期与振幅无关，即使振幅高达90°时，他对摆的观察也使他看到了比我们现在所能发现的更多的规律性。 11相反，这似乎与天才对中世纪范式转变所带来的感知可能性的运用有关。伽利略并非完全接受亚里士多德式的教育。相反，他接受的训练是用冲力理论来分析运动的。冲力理论是中世纪晚期的一种范式，它认为重物的持续运动是由于其运动的发起者赋予它的内在动力。十四世纪的经院哲学家让·布里丹和妮可·奥雷斯姆将冲力理论带到了现代。布里丹是已知最早在振荡运动中观察到伽利略所见现象的人，他提出的理论最为完善。布里丹将振动弦的运动描述为：弦被敲击时首先产生动量；随后，动量被消耗在克服张力阻力使弦振动；张力使弦振动回弹，并产生越来越大的动量，直至到达运动的中点；之后，动量再次使弦沿相反方向振动，同样克服张力阻力，如此往复，形成一个可以无限循环的对称过程。本世纪晚些时候，奥雷姆对摆动的石头进行了类似的分析，这被认为是首次对摆的讨论。 12他的观点显然与伽利略最初对摆的研究非常接近。至少在奥雷斯姆的例子中，几乎可以肯定在伽利略的例子中也是如此，这种观点的出现得益于运动范式从最初的亚里士多德式向经院式动力范式的转变。在经院式范式出现之前，科学家们看到的只有摆动的石头，而没有钟摆。钟摆的出现，正是源于某种范式转变引发的认知转变。

Why did that shift of vision occur? Through Galileo’s individual genius, of course. But note that genius does not here manifest itself in more accurate or objective observation of the swinging body. Descriptively, the Aristotelian perception is just as accurate. When Galileo reported that the pendulum’s period was independent of amplitude for amplitudes as great as 90°, his view of the pendulum led him to see far more regularity than we can now discover there.11 Rather, what seems to have been involved was the exploitation by genius of perceptual possibilities made available by a medieval paradigm shift. Galileo was not raised completely as an Aristotelian. On the contrary, he was trained to analyze motions in terms of the impetus theory, a late medieval paradigm which held that the continuing motion of a heavy body is due to an internal power implanted in it by the projector that initiated its motion. Jean Buridan and Nicole Oresme, the fourteenth-century scholastics who brought the impetus theory to its most perfect formulations, are the first men known to have seen in oscillatory motions any part of what Galileo saw there. Buridan describes the motion of a vibrating string as one in which impetus is first implanted when the string is struck; the impetus is next consumed in displacing the string against the resistance of its tension; tension then carries the string back, implanting increasing impetus until the mid-point of motion is reached; after that the impetus displaces the string in the opposite direction, again against the string’s tension, and so on in a symmetric process that may continue indefinitely. Later in the century Oresme sketched a similar analysis of the swinging stone in what now appears as the first discussion of a pendulum.12 His view is clearly very close to the one with which Galileo first approached the pendulum. At least in Oresme’s case, and almost certainly in Galileo’s as well, it was a view made possible by the transition from the original Aristotelian to the scholastic impetus paradigm for motion. Until that scholastic paradigm was invented, there were no pendulums, but only swinging stones, for the scientist to see. Pendulums were brought into existence by something very like a paradigm-induced gestalt switch.

然而，我们真的需要将伽利略与亚里士多德、拉瓦锡与普里斯特利之间的区别描述为一种视觉上的转变吗？这些人观察同类物体时，真的看到了不同的东西吗？我们真的能说他们是在不同的领域进行研究吗？这些问题不容忽视，因为显然还有另一种更为常见的解释方式来阐述上述所有历史案例。许多读者肯定会认为，范式转变所改变的仅仅是科学家对观察结果的解读，而观察结果本身则由环境和感知机制的本质决定，是一劳永逸的。按照这种观点，普里斯特利和拉瓦锡都看到了氧气，但他们对观察结果的解读不同；亚里士多德和伽利略都看到了摆，但他们对所见之物的解释也不同。

Do we, however, really need to describe what separates Galileo from Aristotle, or Lavoisier from Priestley, as a transformation of vision? Did these men really see different things when looking at the same sorts of objects? Is there any legitimate sense in which we can say that they pursued their research in different worlds? Those questions can no longer be postponed, for there is obviously another and far more usual way to describe all of the historical examples outlined above. Many readers will surely want to say that what changes with a paradigm is only the scientist’s interpretation of observations that themselves are fixed once and for all by the nature of the environment and of the perceptual apparatus. On this view, Priestley and Lavoisier both saw oxygen, but they interpreted their observations differently; Aristotle and Galileo both saw pendulums, but they differed in their interpretations of what they both had seen.

首先我要指出，这种关于科学家在基本问题上改变想法的常见观点，既非完全错误，也非仅仅是一个错误。相反，它是笛卡尔开创的哲学范式的重要组成部分，该范式与牛顿动力学几乎同时发展起来。这一范式对科学和哲学都大有裨益。它的应用，如同动力学本身的应用一样，促成了一种或许无法通过其他途径获得的根本性理解。但正如牛顿动力学的例子也表明的那样，即使是过去最显著的成功也无法保证危机可以无限期地推迟。如今，哲学、心理学、语言学乃至艺术史等领域的研究都指向同一个结论：传统范式在某种程度上存在偏差。而我们在此必须重点关注的科学史研究，也日益凸显了这种不适用性。

Let me say at once that this very usual view of what occurs when scientists change their minds about fundamental matters can be neither all wrong nor a mere mistake. Rather it is an essential part of a philosophical paradigm initiated by Descartes and developed at the same time as Newtonian dynamics. That paradigm has served both science and philosophy well. Its exploitation, like that of dynamics itself, has been fruitful of a fundamental understanding that perhaps could not have been achieved in another way. But as the example of Newtonian dynamics also indicates, even the most striking past success provides no guarantee that crisis can be indefinitely postponed. Today research in parts of philosophy, psychology, linguistics, and even art history, all converge to suggest that the traditional paradigm is somehow askew. That failure to fit is also made increasingly apparent by the historical study of science to which most of our attention is necessarily directed here.

这些引发危机的议题尚未提出任何可行的替代传统认识论范式的方案，但它们确实开始揭示该范式的一些特征。例如，我深切地意识到，如果说亚里士多德和伽利略观察摆动的石头时，前者看到的是受限的下落，后者看到的是钟摆，这种说法会带来诸多难题。本节开篇的几句话以更为根本的形式呈现了同样的难题：尽管范式的改变不会改变世界，但科学家此后所处的世界却截然不同。然而，我确信我们必须学会理解至少与此类似的陈述。科学革命期间发生的一切都不能完全简化为对单个稳定数据的重新诠释。首先，数据本身并非绝对稳定。钟摆并非下落的石头，氧气也并非脱燃素的空气。因此，正如我们稍后将看到的，科学家从这些不同的对象中收集到的数据本身就各不相同。更重要的是，无论是个人还是群体，从受限的下落状态过渡到钟摆状态，或者从脱燃素空气过渡到氧气状态的过程，都与诠释截然不同。在缺乏可供科学家诠释的固定数据的情况下，它又如何能够做到这一点呢？作为一名诠释者，拥抱新范式的科学家就像戴着倒置眼镜的人。他面对的依然是同样的物体，并且明知如此，却发现它们的许多细节都已彻底改变。

None of these crisis-promoting subjects has yet produced a viable alternate to the traditional epistemological paradigm, but they do begin to suggest what some of that paradigm’s characteristics will be. I am, for example, acutely aware of the difficulties created by saying that when Aristotle and Galileo looked at swinging stones, the first saw constrained fall, the second a pendulum. The same difficulties are presented in an even more fundamental form by the opening sentences of this section: though the world does not change with a change of paradigm, the scientist afterward works in a different world. Nevertheless, I am convinced that we must learn to make sense of statements that at least resemble these. What occurs during a scientific revolution is not fully reducible to a reinterpretation of individual and stable data. In the first place, the data are not unequivocally stable. A pendulum is not a falling stone, nor is oxygen dephlogisticated air. Consequently, the data that scientists collect from these diverse objects are, as we shall shortly see, themselves different. More important, the process by which either the individual or the community makes the transition from constrained fall to the pendulum or from dephlogisticated air to oxygen is not one that resembles interpretation. How could it do so in the absence of fixed data for the scientist to interpret? Rather than being an interpreter, the scientist who embraces a new paradigm is like the man wearing inverting lenses. Confronting the same constellation of objects as before and knowing that he does so, he nevertheless finds them transformed through and through in many of their details.

这些论述并非意在表明科学家通常不会对观察结果和数据进行解释。恰恰相反，伽利略解释了对摆锤的观察结果，亚里士多德解释了对落石的观察结果，穆申布鲁克解释了对带电瓶子的观察结果，富兰克林解释了对冷凝器的观察结果。但每一种解释都预设了一种范式。它们是常规科学的一部分，正如我们已经看到的，常规科学旨在完善、扩展和阐明已有的范式。第三部分提供了许多解释发挥核心作用的例子。这些例子代表了绝大多数研究的典型特征。在每个例子中，科学家都基于公认的范式，知道什么是数据，可以使用哪些仪器来获取数据，以及哪些概念与数据的解释相关。在既定的范式下，对数据的解释是探索该范式的核心。

None of these remarks is intended to indicate that scientists do not characteristically interpret observations and data. On the contrary, Galileo interpreted observations on the pendulum, Aristotle observations on falling stones, Musschenbroek observations on a charge-filled bottle, and Franklin observations on a condenser. But each of these interpretations presupposed a paradigm. They were parts of normal science, an enterprise that, as we have already seen, aims to refine, extend, and articulate a paradigm that is already in existence. Section III provided many examples in which interpretation played a central role. Those examples typify the overwhelming majority of research. In each of them the scientist, by virtue of an accepted paradigm, knew what a datum was, what instruments might be used to retrieve it, and what concepts were relevant to its interpretation. Given a paradigm, interpretation of data is central to the enterprise that explores it.

但这种诠释性的努力——这也是倒数第二段的重点——只能阐明一种范式，而不能纠正它。范式根本无法通过常规科学进行修正。相反，正如我们已经看到的，常规科学最终只会导致对异常现象和危机的认识。而这些危机的终结，并非通过深思熟虑和诠释，而是通过一种相对突然且非结构化的事件，例如“格式塔转换”。科学家们常常用“醍醐灌顶”或“灵光乍现”来形容这种顿悟，它“照亮”了先前晦涩难懂的谜题，使人们能够以一种全新的视角看待其组成部分，从而首次找到答案。有时，相关的顿悟甚至出现在睡梦中。 13 “诠释”一词的任何通常含义都无法涵盖这些灵光乍现的直觉，通过这些直觉，新范式由此诞生。尽管此类直觉依赖于旧范式下获得的经验（包括异常经验和一致经验），但它们并非像诠释那样，与该经验的特定部分进行逻辑或零散的关联。相反，它们汇集了该经验的大部分，并将其转化为一种截然不同的经验集合，这种集合随后将零散地与新范式关联起来，但与旧范式无关。

But that interpretive enterprise—and this was the burden of the paragraph before last—can only articulate a paradigm, not correct it. Paradigms are not corrigible by normal science at all. Instead, as we have already seen, normal science ultimately leads only to the recognition of anomalies and to crises. And these are terminated, not by deliberation and interpretation, but by a relatively sudden and unstructured event like the gesalt switch. Scientists then often speak of the “scales falling from the eyes” or of the “lightning flash” that “inundates” a previously obscure puzzle, enabling its components to be seen in a new way that for the first time permits its solution. On other occasions the relevant illumination comes in sleep.13 No ordinary sense of the term ‘interpretation’ fits these flashes of intuition through which a new paradigm is born. Though such intuitions depend upon the experience, both anomalous and congruent, gained with the old paradigm, they are not logically or piecemeal linked to particular items of that experience as an interpretation would be. Instead, they gather up large portions of that experience and transform them to the rather different bundle of experience that will thereafter be linked piecemeal to the new paradigm but not to the old.

为了更深入地了解这些经验差异，让我们回到亚里士多德、伽利略和摆锤的话题。他们各自不同的范式和共同的环境，究竟为他们各自提供了哪些数据？亚里士多德主义者在观察受限下落时，会测量（或者至少讨论——亚里士多德主义者很少实际测量）石头的重量、被提升到的垂直高度以及它最终静止所需的时间。连同介质的阻力，这些构成了亚里士多德科学在研究下落物体时所使用的概念范畴。14按照这些范畴进行的常规研究不可能得出伽利略发现的定律。它只能——而且确实通过另一种途径——导致一系列危机，而伽利略对摆锤的看法正是从这些危机中产生的。由于这些危机以及其他一些思想上的转变，伽利略对摆锤的看法截然不同。阿基米德关于浮体的研究使介质不再是关键因素；冲力理论使运动呈现出对称性和持久性；而新柏拉图主义则引导伽利略关注运动的圆形形态。15因此，他只测量了重量、半径、角位移和每次摆动的时间，这些数据恰好可以用来解释伽利略关于摆的定律。事实上，解释几乎是多余的。在伽利略的范式下，类似摆的规律几乎是显而易见的。否则，我们又该如何解释伽利略发现摆锤的周期与振幅完全无关这一发现呢？源于伽利略的常规科学不得不摒弃那些我们今天完全无法证实的现象。对于像伽利略那样目睹摆动石块的人来说，那些在亚里士多德主义者看来不可能存在的规律（事实上，自然界中也找不到任何精确的例证）却是直接经验的结果。

To learn more about what these differences in experience can be, return for a moment to Aristotle, Galileo, and the pendulum. What data did the interaction of their different paradigms and their common environment make accessible to each of them? Seeing constrained fall, the Aristotelian would measure (or at least discuss—the Aristotelian seldom measured) the weight of the stone, the vertical height to which it had been raised, and the time required for it to achieve rest. Together with the resistance of the medium, these were the conceptual categories deployed by Aristotelian science when dealing with a falling body.14 Normal research guided by them could not have produced the laws that Galileo discovered. It could only—and by another route it did—lead to the series of crises from which Galileo’s view of the swinging stone emerged. As a result of those crises and of other intellectual changes besides, Galileo saw the swinging stone quite differently. Archimedes’ work on floating bodies made the medium non-essential; the impetus theory rendered the motion symmetrical and enduring; and Neoplatonism directed Galileo’s attention to the motion’s circular form.15 He therefore measured only weight, radius, angular displacement, and time per swing, which were precisely the data that could be interpreted to yield Galileo’s laws for the pendulum. In the event, interpretation proved almost unnecessary. Given Galileo’s paradigms, pendulum-like regularities were very nearly accessible to inspection. How else are we to account for Galileo’s discovery that the bob’s period is entirely independent of amplitude, a discovery that the normal science stemming from Galileo had to eradicate and that we are quite unable to document today. Regularities that could not have existed for an Aristotelian (and that are, in fact, nowhere precisely exemplified by nature) were consequences of immediate experience for the man who saw the swinging stone as Galileo did.

或许这个例子过于虚构，因为亚里士多德学派并没有记录关于摆动石头的讨论。在他们的范式中，这是一种极其复杂的现象。但亚里士多德学派确实讨论过更简单的情况，即石头在不受特殊约束的情况下下落，而同样的视角差异也体现在那里。亚里士多德在观察下落的石头时，看到的是状态的变化，而非过程。因此，对他而言，运动的相关度量是总运动距离和总运动时间，这两个参数得出的不是我们现在所说的速度，而是平均速度。 16同样，由于石头受其自身性质的驱使而到达最终静止点，亚里士多德认为运动过程中任何时刻的相关距离参数是到最终终点的距离，而不是到运动起点的距离。17这些概念参数构成了他大多数著名的“运动定律”的基础，并赋予其意义。然而，经院哲学批评部分地通过冲力范式，部分地通过被称为“形式自由度”的学说，改变了这种看待运动的方式。一块受惯性作用而运动的石头，在远离起始点的过程中，惯性越来越大；因此，起止点的距离而非终点的距离，成为了相关的参数。此外，亚里士多德的速度概念被经院哲学家们二元化，在伽利略之后，这些概念演变成了我们今天所说的平均速度和瞬时速度。但是，当我们透过这些概念所属的范式来观察时，下落的石头，就像钟摆一样，几乎一眼就能看出其运动规律。伽利略并非最早提出石头做匀加速运动的人之一。18此外，他还与许多其他学者共同发展了他的相关定理。在伽利略进行斜面实验之前，他就已经了解了落石的后果。这个定理是天才们在自然和伽利略及其同时代人所受的范式共同塑造的世界中所能发现的众多新规律之一。生活在这样的世界里，伽利略仍然可以在需要的时候解释亚里士多德的所见所闻。然而，伽利略对落石的直接体验与亚里士多德的体验并不相同。

Perhaps that example is too fanciful since the Aristotelians recorded no discussions of swinging stones. On their paradigm it was an extraordinarily complex phenomenon. But the Aristotelians did discuss the simpler case, stones falling without uncommon constraints, and the same differences of vision are apparent there. Contemplating a falling stone, Aristotle saw a change of state rather than a process. For him the relevant measures of a motion were therefore total distance covered and total time elapsed, parameters which yield what we should now call not speed but average speed.16 Similarly, because the stone was impelled by its nature to reach its final resting point, Aristotle saw the relevant distance parameter at any instant during the motion as the distance to the final end point rather than as that from the origin of motion.17 Those conceptual parameters underlie and give sense to most of his well-known “laws of motion.” Partly through the impetus paradigm, however, and partly through a doctrine known as the latitude of forms, scholastic criticism changed this way of viewing motion. A stone moved by impetus gained more and more of it while receding from its starting point; distance from rather than distance to therefore became the revelant parameter. In addition, Aristotle’s notion of speed was bifurcated by the scholastics into concepts that soon after Galileo became our average speed and instantaneous speed. But when seen through the paradigm of which these conceptions were a part, the falling stone, like the pendulum, exhibited its governing laws almost on inspection. Galileo was not one of the first men to suggest that stones fall with a uniformly accelerated motion.18 Furthermore, he had developed his theorem on this subject together with many of its consequences before he experimented with an inclined plane. That theorem was another one of the network of new regularities accessible to genius in the world determined jointly by nature and by the paradigms upon which Galileo and his contemporaries had been raised. Living in that world, Galileo could still, when he chose, explain why Aristotle had seen what he did. Nevertheless, the immediate content of Galileo’s experience with falling stones was not what Aristotle’s had been.

当然，我们是否需要如此关注“直接经验”——即那些被范式所强调、以至于几乎一经审视便失去规律性的感知特征——远非显而易见。这些特征显然会随着科学家对范式的认同而改变，但它们与我们通常所说的科学研究赖以开展的原始数据或直接经验相去甚远。或许我们应该将直接经验视为一种流动状态而搁置一旁，转而讨论科学家在实验室中进行的具体操作和测量。又或许，我们应该进一步拓展分析的范围，使其脱离直接经验。例如，我们可以采用某种中立的观察语言来进行分析，这种语言的设计或许是为了契合科学家所见的视网膜印记。只有通过这些方法之一，我们才能希望恢复一个经验一劳永逸地再次稳定的领域——在这个领域里，钟摆和受限下落不是不同的感知，而是对观察摆动的石头所提供的明确数据的不同解释。

It is, of course, by no means clear that we need be so concerned with “immediate experience”—that is, with the perceptual features that a paradigm so highlights that they surrender their regularities almost upon inspection. Those features must obviously change with the scientist’s commitments to paradigms, but they are far from what we ordinarily have in mind when we speak of the raw data or the brute experience from which scientific research is reputed to proceed. Perhaps immediate experience should be set aside as fluid, and we should discuss instead the concrete operations and measurements that the scientist performs in his laboratory. Or perhaps the analysis should be carried further still from the immediately given. It might, for example, be conducted in terms of some neutral observation-language, perhaps one designed to conform to the retinal imprints that mediate what the scientist sees. Only in one of these ways can we hope to retrieve a realm in which experience is again stable once and for all—in which the pendulum and constrained fall are not different perceptions but rather different interpretations of the unequivocal data provided by observation of a swinging stone.

但感官体验是固定不变且中立的吗？理论仅仅是对既定数据的人为诠释吗？三个世纪以来，西方哲学最常采用的认识论观点给出了一个直接而明确的答案：是的！在没有成熟的替代方案的情况下，我发现自己无法完全放弃这种观点。然而，它已不再有效，试图通过引入一种中立的观察语言来使其恢复效用的努力，在我看来也是徒劳的。

But is sensory experience fixed and neutral? Are theories simply man-made interpretations of given data? The epistemological viewpoint that has most often guided Western philosophy for three centuries dictates an immediate and unequivocal, Yes! In the absence of a developed alternative, I find it impossible to relinquish entirely that viewpoint. Yet it no longer functions effectively, and the attempts to make it do so through the introduction of a neutral language of observations now seem to me hopeless.

科学家在以下方面进行的操作和测量：实验室并非经验的“既定事实”，而是“费尽心力收集”的结果。它们并非科学家所见——至少在其研究深入、注意力集中之前并非如此。相反，它们是更基本感知内容的具体指标，因此，它们之所以被选中进行常规研究的密切考察，仅仅是因为它们有望为对既定范式的富有成效的阐述提供机会。与它们部分源自的直接经验相比，操作和测量显然是由范式决定的。科学并非处理所有可能的实验室操作。相反，它选择那些与范式及其部分决定的直接经验并置相关的操作。因此，持有不同范式的科学家会进行不同的具体实验室操作。例如，对摆锤进行的测量与受限下落的情况并不相同。阐明氧气性质的相关操作与研究脱燃素空气的特性所需的操作也不尽相同。

The operations and measurements that a scientist undertakes in the laboratory are not “the given” of experience but rather “the collected with difficulty.” They are not what the scientist sees—at least not before his research is well advanced and his attention focused. Rather, they are concrete indices to the content of more elementary perceptions, and as such they are selected for the close scrutiny of normal research only because they promise opportunity for the fruitful elaboration of an accepted paradigm. Far more clearly than the immediate experience from which they in part derive, operations and measurements are paradigm-determined. Science does not deal in all possible laboratory manipulations. Instead, it selects those relevant to the juxtaposition of a paradigm with the immediate experience that that paradigm has partially determined. As a result, scientists with different paradigms engage in different concrete laboratory manipulations. The measurements to be performed on a pendulum are not the ones relevant to a case of constrained fall. Nor are the operations relevant for the elucidation of oxygen’s properties uniformly the same as those required when investigating the characteristics of dephlogisticated air.

至于纯粹的观察语言，或许将来终有一天会被创造出来。然而，在笛卡尔之后三个世纪，我们对这种可能性的希望仍然完全依赖于知觉和心灵理论。而现代心理学实验正在迅速涌现出大量该理论难以解释的现象。鸭兔实验表明，两个视网膜印象相同的人可以看到不同的事物；倒置透镜实验表明，两个视网膜印象不同的人可以看到相同的事物。心理学提供了大量其他类似的证据，而由此产生的疑虑也因以往试图构建一种真正的观察语言的尝试而得到印证。目前，没有任何一种尝试能够接近一种普遍适用的纯粹知觉语言。而那些最接近目标的尝试都具有一个共同的特征，这有力地强化了本文的几个主要论点。从一开始，他们就预设了一种范式，这种范式要么来自当前的科学理论，要么来自日常话语的某个部分，然后他们试图从中剔除所有非逻辑和非感知性的术语。在某些话语领域，这种努力已经走得很远了，其成果令人着迷。毫无疑问，这类努力值得继续。但其结果却是一种语言——如同科学中使用的语言一样——它蕴含着诸多关于自然的预期，一旦这些预期被打破，它便无法发挥作用。纳尔逊·古德曼在描述其著作《表象结构》的目标时，恰恰指出了这一点： “幸运的是，除了已知存在的现象之外，没有其他问题；因为‘可能’的情况，即那些不存在但可能存在的情况，其概念远非清晰。” 19任何仅限于描述一个事先完全已知的世界的语言，都无法对“既定事物”做出纯粹中立客观的描述。哲学研究至今尚未揭示出一种能够做到这一点的语言究竟会是什么样子。

As for a pure observation-language, perhaps one will yet be devised. But three centuries after Descartes our hope for such an eventuality still depends exclusively upon a theory of perception and of the mind. And modern psychological experimentation is rapidly proliferating phenomena with which that theory can scarcely deal. The duck-rabbit shows that two men with the same retinal impressions can see different things; the inverting lenses show that two men with different retinal impressions can see the same thing. Psychology supplies a great deal of other evidence to the same effect, and the doubts that derive from it are readily reinforced by the history of attempts to exhibit an actual language of observation. No current attempt to achieve that end has yet come close to a generally applicable language of pure percepts. And those attempts that come closest share one characteristic that strongly reinforces several of this essay’s main theses. From the start they presuppose a paradigm, taken either from a current scientific theory or from some fraction of everyday discourse, and they then try to eliminate from it all non-logical and non-perceptual terms. In a few realms of discourse this effort has been carried very far and with fascinating results. There can be no question that efforts of this sort are worth pursuing. But their result is a language that—like those employed in the sciences—embodies a host of expectations about nature and fails to function the moment these expectations are violated. Nelson Goodman makes exactly this point in describing the aims of his Structure of Appearance: “It is fortunate that nothing more [than phenomena known to exist] is in question; for the notion of ‘possible’ cases, of cases that do not exist but might have existed, is far from clear.”19 No language thus restricted to reporting a world fully known in advance can produce mere neutral and objective reports on “the given.” Philosophical investigation has not yet provided even a hint of what a language able to do that would be like.

在这种情况下，我们至少可以怀疑，科学家们将氧气和摆锤（或许还有原子和电子）视为其直接经验的基本组成部分，无论从原则上还是实践上都是正确的。由于种族、文化以及最终的职业所形成的范式化经验，科学家的世界逐渐被行星、摆锤、电容器、复合矿石以及其他类似的物体所占据。与这些感知对象相比，无论是米尺读数还是视网膜印记，都是复杂的构造，只有当科学家为了其研究的特殊目的而安排其中之一时，经验才能直接接触到它们。这并非暗示，例如，当科学家观察一块摆动的石头时，他们所能看到的只有摆锤。（我们已经注意到，另一个科学界的成员可以看到受限的下落。）而是暗示，科学家观看摆动的石头的人，其体验本质上不可能比观看钟摆更原始。另一种可能性并非某种假设的“固定”视角，而是通过另一种范式进行的观察，在这种范式下，摆动的石头呈现出另一种面貌。

Under these circumstances we may at least suspect that scientists are right in principle as well as in practice when they treat oxygen and pendulums (and perhaps also atoms and electrons) as the fundamental ingredients of their immediate experience. As a result of the paradigm-embodied experience of the race, the culture, and, finally, the profession, the world of the scientist has come to be populated with planets and pendulums, condensers and compound ores, and other such bodies besides. Compared with these objects of perception, both meter stick readings and retinal imprints are elaborate constructs to which experience has direct access only when the scientist, for the special purposes of his research, arranges that one or the other should do so. This is not to suggest that pendulums, for example, are the only things a scientist could possibly see when looking at a swinging stone. (We have already noted that members of another scientific community could see constrained fall.) But it is to suggest that the scientist who looks at a swinging stone can have no experience that is in principle more elementary than seeing a pendulum. The alternative is not some hypothetical “fixed” vision, but vision through another paradigm, one which makes the swinging stone something else.

如果我们再次记住，无论是科学家还是普通人，都不是零散地、逐个事物地认识世界的，那么这一切似乎就更合情理了。除非所有概念和操作范畴都预先准备好——例如，为了发现一种新的超铀元素或看到一栋新房子——否则，科学家和普通人都是从经验的洪流中整体梳理出整个领域。一个孩子将“妈妈”这个词从所有人类转移到所有女性，然后再转移到他的母亲身上，他不仅仅是在学习“妈妈”的含义或他的母亲是谁。与此同时，他也在学习男性和女性之间的一些差异，以及除了一个例外，所有女性对待他的方式。他的反应、期望和信念——实际上，他感知到的大部分世界——都随之改变。同样，否认太阳拥有“行星”这一传统称谓的哥白尼学派，也不仅仅是在学习“行星”的含义或太阳是什么。相反，他们改变了“行星”的含义，使其能够在这样一个世界中继续发挥有用的区分作用：所有天体，而不仅仅是太阳，其观测方式都与以往截然不同。这一点同样适用于我们之前的任何例子。用氧气代替脱燃素空气，用冷凝器代替莱顿瓶，用摆代替受限下落，这仅仅是科学家们对众多相关化学、电学或动力学现象的认知转变的一部分。范式同时决定着我们认知的诸多领域。

All of this may seem more reasonable if we again remember that neither scientists nor laymen learn to see the world piecemeal or item by item. Except when all the conceptual and manipulative categories are prepared in advance—e.g., for the discovery of an additional transuranic element or for catching sight of a new house—both scientists and laymen sort out whole areas together from the flux of experience. The child who transfers the word ‘mama’ from all humans to all females and then to his mother is not just learning what ‘mama’ means or who his mother is. Simultaneously he is learning some of the differences between males and females as well as something about the ways in which all but one female will behave toward him. His reactions, expectations, and beliefs—indeed, much of his perceived world—change accordingly. By the same token, the Copernicans who denied its traditional title ‘planet’ to the sun were not only learning what ‘planet’ meant or what the sun was. Instead, they were changing the meaning of ‘planet’ so that it could continue to make useful distinctions in a world where all celestial bodies, not just the sun, were seen differently from the way they had been seen before. The same point could be made about any of our earlier examples. To see oxygen instead of dephlogisticated air, the condenser instead of the Leyden jar, or the pendulum instead of constrained fall, was only one part of an integrated shift in the scientist’s vision of a great many related chemical, electrical, or dynamical phenomena. Paradigms determine large areas of experience at the same time.

然而，只有在经验被如此确定之后，才能开始寻求操作性定义或纯粹的观察语言。科学家或哲学家如果想探究是什么测量或视网膜印记使摆成为它现在的样子，就必须已经能够识别出摆。如果他看到的是受限的下落，那么他根本无法提出这个问题。如果他看到的是摆，但却像看到音叉一样看待它，那么他根本无法提出这个问题。由于存在一种摇摆不定的平衡，他的问题无法得到解答。至少无法用同样的方式解答，因为那样就不是同一个问题了。因此，尽管关于视网膜印记或特定实验室操作后果的问题总是合理的，并且有时极具启发性，但它们都预设了一个在感知和概念上已经以某种方式划分的世界。从某种意义上说，这类问题是常规科学的一部分，因为它们依赖于范式的存在，并且会随着范式的改变而得到不同的答案。

It is, however, only after experience has been thus determined that the search for an operational definition or a pure observation-language can begin. The scientist or philosopher who asks what measurements or retinal imprints make the pendulum what it is must already be able to recognize a pendulum when he sees one. If he saw constrained fall instead, his question could not even be asked. And if he saw a pendulum, but saw it in the same way he saw a tuning fork or an oscillating balance, his question could not be answered. At least it could not be answered in the same way, because it would not be the same question. Therefore, though they are always legitimate and are occasionally extraordinarily fruitful, questions about retinal imprints or about the consequences of particular laboratory manipulations presuppose a world already perceptually and conceptually subdivided in a certain way. In a sense such questions are parts of normal science, for they depend upon the existence of a paradigm and they receive different answers as a result of paradigm change.

本节最后，我们暂且忽略视网膜印象，再次将注意力集中于实验室操作上。这些操作为科学家提供了具体但零散的指标，以佐证他已观察到的现象。此类实验室操作随范式变化的一种方式已被反复观察到。科学革命之后，许多旧的测量和操作变得无关紧要，并被其他方法所取代。例如，人们不会对氧气和脱燃素空气应用完全相同的测试方法。但这类变化从来都不是彻底的。无论科学家在革命后观察到什么，他看到的仍然是同一个世界。此外，尽管他之前可能以不同的方式使用它们，但他的大部分语言和大多数实验室仪器仍然与以前相同。因此，后革命时代的科学总是包含许多与革命前相同的操作，使用相同的仪器进行操作，并以相同的术语进行描述。如果这些沿用至今的操作有任何改变，那么这种改变必然存在于它们与范式的关系或其具体结果之中。现在，我将通过引入最后一个新例子来表明，这两种变化确实存在。考察道尔顿及其同时代人的研究，我们将发现，同一种操作，当它通过不同的范式与自然联系起来时，就能成为自然规律截然不同的一个方面的指标。此外，我们还会看到，有时，旧的操作方式在新角色下会产生不同的具体结果。

To conclude this section, let us henceforth neglect retinal impressions and again restrict attention to the laboratory operations that provide the scientist with concrete though fragmentary indices to what he has already seen. One way in which such laboratory operations change with paradigms has already been observed repeatedly. After a scientific revolution many old measurements and manipulations become irrelevant and are replaced by others instead. One does not apply all the same tests to oxygen as to dephlogisticated air. But changes of this sort are never total. Whatever he may then see, the scientist after a revolution is still looking at the same world. Furthermore, though he may previously have employed them differently, much of his language and most of his laboratory instruments are still the same as they were before. As a result, postrevolutionary science invariably includes many of the same manipulations, performed with the same instruments and described in the same terms, as its prerevolutionary predecessor. If these enduring manipulations have been changed at all, the change must lie either in their relation to the paradigm or in their concrete results. I now suggest, by the introduction of one last new example, that both these sorts of changes occur. Examining the work of Dalton and his contemporaries, we shall discover that one and the same operation, when it attaches to nature through a different paradigm, can become an index to a quite different aspect of nature’s regularity. In addition, we shall see that occasionally the old manipulation in its new role will yield different concrete results.

在十八世纪的大部分时间和十九世纪初期，欧洲化学家几乎一致认为，基本元素构成所有化学物质的原子都通过相互亲和力结合在一起。因此，一块银之所以能凝聚在一起，是因为银粒子之间的亲和力（在拉瓦锡之前，人们认为这些粒子本身是由更基本的粒子组成的）。根据同样的理论，银会溶解在酸中（或盐会溶解在水中），因为酸的粒子对银的粒子（或水的粒子对盐的粒子）的吸引力大于这些溶质粒子之间的相互吸引力。再者，铜会溶解在银溶液中并沉淀出银，因为铜对酸的亲和力大于酸对银的亲和力。许多其他现象也用同样的方法进行了解释。在十八世纪，选择性亲和理论是一个卓越的化学范式，被广泛且有时卓有成效地应用于化学实验的设计和分析中。 20

Throughout much of the eighteenth century and into the nineteenth, European chemists almost universally believed that the elementary atoms of which all chemical species consisted were held together by forces of mutual affinity. Thus a lump of silver cohered because of the forces of affinity between silver corpuscles (until after Lavoisier these corpuscles were themselves thought of as compounded from still more elementary particles). On the same theory silver dissolved in acid (or salt in water) because the particles of acid attracted those of silver (or the particles of water attracted those of salt) more strongly than particles of these solutes attracted each other. Or again, copper would dissolve in the silver solution and precipitate silver, because the copper-acid affinity was greater than the affinity of acid for silver. A great many other phenomena were explained in the same way. In the eighteenth century the theory of elective affinity was an admirable chemical paradigm, widely and sometimes fruitfully deployed in the design and analysis of chemical experimentation.20

然而，亲和力理论对物理混合物和化学化合物的划分方式，自道尔顿的理论被广泛接受以来，已变得不再为人所熟知。十八世纪的化学家确实认识到两种过程。当混合产生热、光、气泡或其他类似现象时，就认为发生了化学结合。另一方面，如果混合物中的粒子可以用肉眼区分或通过机械方法分离，则仅仅是物理混合物。但在大量的中间情况下——例如水中的盐、合金、玻璃、大气中的氧气等等——这些粗略的标准几乎毫无用处。受其范式的指导，大多数化学家将整个中间范围视为化学过程，因为构成该范围的过程都受同一种力的支配。水中的盐或氮气中的氧气与氧化铜产生的化合物一样，都是化学结合的例子。将溶液视为化合物的论据非常充分。亲和力理论本身也得到了充分的验证。此外，化合物的形成解释了溶液所观察到的均一性。例如，如果只有氧和氮存在，则溶液的均一性就会降低。如果大气中的气体是混合的而非结合的，那么较重的氧气应该沉到水底。道尔顿认为大气是混合气体，但他始终无法令人满意地解释氧气为何没有沉到水底。他的原子理论最终导致了此前并不存在异常现象。21

Affinity theory, however, drew the line separating physical mixtures from chemical compounds in a way that has become unfamiliar since the assimilation of Dalton’s work. Eighteenth-century chemists did recognize two sorts of processes. When mixing produced heat, light, effervescence or something else of the sort, chemical union was seen to have taken place. If, on the other hand, the particles in the mixture could be distinguished by eye or mechanically separated, there was only physical mixture. But in the very large number of intermediate cases—salt in water, alloys, glass, oxygen in the atmosphere, and so on—these crude criteria were of little use. Guided by their paradigm, most chemists viewed this entire intermediate range as chemical, because the processes of which it consisted were all governed by forces of the same sort. Salt in water or oxygen in nitrogen was just as much an example of chemical combination as was the combination produced by oxidizing copper. The arguments for viewing solutions as compounds were very strong. Affinity theory itself was well attested. Besides, the formation of a compound accounted for a solution’s observed homogeneity. If, for example, oxygen and nitrogen were only mixed and not combined in the atmosphere, then the heavier gas, oxygen, should settle to the bottom. Dalton, who took the atmosphere to be a mixture, was never satisfactorily able to explain oxygen’s failure to do so. The assimilation of his atomic theory ultimately created an anomaly where there had been none before.21

人们很容易认为，将溶液视为化合物的化学家与后世的化学家之间的区别仅仅在于定义问题。从某种意义上说，情况或许如此。但这种意义上的定义并非仅仅是约定俗成的便利。在十八世纪，人们无法通过操作性测试完全区分混合物和化合物，或许也无法做到。即使化学家们寻求此类测试，他们也会寻找能够将溶液定义为化合物的标准。混合物与化合物的区分是他们范式的一部分——是他们看待整个研究领域的方式之一——因此，这种区分先于任何特定的实验室测试，尽管它并非先于整个化学领域的经验积累。

One is tempted to say that the chemists who viewed solutions as compounds differed from their successors only over a matter of definition. In one sense that may have been the case. But that sense is not the one that makes definitions mere conventional conveniences. In the eighteenth century mixtures were not fully distinguished from compounds by operational tests, and perhaps they could not have been. Even if chemists had looked for such tests, they would have sought criteria that made the solution a compound. The mixture-compound distinction was part of their paradigm—part of the way they viewed their whole field of research—and as such it was prior to any particular laboratory test, though not to the accumulated experience of chemistry as a whole.

然而，尽管人们如此看待化学，但化学现象所展现的规律却与吸收道尔顿新范式后出现的规律截然不同。尤其值得注意的是，尽管溶液仍是化合物，但单凭任何化学实验都无法得出定比定律。十八世纪末，人们普遍知道某些化合物通常包含固定重量比例的组成成分。德国化学家里希特甚至注意到，某些类型的反应还具有化学当量定律所涵盖的进一步规律。 22 但除了在配方中，没有化学家利用过这些规律，直到世纪末才有人想到要对其进行概括。考虑到玻璃或盐溶于水等显而易见的反例，如果不放弃亲和力理论并重新定义化学领域的边界，任何概括都是不可能的。这一后果在世纪末法国化学家普鲁斯特和贝托莱的一场著名辩论中得到了明确体现。前者声称所有化学反应都以固定比例进行，后者则持相反观点。两人都收集了大量令人印象深刻的实验证据来支持各自的观点。然而，两人的论述必然相互矛盾，他们的辩论最终毫无定论。贝托莱认为化合物的比例可以变化，而普鲁斯特则认为它只是物理混合物。23对于这个问题，实验或定义惯例的改变都无济于事。两人根本上就存在分歧，就像伽利略和亚里士多德一样。

But while chemistry was viewed in this way, chemical phenomena exemplified laws different from those that emerged with the assimilation of Dalton’s new paradigm. In particular, while solutions remained compounds, no amount of chemical experimentation could by itself have produced the law of fixed proportions. At the end of the eighteenth century it was widely known that some compounds ordinarily contained fixed proportions by weight of their constituents. For some categories of reactions the German chemist Richter had even noted the further regularities now embraced by the law of chemical equivalents.22 But no chemist made use of these regularities except in recipes, and no one until almost the end of the century thought of generalizing them. Given the obvious counterinstances, like glass or like salt in water, no generalization was possible without an abandonment of affinity theory and a reconceptualization of the boundaries of the chemist’s domain. That consequence became explicit at the very end of the century in a famous debate between the French chemists Proust and Berthollet. The first claimed that all chemical reactions occurred in fixed proportion, the latter that they did not. Each collected impressive experimental evidence for his view. Nevertheless, the two men necessarily talked through each other, and their debate was entirely inconclusive. Where Berthollet saw a compound that could vary in proportion, Proust saw only a physical mixture.23 To that issue neither experiment nor a change of definitional convention could be relevant. The two men were as fundamentally at cross-purposes as Galileo and Aristotle had been.

约翰·道尔顿开展最终促成其著名的化学原子理论的研究时，情况正是如此。但在研究的最后阶段之前，道尔顿既不是化学家，也对化学不感兴趣。相反，他是一位气象学家，研究在他看来是物理问题的问题，例如气体被水吸收以及水被大气吸收。部分原因是他的专业训练与化学不同，部分原因是他自身在该领域的研究，因此他处理这些问题的范式与当时的化学家截然不同。具体而言，他将气体的混合或气体被水吸收视为一个物理过程，在这个过程中，亲和力不起作用。因此，对他来说，观察到的溶液均一性是一个问题，但他认为，如果能够确定实验混合物中各种原子粒子的相对大小和质量，就能解决这个问题。为了确定这些粒子的大小和重量，道尔顿最终转向了化学。他从一开始就假设，在他所认为的化学反应的有限范围内，原子只能以一对一或其他简单的整数比结合。 24这一自然假设确实使他能够确定基本粒子的大小和重量，但也使恒比定律变成了同义反复。对道尔顿来说，任何反应中，如果反应物的组成比例不相等，那么该反应就无法成立。按固定比例进入体系本身就并非纯粹的化学过程。在道尔顿的著作问世之前，实验无法确立的定律，一旦被广泛接受，便成为一项构成性原则，任何单一的化学测量都无法推翻它。这或许是我们所能找到的最完整的科学革命的例证，它使得同样的化学操作与化学概括之间的关系，与以往截然不同。

This was the situation during the years when John Dalton undertook the investigations that led finally to his famous chemical atomic theory. But until the very last stages of those investigations, Dalton was neither a chemist nor interested in chemistry. Instead, he was a meteorologist investigating the, for him, physical problems of the absorption of gases by water and of water by the atmosphere. Partly because his training was in a different specialty and partly because of his own work in that specialty, he approached these problems with a paradigm different from that of contemporary chemists. In particular, he viewed the mixture of gases or the absorption of a gas in water as a physical process, one in which forces of affinity played no part. To him, therefore, the observed homogeneity of solutions was a problem, but one which he thought he could solve if he could determine the relative sizes and weights of the various atomic particles in his experimental mixtures. It was to determine these sizes and weights that Dalton finally turned to chemistry, supposing from the start that, in the restricted range of reactions that he took to be chemical, atoms could only combine one-to-one or in some other simple whole-number ratio.24 That natural assumption did enable him to determine the sizes and weights of elementary particles, but it also made the law of constant proportion a tautology. For Dalton, any reaction in which the ingredients did not enter in fixed proportion was ipso facto not a purely chemical process. A law that experiment could not have established before Dalton’s work, became, once that work was accepted, a constitutive principle that no single set of chemical measurements could have upset. As a result of what is perhaps our fullest example of a scientific revolution, the same chemical manipulations assumed a relationship to chemical generalization very different from the one they had had before.

毋庸置疑，道尔顿的结论在最初公布时遭到了广泛的抨击。尤其是贝托莱，他始终不为所动。考虑到问题的性质，他其实不必如此。但对大多数化学家而言，道尔顿的新范式比普鲁斯特的更有说服力，因为它具有比区分混合物和化合物的新标准更广泛、更重要的意义。例如，如果原子只能以简单的整数比进行化学结合，那么重新审视现有的化学数据就应该能发现倍数比以及固定比例的例子。化学家们不再写两种氧化物（比如碳）分别含有56%和72%（重量比）的氧；而是写成1重量的碳可以与1.3重量或2.6重量的氧结合。当用这种方式记录旧的实验结果时，2:1的比例就跃然纸上；这种情况发生在对许多著名反应以及一些新反应的分析中。此外，道尔顿的范式使得人们能够吸收里希特的工作并理解其全部普遍性。它还启发了新的实验，特别是盖-吕萨克关于体积混合的实验，这些实验揭示了化学家们此前从未想到的其他规律。化学家们从道尔顿那里获得的并非新的实验定律，而是一种新的化学实践方法（他本人称之为“新的化学哲学体系”），这种方法迅速取得了丰硕的成果，以至于只有少数法国和英国的老一辈化学家能够抵制它。 25结果，化学家们开始生活在一个反应​​行为与以往截然不同的世界里。

Needless to say, Dalton’s conclusions were widely attacked when first announced. Berthollet, in particular, was never convinced. Considering the nature of the issue, he need not have been. But to most chemists Dalton’s new paradigm proved convincing where Proust’s had not been, for it had implications far wider and more important than a new criterion for distinguishing a mixture from a compound. If, for example, atoms could combine chemically only in simple whole-number ratios, then a re-examination of existing chemical data should disclose examples of multiple as well as of fixed proportions. Chemists stopped writing that the two oxides of, say, carbon contained 56 per cent and 72 per cent of oxygen by weight; instead they wrote that one weight of carbon would combine either with 1.3 or with 2.6 weights of oxygen. When the results of old manipulations were recorded in this way, a 2:1 ratio leaped to the eye; and this occurred in the analysis of many well-known reactions and of new ones besides. In addition, Dalton’s paradigm made it possible to assimilate Richter’s work and to see its full generality. Also, it suggested new experiments, particularly those of Gay-Lussac on combining volumes, and these yielded still other regularities, ones that chemists had not previously dreamed of. What chemists took from Dalton was not new experimental laws but a new way of practicing chemistry (he himself called it the “new system of chemical philosophy”), and this proved so rapidly fruitful that only a few of the older chemists in France and Britain were able to resist it.25 As a result, chemists came to live in a world where reactions behaved quite differently from the way they had before.

与此同时，另一个典型且非常重要的变化发生了。化学领域的一些数值数据开始出现偏差。当道尔顿最初在化学文献中寻找数据来支持他的物理理论时，他发现了一些符合理论的反应记录，但几乎不可能避免发现一些不符合理论的记录。例如，普鲁斯特对两种氧化铜的测量结果显示，氧的质量比为1.47:1，而不是原子理论所要求的2:1；而普鲁斯特正是人们预期能够达到道尔顿比例的人。 26也就是说，他是一位优秀的实验家，他对混合物和化合物之间关系的看法与道尔顿非常接近。但是，要让自然界符合某种范式是很难的。这就是为什么常规科学的难题如此具有挑战性，也是为什么在没有范式的情况下进行的测量很少能得出任何结论的原因。因此，化学家们不能仅仅根据现有证据就接受道尔顿的理论，因为当时的证据大多是否定的。相反，即便接受了这一理论，他们仍然需要说服自然界接受它，而这个过程最终耗费了几乎一代人的时间。当最终完成时，就连一些众所周知的化合物的百分比组成也发生了变化。数据本身也发生了改变。这或许可以解释为什么在一次革命之后，科学家们所处的世界已经截然不同。

As all this went on, one other typical and very important change occurred. Here and there the very numerical data of chemistry began to shift. When Dalton first searched the chemical literature for data to support his physical theory, he found some records of reactions that fitted, but he can scarcely have avoided finding others that did not. Proust’s own measurements on the two oxides of copper yielded, for example, an oxygen weight-ratio of 1.47:1 rather than the 2:1 demanded by the atomic theory; and Proust is just the man who might have been expected to achieve the Daltonian ratio.26 He was, that is, a fine experimentalist, and his view of the relation between mixtures and compounds was very close to Dalton’s. But it is hard to make nature fit a paradigm. That is why the puzzles of normal science are so challenging and also why measurements undertaken without a paradigm so seldom lead to any conclusions at all. Chemists could not, therefore, simply accept Dalton’s theory on the evidence, for much of that was still negative. Instead, even after accepting the theory, they had still to beat nature into line, a process which, in the event, took almost another generation. When it was done, even the percentage composition of well-known compounds was different. The data themselves had changed. That is the last of the senses in which we may want to say that after a revolution scientists work in a different world.

[ XI ]

[XI]

革命的隐形性

The Invisibility of Revolutions

我们仍然需要探究科学革命是如何终结的。然而，在此之前，似乎有必要做最后的努力，以强化人们对科学革命的存在及其本质的信念。到目前为止，我一直试图通过例证来展示革命，这样的例子不胜枚举。但显然，其中大多数例子都是经过精心挑选的，因为它们为人熟知，而人们通常并不将其视为革命，而是将其视为对科学知识的补充。任何补充例证都可能被赋予同样的观点，而这些例证很可能收效甚微。我认为，科学革命之所以几乎不为人知，是有其充分理由的。科学家和普通民众对创造性科学活动的认知很大程度上来源于权威来源，而这个权威来源系统性地掩盖了科学革命的存在及其意义——部分原因是出于重要的功能性原因。只有当我们认识到并分析了这种权威的本质，才能使历史例证发挥其应有的作用。此外，虽然这一点只能在我的结论部分进行充分阐述，但现在需要进行的分析将初步揭示科学工作的一个方面，正是这一点使其与其他所有创造性活动（或许神学除外）最显著的区别。

We must still ask how scientific revolutions close. Before doing so, however, a last attempt to reinforce conviction about their existence and nature seems called for. I have so far tried to display revolutions by illustration, and the examples could be multiplied ad nauseam. But clearly, most of them, which were deliberately selected for their familiarity, have customarily been viewed not as revolutions but as additions to scientific knowledge. That same view could equally well be taken of any additional illustrations, and these would probably be ineffective. I suggest that there are excellent reasons why revolutions have proved to be so nearly invisible. Both scientists and laymen take much of their image of creative scientific activity from an authoritative source that systematically disguises—partly for important functional reasons—the existence and significance of scientific revolutions. Only when the nature of that authority is recognized and analyzed can one hope to make historical example fully effective. Furthermore, though the point can be fully developed only in my concluding section, the analysis now required will begin to indicate one of the aspects of scientific work that most clearly distinguishes it from every other creative pursuit except perhaps theology.

作为权威来源，我主要指的是科学教科书，以及以教科书为蓝本的科普读物和哲学著作。这三类文献——直到最近，除了科研实践之外，几乎没有其他重要的科学信息来源——有一个共同点：它们都针对一套已经构建完善的问题、数据和理论体系，通常也针对当时科学界所秉持的特定范式。教科书旨在传达当代科学语言的词汇和句法；科普读物则试图用更贴近日常生活的语言来描述这些应用；而科学哲学，特别是英语世界的科学哲学，则分析同一套完整的科学知识体系的逻辑结构。尽管更全面的论述必然会涉及这三种文体之间诸多本质区别，但在此我们更关注的是它们的相似之处。这三者都记录了过去变革的稳定结果，从而展现了当前常规科学传统的根基。为了发挥其作用，它们无需提供关于这些理论基础最初如何被业界认识和接受的真实信息。至少就教科书而言，它们在这些问题上系统性地误导读者甚至有充分的理由。

As the source of authority, I have in mind principally textbooks of science together with both the popularizations and the philosophical works modeled on them. All three of these categories—until recently no other significant sources of information about science have been available except through the practice of research—have one thing in common. They address themselves to an already articulated body of problems, data, and theory, most often to the particular set of paradigms to which the scientific community is committed at the time they are written. Textbooks themselves aim to communicate the vocabulary and syntax of a contemporary scientific language. Popularizations attempt to describe these same applications in a language closer to that of everyday life. And philosophy of science, particularly that of the English-speaking world, analyzes the logical structure of the same completed body of scientific knowledge. Though a fuller treatment would necessarily deal with the very real distinctions between these three genres, it is their similarities that most concern us here. All three record the stable outcome of past revolutions and thus display the bases of the current normal-scientific tradition. To fulfill their function they need not provide authentic information about the way in which those bases were first recognized and then embraced by the profession. In the case of textbooks, at least, there are even good reasons why, in these matters, they should be systematically misleading.

我们在第二部分指出，对教科书或其类似资料的日益依赖，是任何科学领域第一个范式出现时必然伴随的现象。本文的最后一部分将论证，成熟科学对这类文本的依赖，显著区别于其他领域的发展模式。目前，我们不妨先假定，在其他领域前所未有的程度上，普通人和从业者的科学知识都建立在教科书及其衍生的其他一些文献之上。然而，作为延续常规科学的教学工具，教科书必须在常规科学的语言、问题结构或标准发生变化时，全部或部分地进行重写。简而言之，每次科学革命之后，教科书都必须重写；而且，一旦科学革命结束，教科书也必须重写。改写之后，这些文献不可避免地不仅掩盖了催生它们的革命的作用，甚至掩盖了这些革命本身的存在。除非亲身经历过革命，否则无论是从事科研工作的科学家还是阅读教科书的普通读者，其历史意识都仅限于该领域最近一次革命的成果。

We noted in Section II that an increasing reliance on textbooks or their equivalent was an invariable concomitant of the emergence of a first paradigm in any field of science. The concluding section of this essay will argue that the domination of a mature science by such texts significantly differentiates its developmental pattern from that of other fields. For the moment let us simply take it for granted that, to an extent unprecedented in other fields, both the layman’s and the practitioner’s knowledge of science is based on textbooks and a few other types of literature derived from them. Textbooks, however, being pedagogic vehicles for the perpetuation of normal science, have to be rewritten in whole or in part whenever the language, problem-structure, or standards of normal science change. In short, they have to be rewritten in the aftermath of each scientific revolution, and, once rewritten, they inevitably disguise not only the role but the very existence of the revolutions that produced them. Unless he has personally experienced a revolution in his own lifetime, the historical sense either of the working scientist or of the lay reader of textbook literature extends only to the outcome of the most recent revolutions in the field.

因此，教科书首先截断了科学家对其学科历史的理解，然后用其他内容来替代被剔除的部分。典型的科学教科书只包含少量历史内容，要么在导论章节中提及，要么更常见的是零星地提及早期时代的伟大人物。通过这些提及，学生和专业人士都感觉自己是悠久历史传统的参与者。然而，科学家们从教科书中感受到的这种传统，实际上从未存在过。出于显而易见且极具功能性的原因，科学教科书（以及太多早期的科学史著作）只提及过去科学家工作中那些容易被视为对文本范式问题的阐述和解决做出贡献的部分。通过选择性的选取和对事实的歪曲，早期时代的科学家被隐晦地描绘成在同一套固定问题上工作，并遵循着同一套固定的准则——而这些准则正是最近一次科学理论和方法革命所赋予科学性的。难怪每次科学革命之后，教科书及其所蕴含的历史传统都必须重写。也难怪随着教科书的重写，科学最终又显得主要是累积性的。

Textbooks thus begin by truncating the scientist’s sense of his discipline’s history and then proceed to supply a substitute for what they have eliminated. Characteristically, textbooks of science contain just a bit of history, either in an introductory chapter or, more often, in scattered references to the great heroes of an earlier age. From such references both students and professionals come to feel like participants in a long-standing historical tradition. Yet the textbook-derived tradition in which scientists come to sense their participation is one that, in fact, never existed. For reasons that are both obvious and highly functional, science textbooks (and too many of the older histories of science) refer only to that part of the work of past scientists that can easily be viewed as contributions to the statement and solution of the texts’ paradigm problems. Partly by selection and partly by distortion, the scientists of earlier ages are implicitly represented as having worked upon the same set of fixed problems and in accordance with the same set of fixed canons that the most recent revolution in scientific theory and method has made seem scientific. No wonder that textbooks and the historical tradition they imply have to be rewritten after each scientific revolution. And no wonder that, as they are rewritten, science once again comes to seem largely cumulative.

当然，科学家并非唯一倾向于将自身学科的过去线性发展并最终形成现在这种观点的群体。倒叙历史的诱惑无处不在，而且由来已久。但科学家更容易受到这种诱惑的影响，部分原因是科学研究的成果似乎并不明显依赖于研究的历史背景，部分原因是，除了危机和革命时期，科学家当下的地位似乎非常稳固。因此，无论是关于科学的现在还是过去，更多的历史细节，或者说对历史承担更多责任，都可能成为一种阻碍。所呈现的细节，只会人为地赋予人类的怪癖、错误和混乱以某种地位。科学经过最不懈的努力，已经能够摒弃的东西，为何还要赋予其尊严呢？对历史事实的贬低，深深地、或许是功能性的地根植于科学界的意识形态之中——而正是这个行业，将其他类型的事实细节奉为至高无上的价值。怀特海曾写道：“一门不愿忘记其创始人的科学，终将走向衰落。”他一语道破了科学界这种非历史性的精神。然而，他的说法并不完全正确，因为科学和其他专业领域一样，需要它们的英雄，也需要保留它们的名字。幸运的是，科学家们并没有忘记这些英雄，而是选择遗忘或修正他们的著作。

Scientists are not, of course, the only group that tends to see its discipline’s past developing linearly toward its present vantage. The temptation to write history backward is both omnipresent and perennial. But scientists are more affected by the temptation to rewrite history, partly because the results of scientific research show no obvious dependence upon the historical context of the inquiry, and partly because, except during crisis and revolution, the scientist’s contemporary position seems so secure. More historical detail, whether of science’s present or of its past, or more responsibility to the historical details that are presented, could only give artificial status to human idiosyncrasy, error, and confusion. Why dignify what science’s best and most persistent efforts have made it possible to discard? The depreciation of historical fact is deeply, and probably functionally, ingrained in the ideology of the scientific profession, the same profession that places the highest of all values upon factual details of other sorts. Whitehead caught the unhistorical spirit of the scientific community when he wrote, “A science that hesitates to forget its founders is lost.” Yet he was not quite right, for the sciences, like other professional enterprises, do need their heroes and do preserve their names. Fortunately, instead of forgetting these heroes, scientists have been able to forget or revise their works.

其结果导致人们倾向于将科学史视为线性或累积性的，这种倾向甚至影响到科学家回顾自己的研究。例如，道尔顿关于其化学原子论发展历程的三种相互矛盾的描述，都让人觉得他从一开始就只对那些后来让他名声大噪的化学配比问题感兴趣。事实上，这些问题似乎是在他找到解决方案之后才想到的，而且是在他自己的创造性工作几乎完成之后。1道尔顿的所有描述都忽略了将一系列先前仅限于物理学和气象学的问题和概念应用于化学所带来的革命性影响。这正是道尔顿所做的，其结果是化学领域的重新定位，这种重新定位教会了化学家们对旧数据提出新问题并从中得出新结论。

The result is a persistent tendency to make the history of science look linear or cumulative, a tendency that even affects scientists looking back at their own research. For example, all three of Dalton’s incompatible accounts of the development of his chemical atomism make it appear that he was interested from an early date in just those chemical problems of combining proportions that he was later famous for having solved. Actually those problems seem only to have occurred to him with their solutions, and then not until his own creative work was very nearly complete.1 What all of Dalton’s accounts omit are the revolutionary effects of applying to chemistry a set of questions and concepts previously restricted to physics and meteorology. That is what Dalton did, and the result was a reorientation toward the field, a reorientation that taught chemists to ask new questions about and to draw new conclusions from old data.

或者，牛顿又写道，伽利略发现恒引力产生的运动与时间的平方成正比。事实上，当伽利略的运动学定理被纳入牛顿的动力学概念体系时，它的确呈现出这种形式。但伽利略本人却从未提及此事。他对落体运动的讨论很少提及力，更遑论提及均匀的引力。导致物体下落。2牛顿将伽利略对一个伽利略范式不允许提出的问题的解答归功于伽利略，从而掩盖了科学家们在运动问题及其答案方面所提出的细微但革命性的重新表述。然而，正是这种问题和答案表述方式的改变，远比新的经验发现更能解释从亚里士多德动力学到伽利略动力学，再从伽利略动力学到牛顿动力学的转变。教科书倾向于将科学发展线性化，这种做法掩盖了科学发展中最重要阶段的核心过程，而这一过程恰恰隐藏在这些变化之中。

Or again, Newton wrote that Galileo had discovered that the constant force of gravity produces a motion proportional to the square of the time. In fact, Galileo’s kinematic theorem does take that form when embedded in the matrix of Newton’s own dynamical concepts. But Galileo said nothing of the sort. His discussion of falling bodies rarely alludes to forces, much less to a uniform gravitational force that causes bodies to fall.2 By crediting to Galileo the answer to a question that Galileo’s paradigms did not permit to be asked, Newton’s account hides the effect of a small but revolutionary reformulation in the questions that scientists asked about motion as well as in the answers they felt able to accept. But it is just this sort of change in the formulation of questions and answers that accounts, far more than novel empirical discoveries, for the transition from Aristotelian to Galilean and from Galilean to Newtonian dynamics. By disguising such changes, the textbook tendency to make the development of science linear hides a process that lies at the heart of the most significant episodes of scientific development.

前述例子均以一场革命为背景，展现了历史重构的开端，而这种重构往往由后革命时代的科学文本完成。然而，这种完成远不止是上述历史误读的简单叠加。这些误读使革命变得隐形；科学文本中对现存材料的编排方式暗示了一种过程，如果这种过程存在，它将否定革命的作用。由于教科书旨在迅速让学生了解当代科学界自认为掌握的知识，因此它们尽可能地将当前常规科学的各种实验、概念、定律和理论分开且几乎按顺序地进行讲解。作为一种教学方法，这种呈现方式无可指摘。但是，当它与科学写作普遍缺乏历史性的倾向以及上文讨论的偶尔出现的系统性误读相结合时，一种强烈的印象很可能随之而来：科学的现状是由一系列独立的发现和发明构成的，这些发现和发明汇集在一起​​，便构成了现代技术知识体系。教科书式的论述表明，从科学事业伊始，科学家们就一直致力于实现当今范式所体现的特定目标。科学家们像砌砖盖楼一样，一个接一个地将新的事实、概念、定律或理论添加到当代科学教科书中提供的信息体系中。

The preceding examples display, each within the context of a single revolution, the beginnings of a reconstruction of history that is regularly completed by postrevolutionary science texts. But in that completion more is involved than a multiplication of the historical misconstructions illustrated above. Those misconstructions render revolutions invisible; the arrangement of the still visible material in science texts implies a process that, if it existed, would deny revolutions a function. Because they aim quickly to acquaint the student with what the contemporary scientific community thinks it knows, textbooks treat the various experiments, concepts, laws, and theories of the current normal science as separately and as nearly seriatim as possible. As pedagogy this technique of presentation is unexceptionable. But when combined with the generally unhistorical air of science writing and with the occasional systematic misconstructions discussed above, one strong impression is overwhelmingly likely to follow: science has reached its present state by a series of individual discoveries and inventions that, when gathered together, constitute the modern body of technical knowledge. From the beginning of the scientific enterprise, a textbook presentation implies, scientists have striven for the particular objectives that are embodied in today’s paradigms. One by one, in a process often compared to the addition of bricks to a building, scientists have added another fact, concept, law, or theory to the body of information supplied in the contemporary science text.

但科学的发展并非如此。当代常规科学中的许多难题，直到最近一次科学革命之后才出现。它们中极少有可以追溯到其所在科学领域的历史开端。前人用他们自己的仪器和解题方法研究他们自己的问题。改变的不仅仅是问题本身，而是教科书范式所构建的、与自然相契合的整个事实和理论网络都发生了转变。例如，化学组成的恒定性仅仅是化学家在他们所研究的任何领域中都能通过实验发现的经验事实吗？或者，它是否是道尔顿构建的、与早期化学经验相契合的全新事实和理论体系中的一个要素——而且是一个无可辩驳的要素——并在这一过程中改变了早期化学经验本身？或者同样地，恒力产生的恒定加速度仅仅是动力学研究者们一直以来所追求的事实，还是牛顿理论最初提出的一个问题的答案，而该理论能够根据提出问题之前已有的信息来回答这个问题？

But that is not the way a science develops. Many of the puzzles of contemporary normal science did not exist until after the most recent scientific revolution. Very few of them can be traced back to the historic beginning of the science within which they now occur. Earlier generations pursued their own problems with their own instruments and their own canons of solution. Nor is it just the problems that have changed. Rather the whole network of fact and theory that the textbook paradigm fits to nature has shifted. Is the constancy of chemical composition, for example, a mere fact of experience that chemists could have discovered by experiment within any one of the worlds within which chemists have practiced? Or is it rather one element—and an indubitable one, at that—in a new fabric of associated fact and theory that Dalton fitted to the earlier chemical experience as a whole, changing that experience in the process? Or by the same token, is the constant acceleration produced by a constant force a mere fact that students of dynamics have always sought, or is it rather the answer to a question that first arose only within Newtonian theory and that that theory could answer from the body of information available before the question was asked?

这里提出的问题针对的是教科书中看似零散呈现的事实。但显然，这些问题也对文本所呈现的理论具有重要意义。这些理论当然“符合事实”，但前提是它们将先前可获取的信息转化为事实，而这些事实在之前的范式下根本不存在。这意味着，理论的形成并非是为了零散地适应那些一直存在的事实。相反，它们与所适应的事实一同出现，源于对先前科学传统的革命性重构——在先前的传统中，科学家与自然之间基于知识的关系与现在截然不同。

These questions are here asked about what appear as the piecemeal-discovered facts of a textbook presentation. But obviously, they have implications as well for what the text presents as theories. Those theories, of course, do “fit the facts,” but only by transforming previously accessible information into facts that, for the preceding paradigm, had not existed at all. And that means that theories too do not evolve piecemeal to fit facts that were there all the time. Rather, they emerge together with the facts they fit from a revolutionary reformulation of the preceding scientific tradition, a tradition within which the knowledge-mediated relationship between the scientist and nature was not quite the same.

最后一个例子或许能更好地说明教科书的影响我们对科学发展的认​​知深受其影响。每一本基础化学教材都必须讨论化学元素的概念。几乎所有教材在介绍这一概念时，都会将其起源归功于十七世纪的化学家罗伯特·波义耳。细心的读者可以在波义耳的《怀疑的化学家》一书中找到与当今“元素”定义非常接近的解释。提及波义耳的贡献有助于让初学者意识到化学并非始于磺胺类药物；此外，它还告诉他们，科学家的一项传统任务就是创造这类概念。作为培养科学家的教学手段之一，这种归因无疑非常成功。然而，这也再次印证了历史上常见的错误模式，这些错误常常误导学生和普通读者对科学事业本质的理解。

One last example may clarify this account of the impact of textbook presentation upon our image of scientific development. Every elementary chemistry text must discuss the concept of a chemical element. Almost always, when that notion is introduced, its origin is attributed to the seventeenth-century chemist, Robert Boyle, in whose Sceptical Chymist the attentive reader will find a definition of ‘element’ quite close to that in use today. Reference to Boyle’s contribution helps to make the neophyte aware that chemistry did not begin with the sulfa drugs; in addition, it tells him that one of the scientist’s traditional tasks is to invent concepts of this sort. As a part of the pedagogic arsenal that makes a man a scientist, the attribution is immensely successful. Nevertheless, it illustrates once more the pattern of historical mistakes that misleads both students and laymen about the nature of the scientific enterprise.

根据波义耳的说法（他的观点完全正确），他对元素的“定义”只不过是对传统化学概念的改写；波义耳提出这个定义仅仅是为了论证化学元素并不存在；从历史角度来看，教科书中对波义耳贡献的描述是完全错误的。3当然，这个错误微不足道，与其他任何对数据的曲解一样。然而，真正不容忽视的是，当这种错误被不断累积，并最终融入文本的技术结构中时，会给人造成一种科学的错觉。就像“时间”、“能量”、“力”或“粒子”一样，元素的概念也常常是教科书中常见的成分，而这些成分往往并非发明或发现的。特别是波义耳的定义，至少可以追溯到亚里士多德，并通过拉瓦锡延续到现代文献中。但这并不意味着科学自古以来就拥有现代意义上的元素概念。像博伊尔那样的文字定义本身几乎没有科学内涵。它们并非对意义的完整逻辑阐释（即便存在这样的阐释），而更像是教学辅助工具。它们所指向的科学概念只有在文本或其他系统性论述中与其他科学概念、操作性实验联系起来时，才能获得完整的意义。程序和范例应用。由此可见，像元素这样的概念几乎不可能脱离语境而凭空捏造。此外，在既定的语境下，它们很少需要凭空捏造，因为它们早已存在。波义耳和拉瓦锡都从重要方面改变了“元素”的化学意义。但他们并没有发明这个概念，甚至没有改变作为其定义的文字表述。正如我们所见，爱因斯坦也无需发明或明确重新定义“空间”和“时间”，就能赋予它们在其著作语境中新的含义。

According to Boyle, who was quite right, his “definition” of an element was no more than a paraphrase of a traditional chemical concept; Boyle offered it only in order to argue that no such thing as a chemical element exists; as history, the textbook version of Boyle’s contribution is quite mistaken.3 That mistake, of course, is trivial, though no more so than any other misrepresentation of data. What is not trivial, however, is the impression of science fostered when this sort of mistake is first compounded and then built into the technical structure of the text. Like ‘time,’ ‘energy,’ ‘force,’ or ‘particle,’ the concept of an element is the sort of textbook ingredient that is often not invented or discovered at all. Boyle’ås definition, in particular, can be traced back at least to Aristotle and forward through Lavoisier into modern texts. Yet that is not to say that science has possessed the modern concept of an element since antiquity. Verbal definitions like Boyle’s have little scientific content when considered by themselves. They are not full logical specifications of meaning (if there are such), but more nearly pedagogic aids. The scientific concepts to which they point gain full significance only when related, within a text or other systematic presentation, to other scientific concepts, to manipulative procedures, and to paradigm applications. It follows that concepts like that of an element can scarcely be invented independent of context. Furthermore, given the context, they rarely require invention because they are already at hand. Both Boyle and Lavoisier changed the chemical significance of ‘element’ in important ways. But they did not invent the notion or even change the verbal formula that serves as its definition. Nor, as we have seen, did Einstein have to invent or even explicitly redefine ‘space’ and ‘time’ in order to give them new meaning within the context of his work.

那么，在波义耳的著作中，包括其著名的“定义”在内，他的历史作用是什么？他是一位科学革命的领军人物，这场革命通过改变“元素”与化学操作和化学理论的关系，将这一概念转变为一种与以往截然不同的工具，并在此过程中改变了化学以及化学家的世界。4其他一些革命，包括以拉瓦锡为中心的革命，也对赋予这一概念现代形式和功能起到了作用。但波义耳提供了一个典型的例子，既展现了每个阶段所涉及的过程，也展现了当现有知识被写入教科书时，这一过程会发生怎样的变化。这种教学形式比科学的任何其他方面都更能决定我们对科学本质以及发现和发明在科学发展中所扮演角色的理解。

What then was Boyle’s historical function in that part of his work that includes the famous “definition”? He was a leader of a scientific revolution that, by changing the relation of ‘element’ to chemical manipulation and chemical theory, transformed the notion into a tool quite different from what it had been before and transformed both chemistry and the chemist’s world in the process.4 Other revolutions, including the one that centers around Lavoisier, were required to give the concept its modern form and function. But Boyle provides a typical example both of the process involved at each of these stages and of what happens to that process when existing knowledge is embodied in a textbook. More than any other single aspect of science, that pedagogic form has determined our image of the nature of science and of the role of discovery and invention in its advance.

[十二]

[XII]

革命的解决

The Resolution of Revolutions

我们刚才讨论的这些教科书，只有在科学革命之后才得以问世。它们是新常态科学传统的基石。在探讨它们的结构时，我们显然忽略了一个关键步骤。一个新的范式是如何取代其前身的？任何对自然的新诠释，无论是发现还是理论，都首先出现在一两个人的脑海中。正是他们率先学会以不同的视角看待科学和世界，而他们之所以能够完成这种转变，得益于两个其他同行所不具备的条件。首先，他们总是高度关注那些引发危机的难题；其次，他们通常都很年轻，或者在这个危机四伏的领域经验尚浅，因此，与大多数同行相比，他们受旧范式所决定的世界观和规则的影响较小。那么，他们如何才能，或者说他们必须做些什么，才能使整个行业或相关的专业群体接受他们看待科学和世界的方式呢？是什么原因导致该团队放弃一种常规研究方法而选择另一种？

The textbooks we have just been discussing are produced only in the aftermath of a scientific revolution. They are the bases for a new tradition of normal science. In taking up the question of their structure we have clearly missed a step. What is the process by which a new candidate for paradigm replaces its predecessor? Any new interpretation of nature, whether a discovery or a theory, emerges first in the mind of one or a few individuals. It is they who first learn to see science and the world differently, and their ability to make the transition is facilitated by two circumstances that are not common to most other members of their profession. Invariably their attention has been intensely concentrated upon the crisis-provoking problems; usually, in addition, they are men so young or so new to the crisis-ridden field that practice has committed them less deeply than most of their contemporaries to the world view and rules determined by the old paradigm. How are they able, what must they do, to convert the entire profession or the relevant professional subgroup to their way of seeing science and the world? What causes the group to abandon one tradition of normal research in favor of another?

要理解这些问题的紧迫性，请记住，它们是历史学家能够为哲学家提供的唯一重建。对既有科学理论的检验、验证或证伪的探究。就其从事的常规科学而言，研究人员是难题的解决者，而非范式的检验者。尽管在寻找特定难题的解决方案时，他可能会尝试多种替代方法，并舍弃那些未能得出预期结果的方法，但他这样做并非在检验范式。相反，他更像是棋手，面对一个问题，棋盘就在眼前（无论是实际的还是想象的），他尝试各种不同的走法以寻找解决方案。这些尝试，无论是棋手还是科学家，都只是对尝试本身的检验，而非对游戏规则的检验。这些尝试只有在范式本身被视为理所当然的情况下才有可能发生。因此，范式检验只有在持续无法解决一个重要的难题并引发危机之后才会发生。即便如此，它也只有在危机感催生出新的范式候选者之后才会发生。在科学领域，检验情境绝非像解谜那样，仅仅是将单一范式与自然进行比较。相反，检验是两种相互竞争的范式争夺科学界支持的过程。

To see the urgency of those questions, remember that they are the only reconstructions the historian can supply for the philosopher’s inquiry about the testing, verification, or falsification of established scientific theories. In so far as he is engaged in normal science, the research worker is a solver of puzzles, not a tester of paradigms. Though he may, during the search for a particular puzzle’s solution, try out a number of alternative approaches, rejecting those that fail to yield the desired result, he is not testing the paradigm when he does so. Instead he is like the chess player who, with a problem stated and the board physically or mentally before him, tries out various alternative moves in the search for a solution. These trial attempts, whether by the chess player or by the scientist, are trials only of themselves, not of the rules of the game. They are possible only so long as the paradigm itself is taken for granted. Therefore, paradigm-testing occurs only after persistent failure to solve a noteworthy puzzle has given rise to crisis. And even then it occurs only after the sense of crisis has evoked an alternate candidate for paradigm. In the sciences the testing situation never consists, as puzzle-solving does, simply in the comparison of a single paradigm with nature. Instead, testing occurs as part of the competition between two rival paradigms for the allegiance of the scientific community.

仔细审视这一表述，会发现它与当代两种最流行的关于验证的哲学理论有着出人意料且可能意义重大的相似之处。如今，鲜有科学哲学家仍在寻求科学理论验证的绝对标准。他们指出，任何理论都不可能经受所有相关检验，因此他们关注的并非某个理论是否已被验证，而是根据现有证据，该理论被验证的可能性。为了回答这个问题，一个重要的学派致力于比较不同理论解释现有证据的能力。这种对理论比较的坚持也体现了新理论被接受的历史背景。它很可能指明了未来关于验证的讨论方向之一。

Closely examined, this formulation displays unexpected and probably significant parallels to two of the most popular contemporary philosophical theories about verification. Few philosophers of science still seek absolute criteria for the verification of scientific theories. Noting that no theory can ever be exposed to all possible relevant tests, they ask not whether a theory has been verified but rather about its probability in the light of the evidence that actually exists. And to answer that question one important school is driven to compare the ability of different theories to explain the evidence at hand. That insistence on comparing theories also characterizes the historical situation in which a new theory is accepted. Very probably it points one of the directions in which future discussions of verification should go.

然而，在最常见的形式中，概率验证理论都依赖于第十节讨论的某种纯粹或中立的观察语言。其中一种概率理论要求我们将给定的科学理论与所有其他可能的理论进行比较。设想符合同一组观测数据。另一种设想则要求在想象中构建给定科学理论可能需要通过的所有检验。1显然，计算特定概率（绝对概率或相对概率）需要某种这样的构建，但很难想象这种构建如何实现。正如我之前所强调的，如果不存在科学或经验中立的语言或概念体系，那么所提出的替代检验和理论的构建就必须基于某种范式传统。如此一来，它将无法接触到所有可能的经验或所有可能的理论。因此，概率理论在阐明验证情境的同时，也掩盖了它。尽管如它们所坚持的那样，验证情境确实取决于理论的比较和大量广泛证据的比较，但所讨论的理论和观察结果总是与已存在的理论和观察结果密切相关。验证就像自然选择：它在特定的历史情境中，从实际的备选方案中选出最可行的方案。如果还有其他选择，或者数据是另一种类型，那么这个选择是否是最佳选择？这个问题很难提出，也没有任何工具可以用来寻找答案。

In their most usual forms, however, probabilistic verification theories all have recourse to one or another of the pure or neutral observation-languages discussed in Section X. One probabilistic theory asks that we compare the given scientific theory with all others that might be imagined to fit the same collection of observed data. Another demands the construction in imagination of all the tests that the given scientific theory might conceivably be asked to pass.1 Apparently some such construction is necessary for the computation of specific probabilities, absolute or relative, and it is hard to see how such a construction can possibly be achieved. If, as I have already urged, there can be no scientifically or empirically neutral system of language or concepts, then the proposed construction of alternate tests and theories must proceed from within one or another paradigm-based tradition. Thus restricted it would have no access to all possible experiences or to all possible theories. As a result, probabilistic theories disguise the verification situation as much as they illuminate it. Though that situation does, as they insist, depend upon the comparison of theories and of much widespread evidence, the theories and observations at issue are always closely related to ones already in existence. Verification is like natural selection: it picks out the most viable among the actual alternatives in a particular historical situation. Whether that choice is the best that could have been made if still other alternatives had been available or if the data had been of another sort is not a question that can usefully be asked. There are no tools to employ in seeking answers to it.

卡尔·R·波普尔对这一系列问题提出了截然不同的解决之道，他完全否认任何验证程序的存在。2相反，他强调证伪的重要性，即检验的否定结果必然导致对既有理论的否定。显然，证伪的作用与本文赋予异常经验的作用非常相似，即通过引发危机，为新理论的出现铺平道路的经验。然而，异常经验不能等同于证伪经验。事实上，我怀疑后者是否存在。正如之前反复强调的那样，没有任何理论能够解决它在特定时期面临的所有难题；已取得的解决方案往往完美无缺。恰恰相反，正是现有数据与理论拟合的不完整性和不完美性，才构成了常规科学中诸多难题的根源。如果任何拟合失败都成为否定理论的理由，那么所有理论都应该被否定。另一方面，如果只有严重的拟合失败才足以否定理论，那么波普尔主义者就需要某种“概率极低”或“证伪程度”的标准。在构建这样的标准时，他们几乎肯定会遇到与各种概率验证理论的支持者们所面临的同样的难题。

A very different approach to this whole network of problems has been developed by Karl R. Popper who denies the existence of any verification procedures at all.2 Instead, he emphasizes the importance of falsification, i.e., of the test that, because its outcome is negative, necessitates the rejection of an established theory. Clearly, the role thus attributed to falsification is much like the one this essay assigns to anomalous experiences, i.e., to experiences that, by evoking crisis, prepare the way for a new theory. Nevertheless, anomalous experiences may not be identified with falsifying ones. Indeed, I doubt that the latter exist. As has repeatedly been emphasized before, no theory ever solves all the puzzles with which it is confronted at a given time; nor are the solutions already achieved often perfect. On the contrary, it is just the incompleteness and imperfection of the existing data-theory fit that, at any time, define many of the puzzles that characterize normal science. If any and every failure to fit were ground for theory rejection, all theories ought to be rejected at all times. On the other hand, if only severe failure to fit justifies theory rejection, then the Popperians will require some criterion of “improbability” or of “degree of falsification.” In developing one they will almost certainly encounter the same network of difficulties that has haunted the advocates of the various probabilistic verification theories.

认识到这两种关于科学探究基本逻辑的普遍且对立的观点都试图将两个截然不同的过程压缩成一个，就能避免许多前述的困难。波普尔的异常经验对科学至关重要，因为它引发了对现有范式的挑战。然而，证伪虽然确实存在，但并非伴随异常或证伪实例的出现而发生，也并非仅仅因为这些实例的出现。相反，它是一个后续的、独立的过程，也可以称之为验证，因为它体现了新范式对旧范式的胜利。此外，概率论者对理论的比较正是在这一验证-证伪的联合过程中发挥着核心作用。我认为，这种两阶段的表述具有高度的逼真性，并且或许能够帮助我们开始阐明事实与理论在验证过程中的一致性（或不一致性）的作用。至少对历史学家而言，认为验证就是确立事实与理论的一致性是毫无意义的。所有具有历史意义的理论都与事实相符，但只是或多或少而已。对于某个理论是否或多大程度上符合事实，并没有更精确的答案。然而，当把各种理论放在一起，甚至两两比较时，我们就可以提出类似的问题。询问两个相互竞争的理论中哪一个更符合事实，就显得非常有意义。例如，尽管普里斯特利和拉瓦锡的理论都与当时的观测结果并不完全一致，但几乎所有人都毫不犹豫地在十多年后得出结论：拉瓦锡的理论比普里斯特利的理论更符合事实。

Many of the preceding difficulties can be avoided by recognizing that both of these prevalent and opposed views about the underlying logic of scientific inquiry have tried to compress two largely separate processes into one. Popper’s anomalous experience is important to science because it evokes competitors for an existing paradigm. But falsification, though it surely occurs, does not happen with, or simply because of, the emergence of an anomaly or falsifying instance. Instead, it is a subsequent and separate process that might equally well be called verification since it consists in the triumph of a new paradigm over the old one. Furthermore, it is in that joint verification-falsification process that the probabilist’s comparison of theories plays a central role. Such a two-stage formulation has, I think, the virtue of great verisimilitude, and it may also enable us to begin explicating the role of agreement (or disagreement) between fact and theory in the verification process. To the historian, at least, it makes little sense to suggest that verification is establishing the agreement of fact with theory. All historically significant theories have agreed with the facts, but only more or less. There is no more precise answer to the question whether or how well an individual theory fits the facts. But questions much like that can be asked when theories are taken collectively or even in pairs. It makes a great deal of sense to ask which of two actual and competing theories fits the facts better. Though neither Priestley’s nor Lavoisier’s theory, for example, agreed precisely with existing observations, few contemporaries hesitated more than a decade in concluding that Lavoisier’s theory provided the better fit of the two.

然而，这种表述使得在不同范式之间进行选择的任务看起来比实际情况更容易、更熟悉。如果只有一套科学问题、一个研究这些问题的框架以及一套解决问题的标准，那么范式之争或许可以通过某种常规方法来解决，例如统计每种范式解决的问题数量。但事实上，这些条件永远无法完全满足。相互竞争的范式的支持者之间总是存在着至少轻微的分歧。任何一方都不会接受对方为了论证自身观点而需要的所有非经验性假设。就像普鲁斯特和贝托莱争论化学化合物的组成一样，他们必然会在某种程度上互相干扰。尽管双方都希望对方能够接受自己看待科学及其问题的方式，但谁也无法证明自己的观点。范式之间的竞争并非那种可以通过证明来解决的争论。

This formulation, however, makes the task of choosing between paradigms look both easier and more familiar than it is. If there were but one set of scientific problems, one world within which to work on them, and one set of standards for their solution, paradigm competition might be settled more or less routinely by some process like counting the number of problems solved by each. But, in fact, these conditions are never met completely. The proponents of competing paradigms are always at least slightly at cross-purposes. Neither side will grant all the non-empirical assumptions that the other needs in order to make its case. Like Proust and Berthollet arguing about the composition of chemical compounds, they are bound partly to talk through each other. Though each may hope to convert the other to his way of seeing his science and its problems, neither may hope to prove his case. The competition between paradigms is not the sort of battle that can be resolved by proofs.

我们已经看到，相互竞争的范式的支持者们无法完全理解彼此观点的几个原因。这些原因统称为革命前后常规科学传统的不可通约性，我们在此只需简要回顾一下。首先，相互竞争的范式的支持者们常常对任何候选范式必须解决的问题清单存在分歧。他们对科学的标准或定义并不相同。运动理论必须解释物质粒子间吸引力的成因，还是仅仅指出这种力的存在即可？牛顿动力学曾被广泛拒绝，因为它与亚里士多德和笛卡尔的理论不同，它暗示了后一种答案。因此，当牛顿的理论被接受时，一个问题就被科学界所摒弃。然而，广义相对论却可以自豪地宣称已经解决了这个问题。或者说，正如十九世纪传播的那样，拉瓦锡的化学理论阻碍了化学家们探究金属为何如此相似——而燃素化学恰恰提出并解答了这个问题。向拉瓦锡范式的过渡，如同向牛顿范式的过渡一样，不仅意味着失去了一个可以探讨的问题，也意味着失去了一个已经得到解答的问题。然而，这种损失也并非永久性的。在二十世纪，关于化学物质性质的问题再次进入科学界，同时也出现了一些答案。

We have already seen several reasons why the proponents of competing paradigms must fail to make complete contact with each other’s viewpoints. Collectively these reasons have been described as the incommensurability of the pre- and postrevolutionary normal-scientific traditions, and we need only recapitulate them briefly here. In the first place, the proponents of competing paradigms will often disagree about the list of problems that any candidate for paradigm must resolve. Their standards or their definitions of science are not the same. Must a theory of motion explain the cause of the attractive forces between particles of matter or may it simply note the existence of such forces? Newton’s dynamics was widely rejected because, unlike both Aristotle’s and Descartes’s theories, it implied the latter answer to the question. When Newton’s theory had been accepted, a question was therefore banished from science. That question, however, was one that general relativity may proudly claim to have solved. Or again, as disseminated in the nineteenth century, Lavoisier’s chemical theory inhibited chemists from asking why the metals were so much alike, a question that phlogistic chemistry had both asked and answered. The transition to Lavoisier’s paradigm had, like the transition to Newton’s, meant a loss not only of a permissible question but of an achieved solution. That loss was not, however, permanent either.
