A second issue, more important at least to historians, concerns this book’s implicit one-to-one identification of scientific communities with scientific subject matters. I have, that is, repeatedly acted as though, say, ‘physical optics,’ ‘electricity,’ and ‘heat’ must name scientific communities because they do name subject matters for research. The only alternative my text has seemed to allow is that all these subjects have belonged to the physics community. Identifications of that sort will not, however, usually withstand examination, as my colleagues in history have repeatedly pointed out. There was, for example, no physics community before the mid-nineteenth century, and it was then formed by the merger of parts of two previously separate communities, mathematics and natural philosophy (physique expérimentale). What is today the subject matter for a single broad community has been variously distributed among diverse communities in the past. Other narrower subjects, for example heat and the theory of matter, have existed for long periods without becoming the special province of any single scientific community. Both normal science and revolutions are, however, community-based activities. To discover and analyze them, one must first unravel the changing community structure of the sciences over time. A paradigm governs, in the first instance, not a subject matter but rather a group of practitioners. Any study of paradigm-directed or of paradigm-shattering research must begin by locating the responsible group or groups.

如果以这种方式分析科学发展，一些曾引起广泛关注的难题或许就会迎刃而解。例如，一些评论家曾以物质理论为例，指出我过分夸大了科学家们对某种范式的认同程度。他们指出，直到不久前，这些理论一直是争论不休的话题。我同意这种说法，但认为这并非反例。至少在1920年之前，物质理论并非任何科学共同体的专属领域或研究对象。相反，它们是众多专业群体使用的工具。不同群体的成员有时会选择不同的工具，并对其他人的选择提出批评。更重要的是，物质理论并非一个即使是同一群体成员也必须达成共识的话题。是否需要达成共识取决于该群体的研究方向。19世纪上半叶的化学就是一个很好的例子。尽管该领域的一些基本工具——恒定比例、倍数比例和权重组合——已经变得很常见由于道尔顿的原子理论赋予了化学性质，事后化学家们完全有可能基于这些工具开展研究，并对原子的存在产生分歧，有时甚至是激烈的争论。

When the analysis of scientific development is approached in that way, several difficulties which have been foci for critical attention are likely to vanish. A number of commentators have, for example, used the theory of matter to suggest that I drastically overstate the unanimity of scientists in their allegiance to a paradigm. Until comparatively recently, they point out, those theories have been topics for continuing disagreement and debate. I agree with the description but think it no counterexample. Theories of matter were not, at least until about 1920, the special province or the subject matter for any scientific community. Instead, they were tools for a large number of specialists’ groups. Members of different communities sometimes chose different tools and criticized the choice made by others. Even more important, a theory of matter is not the sort of topic on which the members of even a single community must necessarily agree. The need for agreement depends on what it is the community does. Chemistry in the first half of the nineteenth century provides a case in point. Though several of the community’s fundamental tools—constant proportion, multiple proportion, and combining weights—had become common property as a result of Dalton’s atomic theory, it was quite possible for chemists, after the event, to base their work on these tools and to disagree, sometimes vehemently, about the existence of atoms.

我相信，其他一些困难和误解也会以同样的方式消除。部分原因是由于我选择的例子，部分原因是由于我对相关社群的性质和规模语焉不详，本书的一些读者认为我主要或完全关注的是像哥白尼、牛顿、达尔文或爱因斯坦那样的重大革命。然而，对社群结构的更清晰界定应该有助于强化我试图营造的截然不同的印象。对我而言，革命是一种特殊的变革，涉及群体承诺的某种重构。但它不必是巨大的变革，也不必在单一社群之外的人看来是革命性的，即使这个社群可能不足二十五人。正是因为这种变革在科学哲学文献中鲜有提及或讨论，却在如此小的范围内频繁发生，所以才迫切需要理解革命性的变革，而非累积性的变革。

Some other difficulties and misunderstandings will, I believe, be dissolved in the same way. Partly because of the examples I have chosen and partly because of my vagueness about the nature and size of the relevant communities, a few readers of this book have concluded that my concern is primarily or exclusively with major revolutions such as those associated with Copernicus, Newton, Darwin, or Einstein. A clearer delineation of community structure should, however, help to enforce the rather different impression I have tried to create. A revolution is for me a special sort of change involving a certain sort of reconstruction of group commitments. But it need not be a large change, nor need it seem revolutionary to those outside a single community, consisting perhaps of fewer than twenty-five people. It is just because this type of change, little recognized or discussed in the literature of the philosophy of science, occurs so regularly on this smaller scale that revolutionary, as against cumulative, change so badly needs to be understood.

最后一点修改与前文密切相关，或许有助于理解。一些批评家质疑，危机——即人们普遍意识到出了问题——是否像我在原文中所暗示的那样，总是先于革命发生。然而，我的论证并不依赖于危机是否是革命的绝对前提；危机仅仅是通常的前奏，也就是说，它提供了一种自我纠正机制，确保常规科学的僵化不会永远不受挑战。革命也可以通过其他方式引发，尽管我认为这种情况很少见。此外，我现在要指出，由于上文缺乏对社群结构的充分讨论而掩盖了一点：危机并非必然由经历危机并因此发生革命的社群自身所引发。例如，像电子显微镜这样的新仪器或像麦克斯韦定律这样的新定律可能在一个专业领域发展起来，而它们的应用却会在另一个领域引发危机。

One last alteration, closely related to the preceding, may help to facilitate that understanding. A number of critics have doubted whether crisis, the common awareness that something has gone wrong, precedes revolutions so invariably as I have implied in my original text. Nothing important to my argument depends, however, on crises’ being an absolute prerequisite to revolutions; they need only be the usual prelude, supplying, that is, a self-correcting mechanism which ensures that the rigidity of normal science will not forever go un- challenged. Revolutions may also be induced in other ways, though I think they seldom are. In addition, I would now point out what the absence of an adequate discussion of community structure has obscured above: crises need not be generated by the work of the community that experiences them and that sometimes undergoes revolution as a result. New instruments like the electron microscope or new laws like Maxwell’s may develop in one specialty and their assimilation create crisis in another.

2. 作为群体承诺的集合体的范式

2. Paradigms as the Constellation of Group Commitments

现在让我们转向“范式”，并探究它们究竟是什么。我的原文已经没有留下任何晦涩或重要的问题。一位与我志同道合的读者，也认为“范式”指代了本书的核心哲学要素，他编制了一份部分分析索引，并得出结论：该术语至少有二十二种不同的用法。7我现在认为，这些差异大多源于文风上的不一致（例如，牛顿定律有时被视为范式，有时被视为范式的一部分，有时又被视为具有范式意义），这些差异可以相对容易地消除。但是，即便完成了这些编辑工作，该术语仍会保留两种截然不同的用法，需要加以区分。本小节将讨论较为宽泛的用法；另一种用法将在下一小节中探讨。

Turn now to paradigms and ask what they can possibly be. My original text leaves no more obscure or important question. One sympathetic reader, who shares my conviction that ‘paradigm’ names the central philosophical elements of the book, prepared a partial analytic index and concluded that the term is used in at least twenty-two different ways.7 Most of those differences are, I now think, due to stylistic inconsistencies (e.g., Newton’s Laws are sometimes a paradigm, sometimes parts of a paradigm, and sometimes paradigmatic), and they can be eliminated with relative ease. But, with that editorial work done, two very different usages of the term would remain, and they require separation. The more global use is the subject of this subsection; the other will be considered in the next.

通过刚才讨论的方法筛选出一个特定的专家群体后，我们可以提出这样一个问题：这个群体的成员有哪些共同之处，使得他们的专业交流相对充分，专业判断相对一致？对于这个问题，我的原文给出的答案是范式或范式集合。但与下文将要讨论的用法不同，这个术语在这里并不适用。科学家们会说他们共享一种理论或一系列理论，如果这个术语最终能被重新赋予此用法，我将非常高兴。然而，就目前科学哲学中的用法而言，“理论”一词所指的结构在性质和范围上都远比这里所需的结构要局限得多。在摆脱其当前含义之前，为了避免混淆，最好采用其他术语。就目前而言，我建议使用“学科矩阵”：之所以称为“学科”，是因为它指的是特定学科从业者的共同拥有；之所以称为“矩阵”，是因为它由各种有序元素组成，每个元素都需要进一步阐述。我的原文中所有或大部分群体承诺对象，无论是范式、范式的一部分，还是具有范式特征的对象，都是学科矩阵的组成部分，因此它们构成一个整体并发挥作用。它们共同构成一个整体。然而，我们不能再将它们视为一个整体来讨论。我在此不打算列举所有组成部分，但指出学科矩阵的主要构成要素，既能阐明我目前的研究方法，也能为我的下一个要点做好铺垫。

Having isolated a particular community of specialists by techniques like those just discussed, one may usefully ask: What do its members share that accounts for the relative fulness of their professional communication and the relative unanimity of their professional judgments? To that question my original text licenses the answer, a paradigm or set of paradigms. But for this use, unlike the one to be discussed below, the term is inappropriate. Scientists themselves would say they share a theory or set of theories, and I shall be glad if the term can ultimately be recaptured for this use. As currently used in philosophy of science, however, ‘theory’ connotes a structure far more limited in nature and scope than the one required here. Until the term can be freed from its current implications, it will avoid confusion to adopt another. For present purposes I suggest ‘disciplinary matrix’: ‘disciplinary’ because it refers to the common possession of the practitioners of a particular discipline; ‘matrix’ because it is composed of ordered elements of various sorts, each requiring further specification. All or most of the objects of group commitment that my original text makes paradigms, parts of paradigms, or paradigmatic are constituents of the disciplinary matrix, and as such they form a whole and function together. They are, however, no longer to be discussed as though they were all of a piece. I shall not here attempt an exhaustive list, but noting the main sorts of components of a disciplinary matrix will both clarify the nature of my present approach and simultaneously prepare for my next main point.

我将一种重要的组成部分称为“符号概括”，指的是那些被群体成员毫不质疑或反对地使用的表达方式，它们可以很容易地用逻辑形式表示，例如 ( x )( y )( z ) ( x, y, z )。它们是学科矩阵中的形式化或易于形式化的组成部分。有时它们已经以符号形式出现：例如f = ma或I = V/R。其他一些则通常用文字表达：“元素按重量以恒定比例结合”，或“作用力等于反作用力”。如果没有对这类表达方式的普遍接受，群体成员就无法在解决问题的过程中运用强大的逻辑和数学操作技巧。虽然分类学的例子表明，常规科学可以用很少的这类表达方式进行，但一般来说，一门科学的力量似乎会随着其实践者所掌握的符号概括方式的数量而增强。

One important sort of component I shall label ‘symbolic generalizations,’ having in mind those expressions, deployed without question or dissent by group members, which can readily be cast in a logical form like (x)(y)(z)(x, y, z). They are the formal or the readily formalizable components of the disciplinary matrix. Sometimes they are found already in symbolic form: f = ma or I = V/R. Others are ordinarily expressed in words: “elements combine in constant proportion by weight,” or “action equals reaction.” If it were not for the general acceptance of expressions like these, there would be no points at which group members could attach the powerful techniques of logical and mathematical manipulation in their puzzle-solving enterprise. Though the example of taxonomy suggests that normal science can proceed with few such expressions, the power of a science seems quite generally to increase with the number of symbolic generalizations its practitioners have at their disposal.

这些概括看似自然法则，但它们对群体成员的功能往往不止于此。有时的确如此：例如焦耳-楞次定律，H = RI² 。当这条定律被发现时，群体成员已经知道H、R和I分别代表什么，这些概括只是告诉了他们一些关于热、电流和电阻行为的新知识。但更多时候，正如本书前面讨论的那样，符号概括同时还具有第二种功能，这种功能通常在科学哲学家的分析中被明确区分开来。就像f = ma或I = V/R一样，它们部分地作为定律发挥作用，部分地作为对某些符号的定义。此外，它们不可分割的立法效力和定义效力之间的平衡会随着时间而变化。在其他语境下，这些要点值得进行详细分析，因为对定律的承诺与对定义的承诺性质截然不同。定律通常是可以逐步修正的，但定义本身并非同义反复，因此并非如此。例如，欧姆定律的接受部分要求重新定义“电流”和“电阻”；如果这些术语的含义与之前相同，欧姆定律就不可能正确；这就是为什么它遭到如此强烈的反对，而焦耳-楞次定律却没有。8这种情况可能很典型。我目前怀疑，所有革命都包含着对某些概括的放弃，而这些概括的力量在某种程度上类似于同义反复。爱因斯坦是证明了同时性是相对的，还是改变了同时性本身的概念？那些在“同时性的相对性”这一短语中听到悖论的人，难道仅仅是误解了吗？

These generalizations look like laws of nature, but their function for group members is not often that alone. Sometimes it is: for example the Joule-Lenz Law, H = RI2. When that law was discovered, community members already knew what H, R, and I stood for, and these generalizations simply told them something about the behavior of heat, current, and resistance that they had not known before. But more often, as discussion earlier in the book indicates, symbolic generalizations simultaneously serve a second function, one that is ordinarily sharply separated in analyses by philosophers of science. Like f = ma or I = V/R, they function in part as laws but also in part as definitions of some of the symbols they deploy. Furthermore, the balance between their inseparable legislative and definitional force shifts over time. In another context these points would repay detailed analysis, for the nature of the commitment to a law is very different from that of commitment to a definition. Laws are often corrigible piecemeal, but definitions, being tautologies, are not. For example, part of what the acceptance of Ohm’s Law demanded was a redefinition of both ‘current’ and ‘resistance’; if those terms had continued to mean what they had meant before, Ohm’s Law could not have been right; that is why it was so strenuously opposed as, say, the Joule-Lenz Law was not.8 Probably that situation is typical. I currently suspect that all revolutions involve, among other things, the abandonment of generalizations the force of which had previously been in some part that of tautologies. Did Einstein show that simultaneity was relative or did he alter the notion of simultaneity itself? Were those who heard paradox in the phrase ‘relativity of simultaneity’ simply wrong?

接下来，我们来探讨学科矩阵的第二种组成部分，我在原文中已就此进行了详尽的论述，例如“形而上学范式”或“范式的形而上学部分”。我指的是对某些信念的共同认同，例如：热是物体组成部分的动能；所有可感知的现象都是由于虚空中性质中性原子的相互作用造成的，或者，也可以说是由于物质和力，或者是由于场造成的。如果现在重写这本书，我会将这类认同描述为对特定模型的信念，并且我会扩展模型的范畴，使其也包括相对启发式的模型：例如，电路可以被视为一个稳态流体动力学系统；气体分子就像随机运动的微小弹性台球。尽管群体认同的强度会随着模型从启发式到本体论的转变而变化，并产生重要的后果，但所有模型都具有相似的功能。其中一项功能是为群体提供首选或可接受的类比和隐喻。这样做有助于确定哪些解释和谜题解决方案会被接受；反之，它们也有助于确定未解谜题的清单，并评估每个谜题的重要性。然而，需要注意的是，科学界的成员……虽然通常情况下，不同学术群体之间并不一定需要共享启发式模型。我已经指出，在十九世纪上半叶，化学家群体成员并不要求他们相信原子的存在。

Consider next a second type of component of the disciplinary matrix, one about which a good deal has been said in my original text under such rubrics as ‘metaphysical paradigms’ or ‘the metaphysical parts of paradigms.’ I have in mind shared commitments to such beliefs as: heat is the kinetic energy of the constituent parts of bodies; all perceptible phenomena are due to the interaction of qualitatively neutral atoms in the void, or, alternatively, to matter and force, or to fields. Rewriting the book now I would describe such commitments as beliefs in particular models, and I would expand the category models to include also the relatively heuristic variety: the electric circuit may be regarded as a steady-state hydrodynamic system; the molecules of a gas behave like tiny elastic billiard balls in random motion. Though the strength of group commitment varies, with nontrivial consequences, along the spectrum from heuristic to ontological models, all models have similar functions. Among other things they supply the group with preferred or permissible analogies and metaphors. By doing so they help to determine what will be accepted as an explanation and as a puzzle-solution; conversely, they assist in the determination of the roster of unsolved puzzles and in the evaluation of the importance of each. Note, however, that the members of scientific communities may not have to share even heuristic models, though they usually do so. I have already pointed out that membership in the community of chemists during the first half of the nineteenth century did not demand a belief in atoms.

我在此要描述的学科矩阵中的第三类要素是价值观。通常，价值观比符号概括或模型更容易被不同群体广泛接受，它们极大地增强了自然科学家的群体归属感。尽管价值观始终发挥作用，但当特定群体的成员必须识别危机，或者在之后需要在相互矛盾的学科实践方式之间做出选择时，它们的重要性就凸显出来。或许最根深蒂固的价值观与预测有关：预测应当准确；定量预测优于定性预测；无论允许的误差范围是多少，在特定领域内都应当始终满足这一要求；等等。然而，在评判整个理论时也需要运用一些价值观：首先，理论必须能够构建和解决难题；在可能的情况下，理论应当简洁、自洽、合理，并且与其他现有理论相兼容。 （我现在认为我原文的一个缺陷是，在考虑危机根源和理论选择因素时，对内部和外部一致性等价值观关注甚少。）当然也存在其他类型的价值观——例如，科学应该（或不必）对社会有用——但前面的内容应该足以表明我的想法。

A third sort of element in the disciplinary matrix I shall here describe as values. Usually they are more widely shared among different communities than either symbolic generalizations or models, and they do much to provide a sense of community to natural scientists as a whole. Though they function at all times, their particular importance emerges when the members of a particular community must identify crisis or, later, choose between incompatible ways of practicing their discipline. Probably the most deeply held values concern predictions: they should be accurate; quantitative predictions are preferable to qualitative ones; whatever the margin of permissible error, it should be consistently satisfied in a given field; and so on. There are also, however, values to be used in judging whole theories: they must, first and foremost, permit puzzle-formulation and solution; where possible they should be simple, self-consistent, and plausible, compatible, that is, with other theories currently deployed. (I now think it a weakness of my original text that so little attention is given to such values as internal and external consistency in considering sources of crisis and factors in theory choice.) Other sorts of values exist as well—for example, science should (or need not) be socially useful—but the preceding should indicate what I have in mind.

然而，共享价值观的一个方面确实需要特别提及。与其他学科构成要素相比，价值观更容易被那些在应用方式上有所不同的人所共享。对准确性的判断相对稳定，尽管并非完全如此，但这种稳定会随着时间推移以及特定群体中不同成员之间的差异而变化。然而，对简洁性、一致性、合理性等等的判断却往往因人而异。对爱因斯坦而言，旧量子理论中一个无法容忍的矛盾，一个使常规科学研究无法进行的矛盾，对玻尔等人来说，却是一个可以通过常规方法解决的难题。更重要的是，在这些情况下，在必须运用价值观的情况下，不同的价值观单独来看往往会导致不同的选择。一种理论可能比另一种理论更准确，但却缺乏一致性或合理性；古老的量子理论就是一个例子。简而言之，尽管科学家们普遍认同某些价值观，并且对这些价值观的坚持既深刻又构成科学的本质，但价值观的应用有时会受到群体成员之间人格特征和个人经历的显著影响。

One aspect of shared values does, however, require particular mention. To a greater extent than other sorts of components of the disciplinary matrix, values may be shared by men who differ in their application. Judgments of accuracy are relatively, though not entirely, stable from one time to another and from one member to another in a particular group. But judgments of simplicity, consistency, plausibility, and so on often vary greatly from individual to individual. What was for Einstein an insupportable inconsistency in the old quantum theory, one that rendered the pursuit of normal science impossible, was for Bohr and others a difficulty that could be expected to work itself out by normal means. Even more important, in those situations where values must be applied, different values, taken alone, would often dictate different choices. One theory may be more accurate but less consistent or plausible than another; again the old quantum theory provides an example. In short, though values are widely shared by scientists and though commitment to them is both deep and constitutive of science, the application of values is sometimes considerably affected by the features of individual personality and biography that differentiate the members of the group.

对于前几章的许多读者来说，共享价值观运作的这一特性似乎是我观点的一个主要弱点。因为我坚持认为，科学家们所共享的价值观不足以在诸如相互竞争的理论之间的选择，或者区分普通异常和引发危机的异常等问题上达成一致意见，所以我有时会被指责美化主观性，甚至是非理性。9但这种反应忽略了任何领域价值判断所展现的两个特征。首先，即使群体成员并非都以相同的方式运用共享价值观，它们仍然可以成为群体行为的重要决定因素。（如果不是这样，就不会出现关于价值理论或美学的特殊哲学问题。）在以再现为主要价值的时期，人们的绘画风格并不完全相同，但当这一价值被摒弃后，造型艺术的发展模式发生了剧烈的变化。10试想一下，如果一致性不再是主要价值，科学领域将会发生什么。其次，个体在运用共享价值观方面的差异可能对科学至关重要。必须运用价值观的地方，往往也是必须承担风险的地方。大多数异常情况都能通过常规手段解决；大多数新理论的提出最终都被证明是错误的。如果一个社群的所有成员都对每一种异常情况做出反应……如果将科学视为危机之源，或者盲目接受同事提出的每一项新理论，科学就会停滞不前。反之，如果无人以高风险的方式应对异常现象或全新理论，革命便会寥寥无几，甚至根本不会发生。在诸如此类的问题上，诉诸共同价值观而非约束个人选择的共同规则，或许才是社群分散风险、确保其事业长期成功的方式。

To many readers of the preceding chapters, this characteristic of the operation of shared values has seemed a major weakness of my position. Because I insist that what scientists share is not sufficient to command uniform assent about such matters as the choice between competing theories or the distinction between an ordinary anomaly and a crisis-provoking one, I am occasionally accused of glorifying subjectivity and even irrationality.9 But that reaction ignores two characteristics displayed by value judgments in any field. First, shared values can be important determinants of group behavior even though the members of the group do not all apply them in the same way. (If that were not the case, there would be no special philosophic problems about value theory or aesthetics.) Men did not all paint alike during the periods when representation was a primary value, but the developmental pattern of the plastic arts changed drastically when that value was abandoned.10 Imagine what would happen in the sciences if consistency ceased to be a primary value. Second, individual variability in the application of shared values may serve functions essential to science. The points at which values must be applied are invariably also those at which risks must be taken. Most anomalies are resolved by normal means; most proposals for new theories do prove to be wrong. If all members of a community responded to each anomaly as a source of crisis or embraced each new theory advanced by a colleague, science would cease. If, on the other hand, no one reacted to anomalies or to brand-new theories in high-risk ways, there would be few or no revolutions. In matters like these the resort to shared values rather than to shared rules governing individual choice may be the community’s way of distributing risk and assuring the long-term success of its enterprise.

现在转向学科矩阵中的第四类要素，这并非唯一一类，但却是我将在此讨论的最后一类。从语文学和自传体的角度来看，“范式”一词完全恰当；正是群体共同承诺的这一组成部分，最初促使我选择了这个词。然而，由于该术语已发展出其自身的内涵，我在此将用“范例”来代替。我最初指的是学生从科学教育之初就遇到的具体问题解决方案，无论是在实验室、考试中，还是在科学教材的章节末尾。然而，除了这些共同的例子之外，还应该包括科学家在毕业后的研究生涯中，在期刊文献中遇到的一些技术性问题解决方案，这些解决方案也通过实例向他们展示了如何完成工作。与其他学科矩阵的组成部分相比，不同范例之间的差异更能构成科学共同体的精细结构。例如，所有物理学家最初学习的都是相同的范例：斜面、圆锥摆和开普勒轨道等问题；游标卡尺、量热器和惠斯通电桥等仪器。然而，随着训练的深入，他们共同掌握的符号概括越来越多地通过不同的范例来阐释。尽管固体物理学家和场论物理学家都使用薛定谔方程，但只有其较为基础的应用是两类物理学家共有的。

Turn now to a fourth sort of element in the disciplinary matrix, not the only other kind but the last I shall discuss here. For it the term ‘paradigm’ would be entirely appropriate, both philologically and autobiographically; this is the component of a group’s shared commitments which first led me to the choice of that word. Because the term has assumed a life of its own, however, I shall here substitute ‘exemplars.’ By it I mean, initially, the concrete problem-solutions that students encounter from the start of their scientific education, whether in laboratories, on examinations, or at the ends of chapters in science texts. To these shared examples should, however, be added at least some of the technical problem-solutions found in the periodical literature that scientists encounter during their post-educational research careers and that also show them by example how their job is to be done. More than other sorts of components of the disciplinary matrix, differences between sets of exemplars provide the community fine-structure of science. All physicists, for example, begin by learning the same exemplars: problems such as the inclined plane, the conical pendulum, and Keplerian orbits; instruments such as the vernier, the calorimeter, and the Wheatstone bridge. As their training develops, however, the symbolic generalizations they share are increasingly illustrated by different exemplars. Though both solid-state and field-theoretic physicists share the Schrödinger equation, only its more elementary applications are common to both groups.

3. 作为共享示例的范式

3. Paradigms as Shared Examples

以共享范例为范式，是我认为本书中最新颖、最不为人所理解的部分的核心要素。因此，范例比学科矩阵中的其他组成部分更值得关注。科学哲学家通常不讨论学生在实验室或科学教材中遇到的问题，因为他们认为这些问题仅仅是学生运用已有知识的练习。据说，除非学生先学习理论及其应用规则，否则根本无法解决问题。科学知识蕴含于理论和规则之中；问题的存在是为了帮助学生熟练运用这些理论和规则。然而，我一直试图论证，这种对科学认知内容的定位是错误的。学生在完成大量问题后，或许可以通过解决更多问题来进一步提升能力。但在学习初期以及之后的一段时间内，解决问题本身就是学习关于自然的重要知识。如果没有这样的范例，学生先前学习的定律和理论将缺乏经验内涵。

The paradigm as shared example is the central element of what I now take to be the most novel and least understood aspect of this book. Exemplars will therefore require more attention than the other sorts of components of the disciplinary matrix. Philosophers of science have not ordinarily discussed the problems encountered by a student in laboratories or in science texts, for these are thought to supply only practice in the application of what the student already knows. He cannot, it is said, solve problems at all unless he has first learned the theory and some rules for applying it. Scientific knowledge is embedded in theory and rules; problems are supplied to gain facility in their application. I have tried to argue, however, that this localization of the cognitive content of science is wrong. After the student has done many problems, he may gain only added facility by solving more. But at the start and for some time after, doing problems is learning consequential things about nature. In the absence of such exemplars, the laws and theories he has previously learned would have little empirical content.

为了阐明我的想法，我先简要地回到符号概括上来。一个广为流传的例子是牛顿第二运动定律，通常写作f = ma。比如说，一位社会学家或语言学家发现，某个特定群体的成员能够毫无障碍地使用和接受这一表达方式，但如果不进行大量的深入研究，他们并不能真正了解这一表达方式或其组成术语的含义，也不能了解该群体中的科学家是如何将这一表达方式与自然联系起来的。事实上，他们毫不质疑地接受这一表达方式，并将其作为引入逻辑和数学运算的切入点，这本身并不意味着他们在诸如含义和应用等问题上达成了一致。当然，他们在很大程度上是一致的，否则这一点会在他们随后的讨论中很快显现出来。但我们不妨追问，他们是在何时、通过何种方式达成共识的？面对特定的实验情境，他们是如何学会辨别相关的力、质量和加速度的？

To indicate what I have in mind I revert briefly to symbolic generalizations. One widely shared example is Newton’s Second Law of Motion, generally written as f = ma. The sociologist, say, or the linguist who discovers that the corresponding expression is unproblematically uttered and received by the members of a given community will not, without much additional investigation, have learned a great deal about what either the expression or the terms in it mean, about how the scientists of the community attach the expression to nature. Indeed, the fact that they accept it without question and use it as a point at which to introduce logical and mathematical manipulation does not of itself imply that they agree at all about such matters as meaning and application. Of course they do agree to a considerable extent, or the fact would rapidly emerge from their subsequent conversation. But one may well ask at what point and by what means they have come to do so. How have they learned, faced with a given experimental situation, to pick out the relevant forces, masses, and accelerations?

实际上，尽管这种情况很少或从未被注意到，但学生需要学习的内容远比这复杂得多。逻辑和数学运算并非直接应用于f = ma。经检验，该表达式证明是定律草图或定律框架。随着学生或实践科学家从一个问题情境过渡到下一个问题情境，此类操作所适用的符号概括也会发生变化。对于自由落体，f = ma变为mg = m ( d 2 s/dt 2 )；对于单摆，它变为mg sin θ = – ml ( d 2 θ/dt 2 )；对于一对相互作用的谐振子，它变为两个方程，第一个方程可以写成m 1 ( d 2 s 1 / dt 2 ) + k 1 s 1 = k 2 ( s 2 – s 1 + d )；而对于更复杂的情况，例如陀螺仪，它又呈现出其他形式，这些形式与f = ma的相似之处更难发现。然而，在学习识别各种以前从未遇到过的物理情境中的力、质量和加速度的同时，这位学生也学会了设计合适的f = ma公式来关联它们，而这种公式通常是他以前从未接触过的。他是如何学会做到这一点的呢？

In practice, though this aspect of the situation is seldom or never noted, what students have to learn is even more complex than that. It is not quite the case that logical and mathematical manipulation are applied directly to f = ma. That expression proves on examination to be a law-sketch or a law-schema. As the student or the practicing scientist moves from one problem situation to the next, the symbolic generalization to which such manipulations apply changes. For the case of free fall, f = ma becomes mg = m(d2s/dt2); for the simple pendulum it is transformed to mg sinθ = –ml(d2θ/dt2); for a pair of interacting harmonic oscillators it becomes two equations, the first of which may be written m1(d2s1/dt2) + k1s1 = k2(s2 –s1 + d); and for more complex situations, such as the gyroscope, it takes still other forms, the family resemblance of which to f = ma is still harder to discover. Yet, while learning to identify forces, masses, and accelerations in a variety of physical situations not previously encountered, the student has also learned to design the appropriate version of f = ma through which to interrelate them, often a version for which he has encountered no literal equivalent before. How has he learned to do this?

科学学生和科学史学家都熟悉的一种现象为我们提供了线索。科学学生经常反映，他们读完一章教材后，完全理解了内容，但却难以解答章末的一些习题。通常情况下，这些难题也会以同样的方式迎刃而解。学生会发现，无论是否得到老师的帮助，他们都能找到一种方法，将当前的问题与之前遇到的问题联系起来。一旦发现了相似之处，理解了两个或多个不同问题之间的类比，他们就能将符号关联起来，并以以往行之有效的方式将其与自然联系起来。例如，定律草图（如f = ma）就起到了工具的作用，它告诉学生应该寻找哪些相似之处，并指明了看待问题的整体框架。我认为，学生通过练习例题（无论是在纸笔上还是在精心设计的实验室里）所获得的主要能力，就是能够将各种情况视为彼此相似，并将它们视为f = ma或其他符号概括的对象。当他完成一定数量的例题后（这个数量因人而异），他就能以与其他专家相同的视角看待自己作为科学家所面临的各种情况。对他而言，这些情况不再是他之前遇到的相同情况。在他开始接受训练之后，他已经吸收了一种经过时间检验并得到团体认可的观察方式。

A phenomenon familiar to both students of science and historians of science provides a clue. The former regularly report that they have read through a chapter of their text, understood it perfectly, but nonetheless had difficulty solving a number of the problems at the chapter’s end. Ordinarily, also, those difficulties dissolve in the same way. The student discovers, with or without the assistance of his instructor, a way to see his problem as like a problem he has already encountered. Having seen the resemblance, grasped the analogy between two or more distinct problems, he can interrelate symbols and attach them to nature in the ways that have proved effective before. The law-sketch, say f = ma, has functioned as a tool, informing the student what similarities to look for, signaling the gestalt in which the situation is to be seen. The resultant ability to see a variety of situations as like each other, as subjects for f = ma or some other symbolic generalization, is, I think, the main thing a student acquires by doing exemplary problems, whether with a pencil and paper or in a well-designed laboratory. After he has completed a certain number, which may vary widely from one individual to the next, he views the situations that confront him as a scientist in the same gestalt as other members of his specialists’ group. For him they are no longer the same situations he had encountered when his training began. He has meanwhile assimilated a time-tested and group-licensed way of seeing.

在科学史上，习得相似关系的作用也清晰可见。科学家们通过借鉴以往的解法来解决难题，通常只需极少地运用符号概括。伽利略发现，一个球沿斜坡滚下时，其速度恰好足以使其在任意坡度的第二个斜坡上回到相同的垂直高度。他由此领悟到，这种实验情境类似于以质点为摆锤的单摆。惠更斯随后解决了物理单摆的振荡中心问题，他设想单摆的延伸部分由伽利略式的点摆组成，这些点摆之间的连接可以在摆动过程中的任何时刻瞬间断开。连接断开后，各个点摆可以自由摆动，但它们到达最高点时的总重心，就像伽利略的单摆一样，只会上升到延伸单摆重心开始下落的高度。最后，丹尼尔·伯努利发现了如何使水从孔口流出的运动类似于惠更斯摆的运动。首先，确定水箱和喷嘴中水的重心在极短时间间隔内的下降量。然后，假设每个水粒子随后分别向上运动到该时间间隔内所达到的最大高度。那么，各个水粒子的重心上升量必须等于水箱和喷嘴中水的重心下降量。从这个角度来看，人们苦苦追寻的流速便迎刃而解了。11

The role of acquired similarity relations also shows clearly in the history of science. Scientists solve puzzles by modeling them on previous puzzle-solutions, often with only minimal recourse to symbolic generalizations. Galileo found that a ball rolling down an incline acquires just enough velocity to return it to the same vertical height on a second incline of any slope, and he learned to see that experimental situation as like the pendulum with a point-mass for a bob. Huyghens then solved the problem of the center of oscillation of a physical pendulum by imagining that the extended body of the latter was composed of Galilean point-pendula, the bonds between which could be instantaneously released at any point in the swing. After the bonds were released, the individual point-pendula would swing freely, but their collective center of gravity when each attained its highest point would, like that of Galileo’s pendulum, rise only to the height from which the center of gravity of the extended pendulum had begun to fall. Finally, Daniel Bernoulli discovered how to make the flow of water from an orifice resemble Huyghens’ pendulum. Determine the descent of the center of gravity of the water in tank and jet during an infinitesimal interval of time. Next imagine that each particle of water afterward moves separately upward to the maximum height attainable with the velocity acquired during that interval. The ascent of the center of gravity of the individual particles must then equal the descent of the center of gravity of the water in tank and jet. From that view of the problem the long-sought speed of efflux followed at once.11

这个例子应该能开始清楚地说明我所说的从问题中学习，将各种情况视为彼此相似、都是研究对象是什么意思。应用相同的科学定律或定律概要。同时，这也应该说明为什么我指的是在学习相似关系的过程中获得的、并随后体现在看待物理情境方式中的自然知识，而不是规则或定律。示例中的三个问题，都是十八世纪力学家的典型范例，它们都只运用了一条自然定律。这条定律被称为“活物原理”，通常表述为：“实际下降等于潜在上升”。伯努利对这条定律的应用应该能说明它的重要性。然而，单就定律的文字表述而言，它几乎毫无意义。把它呈现给一位当代物理学学生，他知道这些文字，也能解决所有这些问题，但他现在采用的是不同的方法。然后想象一下，这些文字，即使众所周知，对于一个甚至不知道这些问题的人来说，又意味着什么呢？对他而言，只有当他学会将“实际下降”和“潜在上升”视为自然界的组成部分时，概括才能开始发挥作用。也就是说，在了解规律之前，他必须先了解自然界呈现和不呈现的情境。这种学习并非完全通过语言方式获得。相反，它需要将词语与具体的实例结合起来，才能理解它们在实际应用中的运作方式；自然与词语是相辅相成的。再次借用迈克尔·波兰尼的精辟论述，这一过程的最终成果是“隐性知识”，它是通过实践科学而非学习科学规则而获得的。

That example should begin to make clear what I mean by learning from problems to see situations as like each other, as subjects for the application of the same scientific law or law-sketch. Simultaneously it should show why I refer to the consequential knowledge of nature acquired while learning the similarity relationship and thereafter embodied in a way of viewing physical situations rather than in rules or laws. The three problems in the example, all of them exemplars for eighteenth-century mechanicians, deploy only one law of nature. Known as the Principle of vis viva, it was usually stated as: “Actual descent equals potential ascent.” Bernoulli’s application of the law should suggest how consequential it was. Yet the verbal statement of the law, taken by itself, is virtually impotent. Present it to a contemporary student of physics, who knows the words and can do all these problems but now employs different means. Then imagine what the words, though all well known, can have said to a man who did not know even the problems. For him the generalization could begin to function only when he learned to recognize “actual descents” and “potential ascents” as ingredients of nature, and that is to learn something, prior to the law, about the situations that nature does and does not present. That sort of learning is not acquired by exclusively verbal means. Rather it comes as one is given words together with concrete examples of how they function in use; nature and words are learned together. To borrow once more Michael Polanyi’s useful phrase, what results from this process is “tacit knowledge” which is learned by doing science rather than by acquiring rules for doing it.

4. 隐性知识和直觉

4. Tacit Knowledge and Intuition

提及隐性知识并同时摒弃规则，凸显了另一个困扰我诸多批评者的问题，这个问题似乎也为指责我主观性和非理性提供了依据。一些读者认为，我试图让科学建立在无法分析的个人直觉之上，而非逻辑和法则之上。但这种解读在两个关键方面是错误的。首先，即便我谈论的是直觉，它们也并非个人的。相反，它们是经过检验并由成功群体成员共享的经验，新手则是通过训练来习得这些经验的。首先，为加入小组做准备。其次，它们并非原则上不可分析。相反，我目前正在试验一个计算机程序，旨在从基础层面研究它们的性质。

That reference to tacit knowledge and the concurrent rejection of rules isolates another problem that has bothered many of my critics and seemed to provide a basis for charges of subjectivity and irrationality. Some readers have felt that I was trying to make science rest on unanalyzable individual intuitions rather than on logic and law. But that interpretation goes astray in two essential respects. First, if I am talking at all about intuitions, they are not individual. Rather they are the tested and shared possessions of the members of a successful group, and the novice acquires them through training as a part of his preparation for group-membership. Second, they are not in principle unanalyzable. On the contrary, I am currently experimenting with a computer program designed to investigate their properties at an elementary level.

关于那个项目，我在此不做赘述，12但即便提及它，也足以阐明我的核心观点。当我谈到蕴含于共享范例中的知识时，我指的并非一种不如蕴含于规则、法则或识别标准中的知识那样系统或可分析的认知模式。相反，我指的是一种认知方式，如果将其重构为首先从范例中抽象出来并取代范例发挥作用的规则，则会被误解。或者，换一种说法，当我谈到从范例中获得识别特定情境与先前见过的某些情境相似、与另一些情境不同的能力时，我并非暗示一个无法用神经脑机制完全解释的过程。相反，我主张，这种解释本质上无法回答“相似之处体现在哪些方面？”这个问题。这个问题实际上是在请求一条规则，具体来说，就是请求提供将特定情况归类为相似集合的标准。而我认为，在这种情况下，我们应该抵制寻求标准（或者至少是一套完整的标准）的诱惑。然而，我反对的并非整个系统，而是某种特定类型的系统。

About that program I shall have nothing to say here,12 but even mention of it should make my most essential point. When I speak of knowledge embedded in shared exemplars, I am not referring to a mode of knowing that is less systematic or less analyzable than knowledge embedded in rules, laws, or criteria of identification. Instead I have in mind a manner of knowing which is miscontrued if reconstructed in terms of rules that are first abstracted from exemplars and thereafter function in their stead. Or, to put the same point differently, when I speak of acquiring from exemplars the ability to recognize a given situation as like some and unlike others that one has seen before, I am not suggesting a process that is not potentially fully explicable in terms of neuro-cerebral mechanism. Instead I am claiming that the explication will not, by its nature, answer the question, “Similar with respect to what?” That question is a request for a rule, in this case for the criteria by which particular situations are grouped into similarity sets, and I am arguing that the temptation to seek criteria (or at least a full set) should be resisted in this case. It is not, however, system but a particular sort of system that I am opposing.

为了阐明这一点，我必须先稍作补充。接下来的内容现在对我来说似乎显而易见，但我在原文中反复使用“世界在变化”之类的短语表明，情况并非一直如此。如果两个人站在同一个地方，目光看向同一个方向，那么我们不得不承认，他们接收到的刺激非常相似，否则就会陷入唯我论的陷阱。（如果两人都能将目光聚焦在同一个位置，那么他们接收到的刺激就完全相同。）但人们并非直接看到刺激；我们对刺激的认知是高度理论化和抽象的。相反，人们拥有的是感觉，而我们完全没有理由假定两位观察者的感觉是相同的。（怀疑论者或许会记得，在约翰·道尔顿描述色盲之前，色盲现象几乎无人知晓。）（1794年。）相反，在接收到刺激和意识到感觉之间，会发生大量的神经处理过程。我们确信无疑的几件事包括：截然不同的刺激可以产生相同的感觉；相同的刺激可以产生截然不同的感觉；最后，从刺激到感觉的路径部分受到教育的影响。在不同社会中成长的人，在某些情况下表现得好像他们看到了不同的事物。如果我们不倾向于将刺激与感觉一一对应，我们或许会意识到，他们实际上确实如此。

To give that point substance, I must briefly digress. What follows seems obvious to me now, but the constant recourse in my original text to phrases like “the world changes” suggests that it has not always been so. If two people stand at the same place and gaze in the same direction, we must, under pain of solipsism, conclude that they receive closely similar stimuli. (If both could put their eyes at the same place, the stimuli would be identical.) But people do not see stimuli; our knowledge of them is highly theoretical and abstract. Instead they have sensations, and we are under no compulsion to suppose that the sensations of our two viewers are the same. (Sceptics might remember that color blindness was nowhere noticed until John Dalton’s description of it in 1794.) On the contrary, much neural processing takes place between the receipt of a stimulus and the awareness of a sensation. Among the few things that we know about it with assurance are: that very different stimuli can produce the same sensations; that the same stimulus can produce very different sensations; and, finally, that the route from stimulus to sensation is in part conditioned by education. Individuals raised in different societies behave on some occasions as though they saw different things. If we were not tempted to identify stimuli one-to-one with sensations, we might recognize that they actually do so.

现在请注意，两个群体成员对相同刺激产生系统性不同的感受，从某种意义上说，它们生活在不同的世界中。我们假设刺激的存在是为了解释我们对世界的感知，我们假设刺激的不变性是为了避免个体和社会的唯我论。我对这两个假设都毫无保留。但是，我们的世界首先并非由刺激构成，而是由我们感受的对象构成，而这些对象未必相同，个体之间或群体之间都可能不同。当然，如果个体属于同一群体，从而共享教育、语言、经验和文化，那么我们有充分的理由假设他们的感受是相同的。否则，我们如何理解他们之间充分的交流以及他们对环境行为反应的共性呢？他们看待事物、处理刺激的方式必然大致相同。但是，一旦群体开始分化和专业化，我们就找不到类似的证据来证明感受的不变性了。我怀疑，仅仅是狭隘的地方主义就让我们认为，从刺激到感觉的路径对于所有群体成员来说都是相同的。

Notice now that two groups, the members of which have systematically different sensations on receipt of the same stimuli, do in some sense live in different worlds. We posit the existence of stimuli to explain our perceptions of the world, and we posit their immutability to avoid both individual and social solipsism. About neither posit have I the slightest reservation. But our world is populated in the first instance not by stimuli but by the objects of our sensations, and these need not be the same, individual to individual or group to group. To the extent, of course, that individuals belong to the same group and thus share education, language, experience, and culture, we have good reason to suppose that their sensations are the same. How else are we to understand the fulness of their communication and the communality of their behavioral responses to their environment? They must see things, process stimuli, in much the same ways. But where the differentiation and specialization of groups begins, we have no similar evidence for the immutability of sensation. Mere parochialism, I suspect, makes us suppose that the route from stimuli to sensation is the same for the members of all groups.

现在回到范例和规则的话题，我一直试图提出的，尽管只是初步的，是这样的：一个群体（无论是整个文化群体还是其中的某个专家小组）的成员，在面对相同刺激时，学会看待相同事物的基本技巧之一，就是通过向他们展示群体中前辈已经学会区分彼此相似和不同的情境范例。其他类型的情境。这些相似的情境可能是对同一人的连续感官呈现——例如，对母亲的呈现，最终人们会通过视觉识别出她的身份，并将其与父亲或姐妹区分开来。它们也可能是对自然家庭成员的呈现，例如，先是天鹅，然后是鹅。或者，对于更专业群体的成员而言，它们可能是牛顿情境的例证，即那些都遵循某种形式的符号公式f = ma的情境，但与例如光学定律草图所适用的情境不同。

Returning now to exemplars and rules, what I have been trying to suggest, in however preliminary a fashion, is this. One of the fundamental techniques by which the members of a group, whether an entire culture or a specialists’ sub-community within it, learn to see the same things when confronted with the same stimuli is by being shown examples of situations that their predecessors in the group have already learned to see as like each other and as different from other sorts of situations. These similar situations may be successive sensory presentations of the same individual—say of mother, who is ultimately recognized on sight as what she is and as different from father or sister. They may be presentations of the members of natural families, say of swans on the one hand and of geese on the other. Or they may, for the members of more specialized groups, be examples of the Newtonian situation, of situations, that is, that are alike in being subject to a version of the symbolic form f = ma and that are different from those situations to which, for example, the law-sketches of optics apply.

暂且假设这类事情确实存在。我们是否可以说，我们从范例中获得的是规则以及运用这些规则的能力？这种描述颇具诱惑力，因为我们之所以会将某种情况与之前遇到的情况相提并论，必然是神经处理的结果，而神经处理完全受物理和化学定律的支配。从这个意义上讲，一旦我们学会了这种能力，对相似性的识别就必然像我们的心跳一样完全系统化。但这种类比本身也暗示着，这种识别也可能是无意识的，一个我们无法控制的过程。如果是这样，那么我们就不能将其理解为我们通过运用规则和标准来控制的事情。如果这样理解，就意味着我们还有其他选择，例如，我们可能违反了某条规则，或者错误地运用了某个标准，或者尝试了其他一些看待问题的方式。13我认为，这些恰恰是我们无法做到的事情。

Grant for the moment that something of this sort does occur. Ought we say that what has been acquired from exemplars is rules and the ability to apply them? That description is tempting because our seeing a situation as like ones we have encountered before must be the result of neural processing, fully governed by physical and chemical laws. In this sense, once we have learned to do it, recognition of similarity must be as fully systematic as the beating of our hearts. But that very parallel suggests that recognition may also be involuntary, a process over which we have no control. If it is, then we may not properly conceive it as something we manage by applying rules and criteria. To speak of it in those terms implies that we have access to alternatives, that we might, for example, have disobeyed a rule, or misapplied a criterion, or experimented with some other way of seeing.13 Those, I take it, are just the sorts of things we cannot do.

或者更准确地说，这些事情只有在我们产生感觉、感知到某物之后才能进行。那时我们通常会寻求判断标准并加以运用。然后我们可能会进行诠释，这是一个深思熟虑的过程，在这个过程中，我们会在各种可能性之间做出选择，而这在感知本身中是不会发生的。例如，也许我们所看到的事物有些奇怪（想想那些异常的扑克牌）。在某个角落，我们看到母亲走进市中心的一家商店，而我们原本以为她应该在家。我们回想着刚才所见，突然惊呼：“那不是妈妈，她有一头红发！”走进商店，我们再次看到那位女士，却百思不得其解，怎么会把她误认为是妈妈。又或许，我们看到一只水禽的尾羽在浅水池底觅食。它是天鹅还是鹅？我们仔细观察着眼前的景象，在脑海中将它的尾羽与我们之前见过的天鹅和鹅的尾羽进行比较。或者，也许，我们这些“准科学家”只是想知道某个我们能够轻易辨认的自然家族成员的一些共同特征（例如天鹅的白色羽毛）。于是，我们再次思考之前所见，寻找这个家族成员的共同点。

Or, more precisely, those are things we cannot do until after we have had a sensation, perceived something. Then we do often seek criteria and put them to use. Then we may engage in interpretation, a deliberative process by which we choose among alternatives as we do not in perception itself. Perhaps, for example, something is odd about what we have seen (remember the anomalous playing cards). Turning a corner we see mother entering a downtown store at a time we had thought she was home. Contemplating what we have seen we suddenly exclaim, “That wasn’t mother, for she has red hair!” Entering the store we see the woman again and cannot understand how she could have been taken for mother. Or, perhaps we see the tail feathers of a waterfowl feeding from the bottom of a shallow pool. Is it a swan or a goose? We contemplate what we have seen, mentally comparing the tail feathers with those of swans and geese we have seen before. Or, perhaps, being proto-scientists, we simply want to know some general characteristic (the whiteness of swans, for example) of the members of a natural family we can already recognize with ease. Again, we contemplate what we have previously perceived, searching for what the members of the given family have in common.

这些都是深思熟虑的过程，在这些过程中，我们确实会寻求并运用各种标准和规则。也就是说，我们会尝试解读已有的感觉，分析对我们而言既定的事物。无论我们如何做到这一点，所涉及的过程最终必然是神经性的，因此它们都受制于相同的物理化学定律，这些定律既支配着感知，也支配着我们的心跳。但是，系统在所有三种情况下都遵循相同的定律这一事实，并不能说明我们的神经装置在解释过程中的运作方式与感知过程相同，或者在解释过程中或感知过程中的运作方式与心跳过程相同。因此，我在本书中一直反对的，是自笛卡尔以来（但在此之前并非如此）一直存在的将感知分析为一种解释过程、一种我们感知之后所做行为的无意识版本的尝试。

These are all deliberative processes, and in them we do seek and deploy criteria and rules. We try, that is, to interpret sensations already at hand, to analyze what is for us the given. However we do that, the processes involved must ultimately be neural, and they are therefore governed by the same physicochemical laws that govern perception on the one hand and the beating of our hearts on the other. But the fact that the system obeys the same laws in all three cases provides no reason to suppose that our neural apparatus is programmed to operate the same way in interpretation as in perception or in either as in the beating of our hearts. What I have been opposing in this book is therefore the attempt, traditional since Descartes but not before, to analyze perception as an interpretive process, as an unconscious version of what we do after we have perceived.

之所以强调感知的完整性，当然是因为大量的过往经验都体现在将刺激转化为感觉的神经系统中。一个程序恰当的感知机制具有生存价值。不同群体成员面对相同刺激时可能产生不同的感知，并不意味着他们可以随意产生任何感知。在许多环境中，一个无法区分狼和狗的群体是无法生存的。同样，一个核心群体也无法生存。即使无法识别α粒子和电子的轨迹，今天的物理学家依然可以作为科学家生存下去。正因为能够识别这些轨迹的观察方式寥寥无几，那些经受住群体使用考验的方式才值得代代相传。同样，也正因为它们在历史长河中被成功选择，我们才必须谈论蕴含在刺激到感觉路径中的自然经验和知识。

What makes the integrity of perception worth emphasizing is, of course, that so much past experience is embodied in the neural apparatus that transforms stimuli to sensations. An appropriately programmed perceptual mechanism has survival value. To say that the members of different groups may have different perceptions when confronted with the same stimuli is not to imply that they may have just any perceptions at all. In many environments a group that could not tell wolves from dogs could not endure. Nor would a group of nuclear physicists today survive as scientists if unable to recognize the tracks of alpha particles and electrons. It is just because so very few ways of seeing will do that the ones that have withstood the tests of group use are worth transmitting from generation to generation. Equally, it is because they have been selected for their success over historic time that we must speak of the experience and knowledge of nature embedded in the stimulus-to-sensation route.

或许“知识”这个词用得不太恰当，但使用它也有其原因。将刺激转化为感觉的神经过程本身具有以下特征：它通过教育传承；经实践证明，在群体当前的环境中，它比以往的同类方法更有效；最后，它会随着进一步的教育以及对环境不适应者的发现而发生改变。这些都是知识的特征，也解释了我为何使用这个词。但这种用法有些奇怪，因为它缺少另一个特征。我们无法直接获取我们所知的内容，也没有任何规则或概括可以用来表达这种知识。能够提供这种获取途径的规则指的是刺激而非感觉，而我们只能通过复杂的理论来了解刺激。正因为缺乏这种规则，蕴含在刺激到感觉路径中的知识才仍然是隐性的。

Perhaps ‘knowledge’ is the wrong word, but there are reasons for employing it. What is built into the neural process that transforms stimuli to sensations has the following characteristics: it has been transmitted through education; it has, by trial, been found more effective than its historical competitors in a group’s current environment; and, finally, it is subject to change both through further education and through the discovery of misfits with the environment. Those are characteristics of knowledge, and they explain why I use the term. But it is strange usage, for one other characteristic is missing. We have no direct access to what it is we know, no rules or generalizations with which to express this knowledge. Rules which could supply that access would refer to stimuli not sensations, and stimuli we can know only through elaborate theory. In its absence, the knowledge embedded in the stimulus-to-sensation route remains tacit.

尽管这显然只是初步的，未必在所有细节上都完全正确，但刚才关于感觉的论述是字面意义上的。至少，这是一种关于视觉的假设，应该通过实验研究来验证，尽管可能无需直接检验。但此处对视觉和感觉的描述，正如本书正文中那样，也具有隐喻功能。我们看不到电子，看到的只是它们的轨迹，或者云室中的气泡。我们根本看不到电流，看到的只是电流表或检流计的指针。然而，在前面的章节中，尤其是在第十节中，我反复假设我们确实能够感知到电流、电子和场等理论实体，假设我们是通过观察实例而学会感知的，并且假设在这些情况下，用标准和解释来代替对“看到”的描述也是错误的。将“观看”这一概念生搬硬套到这类语境中，显然不足以支撑此类论断。长此以往，这种隐喻必须被摒弃，取而代之的是更为直白的论述方式。

Though it is obviously preliminary and need not be correct in all details, what has just been said about sensation is meant literally. At the very least it is a hypothesis about vision which should be subject to experimental investigation though probably not to direct check. But talk like this of seeing and sensation here also serves metaphorical functions as it does in the body of the book. We do not see electrons, but rather their tracks or else bubbles of vapor in a cloud chamber. We do not see electric currents at all, but rather the needle of an am- meter or galvanometer. Yet in the preceding pages, particularly in Section X, I have repeatedly acted as though we did perceive theoretical entities like currents, electrons, and fields, as though we learned to do so from examination of exemplars, and as though in these cases too it would be wrong to replace talk of seeing with talk of criteria and interpretation. The metaphor that transfers ‘seeing’ to contexts like these is scarcely a sufficient basis for such claims. In the long run it will need to be eliminated in favor of a more literal mode of discourse.

上文提到的计算机程序开始提出一些实现方法，但无论篇幅如何，也无论我目前的理解能力如何，都不允许我在此省略这个比喻。14因此，我将尝试简要地阐述它。对于不熟悉云室和电流表的人来说，看到水滴或指针在数字刻度上的移动是一种原始的感知体验。因此，在得出关于电子或电流的结论之前，需要进行思考、分析和解释（或者借助外部权威）。但是，对于那些了解这些仪器并拥有大量实践经验的人来说，情况则截然不同，他们处理来自这些仪器的刺激的方式也相应不同。在一个寒冷的冬日午后，当他感受到呼出的气体时，他的感觉可能与普通人相同，但当他观察云室时，他看到的（这里是字面意义上的）不是水滴，而是电子、α粒子等等的轨迹。如果你愿意的话，这些轨迹是他用来解释相应粒子存在的指标的标准，但这条路径既短又与解释液滴的人所采取的路径不同。

The computer program referred to above begins to suggest ways in which that may be done, but neither available space nor the extent of my present understanding permits my eliminating the metaphor here.14 Instead I shall try briefly to bulwark it. Seeing water droplets or a needle against a numerical scale is a primitive perceptual experience for the man unacquainted with cloud chambers and ammeters. It thus requires contemplation, analysis, and interpretation (or else the intervention of external authority) before conclusions can be reached about electrons or currents. But the position of the man who has learned about these instruments and had much exemplary experience with them is very different, and there are corresponding differences in the way he processes the stimuli that reach him from them. Regarding the vapor in his breath on a cold winter afternoon, his sensation may be the same as that of a layman, but viewing a cloud chamber he sees (here literally) not droplets but the tracks of electrons, alpha particles, and so on. Those tracks are, if you will, criteria that he interprets as indices of the presence of the corresponding particles, but that route is both shorter and different from the one taken by the man who interprets droplets.

或者想象一下，一位科学家正在检查电流表，以确定指针最终停在哪个数值上。他的感觉很可能这与普通人的情况类似，尤其对于那些之前已经读取过其他类型仪表的人来说更是如此。因为他已经（通常是字面意义上的）在整个电路的背景下观察过仪表，并且对它的内部结构有所了解。对他而言，指针的位置是一个判断标准，但仅仅代表电流的大小。要解读指针的位置，他只需要确定应该在哪个刻度上读取即可。然而，对于普通人来说，指针的位置除了它本身之外，不代表任何其他东西。要解读指针的位置，他必须检查整个电路的布局，包括内部和外部的线路，还要测试电池和磁铁等等。无论是在比喻意义上还是在字面意义上，“看到”都意味着解释始于感知结束之处。这两个过程并不相同，感知留给解释的后续工作很大程度上取决于先前经验和训练的性质和数量。

Or consider the scientist inspecting an ammeter to determine the number against which the needle has settled. His sensation probably is the same as the layman’s, particularly if the latter has read other sorts of meters before. But he has seen the meter (again often literally) in the context of the entire circuit, and he knows something about its internal structure. For him the needle’s position is a criterion, but only of the value of the current. To interpret it he need determine only on which scale the meter is to be read. For the layman, on the other hand, the needle’s position is not a criterion of anything except itself. To interpret it, he must examine the whole layout of wires, internal and external, experiment with batteries and magnets, and so on. In the metaphorical no less than in the literal use of ‘seeing,’ interpretation begins where perception ends. The two processes are not the same, and what perception leaves for interpretation to complete depends drastically on the nature and amount of prior experience and training.

5. 典范、不可通约性和革命

5. Exemplars, Incommensurability, and Revolutions

刚才所述为阐明本书的另一个方面奠定了基础：我关于不可通约性及其对科学家们在选择不同理论时的影响的论述。 15 在第十节和第十二节中，我论证了此类辩论的各方对于双方都可利用的某些实验或观察情境必然持有不同的观点。然而，由于他们讨论这些情境时所使用的词汇主要由相同的术语构成，他们必然以不同的方式将这些术语与自然联系起来，因此他们的交流必然是片面的。结果，一种理论优于另一种理论是无法在辩论中证明的。相反，我一直坚持认为，每一方都必须尝试通过说服来改变对方的观点。只有哲学家严重误解了我论证的这些部分。然而，一些哲学家却声称我认为： 16不可通约理论的支持者无法与……进行沟通彼此之间完全没有关联；因此，在理论选择的辩论中，不能诉诸合理的理由；相反，理论的选择最终必须基于个人和主观的理由；某种神秘的感知决定了最终做出的决定。本书中，这些误解所依据的段落，比任何其他部分都更容易招致非理性的指责。

What has just been said provides a basis for clarifying one more aspect of the book: my remarks on incommensurability and its consequences for scientists debating the choice between successive theories.15 In Sections X and XII I have argued that the parties to such debates inevitably see differently certain of the experimental or observational situations to which both have recourse. Since the vocabularies in which they discuss such situations consist, however, predominantly of the same terms, they must be attaching some of those terms to nature differently, and their communication is inevitably only partial. As a result, the superiority of one theory to another is something that cannot be proved in the debate. Instead, I have insisted, each party must try, by persuasion, to convert the other. Only philosophers have seriously misconstrued the intent of these parts of my argument. A number of them, however, have reported that I believe the following:16 the proponents of incommensurable theories cannot communicate with each other at all; as a result, in a debate over theory-choice there can be no recourse to good reasons; instead theory must be chosen for reasons that are ultimately personal and subjective; some sort of mystical apperception is responsible for the decision actually reached. More than any other parts of the book, the passages on which these misconstructions rest have been responsible for charges of irrationality.

首先，请考虑我对证明的论述。我一直试图阐明的观点很简单，在科学哲学领域早已为人熟知。关于理论选择的争论无法完全以逻辑或数学证明的形式展开。在后者中，前提和推理规则从一开始就被设定。如果对结论存在分歧，随后争论的双方可以逐一回溯他们的推理过程，对照先前的设定进行检查。在这个过程的最后，一方必须承认自己犯了错误，违反了先前接受的规则。一旦承认错误，他就无计可施，对方的证明就具有说服力。只有当双方发现他们对既定规则的含义或应用存在分歧，他们先前的共识不足以构成证明的充分基础时，争论才会继续进行，并最终演变为科学革命中不可避免的那种形式。这种争论的核心在于前提，其手段是说服，以此作为证明的先决条件。

Consider first my remarks on proof. The point I have been trying to make is a simple one, long familiar in philosophy of science. Debates over theory-choice cannot be cast in a form that fully resembles logical or mathematical proof. In the latter, premises and rules of inference are stipulated from the start. If there is disagreement about conclusions, the parties to the ensuing debate can retrace their steps one by one, checking each against prior stipulation. At the end of that process one or the other must concede that he has made a mistake, violated a previously accepted rule. After that concession he has no recourse, and his opponent’s proof is then compelling. Only if the two discover instead that they differ about the meaning or application of stipulated rules, that their prior agreement provides no sufficient basis for proof, does the debate continue in the form it inevitably takes during scientific revolutions. That debate is about premises, and its recourse is to persuasion as a prelude to the possibility of proof.

这个相对熟悉的论点并不意味着不存在被说服的充分理由，也不意味着这些理由最终对群体而言不是决定性的。它甚至没有暗示选择的理由与科学哲学家通常列举的理由（例如准确性、简洁性、有效性等等）有所不同。然而，它应该表明的是，这些理由本身就是一种价值，因此，认同这些理由的人可以以不同的方式，无论是个体还是群体，运用这些理由。例如，如果两个人对各自理论的有效性存在分歧，或者他们对有效性达成共识，但在有效性和范围等因素在做出选择时的相对重要性上存在分歧，那么双方都不能被指责犯错。这两种情况都不算不科学。不存在中立的理论选择算法，也不存在系统性的决策程序，只要正确运用，就必然会导致群体中的每个人做出相同的决定。从这个意义上讲，真正做出有效决策的是专家群体，而非其成员个体。要理解科学为何如此发展，我们无需探究每个人做出特定选择的个人经历和性格细节（尽管这方面的话题引人入胜）。然而，我们必须理解的是，一套特定的共同价值观如何与专家群体所共享的特定经验相互作用，从而确保群体中的大多数成员最终会选择一套论证而非另一套论证作为决定性因素。

Nothing about that relatively familiar thesis implies either that there are no good reasons for being persuaded or that those reasons are not ultimately decisive for the group. Nor does it even imply that the reasons for choice are different from those usually listed by philosophers of science: accuracy, simplicity, fruitfulness, and the like. What it should suggest, however, is that such reasons function as values and that they can thus be differently applied, individually and collectively, by men who concur in honoring them. If two men disagree, for example, about the relative fruitfulness of their theories, or if they agree about that but disagree about the relative importance of fruitfulness and, say, scope in reaching a choice, neither can be convicted of a mistake. Nor is either being unscientific. There is no neutral algorithm for theory-choice, no systematic decision procedure which, properly applied, must lead each individual in the group to the same decision. In this sense it is the community of specialists rather than its individual members that makes the effective decision. To understand why science develops as it does, one need not unravel the details of biography and personality that lead each individual to a particular choice, though that topic has vast fascination. What one must understand, however, is the manner in which a particular set of shared values interacts with the particular experiences shared by a community of specialists to ensure that most members of the group will ultimately find one set of arguments rather than another decisive.

这个过程本身就是一种说服，但它引出了一个更深层次的问题。两个人如果对同一情况的理解不同，却在讨论中使用相同的词汇，那么他们使用的词语必然不同。也就是说，他们是从我所说的不可通约的视角出发进行讨论的。他们又怎能指望进行有效的沟通，更遑论达成共识呢？即使是对这个问题的初步解答，也需要进一步阐明问题的本质。我认为，至少在某种程度上，这个问题可以归结为以下形式。

That process is persuasion, but it presents a deeper problem. Two men who perceive the same situation differently but nevertheless employ the same vocabulary in its discussion must be using words differently. They speak, that is, from what I have called incommensurable viewpoints. How can they even hope to talk together much less to be persuasive. Even a preliminary answer to that question demands further specification of the nature of the difficulty. I suppose that, at least in part, it takes the following form.

常规科学的实践依赖于从范例中习得的能力，即把物体和情境归类到相似性集合中。这种归类是原始的，因为归类本身并不回答“相似于什么？”这个问题。因此，任何革命的核心特征之一就是某些相似性关系的改变。之前被归入同一集合的物体，之后可能被归入不同的集合，反之亦然。想想哥白尼之前和之后太阳、月亮、火星和地球的变化；伽利略之前和之后自由落体、钟摆和行星运动的变化；或者道尔顿之前和之后盐、合金和硫铁混合物的变化。由于即使在改变后的集合中，大多数物体仍然被归为一类，因此集合的名称通常得以保留。然而，子集的转移通常是它们之间相互关系网络发生重大变化的一部分。将金属从化合物集合转移到元素集合，在燃烧理论、酸度理论以及物理和化学结合理论的出现过程中发挥了至关重要的作用。这些变化很快便传播到整个化学领域。因此，当这种重新分配……例如，两个此前看似完全理解的讨论者，可能会突然发现他们对同一刺激的描述和概括截然不同。这些困难并非在他们所有科学讨论领域都会出现，但它们确实会出现，并且会在理论选择最为关键的现象周围最为集中。

The practice of normal science depends on the ability, acquired from exemplars, to group objects and situations into similarity sets which are primitive in the sense that the grouping is done without an answer to the question, “Similar with respect to what?” One central aspect of any revolution is, then, that some of the similarity relations change. Objects that were grouped in the same set before are grouped in different ones afterward and vice versa. Think of the sun, moon, Mars, and earth before and after Copernicus; of free fall, pendular, and planetary motion before and after Galileo; or of salts, alloys, and a sulphur–iron filing mix before and after Dalton. Since most objects within even the altered sets continue to be grouped together, the names of the sets are usually preserved. Nevertheless, the transfer of a subset is ordinarily part of a critical change in the network of interrelations among them. Transferring the metals from the set of compounds to the set of elements played an essential role in the emergence of a new theory of combustion, of acidity, and of physical and chemical combination. In short order those changes had spread through all of chemistry. Not surprisingly, therefore, when such redistributions occur, two men whose discourse had previously proceeded with apparently full understanding may suddenly find themselves responding to the same stimulus with incompatible descriptions and generalizations. Those difficulties will not be felt in all areas of even their scientific discourse, but they will arise and will then cluster most densely about the phenomena upon which the choice of theory most centrally depends.

这类问题虽然首先在沟通中显现，但并非仅仅是语言问题，也无法简单地通过对棘手术语进行定义来解决。因为造成沟通障碍的词语部分是通过直接应用于范例而习得的，所以沟通障碍的参与者无法说：“我使用‘元素’（或‘混合物’、‘行星’或‘无约束运动’）一词的方式取决于以下标准。”也就是说，他们无法使用一种双方都能以相同方式使用的中立语言，这种语言既能充分表达双方的理论，又能充分表达双方理论的经验结果。部分差异存在于语言运用之前，尽管这种差异最终体现在语言之中。

Such problems, though they first become evident in communication, are not merely linguistic, and they cannot be resolved simply by stipulating the definitions of troublesome terms. Because the words about which difficulties cluster have been learned in part from direct application to exemplars, the participants in a communication breakdown cannot say, “I use the word ‘element’ (or ‘mixture,’ or ‘planet,’ or ‘unconstrained motion’) in ways determined by the following criteria.” They cannot, that is, resort to a neutral language which both use in the same way and which is adequate to the statement of both their theories or even of both those theories’ empirical consequences. Part of the difference is prior to the application of the languages in which it is nevertheless reflected.

然而，经历此类沟通障碍的人们必须有所应对。他们所受到的刺激是相同的，他们的神经系统也基本相同，尽管其程序设定有所不同。此外，除了一个虽小却至关重要的经验领域外，他们的神经程序也几乎相同，因为他们拥有共同的历史，除了近期的过去。因此，他们的日常生活、大部分科学领域以及语言都是共享的。鉴于如此多的共同点，他们应该能够发现彼此之间的诸多差异。然而，所需的技巧既不简单，也不轻松，更不是科学家常用的工具。科学家们很少能真正认识到这些技巧的本质，也很少会长时间使用这些技巧，除非是为了促成对方的转变，或者说服自己转变不会发生。

The men who experience such communication breakdowns must, however, have some recourse. The stimuli that impinge upon them are the same. So is their general neural apparatus, however differently programmed. Furthermore, except in a small, if all-important, area of experience even their neural programming must be very nearly the same, for they share a history, except the immediate past. As a result, both their everyday and most of their scientific world and language are shared. Given that much in common, they should be able to find out a great deal about how they differ. The techniques required are not, however, either straightforward, or comfortable, or parts of the scientist’s normal arsenal. Scientists rarely recognize them for quite what they are, and they seldom use them for longer than is required to induce conversion or convince themselves that it will not be obtained.

简而言之，沟通障碍中的参与者可以做的，是认识到彼此是不同语言的成员。社群成员可以成为翻译者。17他们将自身群体内部和群体间话语的差异作为研究对象，首先尝试找出那些在各自群体内部使用无误，但在群体间讨论中却成为难题的术语和表达方式。（不存在此类难题的表达方式可以进行同音翻译。）在找出科学交流中的这些难点之后，他们可以进一步运用彼此共享的日常词汇来阐明这些难题。也就是说，每个人都可以尝试去理解，当面对一个与自己语言反应不同的刺激时，对方会看到什么、说什么。如果他们能够避免将异常行为简单地解释为错误或疯狂，那么随着时间的推移，他们或许能够很好地预测彼此的行为。每个人都将学会用自己的语言翻译对方的理论及其推论，并同时用自己的语言描述该理论所适用的世界。这就是科学史学家在处理过时的科学理论时经常（或者应该）做的事情。

Briefly put, what the participants in a communication breakdown can do is recognize each other as members of different language communities and then become translators.17 Taking the differences between their own intra- and inter-group discourse as itself a subject for study, they can first attempt to discover the terms and locutions that, used unproblematically within each community, are nevertheless foci of trouble for inter-group discussions. (Locutions that present no such difficulties may be homophonically translated.) Having isolated such areas of difficulty in scientific communication, they can next resort to their shared everyday vocabularies in an effort further to elucidate their troubles. Each may, that is, try to discover what the other would see and say when presented with a stimulus to which his own verbal response would be different. If they can sufficiently refrain from explaining anomalous behavior as the consequence of mere error or madness, they may in time become very good predictors of each other’s behavior. Each will have learned to translate the other’s theory and its consequences into his own language and simultaneously to describe in his language the world to which that theory applies. That is what the historian of science regularly does (or should) when dealing with out-of-date scientific theories.

翻译如果得以实施，可以让沟通障碍的参与者间接地体验到彼此观点的优点和缺点，因此它既是说服的有效工具，也是促成转变的有效工具。但即便说服也未必成功，即使成功，也未必会伴随或促成转变。这两种体验并不相同，而我直到最近才充分认识到这一重要区别。

Since translation, if pursued, allows the participants in a communication breakdown to experience vicariously something of the merits and defects of each other’s points of view, it is a potent tool both for persuasion and for conversion. But even persuasion need not succeed, and, if it does, it need not be accompanied or followed by conversion. The two experiences are not the same, an important distinction that I have only recently fully recognized.

我认为，说服某人就是让他相信自己的观点更优越，因此应该取代他自己的观点。有时，无需借助任何翻译手段，就能达到这种效果。在缺乏翻译的情况下，许多解释和问题陈述都得到了认可。一个科学群体成员能够理解的理论对另一个群体来说是晦涩难懂的。但每个语言群体通常都能从一开始就提出一些具体的研究成果，这些成果虽然可以用两个群体都能理解的句子来描述，但另一个群体却无法用自己的语言来解释。如果新的观点能够持续一段时间并不断取得成果，那么能够以这种方式表达的研究成果的数量很可能会增加。对某些人来说，仅凭这些成果就足以让他们下定决心。他们会说：我不知道新观点的支持者是如何成功的，但我必须学习；无论他们做什么，显然都是正确的。这种反应对于刚入行的人来说尤其容易产生，因为他们还没有掌握任何一个群体特有的词汇和立场。

To persuade someone is, I take it, to convince him that one’s own view is superior and ought therefore supplant his own. That much is occasionally achieved without recourse to anything like translation. In its absence many of the explanations and problem-statements endorsed by the members of one scientific group will be opaque to the other. But each language community can usually produce from the start a few concrete research results that, though describable in sentences understood in the same way by both groups, cannot yet be accounted for by the other community in its own terms. If the new viewpoint endures for a time and continues to be fruitful, the research results verbalizable in this way are likely to grow in number. For some men such results alone will be decisive. They can say: I don’t know how the proponents of the new view succeed, but I must learn; whatever they are doing, it is clearly right. That reaction comes particularly easily to men just entering the profession, for they have not yet acquired the special vocabularies and commitments of either group.

然而，即使双方都使用相同的词汇来陈述论点，通常也并非决定性的，至少在对立观点演变的后期阶段之前是如此。在那些已经入行的人当中，如果不借助翻译所带来的更广泛的比较，很少有人会被说服。尽管代价往往是冗长而复杂的句子（想想普鲁斯特与贝托莱的争论，他们就未使用“元素”一词），但许多额外的研究成果可以从一个群体的语言翻译成另一个群体的语言。此外，随着翻译的进行，双方群体中的一些成员也可能开始间接地理解，先前晦涩难懂的陈述为何在对立群体成员看来似乎是一种解释。当然，这些技巧的运用并不能保证说服。对大多数人来说，翻译是一个令人畏惧的过程，它与常规科学完全格格不入。无论如何，反驳论点总是存在的，而且也没有任何规则规定必须如何权衡。然而，随着争论不断累积，挑战一个接一个地被成功化解，最终只有盲目的固执才能解释持续的抵抗。

Arguments statable in the vocabulary that both groups use in the same way are not, however, usually decisive, at least not until a very late stage in the evolution of the opposing views. Among those already admitted to the profession, few will be persuaded without some recourse to the more extended comparisons permitted by translation. Though the price is often sentences of great length and complexity (think of the Proust-Berthollet controversy conducted without recourse to the term ‘element’), many additional research results can be translated from one community’s language into the other’s. As translation proceeds, furthermore, some members of each community may also begin vicariously to understand how a statement previously opaque could seem an explanation to members of the opposing group. The availability of techniques like these does not, of course, guarantee persuasion. For most people translation is a threatening process, and it is entirely foreign to normal science. Counter-arguments are, in any case, always available, and no rules prescribe how the balance must be struck. Nevertheless, as argument piles on argument and as challenge after challenge is successfully met, only blind stubbornness can at the end account for continued resistance.

既然如此，翻译的第二个方面——历史学家和语言学家都早已熟知这一点——就显得至关重要了。将一种理论或世界观翻译成自己的语言，并非是要将其变成……要真正融入其中，就必须融入当地环境，发现自己是在用一种原本陌生的语言思考和工作，而不仅仅是翻译它。然而，这种转变并非个人可以深思熟虑、自主选择的结果，无论他有多么充分的理由想要这样做。相反，在学习翻译的过程中，他会在某个时刻发现转变已经发生，他不知不觉地就进入了新的语言环境。或者，就像许多在中年才接触相对论或量子力学的人一样，他发现自己完全被新的观点所说服，却仍然无法将其内化，也无法在它所塑造的世界中自在地生活。从理智上讲，这样的人已经做出了选择，但要真正有效地运用这种选择，所需的转变却始终与他无缘。他或许仍然会使用新的理论，但他将以一个身处异乡的外国人的身份使用，而他之所以能选择这种理论，仅仅是因为那里已经有了“本地人”。他的工作是寄生于他们的工作之上的，因为他缺乏未来社区成员通过教育将获得的一系列思维模式。

That being the case, a second aspect of translation, long familiar to both historians and linguists, becomes crucially important. To translate a theory or worldview into one’s own language is not to make it one’s own. For that one must go native, discover that one is thinking and working in, not simply translating out of, a language that was previously foreign. That transition is not, however, one that an individual may make or refrain from making by deliberation and choice, however good his reasons for wishing to do so. Instead, at some point in the process of learning to translate, he finds that the transition has occurred, that he has slipped into the new language without a decision having been made. Or else, like many of those who first encountered, say, relativity or quantum mechanics in their middle years, he finds himself fully persuaded of the new view but nevertheless unable to internalize it and be at home in the world it helps to shape. Intellectually such a man has made his choice, but the conversion required if it is to be effective eludes him. He may use the new theory nonetheless, but he will do so as a foreigner in a foreign environment, an alternative available to him only because there are natives already there. His work is parasitic on theirs, for he lacks the constellation of mental sets which future members of the community will acquire through education.

因此，我曾将这种转变体验比作格式塔开关，它仍然是革命性过程的核心。合理的选择理由为转变提供了动力，并营造了一种更有利于转变发生的氛围。此外，翻译或许还能为神经重塑提供切入点，尽管这种重塑目前尚不为人知，但它必然是转变的基础。然而，合理的选择理由和翻译本身都不能构成转变，而我们必须阐明这一过程，才能理解这种本质上的科学变革。

The conversion experience that I have likened to a gestalt switch remains, therefore, at the heart of the revolutionary process. Good reasons for choice provide motives for conversion and a climate in which it is more likely to occur. Translation may, in addition, provide points of entry for the neural reprogramming that, however inscrutable at this time, must underlie conversion. But neither good reasons nor translation constitute conversion, and it is that process we must explicate in order to understand an essential sort of scientific change.

6. 革命与相对主义

6. Revolutions and Relativism

刚才阐述的立场的一个后果尤其令我的一些批评者感到困扰。 18他们认为我的观点是相对主义的，尤其正如本书最后一节所阐述的那样。我对翻译的评论突显了这种指责的原因。不同理论的支持者就像不同语言文化社群的成员。认识到这种相似性意味着，在某种意义上，双方的观点可能都是正确的。但就文化及其发展而言，这种立场是相对主义的。

One consequence of the position just outlined has particularly bothered a number of my critics.18 They find my viewpoint relativistic, particularly as it is developed in the last section of this book. My remarks about translation highlight the reasons for the charge. The proponents of different theories are like the members of different language-culture communities. Recognizing the parallelism suggests that in some sense both groups may be right. Applied to culture and its development that position is relativistic.

但应用于科学领域，情况可能并非如此，而且无论如何，它远非简单的相对主义，这一点正是其批评者所未能看到的。我认为，无论是作为一个群体还是在不同的群体中，发达科学的实践者本质上都是解谜者。尽管他们在选择理论时所运用的价值观也源于其工作的其他方面，但当价值观发生冲突时，展现出的提出和解决自然难题的能力，是大多数科学群体成员的主导标准。与其他任何价值观一样，解谜能力在实际应用中也存在歧义。即使两个拥有这种能力的人，他们运用这种能力后得出的判断也可能不同。但是，一个将解谜能力置于首位的群体，其行为将与一个不将解谜能力置于首位的群体截然不同。我认为，在科学领域，对解谜能力的高度重视会带来以下后果。

But applied to science it may not be, and it is in any case far from mere relativism in a respect that its critics have failed to see. Taken as a group or in groups, practitioners of the developed sciences are, I have argued, fundamentally puzzle-solvers. Though the values that they deploy at times of theory-choice derive from other aspects of their work as well, the demonstrated ability to set up and to solve puzzles presented by nature is, in case of value conflict, the dominant criterion for most members of a scientific group. Like any other value, puzzle-solving ability proves equivocal in application. Two men who share it may nevertheless differ in the judgments they draw from its use. But the behavior of a community which makes it preeminent will be very different from that of one which does not. In the sciences, I believe, the high value accorded to puzzle-solving ability has the following consequences.

想象一棵进化树，它代表着现代科学各分支从共同起源（例如原始自然哲学和工艺）发展而来的历程。从树干向上画一条线，从树干到某个分支的顶端，这条线永不折返，便可描绘出一系列相互关联的理论。考虑任意两个这样的理论，只要它们并非起源于太近的地方，就很容易设计出一系列标准，使一个不带偏见的观察者能够反复区分较早的理论和较新的理论。其中最有用的标准包括：预测的准确性，尤其是定量预测的准确性；深奥主题与日常主题之间的平衡；以及所解决的不同问题的数量。虽然简洁性、适用范围以及与其他专业的兼容性等因素也是科学发展的重要决定因素，但它们在这方面的作用较小。然而，这些标准清单并非最终版本。虽然这些探索是必要的，但我毫不怀疑它们能够完成。如果它们能够完成，那么科学发展就如同生物学一样，是一个单向且不可逆的过程。在它们应用的环境中，后期的科学理论往往比早期的理论更能有效地解决难题。这并非相对主义的立场，而是我坚信科学进步的体现。

Imagine an evolutionary tree representing the development of the modern scientific specialties from their common origins in, say, primitive natural philosophy and the crafts. A line drawn up that tree, never doubling back, from the trunk to the tip of some branch would trace a succession of theories related by descent. Considering any two such theories, chosen from points not too near their origin, it should be easy to design a list of criteria that would enable an uncommitted observer to distinguish the earlier from the more recent theory time after time. Among the most useful would be: accuracy of prediction, particularly of quantitative prediction; the balance between esoteric and everyday subject matter; and the number of different problems solved. Less useful for this purpose, though also important determinants of scientific life, would be such values as simplicity, scope, and compatibility with other specialties. Those lists are not yet the ones required, but I have no doubt that they can be completed. If they can, then scientific development is, like biological, a unidirectional and irreversible process. Later scientific theories are better than earlier ones for solving puzzles in the often quite different environments to which they are applied. That is not a relativist’s position, and it displays the sense in which I am a convinced believer in scientific progress.

然而，与科学哲学家和普通民众普遍接受的进步观念相比，这种观点缺少一个关键要素。人们通常认为，一个科学理论比之前的理论更好，不仅因为它是发现和解决难题的更佳工具，还因为它在某种程度上更好地展现了自然的真实面貌。人们常常听到这样的说法：后续的理论越来越接近真理，或者说越来越接近真理。显然，这类概括并非指理论所解答的难题和做出的具体预测，而是指理论的本体论，即理论所描述的自然实体与“真实存在”的实体之间的匹配程度。

Compared with the notion of progress most prevalent among both philosophers of science and laymen, however, this position lacks an essential element. A scientific theory is usually felt to be better than its predecessors not only in the sense that it is a better instrument for discovering and solving puzzles but also because it is somehow a better representation of what nature is really like. One often hears that successive theories grow ever closer to, or approximate more and more closely to, the truth. Apparently generalizations like that refer not to the puzzle-solutions and the concrete predictions derived from a theory but rather to its ontology, to the match, that is, between the entities with which the theory populates nature and what is “really there.”

或许还有其他方法可以挽救“真理”这一概念，使其适用于整个理论，但这种方法行不通。我认为，不存在任何独立于理论的方法来重构诸如“真实存在”之类的短语；理论的本体论与其在自然界中的“真实”对应物之间的匹配，在我看来，原则上是难以捉摸的。此外，作为一名历史学家，我对这种观点的荒谬性感到震惊。例如，我并不怀疑牛顿力学在解决难题方面优于亚里士多德力学，爱因斯坦力学也优于牛顿力学。但我无法从它们的演进中看出本体论发展的连贯方向。相反，在某些重要方面（尽管并非全部），爱因斯坦的广义相对论比牛顿力学和亚里士多德力学更接近亚里士多德的理论。尽管人们很容易将这种立场描述为相对主义，但我认为这种描述并不恰当。反之，如果这种立场确实是相对主义，我认为相对主义者并没有失去任何解释科学本质和发展所必需的知识。

Perhaps there is some other way of salvaging the notion of ‘truth’ for application to whole theories, but this one will not do. There is, I think, no theory-independent way to reconstruct phrases like ‘really there’; the notion of a match between the ontology of a theory and its “real” counterpart in nature now seems to me illusive in principle. Besides, as a historian, I am impressed with the implausability of the view. I do not doubt, for example, that Newton’s mechanics improves on Aristotle’s and that Einstein’s improves on Newton’s as instruments for puzzle-solving. But I can see in their succession no coherent direction of ontological development. On the contrary, in some important respects, though by no means in all, Einstein’s general theory of relativity is closer to Aristotle’s than either of them is to Newton’s. Though the temptation to describe that position as relativistic is understandable, the description seems to me wrong. Conversely, if the position be relativism, I cannot see that the relativist loses anything needed to account for the nature and development of the sciences.

7. 科学的本质

7. The Nature of Science

最后，我想简要讨论一下读者对我原文的两种常见反应：一种是批评性的，另一种是赞扬性的。但我认为这两种反应都不完全正确。虽然这两种反应都与我之前讨论的内容无关，彼此之间也无关联，但它们都足够普遍，至少需要我做出一些回应。

I conclude with a brief discussion of two recurrent reactions to my original text, the first critical, the second favorable, and neither, I think, quite right. Though the two relate neither to what has been said so far nor to each other, both have been sufficiently prevalent to demand at least some response.

一些读者注意到，我反复在描述性和规范性模式之间切换，这种转换在一些段落中尤为明显，这些段落以“但科学家并非如此行事”开头，却以“科学家不应该这样做”结尾。一些批评者认为我混淆了描述和规范，违反了古老的哲学定理：“是”不能蕴含“应该”。 19

A few readers of my original text have noticed that I repeatedly pass back and forth between the descriptive and the normative modes, a transition particularly marked in occasional passages that open with, “But that is not what scientists do,” and close by claiming that scientists ought not do so. Some critics claim that I am confusing description with prescription, violating the time-honored philosophical theorem: ‘Is’ cannot imply ‘ought.’19

实际上，该定理已沦为一种标签，不再处处受到推崇。许多当代哲学家发现，规范性和描述性在某些重要语境中密不可分。20 “是”与“应该”绝非总是像表面看起来那样泾渭分明。然而，无需诉诸当代语言哲学的精妙之处，即可厘清我立场中这一方面看似混乱之处。前文阐述了一种关于科学本质的观点或理论，与其他科学哲学一样，该理论对科学家若想成功应如何行事具有影响。尽管它未必正确（与其他任何理论一样），但它为反复强调“应该”和“应当”提供了合法依据。反之，认真对待该理论的一个理由是，科学家们的方法经过开发和选择，旨在取得成功，而他们的行为实际上也符合该理论的预期。我的描述性概括恰恰是该理论的证据，因为它们也可以从该理论中推导出来；而根据其他科学本质的观点，它们则构成了异常行为。

That theorem has, in practice, become a tag, and it is no longer everywhere honored. A number of contemporary philosophers have discovered important contexts in which the normative and the descriptive are inextricably mixed.20 ‘Is’ and ‘ought’ are by no means always so separate as they have seemed. But no recourse to the subtleties of contemporary linguistic philosophy is needed to unravel what has seemed confused about this aspect of my position. The preceding pages present a viewpoint or theory about the nature of science, and, like other philosophies of science, the theory has consequences for the way in which scientists should behave if their enterprise is to succeed. Though it need not be right, any more than any other theory, it provides a legitimate basis for reiterated ‘oughts’ and ‘shoulds.’ Conversely, one set of reasons for taking the theory seriously is that scientists, whose methods have been developed and selected for their success, do in fact behave as the theory says they should. My descriptive generalizations are evidence for the theory precisely because they can also be derived from it, whereas on other views of the nature of science they constitute anomalous behavior.

我认为，这种论证的循环性并非恶性循环。所讨论的观点所带来的后果，并未被其最初所依据的观察结果所穷尽。甚至在本书初版之前，我就发现它所提出的部分理论是探索科学行为和发展的一种有用工具。将这篇后记与原著进行比较，或许会发现它一直发挥着这样的作用。任何纯粹循环论证的观点都无法提供这样的指导。

The circularity of that argument is not, I think, vicious. The consequences of the viewpoint being discussed are not exhausted by the observations upon which it rested at the start. Even before this book was first published, I had found parts of the theory it presents a useful tool for the exploration of scientific behavior and development. Comparison of this postscript with the pages of the original may suggest that it has continued to play that role. No merely circular point of view can provide such guidance.
