对于本书的最后一个反响，我的回答或许有所不同。许多读者之所以从中获益，并非因为本书阐明了科学，而是因为他们认为书中的主要论点也适用于其他诸多领域。我理解他们的意思，也无意阻止他们拓展这一观点，但他们的反应仍然令我感到困惑。本书将科学发展描绘成一系列受传统束缚的时期，其间穿插着非累积性的断裂，因此，其论点无疑具有广泛的适用性。而这本就应该如此，因为它们借鉴自其他领域。文学史、音乐史、艺术史、政治发展史以及许多其他人类活动史的学者，长期以来都以同样的方式描述他们的研究对象。以风格、品味和制度结构的革命性断裂来划分时期，一直是他们的常用工具。如果说我在这些概念上有什么独创之处，那主要在于我将它们应用于科学领域——而人们普遍认为科学的发展方式与其他领域截然不同。或许，将范式视为具体的成就或典范，是第二个贡献。例如，我怀疑，如果绘画作品被视为彼此模仿而非遵循某些抽象的风格准则而创作，那么围绕艺术风格概念的一些众所周知的难题或许就会迎刃而解。21

To one last reaction to this book, my answer must be of a different sort. A number of those who have taken pleasure from it have done so less because it illuminates science than because they read its main theses as applicable to many other fields as well. I see what they mean and would not like to discourage their attempts to extend the position, but their reaction has nevertheless puzzled me. To the extent that the book portrays scientific development as a succession of tradition-bound periods punctuated by non-cumulative breaks, its theses are undoubtedly of wide applicability. But they should be, for they are borrowed from other fields. Historians of literature, of music, of the arts, of political development, and of many other human activities have long described their subjects in the same way. Periodization in terms of revolutionary breaks in style, taste, and institutional structure have been among their standard tools. If I have been original with respect to concepts like these, it has mainly been by applying them to the sciences, fields which had been widely thought to develop in a different way. Conceivably the notion of a paradigm as a concrete achievement, an exemplar, is a second contribution. I suspect, for example, that some of the notorious difficulties surrounding the notion of style in the arts may vanish if paintings can be seen to be modeled on one another rather than produced in conformity to some abstracted canons of style.21

然而，这本书还有另一个目的，那就是要表达另一种观点，而这个观点对于很多读者来说并不那么明显。尽管科学发展与其他领域的相似之处可能比人们通常认为的要多，但两者之间也存在显著差异。例如，无论进步本身的定义是什么，说科学至少在其发展的某个阶段之后，其进步方式与其他领域截然不同，这种说法并非完全错误。本书的目的之一就是探讨这些差异并尝试解释它们。

This book, however, was intended also to make another sort of point, one that has been less clearly visible to many of its readers. Though scientific development may resemble that in other fields more closely than has often been supposed, it is also strikingly different. To say, for example, that the sciences, at least after a certain point in their development, progress in a way that other fields do not, cannot have been all wrong, whatever progress itself may be. One of the objects of the book was to examine such differences and begin accounting for them.

例如，请思考上文反复强调的发达科学领域中缺乏（或者如我现在应该说的，相对稀少）竞争学派这一点。或者回想一下我之前关于特定科学共同体的成员在很大程度上构成该共同体工作的唯一受众和唯一评判者的观点。再想想科学教育的特殊性，以解决难题为目标，以及科学团体在危机和决策时期所运用的价值体系。本书还阐述了其他类似的特征，这些特征并非科学独有，但它们共同构成了科学活动的独特之处。

Consider, for example, the reiterated emphasis, above, on the absence or, as I should now say, on the relative scarcity of competing schools in the developed sciences. Or remember my remarks about the extent to which the members of a given scientific community provide the only audience and the only judges of that community’s work. Or think again about the special nature of scientific education, about puzzle-solving as a goal, and about the value system which the scientific group deploys in periods of crisis and decision. The book isolates other features of the same sort, none necessarily unique to science but in conjunction setting the activity apart.

关于科学的所有这些特征，还有许多值得我们去了解。在后记的开头，我强调了研究科学社群结构的必要性，而结尾，我将着重强调对其他领域相应社群进行类似研究，尤其是进行比较研究的必要性。一个人如何选择加入某个特定的社群（无论是否属于科学领域）？又是如何被选入其中的？融入社群的过程和阶段是什么？社群的集体目标是什么？它能够容忍哪些偏差（无论是个人偏差还是集体偏差）？它又是如何控制那些不可接受的偏差的？对科学更全面的理解也取决于对其他类型问题的解答，但没有哪个领域比科学领域更迫切需要更多的研究。科学知识，如同语言一样，本质上是某个群体的共同财产，否则就什么都不是。为了理解科学知识，我们需要了解创造和运用科学知识的群体的特殊特征。

About all these features of science there is a great deal more to be learned. Having opened this postscript by emphasizing the need to study the community structure of science, I shall close by underscoring the need for similar and, above all, for comparative study of the corresponding communities in other fields. How does one elect and how is one elected to membership in a particular community, scientific or not? What is the process and what are the stages of socialization to the group? What does the group collectively see as its goals; what deviations, individual or collective, will it tolerate; and how does it control the impermissible aberration? A fuller understanding of science will depend on answers to other sorts of questions as well, but there is no area in which more work is so badly needed. Scientific knowledge, like language, is intrinsically the common property of a group or else nothing at all. To understand it we shall need to know the special characteristics of the groups that create and use it.

His paper “Reflections on My Critics” (1970) (in Criticism and the Growth of Knowledge, 231–78; reprinted in Road since Structure, 123–75) uses a trope he repeated for decades. There are, he suggested, two Kuhns: Kuhn1 and Kuhn2. Kuhn 1was himself, but he sometimes felt he had to postulate an imaginary figure, who wrote another text named Structure, saying things other than Kuhn1 intended. He singled out one and only one critic in Lakatos and Musgrave, Masterman, who discussed his own work, namely that of Kuhn1. She was a fierce, acerbic, and iconoclastic thinker, who described herself as scientific, not philosophical, but “in the computer sciences” rather than the physical sciences (“Nature of a Paradigm,” 60). Another critic of comparable impact was Dudley Shapere, to whom Kuhn paid careful attention (“The Structure of Scientific Revolutions,” Philosophical Review 73 [1964]: 383–94.). These two, Masterman and Shapere, got things right, in my opinion, by focusing on obscurities in the concept of a paradigm. It was left to later critics to obsess about incommensurability.

42.奥古斯特·孔德（1798–1857）之所以选择“实证主义”作为其哲学的名称，是因为他认为“实证”在所有欧洲语言中都具有积极的含义。他秉持典型的乐观主义和对进步的信念，认为人类最初通过祈求神灵来理解自身在宇宙中的位置，后来通过形而上学，最终（1840年）进入了实证时代，在这个时代，我们将在科学研究的帮助下，为自己的命运负责。受孔德和伯特兰·罗素启发，维也纳学派自称为逻辑实证主义者，后来又称为逻辑经验主义者。如今，人们通常将逻辑实证主义者称为“实证主义者”，本文也沿用这一惯例。严格来说，实证主义指的是孔德的反形而上学思想。

42. Auguste Comte (1798–1857) chose the name “positivism” for his philosophy because he thought the word positive had positive connotations in all European languages. With typical optimism and faith in progress, he held that the human race had made sense of its place in the universe first by invoking gods, then by metaphysics, but finally (1840) had entered the positive age in which we would be responsible for our own destinies, aided by scientific research. The Vienna Circle, inspired by Comte and Bertrand Russell, called themselves logical positivists, later, logical empiricists. Today it is usual to refer to the logical positivists as “positivists,” and I follow that custom in the text. Strictly speaking, positivism refers to Comte’s antimetaphysical ideas.

9.值得注意的是，富兰克林理论的被接受并没有完全结束争论。1759年，罗伯特·西默提出了该理论的双流体版本，此后多年，电工们一直争论电究竟是由单一流体还是两种流体构成。但关于这一问题的争论恰恰印证了前文所述，即一项普遍认可的成就如何将整个行业团结起来。尽管电工们在这个问题上仍然存在分歧，但他们很快得出结论：没有任何实验测试能够区分该理论的两种版本，因此它们是等价的。此后，两个学派都能够并且确实充分利用了富兰克林理论带来的所有益处（同上，第543-546页，548-554页）。

9. It should be noted that the acceptance of Franklin’s theory did not end quite all debate. In 1759 Robert Symmer proposed a two-fluid version of that theory, and for many years thereafter electricians were divided about whether electricity was a single fluid or two. But the debates on this subject only confirm what has been said above about the manner in which a universally recognized achievement unites the profession. Electricians, though they continued divided on this point, rapidly concluded that no experimental tests could distinguish the two versions of the theory and that they were therefore equivalent. After that, both schools could and did exploit all the benefits that the Franklinian theory provided (ibid., pp. 543–46, 548–54).

11.电学史提供了一个绝佳的例证，普里斯特利、开尔文等人的经历便可与之比肩。富兰克林记载，诺莱特在19世纪中叶是欧洲大陆最具影响力的电学家，“他亲眼目睹了自己成为其学派的最后一人，除了他的弟子兼直属门徒本杰明·富兰克林先生”（马克斯·法兰德编，《本杰明·富兰克林回忆录》，加州伯克利，1949年，第384-386页）。然而，更有趣的是，一些学派在与专业科学日益疏离的情况下依然能够延续下去。例如，占星术曾是天文学不可分割的一部分。又如，在18世纪末19世纪初，曾经备受尊崇的“浪漫”化学传统得以延续。查尔斯·C·吉利斯皮在《百科全书与雅各宾派科学哲学：思想与后果研究》，载于《科学史批判问题》，马歇尔·克拉格特编（威斯康星州麦迪逊，1959 年），第 255-289 页，讨论了这一传统；并在《拉马克进化论的形成》，载于《国际科学史档案》，第 37 卷（1956 年），第 323-338 页，讨论了这一传统。

More interesting, however, is the endurance of whole schools in increasing isolation from professional science. Consider, for example, the case of astrology, which was once an integral part of astronomy. Or consider the continuation in the late eighteenth and early nineteenth centuries of a previously respected tradition of “romantic” chemistry. This is the tradition discussed by Charles C. Gillispie in “The Encyclopédie and the Jacobin Philosophy of Science: A Study in Ideas and Consequences,” Critical Problems in the History of Science, ed. The post-Franklinian developments include an immense increase in the sensitivity of charge detectors, the first reliable and generally diffused techniques for measuring charge, the evolution of the concept of capacity and its relation to a newly refined notion of electric tension, and the quantification of electrostatic force. On all of these see Roller and Roller, op. cit., pp. 66–81; W. C. Walker, “The Detection and Estimation of Electric Charges in the Eighteenth Century,” Annals of Science, I (1936), 66–100; and Edmund Hoppe, Geschichte der Elektrizität (Leipzig, 1884), Part I, chaps. iii–iv.

Krypton, one of the two main fission products, seems not to have been identified by chemical means until after the reaction was well understood. Barium, the other product, was almost identified chemically at a late stage of the investigation because, as it happened, that element had to be added to the radioactive solution to precipitate the heavy element for which nuclear chemists were looking. Failure to separate that added barium from the radioactive product finally led, after the reaction had been repeatedly investigated for almost five years, to the following report: “As chemists we should be led by this research . . . to change all the names in the preceding [reaction] schema and thus write Ba, La, Ce instead of Ra, Ac, Th. But as ‘nuclear chemists,’ with close affiliations to physics, we cannot bring ourselves to this leap which would contradict all previous experience of nuclear physics. It may be that a series of strange accidents renders our results deceptive” (Otto Hahn and Fritz Strassman, “Uber den Nachweis und das Verhalten der bei der Bestrahlung des Urans mittels Neutronen entstehended Erdalkalimetalle,” Die Naturwissenschaften, XXVII [1939], 15).

Nevertheless, the generalization badly needs systematic investigation. Harvey C. Lehman (Age and Achievement [Princeton, 1953]) provides many useful data; but his studies make no attempt to single out contributions that involve fundamental reconceptualization. Nor do they inquire about the special circumstances, if any, that may accompany relatively late productivity in the sciences.

3.科学史学家经常会遇到这种认知盲点，而且这种盲点表现得尤为突出。来自理科专业的学生往往是他们教过的最有成就感的群体​​，但同时，在教学初期，他们也常常是最令人沮丧的。因为理科生“知道正确答案”，所以要让他们用古代科学自身的视角去分析它，就变得格外困难。

3. Historians of science often encounter this blindness in a particularly striking form. The group of students who come to them from the sciences is very often the most rewarding group they teach. But it is also usually the most frustrating at the start. Because science students “know the right answers,” it is particularly difficult to make them analyze an older science in its own terms.

后记——1969年

Postscript—1969

1.这篇后记最初是应我曾经的学生和多年的朋友，东京大学的中山茂博士的建议而撰写的，目的是将其收录在他翻译的本书日文版中。我感谢他提出这个想法，感谢他耐心等待最终完成，也感谢他允许我将这篇后记收录到英文版中。

1. This postscript was first prepared at the suggestion of my onetime student and long-time friend, Dr. Shigeru Nakayama of the University of Tokyo, for inclusion in his Japanese translation of this book. I am grateful to him for the idea, for his patience in awaiting its fruition, and for permission to include the result in the English language edition.

2.本次修订我并未进行系统性的改写，仅对少数排版错误和两处包含个别错误的段落进行了修改。其中一处错误是上文第30-33页对牛顿《自然哲学的数学原理》在十八世纪力学发展中所起作用的描述。另一处错误则涉及第84页对危机的应对。

2. For this edition I have attempted no systematic rewriting, restricting alterations to a few typographical errors plus two passages which contained isolable errors. One of these is the description of the role of Newton’s Principia in the development of eighteenth-century mechanics on pp. 30–33, above. The other concerns the response to crises on p. 84.

3.其他迹象可见于我近期的两篇文章：一篇是《反思我的批评者》，收录于伊姆雷·拉卡托斯和艾伦·马斯格雷夫主编的《批评与知识的增长》（剑桥，1970年）；另一篇是《对范式的再思考》，收录于弗雷德里克·苏佩主编的《科学理论的结构》（伊利诺伊州厄巴纳，1970年或1971年），这两篇文章目前均已出版。下文中，我将把第一篇文章称为“反思”，并将其所在卷册称为《知识的增长》；第二篇文章则称为“再思考”。

3. I shall cite the first of these essays below as “Reflections” and the volume in which it appears as Growth of Knowledge; the second essay will be referred to as “Second Thoughts.”

13.如果所有法律都像牛顿定律那样，所有规则都像十诫那样，那么这一点或许根本无需赘述。那样的话，“违法”一词就毫无意义，拒绝规则也不会让人觉得某个过程不受法律约束。然而不幸的是，交通法规和类似的立法产物是可以被违反的，这就很容易造成误解。

13. This point might never have needed making if all laws were like Newton’s and all rules like the Ten Commandments. In that case the phrase ‘breaking a law’ would be nonsense, and a rejection of rules would not seem to imply a process not governed by law. Unfortunately, traffic laws and similar products of legislation can be broken, which makes the confusion easy.

14.对于《再思考》的读者来说，以下这段晦涩的论述或许具有一定的启发意义。能否立即识别自然界中各个家族的成员，取决于神经处理之后，待区分的家族之间是否存在感知上的空白空间。例如，如果感知到的水禽种类是一个连续谱，从鹅到天鹅，我们就必须引入特定的标准来区分它们。对于不可观察的实体，也可以提出类似的观点。如果一个物理理论只承认电流的存在，那么即使没有一套规则来规定识别电流的必要和充分条件，少量标准（这些标准可能因情况而异）也足以识别电流。这一点引出了一个可能更为重要的推论。如果存在一套识别某个理论实体的必要和充分条件，那么可以通过替换将该实体从理论的本体论中剔除。然而，如果没有这样的规则，这些实体就无法被剔除；该理论因此需要它们的存在。

14. For readers of “Second Thoughts” the following cryptic remarks may be leading. The possibility of immediate recognition of the members of natural families depends upon the existence, after neural processing, of empty perceptual space between the families to be discriminated. If, for example, there were a perceived continuum of waterfowl ranging from geese to swans, we should be compelled to introduce a specific criterion for distinguishing them. A similar point can be made for unobservable entities. If a physical theory admits the existence of nothing else like an electric current, then a small number of criteria, which may vary considerably from case to case, will suffice to identify currents even though there is no set of rules that specifies the necessary and sufficient conditions for the identification. That point suggests a plausible corollary which may be more important. Given a set of necessary and sufficient conditions for identifying a theoretical entity, that entity can be eliminated from the ontology of a theory by substitution. In the absence of such rules, however, these entities are not eliminable; the theory then demands their existence.
